discussions.title: [Bug] Windows: a drive root (`C:\`, `D:\`) cannot be used as a workspace — session creation fails with EPERM and reports nothing
discussions.body:
### Summary
On Windows, selecting a filesystem root (`D:\`) as a workspace succeeds at the registry level,
but the session that should be created in it never appears. The UI shows no error at all.

### Environment
- DSH 0.1.5-rc.1 (`npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`), Windows, Node v24.19.0
- Profile `web` (bundles: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app`)

### Steps to reproduce
1. Open the workspace picker and add `D:\` (any drive root).
2. The picker accepts it; `D:\` is added to the workspace list.
3. A session is never created in it — the UI stays on the previous workspace, with no error.

### Evidence
The workspace record *is* written (`<dshHome>/storages/workspace.json`):

```json
"ba8cae3c-…": { "path": "D:\\", "title": "D:\\", "sessionIds": [] }
```

`sessionIds` stays empty forever. Calling the same RPC the UI uses
(`session/create` with that `workspaceId`) returns the server error verbatim:

```
failed to create session "session-…":
Error: failed to ensure project directory "D:\":
Error: EPERM: operation not permitted, mkdir 'D:\'
```

### Root cause
`packages/api/session-controller/src/index.ts`, in `createOrAdopt`:

```ts
try {
    await mkdir(cwd, { recursive: true });
} catch (error) {
    throw new Error(`failed to ensure project directory "${cwd}": ${String(error)}`, { cause: error });
}
```

`mkdir(cwd, { recursive: true })` is called unconditionally, without checking whether the
directory already exists. On Windows, Node throws `EPERM` for a recursive mkdir on a drive
root even when that root exists. Verified standalone on the same machine:

| call | result |
|---|---|
| `fs.mkdirSync('D:\\', { recursive: true })` | **EPERM** |
| `fs.mkdirSync('C:\\', { recursive: true })` | **EPERM** |
| `fs.mkdirSync('D:\\existing-subdir', { recursive: true })` | ok |
| `fs.mkdirSync(<tmp> + '\\a\\b', { recursive: true })` | ok |

This affects every drive root, not just `D:\`.

Note the documented contract disagrees: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets`'s sibling package
`dsh-workspace` states that a project can be created "from any existing, fully-qualified
directory: filesystem roots such as `C:\` and ordinary directories both work" — so the
workspace layer accepts a drive root that the session layer can never create a session in.

### Suggested fix
Check for existence first (or only mkdir on `ENOENT`), e.g. `stat`/`access` the path and
skip the mkdir when it is already a directory.

### Secondary issue: the failure is completely silent
`packages/client/ui-workspace`, in `startSession`:

```js
this.openWorkspace(target).catch((reason) => {
    console.warn("new session failed:", reason);
});
```

No modal, no toast, no status line — the user only sees that "clicking does nothing".
The directory-picker flow has a proper error modal for the `createWorkspace` failure path
(`folderError`), but the session-creation failure path has none. Making this surface to the
user would have turned a confusing silent failure into a one-line diagnosis.

discussions.title: Issue: child agents do not receive the preset-provided skill tool (spawn delegation route)
discussions.body:
Issue: child agents do not receive the preset-provided skill tool (spawn delegation route)

Environment

  • DSH Web (dsh web), profile web (composition: @deepseek-ai/dsh-base + @deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app + user patches)
  • One user agent preset that mounts skill-filesystem (with a local customSkillDirs root) and tool-skill. The host patch disables both host-plane rows, as its comment intends: "tool-skill is what a preset mounts to give its agent the catalog and loader at all."
  • Node v24.20.0, Windows 11

Problem

A preset row that registers a tool for its agent (@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill, which registers skill and the session skill catalog) is visible to the parent agent but absent from delegated children, even though other preset-provided tools reach the same children on the same delegation route.

This contradicts the stated property of the preset join introduced by child agents join their parent's preset (.agents/notes/implemented/bug-fix/2026-08-10-child-agents-join-their-parent-preset.md):

A child's capabilities are exactly its parent's, minus whatever its own toolFilter removes

Whether this is a regression or an intended exclusion is what I could not determine from the repository; the note's testing section covers the fork route, while the reproducible case below uses provider: spawn.

Reproduction

  1. In a preset, mount an agent-plane tool row and a local skill provider, and give the preset seven flat skill files:

    • skill-filesystem with customSkillDirs pointing at the preset's own subagents/ directory (seven <name>.md files with name + description frontmatter)
    • tool-skill (@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill)

  2. Start a session on that preset. Inspect the tools the model receives (request/header.tools in the session log):

    • parent agent: 44 tools, including skill, plus a skill-catalog user message with 30 entries (seven of them from the preset's directory)

  3. Delegate a child with a @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent row configured as:

    yaml
    provider: spawn
toolName: subagent_exec
backgroundMode: continuable
toolFilter: { deny: ['subagent', 'subagent_exec'] }

  4. Inspect the child's own session log request/header.tools:

    • child: 41 tools, no skill, and no skill-catalog message at all
    • the child also self-reports "no tool named skill" and "no <available_skills> block"

    Both counts are read from the request/header event of the respective session log — the tool list the harness actually sent — not from either agent's self-report. Full tool name lists for both sides can be attached on request.

  5. Control: the child does receive tools that exist only in the preset's layer. tool-pwsh and tool-todo are both disabled by the host patch (packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml) and re-declared by the preset, and the child has both (pwsh, todo_write). So the child is demonstrably inheriting the parent's preset composition — it is not the "child that joined no preset" failure mode.

Observed vs expected

  | parent | child | expected (per the note) -- | -- | -- | -- tool count | 44 | 41 | 44 minus the child's own filter skill | present | absent | present unless the child's filter names it skill catalog message | 30 entries | none | a catalog reflecting the child's visible skill view

The child's filter names only two tools (subagent, subagent_exec). One further inherited tool — skill — is missing without being named by that filter, and without any error, log entry, or empty-catalog notice.

The "the filter did it" explanation is already excluded by experiment: an earlier revision of the same preset denied skill as well, and removing that name from the deny list did not change the child's tool set at all. It only changed the parent's (the same mask had been removing the parent's own loader). So the child never sees skill regardless of what the filter says.

Why this is not the toolFilter doing it (already ruled out)

  • The child's filter denies only subagent and subagent_exec. An earlier revision of the same preset did deny skill as well; removing that name did not change the child's tool set — it only restored skill for the parent, which the same mask had been removing. The child never sees skill either way.
  • The tools registry applies a restriction to what a scope inherits and exempts only what the scope registers itself (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts, the view() doc comment: "A restriction filters what a scope inherits … and never what its OWN layer registers"). A preset row registers into the preset's layer, i.e. into the inherited surface of a child that joined that preset. So a filter that does not name skill is not the reason it is missing.

Relationship to existing coverage

  • The join note's testing section lists packages/subagent/subagent-in-process-driver/tests/preset-inheritance.spec.ts, which asserts "the schemas in the child's own request" against a host composition carrying no model-facing rows. That fixture has no tool-skill row and no skill provider, so a missing skill tool could not appear as a failure there.
  • The same note states that a snapshot scenario would need "an example that mounts a roster AND delegates"; no shipped example does. The reproducible case above is a user preset that both mounts a roster and delegates on provider: spawn.

What I could not determine

  • Whether the child is expected to have a skill tool on the spawn route at all, or whether the loader is deliberately parent-only (the tool-skill source notes that register() files into the calling context's scope, so "a plugin mounted inside an agent preset registers for that agent alone"). If parent-only is intended, the catalog/listener asymmetry below is still unexplained.
  • Why the child receives no catalog message: the tool-skill step listener treats a non-visible tool as an empty snapshot, but the registry view for a joined child should resolve the preset layer's providers. An empty catalog for a child that can see preset-layer tools is the part that looks unintended to me.

Why it matters (user-facing impact)

A preset whose subagents are meant to load their own role instructions by name cannot do so: every role definition must be pasted into each child's prompt by the parent. For a preset that delegates seven single-purpose roles, that is roughly 800–1500 characters duplicated per dispatch in the parent's context, and the child can never reload its role definition mid-task. It also means the /skill-name explicit-invocation gesture has no effect inside a delegated session.

Requested outcome

Clarify which of these is true, and if the first, fix it:

  1. A joined child should see the preset layer's tools and its skill catalog, minus its own filter — the current behavior is a regression of the 2026-08-10 join on the spawn route.
  2. The exclusion is deliberate for the loader and/or the catalog, and the join note's "exactly its parent's, minus whatever its own toolFilter removes" should be narrowed accordingly, plus a documented way for a preset to give its children a skill catalog.

If it helps, I can attach the raw measurements (tool name lists for parent and child, and the decoded event sequence of both sessions)

discussions.title: [Bug] pi-ai/OpenAI Responses: data-only keep-alives reach JSON.parse
discussions.body:
## Summary

With a third-party OpenAI Responses-compatible gateway, data-only keep-alive
frames can reach the OpenAI SDK JSON parser and fail an otherwise healthy DSH
turn.

The gateway is not emitting fully conforming SSE, but a narrowly scoped
compatibility guard would let DSH work with this class of relay without hiding
other malformed payloads.

## Environment

- macOS 26.6.1 (25G76)
- Node.js 24.19.0
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.5-rc.1`
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai@0.1.5-rc.1`
- `@earendil-works/pi-ai@0.85.1`
- `openai@6.40.0`
- custom GPT-family model through `llm-pi-ai` / `openai-responses`

## Sanitized wire evidence

Two observed forms were:

```text
data:

```

and:

```text
: keep-alive
: keep-alive
data: :

```

The proper SSE comment lines are ignored, but the data-only lines are dispatched
as messages and passed to `JSON.parse`.

## Actual behavior

The turn fails with messages equivalent to:

```text
Could not parse message into JSON
From chunk: [ 'data: ' ]

Could not parse message into JSON: :
From chunk: [ ': keep-alive', ': keep-alive', 'data: :' ]
```

The Web UI then surfaces `Unexpected end of JSON input` or
`Unexpected token ':', ":" is not valid JSON`.

## Expected behavior

When an SSE event has no explicit event type and its trimmed data payload is
exactly empty or a single colon, treat it as a malformed-but-empty keep-alive
and skip it. All other invalid JSON must still fail visibly.

## Narrow workaround validated locally

At the streaming parser boundary, before `JSON.parse`:

```js
const payload = sse.data.trim()
if (sse.event === null && (payload === '' || payload === ':')) continue
```

This was tested with:

1. empty `data:` skipped;
2. `data: :` skipped;
3. a following valid `response.completed` event still delivered;
4. `data: not-json` still throwing `SyntaxError`.

The best upstream location may be the pi-ai/OpenAI Responses compatibility
boundary rather than a direct modification of the vendored OpenAI SDK. The
important property is that the tolerance stays exact and does not become a
general “ignore malformed JSON” rule.

discussions.title: [Bug] OpenAI Responses final item completes but missing response.completed hangs until idle timeout
discussions.body:
## Summary

A third-party OpenAI Responses-compatible gateway can complete a final answer
item but omit `response.completed` and keep the SSE connection open. DSH has the
complete answer text, yet waits until the 300-second stream idle timeout and
then marks the turn failed.

## Environment

- macOS 26.6.1 (25G76)
- Node.js 24.19.0
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.5-rc.1`
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai@0.1.5-rc.1`
- `@earendil-works/pi-ai@0.85.1`
- custom GPT-family model through `llm-pi-ai` / `openai-responses`

## Sanitized event sequence

```text
response.output_item.added       item.type=message
response.output_text.delta       ...complete answer text...
response.output_item.done        item.type=message, phase=final_answer
# no response.completed / response.failed / response.incomplete
# connection remains open and may emit keep-alives
```

## Actual behavior

- The full final answer is visible in the received stream.
- No terminal response event arrives.
- After about 300 seconds, the attempt fails with
  `pi-ai stream idle timeout after 300000ms`.
- Retry may repeat the same long wait and discard an otherwise complete answer.

## Expected behavior

DSH should offer a bounded, explicit compatibility path for providers that
finish a `phase=final_answer` message item but omit the response-level terminal
event. Strict behavior can remain the default if accepting the item-level
terminal signal globally is considered too permissive.

## Locally validated compatibility behavior

After `response.output_item.done` for a message whose phase is `final_answer`:

1. wait a short grace period for a conforming response-level terminal event;
2. if it arrives, use it and preserve its usage/status;
3. if it does not arrive, abort the hanging read and finish from the completed
   item with an explicit compatibility stop reason;
4. do not apply this fallback to partial messages or tool-call items.

A 2-second local grace period passed both regression paths: normal
`response.completed` preserved usage, while a deliberately hanging source
ended locally after the completed final item. I am not proposing that 2 seconds
must be the global default; a provider-level option such as
`terminalEventGraceMs` would make the trade-off explicit. When fallback is used,
response-level usage may be unavailable and should not be fabricated.

discussions.title: [Bug] pi-ai localized timeout text is classified as PI_AI_ERROR and skips retry
discussions.body:
## Summary

`dsh-llm-pi-ai` recognizes English `timeout` / `timed out` text, but a gateway
that reports the localized Chinese message `upstream_error: 请求超时` falls
through to `PI_AI_ERROR`. Since the generic code is not retryable by default,
a real transient timeout terminates the turn immediately.

## Environment

- macOS 26.6.1 (25G76)
- Node.js 24.19.0
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.5-rc.1`
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai@0.1.5-rc.1`
- custom GPT-family model through `llm-pi-ai` / `openai-responses`

## Minimal synthetic reproduction

Pass this provider error text through the `stopReason === 'error'` path:

```text
upstream_error: 请求超时
```

Current classification in `packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/stream.ts`:

```ts
if (/\btime(?:d)?\s*out\b|timeout/i.test(message)) return 'TIMEOUT'
```

Observed result: `PI_AI_ERROR` and no `llm/retry` event.

Expected result: `TIMEOUT`, allowing the existing provider retry policy to
decide whether and how often to retry.

## Suggested narrow change

```ts
if (/\btime(?:d)?\s*out\b|timeout|请求超时/i.test(message)) return 'TIMEOUT'
```

Suggested regression cases:

```ts
expect(classify('upstream_error: 请求超时')).toBe('TIMEOUT')
expect(classify('upstream_error: 请求失败')).toBe('PI_AI_ERROR')
```

The negative case is important: this should not turn arbitrary localized
upstream errors into retryable timeouts. No change to the default retry count is
requested; deployments can still choose a smaller `maxRetries` when one gateway
timeout is already expensive.

Longer term, preserving a structured error/status/cause from pi-ai would be
preferable to expanding text heuristics, but the current adapter explicitly has
only flattened `error.message` text available.

discussions.title: User-selectable compute tiers with different token pricing for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
discussions.body:
Hi DeepSeek team,

I would like to suggest an API-level feature for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: user-selectable inference compute tiers, such as `economy`, `standard`, and `full`, with different token pricing for each tier.

This is related to #5254, which proposes auto-adjusting reasoning effort based on task difficulty. I think this proposal is slightly different: instead of only controlling reasoning depth or token usage, it is about exposing a clearer compute / latency / reliability / cost trade-off at the model API level.

My personal use case is ordinary business coding. Most of my daily tasks are not extremely difficult: editing application logic, writing CRUD code, fixing small bugs, reviewing common code paths, or asking an agent to make routine changes. I would like to use DeepSeek models more often, but as a cost-sensitive user, using the full capability and full pricing all the time can feel too expensive for these everyday tasks.

Today, reducing reasoning effort or limiting output tokens can help reduce cost, but from a user perspective this is not as intuitive as choosing a compute tier with a different token price. Ideally, each tier would have its own token pricing, reflecting different inference compute allocation, latency, and reliability trade-offs.

For example, V4.1 Flash could expose something like:

```json
{
  "model": "deepseek-v4.1-flash",
  "compute_tier": "economy"
}
```

or:

```json
{
  "model": "deepseek-v4.1-flash",
  "compute_tier": "full"
}
```

Possible tiers could be:

```text
Economy  - lower inference compute, lower token price, lower latency, suitable for simple coding and routine agent tasks
Standard - balanced default for normal development work
Full     - maximum capability, normal/full token price, suitable for complex reasoning, large refactors, difficult debugging, or high-stakes tasks
```

Ideally, this could support both modes of control:

1. The user can explicitly set a tier when they know the task is simple or difficult.
2. The agent can automatically choose a tier based on task difficulty, similar in spirit to #5254, but at the compute / pricing tier level.

I want to emphasize that I am not asking for a vague "80% performance" mode. Model capability is not a linear slider. A better framing may be reduced inference compute allocation, or an economy compute tier, where the trade-off is documented as lower cost and latency in exchange for a lower ceiling on hard tasks.

This would also be different from only reducing reasoning tokens. Reasoning effort controls how much the model thinks, and output limits control how much it says, but a compute tier could represent a broader product and API contract: capability, latency, reliability, and token pricing. For many developers, especially those doing routine business coding, that may be easier to understand and more useful in daily usage.

I think this could make each model family more flexible without necessarily replacing separate model lines such as Pro and Flash. For example, Flash could still focus on speed and cost, while Pro could focus on stronger capability. Within each family, compute tiers would give users a more practical way to choose the right cost / latency / capability trade-off for each task.

Thanks for considering this.

discussions.title: [Windows] "Show in File Explorer" / revealNativePath creates an invisible Explorer window (windowsHide inherits into the child)
discussions.body:
# Bug 报告草稿（供 GitHub Discussions 使用）

> 目标仓库：`deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness`（Issues 已关闭，CONTRIBUTING 说明暂不接受外部 PR，官方指定渠道为 **Discussions**）
> 版本核验：`LOCAL HEAD = origin/master = c291e7961a`，`packages/util/native-command` 版本 `0.1.5-rc.2`，上游尚未改动相关文件
> 附件：`dsh-fix-reveal-visible.patch`（7 文件，+46/−14）

---

## EN — Bug: "Show in File Explorer" / `revealNativePath` opens an invisible window on Windows

**Environment**: Windows 11 x64 · DSH Web UI (`dsh web`, host runs from source via tsx) · package `@deepseek-ai/dsh-native-command@0.1.5-rc.2` · commit `c291e7961a`.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Start `dsh web` and open the GUI in a browser.
2. Ask the agent to produce a file, so the turn ends with a presented-file card (or use any deliverable card).
3. On the card, open the split **Open ▾** menu and choose **Show in File Explorer** (`在文件资源管理器中显示`).
4. Nothing appears on screen. No error is shown, because Explorer's exit code 1 is intentionally accepted as a delegated handoff.

**Expected**: Explorer comes to the foreground with the file selected.

**Actual**: The window *is* created and the file *is* selected, but the window is **invisible** (`IsWindowVisible == FALSE`), so the user sees nothing and concludes the action failed.

**Root cause**

`packages/util/native-command/src/runner.ts` spawns every native command with `windowsHide: true`:

```ts
execFile(command, [...args], { encoding: 'utf8', signal, windowsHide: true }, …)
```

`revealNativePath` (`packages/util/native-command/src/path-opener.ts`) hands the reveal to that same runner:

```ts
await run('explorer.exe', ['/select,', target], signal)
```

Explorer's newly created window inherits the hidden show-state of the spawn that started it. The command therefore succeeds (exit 1 = delegated to the running shell), the selection is correct, and the user still sees nothing. The file-association path (`Open with default app` → `powershell.exe Invoke-Item`) is unaffected, which is why only the reveal action fails.

**Measured evidence** (same command, only the flag differs; window enumerated through `Shell.Application` COM and `IsWindowVisible`):

| spawn | window exists | file selected | `IsWindowVisible` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `windowsHide: true` (current) | yes | yes | **false** |
| `windowsHide: false` | yes | yes | **true** |

**Suggested minimal fix**

Give the runner an optional per-call option whose default stays `true`, and let the reveal opt out — the only caller whose child *is* the user-facing surface:

```ts
// runner.ts
export interface NativeCommandOptions { readonly windowsHide?: boolean }
export const runNativeCommand: NativeCommandRunner = (command, args, signal, options) =>
  … { encoding: 'utf8', signal, windowsHide: options?.windowsHide ?? true } …

// path-opener.ts (explorer branch)
await run('explorer.exe', ['/select,', target], signal, { windowsHide: false })
```

**Please keep the file-URI form** of the target (`pathToFileURL(windowsPath).href` with commas percent-encoded): a raw path broke on names containing a comma in my testing (Explorer silently opened Documents instead). The URI is not the bug.

**Verification of the patch**: package suite `vitest run packages/util/native-command/tests` → 45/45 pass (including a new regression test named *"spawns the Explorer reveal visibly, because a hidden child hides its window"*); `oxlint` clean; `verify-md-wrap` and `verify-translation-pairing` clean; module-level end-to-end call of the patched `revealNativePath` produced a window with `IsWindowVisible == TRUE`.

**Broader relevance**: any future caller whose child is the user-facing window (native pickers, custom launchers) will hit the same trap, so an explicit per-call option is worth having regardless of which call site is fixed.

---

## 中文 — Bug：“在文件资源管理器中显示”弹出的是不可见窗口（Windows）

**环境**：Windows 11 x64 · DSH Web UI（`dsh web`，host 走 tsx 直接运行源码）· `@deepseek-ai/dsh-native-command@0.1.5-rc.2` · commit `c291e7961a`（= 当前 origin/master）。

**复现步骤**

1. 启动 `dsh web`，在浏览器打开界面。
2. 让 Agent 产出文件，收尾轮次出现交付文件卡片。
3. 在卡片上点开分段控件 **打开 ▾**，选择 **在文件资源管理器中显示**。
4. 屏幕上没有任何反应；也不会报错——因为 Explorer 的退出码 1 被有意当作“已转交请求”。

**期望**：资源管理器前置弹出并选中该文件。
**实际**：窗口**确实被创建**、文件**确实被选中**，但窗口是**不可见**的（`IsWindowVisible == FALSE`），用户据此判断“点击失败”。

**根因**

`packages/util/native-command/src/runner.ts` 对所有原生命令统一使用 `windowsHide: true`；`revealNativePath`（`packages/util/native-command/src/path-opener.ts`）把 reveal 交给同一个 runner 执行 `explorer.exe /select,<file-uri>`。**Explorer 新建的窗口会继承这次 spawn 的隐藏显示状态**：命令执行成功（exit 1 = 已转交常驻的 shell 进程）、选中项正确，但用户什么都看不到。走文件关联的 “Host 默认应用”（`powershell Invoke-Item`）不受影响，这也解释了为什么只有 reveal 这一个动作失败。

**实测对照**（同一命令仅改该标志；窗口用 `Shell.Application` COM 枚举 + `IsWindowVisible` 判定）

| spawn 参数 | 窗口存在 | 选中文件 | 可见 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `windowsHide: true`（现状） | 是 | 是 | **否** |
| `windowsHide: false` | 是 | 是 | **是** |

**建议的最小修复**：给 runner 增加可选的单次调用选项（默认仍为 true），仅让“子进程本身就是用户界面”的 reveal 显式退出隐藏。

**请保留 file URI 形式**的目标参数（逗号需 `%2C` 编码）：实测原生路径形式在文件名含逗号时会静默打开“文档”目录——URI 不是 bug 来源。

**补丁验证**：`vitest run packages/util/native-command/tests` 45/45 通过（新增具名回归测试 *“spawns the Explorer reveal visibly, because a hidden child hides its window”*）；`oxlint` 干净；`verify-md-wrap`、`verify-translation-pairing` 门禁通过；模块级端到端调用打补丁后的 `revealNativePath`，窗口 `IsWindowVisible == TRUE`。

**更普遍的意义**：任何“子进程即用户界面”的后续调用方（原生选择器、自定义启动器）都会踩同一个坑，因此显式的单次调用选项本身值得提供，而不只是修某一个调用点。

discussions.title: Turn stuck on "running" with no output: silent provider stream + lost terminal frame (diagnosis + reference fix)
discussions.body:
Hi team, reporting a freeze I hit repeatedly on 0.1.5-rc.2, with diagnosis from the session logs. Two distinct stall modes, both ending in the UI showing "running" forever with no output while the turn has to be steered manually to unstick it.

Mode 1 — provider goes silent mid-stream (host) A provider that stops delivering chunks without closing or erroring parks the host chunk loop in packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts forever: no settlement, no agent/request-error, no retry. The log shows a turn/start with no matching turn/end and one step/start never closed.

Mode 2 — terminal stream frame lost (client) Even when the turn completes cleanly server-side (turn/end: completed, every tool call answered), the chat can still spin forever. If the terminal end frame is lost, ClientAssistantStream holds the attempt open: the streaming bubble never clears and the durable assistant/message hides in pending instead of rendering.

Reference fix (on my fork, branch fix/assistant-stream-stall-timeout):

    Host: race each chunk against a configurable stall watchdog (default 90s, 0 disables, 10s floor). On stall, push a synthetic finish/error chunk so the attempt settles once as assistant/attempt and the existing agent/request-error waterfall offers llm-retry recovery — the turn resumes automatically.
    Client: ClientAssistantStream expires a frame-starved attempt (30s) — a staged settlement publishes immediately, swapping the stale spinner for the completed message. handleConnected also reopens errored session follows on reconnect so the window re-baselines without user action.
    Tests: watchdog unit specs, end-to-end stall → attempt → retry → recovery spec, client stale-channel spec. Full agent-loop (runnable) and session-controller suites green.

Branch:

discussions.title: [BUG] Windows Terminal 未显示在 DSH “打开方式”菜单
discussions.body:
# Windows Terminal 未显示在 DSH 原生“打开方式”菜单的诊断报告

## 结论

Windows Terminal 已安装，且 `wt.exe` 已在用户 `PATH` 中；未显示的直接原因不是环境变量缺失，而是 DSH 原生 `open-in-app` 的可执行文件验证不兼容 Windows 的 App Execution Alias。

## 已验证事实

| 检查项 | 结果 |
| --- | --- |
| `LOCALAPPDATA` | `C:\Users\FFF\AppData\Local`，存在。 |
| 用户 `PATH` | 已包含 `C:\Users\FFF\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps`。 |
| `where.exe wt` | 返回 `C:\Users\FFF\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps\wt.exe`。 |
| Windows Terminal 包 | 已安装，版本目录位于 `C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\Microsoft.WindowsTerminal_1.24.11911.0_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe`。 |
| Node `fs.stat()` alias | 对 `WindowsApps\wt.exe` 返回 `EACCES`。 |
| Node `fs.access(..., X_OK)` alias | 通过。 |
| DSH `ctx.subprocess.resolveExecutable('wt')` | 失败，报 `command "wt" was not found on PATH`；该服务把 `stat()` 失败视为候选不可用。 |

## 根因

新版 DSH 的原生菜单已有 `windowsterminal` 条目，启动参数为：

```text
wt -d <workspace-directory>
```

但其发现流程通过 `ctx.subprocess.resolveExecutable('wt')` 解析该命令。该解析器会对每个 PATH 候选执行文件状态检查；当 `C:\Users\FFF\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps\wt.exe` 的 `stat()` 返回 `EACCES` 时，解析器将它排除。

该路径是 Windows Store/MSIX 的 **App Execution Alias**：它可被 Windows 的命令解析和 `where.exe` 使用，却不总是能被 Node 当作普通可读取的可执行文件进行文件状态检查。因此菜单不会收到 `windowsterminal` 这一可用项，只会显示能够通过普通文件验证的应用（例如 Git Bash）。

## 推荐修复

修改 DSH 原生 `open-in-app` 的 Windows Terminal 解析逻辑：当普通 `wt` PATH 解析失败时，若 `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps\wt.exe` 存在，则将它作为受支持的 App Execution Alias 接受，并跳过普通 `stat()` 可执行文件验证。

discussions.title: Per-tool agentOptions in custom agent presets are ignored — every subagent child runs the composition-time default route
discussions.body:
## Summary

Per-tool `agentOptions` pinned in a custom agent preset (`agent.cordis.yml`) appear to be silently ignored in my deployment: every subagent child — regardless of which `subagent_*` tool spawned it — runs the **same model route**, which tracks the deployment's default model as of the last composition rebuild. Neither the preset's `agentOptions`, the parent session's route, nor the `agent-default-model` setting is honored. I would expect per-tool pins to work as deployment-owned defaults, per the [2026-08-18 feature note](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-08-18-model-selected-subagent-routes.zh.md) ("配置的 `Config.agentOptions` 仍是部署方所有的默认值").

## Environment

- dsh `0.1.5-rc.1` (npm latest, Web profile via `dsh web`)
- Custom agent preset with multiple `dsh-tool-subagent` rows, each pinning a distinct route (names anonymized):

```yaml
- id: tool-subagent-alpha
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
  config:
    provider: spawn
    toolName: subagent_alpha
    agentOptions:
      provider: provider-a
      model: model-a

- id: tool-subagent-beta
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
  config:
    provider: spawn
    toolName: subagent_beta
    agentOptions:
      provider: provider-b
      model: model-b
```

## Expected

Each named tool spawns its child on its pinned route, so one conversation can mix children on `provider-a/model-a` and `provider-b/model-b`.

## Actual

Every child runs the **same** route — the deployment default model as of the last host (re)composition:

| When | Default model | `subagent_alpha` child | `subagent_beta` child |
|---|---|---|---|
| first epoch | model-x | provider-x/model-x | provider-x/model-x |
| after `dsh web` restart (default changed) | model-y | provider-y/model-y | provider-y/model-y |
| default changed back (no restart) | model-z | still provider-y/model-y | — |

Evidence comes from the children's own session logs (`request/header` events, `reason: initial`), e.g.:

```json
{"type":"request/header","data":{"reason":"initial","header":{"config":{"provider":"provider-y","model":"model-y"}}}}
```

Additional falsifiable observations:

- The parent session's own route was `model-z` throughout — children do **not** inherit it (ruling out plain parent inheritance).
- `agent-default-model` in `settings.yaml` was `model-z` at test time — children do **not** follow it either.
- All presets' children converge on one route per composition epoch; that route only changes when the default model changes **and** the host restarts.
- The behavior is visible in a long-lived session that has been resumed across host restarts. I have not yet confirmed whether a freshly created session composes the pins correctly — per the documented design ("policy is snapshotted per top-level session at creation"), the delivered per-call selection (`subagent-model-selection` setting + `provider`/`model`/`reasoning_effort` tool params) only appears in newly composed sessions, which I understand is intentional. This report is specifically about the **`Config.agentOptions` deployment-default path**, which the feature note says should remain effective regardless.

## What I verified in the code (0.1.5-rc.1)

The intended chain looks intact on paper:

1. `dsh-tool-subagent`: `requestedChildAgentOptions = requestedAgentOptions(parentOptions, config.agentOptions, args, enabled)` → returns `config.agentOptions` when the call carries no model fields.
2. `startInProcessRun` → `resolveChildAgentOptions(parent, request.agentOptions, childDepth)` → `{ ...parentOptions, ...requested }` (`dsh-subagent/child-agent.js`) — the pin should override.
3. `agent-loop`'s `prepareRequest` seeds from `this.options.provider/model`.

Yet the child's **initial** request header already carries the composition-default route, so the override is lost somewhere between the tool's `requestedChildAgentOptions` and `ctx.agents.create(...)` — as if every mounted tool instance's `config.agentOptions` had been replaced by the composition-time default route, or as if the composition the host mounted is not the preset file on disk.

## Reproduction

1. Register a custom preset with two `dsh-tool-subagent` rows pinning different `agentOptions` routes.
2. In one conversation, spawn one child per tool.
3. Read each child's session log `request/header`: both show the same route — the deployment default — not the pins.

## Related

- Discussion #4193 (subagent forced to inherit the parent model — same symptom family)
- Discussion #1369 (cannot invoke subagents by provider/model)
- Feature note: 2026-08-18 model-selected subagent routes

discussions.title: [BUG] Session history becomes unloadable ("corrupt") after a degenerate model tool call persists an empty callId
discussions.body:
## Summary

When the model emits a degenerate tool call (empty `callId` and empty `name`), the harness executes it, gets `ToolNotFoundError`, and persists a `tool/result` event whose `message.source.callId` is `""`. On the next load, the session fails validation and the **entire session history becomes unloadable** from the Web GUI:

```
stored session "session-…" is corrupt: stored session "session-…" failed validation:
Error: session event at seq 850 message must have tool source
```

The write path produced a log that the read path refuses — a log written by the harness itself should always load back.

## Evidence (minimal event pair from a real session log, v3 format)

```json
// seq 849 — tool/call written from degenerate model output
{ "type": "tool/call", "seq": 849, "data": { "turn": 3, "step": 2, "callId": "", "name": "", "arguments": "{}" } }

// seq 850 — harness ran it, got ToolNotFoundError, persisted empty callId
{ "type": "tool/result", "seq": 850, "sourceEventSeqs": [849], "surfaceOp": "append",
  "data": { "turn": 3, "step": 2,
    "message": { "source": { "kind": "tool", "callId": "" },
                 "content": [{ "type": "tool-result", "toolCallId": "", "content": [ … ], "isError": true }],
                 "role": "user", "id": "…" },
    "error": { "name": "ToolNotFoundError", "code": "UNKNOWN_TOOL" } } }
```

The validator that refuses it: `adoptSessionEvent` → `assertMessageEventShape` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-session`, "message must have tool source" — requires `source.kind === "tool"` with a non-empty `callId`), surfaced as `SessionPersistenceCorruptionError` by `validateStoredEvents`.

## Expected behavior

Either:

1. **Write-time guard** — never persist an empty `callId`: synthesize a non-empty id (e.g. a UUID) for degenerate calls, or
2. **Read-time tolerance** — accept an empty `callId` on `tool/result` messages that carry `data.error` (they are produced by the harness's own error path, not by the model).

## Reproduction

1. Use a channel/model that occasionally emits a tool call with empty `callId`/`name` (observed via a community gateway route).
2. Wait for the harness to execute it and persist the error result.
3. Reload the session history in the Web GUI → "历史加载失败 … corrupt", and the session can no longer be opened.

## Workaround

Rewriting the log with a shared synthetic non-empty `callId` on both the `tool/call` and its `tool/result` (seqs, `sourceEventSeqs` and surface markers untouched) fully restores loading; the repaired log passes `adoptSessionEvent` + `Session.fromRestore`.

## Environment

- Windows 11, DSH npm distribution (`npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`), `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session` 0.1.5-rc.2, log format v3 (zstd framed JSONL).

## Related

- "session-format-v0-to-v1 converter refuses loadable v0 sessions over cosmetic fields (history load breaks after upgrade to 0.1.5-rc.1)" — same symptom family (read path refuses a loadable session), different mechanism (this one is write-path/validation mismatch, not a version converter).

discussions.title: dsh-subagent-progress — live mission-control dock for your subagents (npm) | 子代理实时进度停靠栏
discussions.body:
# dsh-subagent-progress — a live mission-control dock for your subagents

[npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-subagent-progress) · [GitHub](https://github.com/edgeseeker7/dsh-subagent-progress) · `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-subagent-progress`

Ever spawned three background subagents and then wondered *"…are they actually doing anything?"* This plugin pins a frosted-glass dock directly above your composer and answers that question at a glance — no digging through child transcripts.

## What you get

- **Live cards, one per subagent** — status dot (running / stalled / failed), label, turn·step, last tool call with its key argument, elapsed time, latest assistant preview. Data comes from a host-side projection that folds every child session's events, so there is progress on the card *even if the model never reports anything*.
- **`notify_user` channel** — every subagent gets a tool to report *progress / eta / finding* in its own words. Findings stick around for a few minutes after the child settles; everything else fades with the card. Hover any update for the full Markdown in a popover.
- **Recursive delegation tree** — a child's own subagents nest under its card, Apple-outline style: pure text-axis indent and a ▾ disclosure chip (click to collapse the whole subtree). No connector lines, no clutter.
- **Model tag on every card** — see which model each subagent is *actually* running (read from dsh's official `modelSelection` projection — zero extra traffic). Hover for provider and reasoning effort. In my deployment this immediately surfaced that all my "different model" presets were silently resolving to the same default route — the tag paid for itself on day one.
- **Failure UX** — a failed turn keeps its card with a distilled one-line error, **Retry** (queues a fresh turn through the real parent→child control channel) and **Pause** buttons, then expires on its own.
- **Motion with manners** — cards rise in, and slide down + fade + collapse out; settled cards shrink to one slim row so running agents own the screen. `prefers-reduced-motion` respected everywhere.
- **Theme-native** — every color comes from dsh's `--dsw-*` variables; light and dark themes both work. Zero build step, hand-written `__ModuleLoader__` client + host projection; the client half hot-swaps under HMR.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-subagent-progress
# then restart `dsh web`
```

No configuration needed. Requires dsh ≥ 0.1.2-rc.1. MIT licensed — issues and PRs welcome on [GitHub](https://github.com/edgeseeker7/dsh-subagent-progress).

---

# dsh-subagent-progress —— 子代理的实时指挥台

[npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-subagent-progress) · [GitHub](https://github.com/edgeseeker7/dsh-subagent-progress) · `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-subagent-progress`

有没有过这种体验：一口气派了三个后台子代理，然后开始怀疑"它们到底还在干活吗？"这个插件在输入框正上方放一块磨砂玻璃停靠栏，一眼回答这个问题——不用再去翻子代理的会话记录。

## 功能一览

- **每个子代理一张实时卡**：状态点（运行/停滞/失败）、标题、轮·步、最近一次工具调用及关键参数、耗时、最新回复预览。数据来自 host 端投影（折叠每个子会话的事件流），**即使模型一句话不说，卡片上也永远有进度**。
- **`notify_user` 主动汇报通道**：每个子代理都获得这个工具，可以用自己的话报告"进展 / 预期 / 发现"。发现类消息在子代理结束后还会保留几分钟，其余随卡片自然消退；悬停任何一条更新可看完整 Markdown 弹窗。
- **递归委托树**：子代理的子代理嵌套挂在父卡下方——苹果大纲视图风格：纯文字轴缩进 + ▾ 披露三角（点击折叠整棵子树），没有一根多余的连接线。
- **每张卡显示真实模型**：直接读 dsh 官方 `modelSelection` 投影（零额外流量），一眼看出这个子代理实际在跑哪个模型，悬停看 provider 和推理强度。在我的部署里，它第一天就揪出"所有 preset 名义上不同模型、实际全跑同一个默认路由"的隐形 bug——这张标签已经值回票价。
- **失败处理**：失败的轮次保留卡片，附一行 distilled 错误、**重试**（走真实的父→子控制通道续跑）和**暂停**按钮，之后自动过期消失。
- **有教养的动效**：卡片上浮入场、下滑+淡出+收起退场；安定的卡片自动瘦身成单行，把屏幕留给正在运行的代理。全面支持 `prefers-reduced-motion`。
- **主题原生**：所有颜色取自 dsh 的 `--dsw-*` 变量，明暗主题通吃。零构建步骤（手写 `__ModuleLoader__` 客户端 + host 投影），客户端改动 HMR 免刷新热替换。

## 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-subagent-progress
# 然后重启 dsh web
```

零配置，装上即用。需要 dsh ≥ 0.1.2-rc.1。MIT 协议，欢迎到 [GitHub](https://github.com/edgeseeker7/dsh-subagent-progress) 提 issue 和 PR。

discussions.title: Fix(cli) Proposal: 让入口守卫在 Node 24.0–24.1 上失败可见，并把它们移出 engines 范围
discussions.body:
## 标题：fix(cli): 让入口守卫在 Node 24.0–24.1 上失败可见，并把它们移出 engines 范围

   关联讨论：#4047（build 静默跳过）、#5082（Node < 24.2 下 build 静默退出、退出码 0）、#5100（残留目录导致误导性
 MISSING_EXPORT）、以及社区帖 https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/5084 相邻的 loader shape 问题
 。

   ---

   ### 摘要

   仓库在 `423412b7bf`（fix(runtime): simplify executable entry dispatch，2026-09-03）把入口判定统一换成了
 `import.meta.main`，共 14 处。该 API 在 **Node 24.0.0–24.1.x 上求值为 `undefined`**（既不是 `true` 也不是 `false`），
 而 `engines.node` 声明为 `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` —— 这些版本**声明支持、却不满足任何入口守卫**。后果是进程零输出、退出
 码 0，`pnpm run build` 与 `pnpm dsh web` 都表现为"没有任何报错，直接退出"。

   ### 影响

   | 入口 | Node 24.0–24.1 上的行为 |
   |---|---|
   | `pnpm dsh web` | 静默退出 0，服务不启动，无任何输出 |
   | `pnpm dsh --profile headless "..."` | 同上 |
   | `pnpm run build` | 静默退出 0，**不生成任何构建产物**（`build:lib` / `build:web` 从未执行） |
   | `dsh`（npm 全局安装，`bin` → `lib/bin.js`） | 同上，用户侧完全不可用 |
   | `name-server`（`subprocess-local/lib/runner.js`） | 同上 |

   二次伤害：`pnpm run build` 静默成功会留下"看似已构建"的残缺工作区（缺 `packages/*/*/lib/client.js`），后续启动才报
 `client bundles not found`，把排查引向错误方向。

   ### 复现

   ```sh
   fnm install 24.1.0 && fnm use 24.1.0
   pnpm install && pnpm run build     # exit 0，无输出，无产物
   pnpm dsh web                        # exit 0，无输出，服务未起
   ```

   ---

   ### 根因与实测

   **1) `import.meta.main` 的版本行为（本机实测，非文档推断）**

   | Node | `import.meta.main`（.mjs / .ts 经 tsx 加载） |
   |---|---|
   | 22.19.0 | `true` |
   | **24.0.0** | **`undefined`** |
   | **24.1.0** | **`undefined`** |
   | 24.2.0 | `true` |
   | 24.3.0 / 24.4.0 / 24.9.0 / 24.19.0 | `true` |
   | 26.8.1 | `true` |

   即 24.x 行的分界是 **24.2.0**。（未找到对应的 Node release note，以上为实测结论；若维护者掌握上游出处，欢迎补充。）

   **2) 同一棵构建产物在不同 Node 上的表现（同一份 `apps/cli/lib/bin.js`）**

   ```
   Node      | esm (.mjs)  | 源码启动 (tsx) | 已构建 dsh 入口
   ----------+-------------+---------------+------------------
   22.19.0   | true        | true          | 0.1.5-rc.2
   24.0.0    | undefined   | undefined     | (无输出)
   24.1.0    | undefined   | undefined     | (无输出)   ← 复现用户报告
   24.2.0    | true        | true          | 0.1.5-rc.2
   24.3.0    | true        | true          | 0.1.5-rc.2
   24.9.0    | true        | true          | 0.1.5-rc.2
   24.19.0   | true        | true          | 0.1.5-rc.2
   26.8.1    | true        | true          | 0.1.5-rc.2
   ```

   **3) 受影响的 14 处源码入口**

   ```
   apps/cli/src/bin.ts:64
   apps/desktop-host/src/index.ts:584
   apps/desktop/scripts/prepare-package-set.ts:172
   packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/bin.ts:18
   scripts/build.ts:53
   scripts/run-gates.ts:99
   scripts/benchmark-next-package-dependency.ts:264
   scripts/benchmark-npm-resolution.ts:544
   scripts/verify-cordis-config.ts:60
   scripts/verify-doc-site-fragments.ts:181
   scripts/verify-npm-install-layout.ts:213
   scripts/verify-package-dependencies.ts:863
   scripts/verify-package-readme-summaries.ts:64
   scripts/verify-runtime-closure.ts:101
   ```

   其中随包发布、直接影响下游的 3 个产物：`apps/cli/lib/bin.js`（`@deepseek-ai/dsh` 的 `bin`）、
 `apps/desktop-host/lib/index.js`、`packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/lib/runner.js`。

   ### 为什么 CI 没有拦住

   两处叠加：

   1. **兼容性矩阵不含 24.0–24.1**。`.github/workflows/ci.yml` 的版本矩阵是 `22.19 / 24.9 / 26`（24.9 是刻意钉住的，注
 释说明 24.0–24.11.1 携带 v1 内部 loader），主 CI 跑 `PRIMARY_NODE_VERSION: '24'` = 最新 24。**24.0–24.1 从未被任何一条
 腿执行到**，而它们又恰好落在 `engines.node` 声明范围内。
   2. **这些版本上 `pnpm install` 不会失败**（24.1 满足 `>=24.0.0`），所以"声明范围"与"实际可用范围"的缺口没有任何信号
 。

   另外，源码启动路径（`node --import tsx/esm apps/cli/src/bin.ts`）与已构建入口在 24.1 上**同样**静默，因此 `pnpm dsh`
 和 `dsh` 都不能作为对照。

   ### 关于"为什么当初改掉旧守卫"

   不能简单回退。`423412b7bf` 把旧的

   ```ts
   const invokedPath = process.argv[1]
   if (invokedPath !== undefined && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(resolve(invokedPath)).href) {
   ```

   换成了 `import.meta.main`，**同时**新增了 `apps/cli/tests/built-bin.e2e.ts` 的 `runs through an installed-style
 symlink` 用例 —— 即旧写法在 npm/pnpm 全局安装的符号链接场景下不可靠，而 `import.meta.main` 能正确处理（并且它本来就是
 为了让 `runCli` 可被 `python/sdk-runtime/runtime-bootstrap.mjs` 直接 import 调用）。所以修复必须**同时**满足：符号链接
 下正确 + 24.0–24.1 上可诊断。

   ---

   ### 建议修复

   **A. 收紧 `engines.node`（必做，最小改动）**

   把声明范围与实测可用范围对齐，排除 24.0–24.1：

   ```jsonc
   // package.json
   "engines": { "node": "^22.19.0 || >=24.2.0" }
   ```

   理由：`^22.19.0` 上 `import.meta.main` 已可用（实测 `true`），24.x 行自 24.2.0 起可用。若维护者希望 24.x 下界取更高
 、更整洁的值（例如与兼容矩阵 24.9 对齐），我按你们的判断调整。

   **B. 入口守卫失败要可见（必做，防止同类回归）**

   `import.meta.main` 在 `undefined` 时**静默不执行**，这是本次事故的放大器。建议在共享位置（或各入口）加一条 fail-loud
 断言，把"版本不被支持"从零输出变成明确报错：

   ```ts
   // import.meta.main 在 Node < 24.2 上为 undefined；静默跳过入口会让
   // `dsh` / `pnpm run build` 以退出码 0 什么都不做。
   if (import.meta.main === undefined) {
     throw new Error(
       `dsh: Node ${process.version} does not provide import.meta.main; use Node 22.19+ or 24.2+`,
     )
   }
   ```

   **C. 补一条落在缺口里的 CI 腿（建议）**

   在兼容矩阵加 `24.1`（或 `24.0`）一条最小腿，跑 `pnpm run build` + `apps/cli/lib/bin.js --version`。这条腿会直接复现"
 退出码 0 且无输出"，是本次缺口唯一的自动化防护。注意 24.0–24.1 与已钉住的 24.9 一样属于 v1 loader 区间
 ，`DSH_GATE_FAIL_FAST` / gate 并发等设置需按现有约定处理。

   **D. 断言层（可选，但推荐）**

   在 `apps/cli/tests/built-bin.e2e.ts` 已有的 built-bin 用例旁，加一条"入口必须真的执行"的断言（例如 `--version` 必须
 有非空 stdout），而不是只断言 `exitCode === 0`。当前 24.1 下 `exitCode` 恰好是 `0`，只用退出码判定会漏掉这个缺陷。

   **同步文档**：`.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-06-node-engine-floor.md` 记录了引擎下限的推导
 （`node:sqlite`、原生类型剥离、pi-ai 依赖下限）。若采纳 A，该 Note 的"24.x 分支保持 `>=24.0.0`"一句需同步更新并补充
 `import.meta.main` 这一条新增约束（按仓库约定，同一 PR 内更新）。

   ### 不推荐的方案

   - **回退到 `argv[1]` + `pathToFileURL` 字符串比较**：会重新引入 `423412b7bf` 修掉的符号链接问题。若要走这条路，必须
 改成 `realpathSync` 规范化后再比较，并保留现有的 symlink e2e 用例。
   - **只加 B（fail-loud）不改 engines**：仍然声明支持 24.0–24.1 却直接报错，属于把"静默不可用"换成"启动即失败"，用户仍
 需自行猜测版本。
   - **只改 A 不加 B**：同类"守卫失效即静默"的回归会在下一次 Node 行为变化时再次发生。

   ---

   ### 验证方式

   ```sh
   # 每个版本上：非 24.0–24.1 必须打印版本号，24.0–24.1 必须失败可见
   for v in 22.19.0 24.0.0 24.1.0 24.2.0 24.9.0 26.8.1; do
     echo -n "node $v -> "
     npx -y node@$v apps/cli/lib/bin.js --version || echo "(fails loud, as intended)"
   done
   ```

   修复后预期：22.19.0 / 24.2.0 / 24.9.0 / 26.8.1 输出 `0.1.5-rc.2`；24.0.0 / 24.1.0 输出明确的 `does not provide
 import.meta.main` 错误并返回非零。

   ---

   ### 附：本次报告者的原始现象

   Node v24.1.0 上：

   ```
   $ pnpm run build
   $ tsx scripts/build.ts        ← 到这里结束，无产物，exit 0

   $ pnpm dsh web
   $ node --import tsx/esm apps/cli/src/bin.ts web
                                 ← 到这里结束，无输出，exit 0
   ```

   切到 Node 24.21.0 后同一工作区：`pnpm run build` → `build: recorded 234 client artifact(s)`，`pnpm dsh web` → `dsh
 web: http://127.0.0.1:3080/?token=...` 并正常常驻。这与上表完全一致。

   （另：排查过程中还遇到 `#5100` 描述的残留目录问题 —— 已从仓库删除但无 `package.json`、不被 `pnpm run clean` 识别的
 `packages/host/apiproxy`、`packages/session/session-persistence-sqlite` 会让 tsdown 报误导性的 `MISSING_EXPORT`。删除
 后构建才通过。此事已在 #5100 单独记录，本 PR 不重复处理。）
 ```

 两点说明：

 - 数据来源：上表的每个数字都是我在本机真实跑出来的（逐一装了 Node 22.19.0 / 24.0.0 / 24.1.0 / 24.2.0 / 24.3.0 / 24.4.0
   / 24.9.0 / 24.19.0 / 26.8.1 对比同一份产物），不是从 changelog 推断的。import.meta.main 的 24.2 分界我没找到上游
   release note，文中已如实标注，避免误导维护者。
- 本建议基于 DeepSeek/DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash 模型产出

discussions.title: Is the AppImage target in `apps/desktop` intended Linux scaffolding, or dead config?
discussions.body:
First, thanks for shipping the desktop app. I'm on Linux x64 and went looking for it, then tried to boot the reserved profile from the CLI and got the expected rejection. In the process I found a small inconsistency I can't resolve from the docs. This isn't a bug report or a demand for a Linux release — I'm asking about intent.

**What I observed**

1. The packaging config already declares a Linux target, `apps/desktop/electron-builder.config.mjs:115-117`:

```js
linux: {
  category: 'Development',
  target: ['AppImage'],
},
```

2. But the target table cannot produce one. `apps/desktop/scripts/package-target.ts:31` types targets as `'mac-arm64' | 'mac-x64' | 'win-x64'` only; `TARGETS` (`:42`) has exactly those three entries; `resolveDesktopBuildTarget` throws for anything else (`:153`, `unsupported target … expected mac-arm64, mac-x64, win-x64`); and a Linux build host is rejected outright by `hostTargetName` (`:180`).

3. There is no `package:desktop:linux:*` script — the root only defines mac and win lanes.

4. The README states the position explicitly: *"Linux is not a supported Desktop release target."* (`apps/desktop/README.md:91`)

So that AppImage block is currently unreachable.

**The question**

Is it (a) intentional forward-looking scaffolding — Linux planned but not yet qualified — or (b) stale config that should be removed so the supported target set is unambiguous? If (a), is the remaining gap mainly release qualification, or is there a known technical blocker?

**Context I've already gathered, to avoid duplicating**

- The Electron shell looks portable, and some Linux-specific handling already exists (`apps/desktop/README.md:44` covers directory symlinks on macOS/Linux; the Windows-only paths — junctions, ACL sandboxing — are clearly branched).
- The blocker that looks most real is native deps in the *bundled runtime*, and it's already reported: no `linux-x64` prebuild for node-pty ([#2194](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/2194), [#605](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/605)). Since the desktop app bundles dsh plus pnpm, that would likely gate a Linux AppImage too, not just `dsh web`.
- Community Linux desktop builds already exist — `dsh-deb-builder` ([#3096](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/3096)), `DSH-Portable` ([#2576](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/2576)), `dsh-launchpad` ([#1430](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1430)). If the intended answer is "community shells are the Linux path", that's a perfectly reasonable answer and I'll consider this resolved.

**If it's useful**

If a `linux-x64` target is wanted, I'm happy to attempt an AppImage build on Linux x64 and report exactly where it fails — including whether the bundled runtime can be assembled through the existing `resources/dsh` preparation path. I'm not asking for signed or notarized release qualification, only whether the target is intended. (I notice Issues and PRs are both disabled on this repo, so this is a question rather than an offer of a patch.)
