discussions.title: Support cwd-less (`_no-cwd`) sessions in Web list/open
discussions.body:
### Problem

Host runtimes persist sessions with no `header.cwd` (JSONL under `_no-cwd/`). Stock Web hides and rejects them, so an embedding host cannot share durable sessions with `dsh web` without mirroring a synthetic `cwd` into a second state root.

### Where

(`master` @ `0d1f500`)

- List skips cwd-less: [`list.ts#L138`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/0d1f50007f9bca3f52b06e1c3074fa14d5fb0720/packages/api/session-controller/src/list.ts#L138)
- Search same filter: [`list.ts#L181`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/0d1f50007f9bca3f52b06e1c3074fa14d5fb0720/packages/api/session-controller/src/list.ts#L181)
- Inspect → not found: [`agent.ts#L122-L124`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/0d1f50007f9bca3f52b06e1c3074fa14d5fb0720/packages/api/session-controller/src/agent.ts#L122-L124)
- Resume → not found: [`agent.ts#L418`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/0d1f50007f9bca3f52b06e1c3074fa14d5fb0720/packages/api/session-controller/src/agent.ts#L418)
- History/follow gate: [`history.ts#L253`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/0d1f50007f9bca3f52b06e1c3074fa14d5fb0720/packages/api/session-controller/src/history.ts#L253)
- Workspace index marks invalid: [`workspace/.../index.ts#L597-L598`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/0d1f50007f9bca3f52b06e1c3074fa14d5fb0720/packages/workspace/workspace/src/index.ts#L597-L598)

### Ask

Allow cwd-less sessions as Ungrouped in list/search and on inspect/follow (title from `session/title`). Keep workspace attach requiring cwd. Read-only from Web vs shared writer can be explicit.

Related (not the same): [#5912](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/5912), [#4548](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/4548). “No folder” plugins still set a real `cwd`, not `undefined`.

discussions.title: [Bug] Session log format drift makes prior history unreadable after upgrading from 0.1.1-rc.1 to 0.1.5 (permission/preset.origin, subagent/descriptor version 2)
discussions.body:
Environment

Item | Value -- | -- OS | Windows 11 x64 Node.js | v24.16.0 npm | 11.16.0 Writer build | @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.1.1-rc.1 (npx-cache install, dsh web) Reader builds (both affected) | @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.1.5-rc.1 and 0.1.5-rc.2 $DSH_HOME | C:\Users\\.dsh Session artifact path | $DSH_HOME/sessions///session.jsonl.zstd

Summary

After upgrading from 0.1.1-rc.1 to 0.1.5-rc.1, all 15 pre-existing sessions still appear in the workspace panel, but they are unusable:

  • the session title falls back to the cwd basename (DSH / my-workspace) instead of the folded title;
  • opening any of them shows no history — reading the log fails.

The v0 header still parses (which is why they are listed at all), so the UI looks like "my conversations were deleted" rather than showing an error. This is a silent-looking data-loss experience on a plain in-channel upgrade.

Reproduction

  1. On 0.1.1-rc.1, create sessions via the web profile. They are stored as .../sessions/<project-key>/<session-id>/session.jsonl.zstd with a v0 header:
    json
    {"type":"session","version":0,"id":"session-2dc4adc5-...","createdAt":1788281854557,"cwd":"E:\\DSH","delegationDepth":0,"agentPreset":"standard"}
    (Zstd artifact = single-frame header + multi-frame event blocks.)
  2. Upgrade to 0.1.5-rc.1 and open the Web UI.
  3. Sessions are listed with fallback titles; reading any of them fails with the errors below.

Minimal programmatic repro (no Web UI required), against a 0.1.5-rc.1 install:

js
import { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
import JsonlSessionPersistence from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl'

const ctx = new Context()
const svc = new JsonlSessionPersistence(ctx, { root: '<DSH_HOME>/sessions', compression: 'zstd' })

await svc.list()                       // OK — headers/listArtifacts succeed
const h = await svc.open('<id>', 'read')  // throws SessionFormatUnsupportedError
// equivalent entry points: svc.findLog(id) then svc.requireStoredLog(id)

Actual errors

1. permission/preset — unknown member (all 9 user conversations)

SessionFormatUnsupportedError: @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-format-v0-to-v1 refuses this format v0 Session:
permission/preset 0 data has unexpected member "origin"; source v0 artifact remains unchanged
(raw log: C:\Users\<user>\.dsh\sessions\--E-DSH--\session-2dc4adc5-.../session.jsonl.zstd)

2. Same field rejected again one stage later (observed after relaxing only the v0→v1 admission, i.e. the member survives v0→v1→v2 and is refused downstream):

SessionFormatUnsupportedError: @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-format-v2-to-v3 refuses this format v2 Session:
permission/preset data has unexpected field origin

3. subagent/descriptor version (all 6 subagent sessions)

@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-format-v0-to-v1 refuses this format v0 Session:
subagent/descriptor 0 uses unsupported descriptor version 2

4. And downstream:

@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-format-v2-to-v3 refuses this format v2 Session:
subagent/descriptor 0 version must be one of 3

Offending v0 payloads (exactly as written by 0.1.1-rc.1)

json
{"type":"permission/preset","seq":0,"time":1788281854802,"data":{"preset":"workspace-write","origin":"default"}}

{"type":"subagent/descriptor","seq":0,"time":1789566240424,"data":{"version":2,"mode":"continuable","provider":"spawn","label":"<task label>","agentProvider":"deepseek-official","agentModel":"deepseek-flash"}}

Scope in the reporting install: 9/9 user conversations affected by origin, 6/6 subagent sessions affected by descriptor version: 2 — i.e. 15/15 legacy sessions were unreadable.

Where it fails (0.1.5-rc.1 package sources)

@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-format-v0-to-v1/lib/index.js

  • assertReleasedV0Keys(data, disposition.required, versionOptional, \event.typeevent.type{event.seq} data`)— thepermission/presetdisposition isdisposition(["preset"]), so theorigin` member written by 0.1.1-rc.1 is refused.
  • subagentDescriptorValue() — literalValue(data["version"], [3], \${label} version`)`.
  • v0 admission — if (event.type === "subagent/descriptor" && data["version"] !== 3) { … if (version === 0) throw new SessionFormatUnsupportedMigrationError(…) }.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-format-v2-to-v3/lib/index.js

  • keys(value, required, optional, label) re-checks the same payload and refuses origin again.
  • It also re-runs the shared v0→v1 payload validator, which refuses descriptor version: 2 again.

Note: the v3 runtime itself tolerates both payloads — after migration, logs still containing origin / descriptor version: 2 load and read fine (verified). Only the migration admission checks are strict.

Workaround that preserved the data (for reference)

  1. Temporarily relax exactly those three checks (allow origin in both validators, accept descriptor version: 2).
  2. For each legacy session: findLog(id) → requireStoredLog(id) → publishStoredMigration(id, prepared) (the same sequence open(id, 'write') performs).
  3. Restore the two package files to their original bytes.

Result: 15/15 legacy sessions converted to v3 and readable again with the unpatched build; original v0 artifacts untouched; full backup kept. Content verified (event counts, conversation messages, restored titles).

Suggestions

  1. Be tolerant on migration admission for released historical formats. A member that a previous released build wrote should not abort the whole session: either admit it, or drop/remap it explicitly during migration.
  2. Accept legacy subagent/descriptor version: 2 in the migration chain (map it to v3, or carry it through — the v3 runtime already accepts it).
  3. Consider an explicit repair entry point, e.g. dsh session migrate --all [--dry-run], that scans legacy artifacts and reports/repairs them, instead of failing lazily at read time.
  4. Surface unreadable stored sessions in the UI. Right now the only hint is a fallback title; an explicit error badge ("stored log cannot be read by this version") would prevent users from concluding their history was deleted.
  5. Ideally the upgrade path should be covered by a fixture test: a session log emitted by each previously released build must be readable by the next release (golden artifacts per released version).

中文摘要（供参考）

从 0.1.1-rc.1 升级到 0.1.5-rc.1 后，升级前创建的 15 个会话全部无法读取（列表还在，但标题退化成文件夹名、点开没有内容）：

  1. permission/preset 事件里旧版写入的 origin 字段被 v0→v1 校验拒绝，且该字段会一路带到 v2→v3 再被拒绝一次（影响 9 个真实对话）；
  2. subagent/descriptor 的 version: 2 被拒绝（新版要求 3，影响 6 个子会话）。

关键点：v3 运行时本身能接受这两个负载（迁移后仍含这些字段的日志可以正常读取），只有迁移准入校验过严。

我的临时修复（数据无损）：临时放宽这三处校验 → 走官方迁移链（v0→v1→v2→v3）转换全部旧会话 → 立刻还原原始包文件。结果：15/15 会话恢复可读，原始 v0 文件一个都没动，另有完整备份。

discussions.title: [Bug] mcp-client: 工具 inputSchema 缺少与 outputSchema 对称的子集规范化
discussions.body:
## Summary

`dsh-mcp-client` 对上游 MCP 工具的 `outputSchema` 做了优雅降级，但 `inputSchema` 原样透传；同时 `ToolRuntime.register()` 只断言 `output.schema`，`parameters` 在整个 harness 中从不做子集校验，直接进入模型请求。两者处理方式不对称，属于潜在缺陷。

需要说明的是：**这不是任何一次会话创建/恢复失败的根因**（见下方「实际影响」中的实测结论），而是一处尚未被触发的边界不一致。

## 证据

**1. 消费侧不对称** —— `packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/tools.ts`

```ts
// :234  inputSchema 原样透传
parameters: inputSchema,
// :235  outputSchema 走优雅降级（:185 supportedOutputSchema）
output: createOutput(rawName, supportedOutputSchema(options.outputSchema)),
```

`:185` 的注释写明该分支的意图：

```ts
/** Keep a supported advertised schema; unsupported MCP vocabulary falls back to JsonValue. */
```

**2. 校验侧不对称** —— `packages/core/tools/src/index.ts`

- `:1051` `register()` 只做 `assertSupportedJsonSchema(output.schema)`；`parameters` 不校验。
- `:1262`–`:1272` `schemaOf()` 对 `parameters` 只做 lossless JSON 检查（`snapshotJsonValue`），不检查 schema 子集。
- `:1804` 执行期只对 `tool.output.schema` 调 `validateJsonSchemaValue`。

**3. 越界词汇确实会到达模型 provider**

- `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/protocols/chat-completions/serialize.ts:346` → `parameters: tool.parameters`
- `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/protocols/messages/serialize.ts:134` → `input_schema: tool.parameters`

**4. 真实越界样本**（`@playwright/mcp@0.0.80`，`browser-use-playwright-mcp/package.json:31` 精确 pin）

实际拉起该 stdio server 并读取 `tools/list`，24 个工具的 `inputSchema` **24/24** 落在 `assertSupportedJsonSchema`（`packages/core/tools/src/json-schema.ts:385`）子集之外：

- 全部 24 个：根级 `$schema`
- `browser_drop`：额外 `propertyNames`，以及非布尔的 `additionalProperties: { "type": "string" }`
- `browser_network_request`：额外 `minimum` / `maximum`

## 实际影响

实测（未打任何临时补丁的 master 源码）：

- 直接以 `failOnStartupError: true` + 生产参数 `--browser chromium --isolated --headless` 挂载：**24 个工具全部注册成功**。
- `packages/experimental/browser-use-playwright-mcp/tests/upstream.e2e.ts` 全链路（Loader → Sessions → Agents → AgentLoop → provider → mcp-client，真实 agent 创建 + 真实浏览器导航）：**2/2 通过**。

因此当前影响仅限于：

1. 越界词汇原样出现在模型可见的 tool 定义中；
2. 一旦将来在参数边界补上子集校验（与 output 对称），这 24 个工具会**同时**失效。

## Deliverables（建议方向）

- 在 `packages/core/tools/src/json-schema.ts` 导出一个规范化工具（例如 `sanitizeJsonSchema`），由 mcp-client 等消费方共用，而不是在 mcp-client 内硬编码。
- 语义保留优先级：丢弃纯元信息（`$schema`、`$id`、`$defs`、`$ref`、`propertyNames`）；`additionalProperties` 非布尔时归为 `true`；`properties` / `items` / `oneOf` 递归处理；数值约束（`minimum` / `maximum` 等）是否折进 `description` 待维护者裁定。
- 在 `tools.ts:234` 接入该规范化，使 input 与 `:235` 的 output 处理对称。
- 补一条回归测试：stdio MCP server 返回带 `$schema` 的 `inputSchema`，断言 `failOnStartupError: true` 时工具仍能注册。

discussions.title: browser-use-runtime: 可选浏览器工具集启动失败不应拖垮整个 Agent 创建/恢复
discussions.body:
## Summary

`mountSessionMcp` 已经为「浏览器不可用」设计了一条降级路径：独占附件被占用时，该次 activation 标记为 `blocked`，会话继续运行、只是没有浏览器工具。但**启动失败**走的是相反的分支：整个 Agent 创建/恢复被拒绝并回滚。两者对使用者而言都是「浏览器工具不可用」，处理方式却不对称——一个降级，一个致命。

这是把「一个可选工具集的问题」放大成「所有会话无法创建/恢复」的根本原因。属于设计取舍问题，不是崩溃缺陷。

## 证据

**1. 致命分支** —— `packages/experimental/browser-use-runtime/src/mcp.ts`

- `:152` 挂载 scoped mcp-client 时写死 `failOnStartupError: true`（并 `reconnect: { enabled: false }`）。
- `:177`–`:190` 在每次 `agent/created` 中 await 发现：

```ts
ctx.on('agent/created', async ({ agent, signal }) => {
  const state: ClientState = { status: resources.available(agent) ? 'ready' : 'blocked' }
  ...
  if (state.status === 'blocked') {          // :183 降级分支
    clients.set(agent, state)
    refreshBlockedMasks()
    return                                    // 会话继续，只是没有浏览器工具
  }
  await resources.get(agent, signal)          // :188 致命分支：open() 抛错即整体拒绝
  clients.set(agent, state)
}, { prepend: true })
```

`open()` 内 `scope.ctx.plugin(McpClient, ...)`（`:144`–`:154`）失败后按 `:163`–`:168` rethrow，`agent/created` 监听器随之 reject → Agent 创建/恢复回滚。

**2. 抛错点** —— `packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/index.ts:199`–`:202`

```ts
const outcome = await connection.ready
if (outcome.error !== undefined && config.failOnStartupError) {
  throw new Error(`mcp-client(${config.serverName}): initial connection or tool synchronization failed`, { cause: outcome.error })
}
```

**3. 设计意图已被记载** —— `packages/experimental/browser-use-runtime/README.md`

- `:32`：Agent 创建或恢复在发现完成后才结束。
- `:34`：`A busy attachment skips startup permanently for that live activation while its other work continues.` 与 `Startup failure or cancellation rejects Agent creation or resume and triggers creation rollback`。

即：文档已经承认「占用 → 继续」与「失败 → 回滚」两种结果并存。

## 为什么值得讨论

- 浏览器工具是**可选增强**。它的启动失败不应等价于「会话不可用」。
- 同文件已经具备降级所需机制（`ClientState.status = 'blocked'` + `refreshBlockedMasks()` + `tools.restrict({ deny })` 屏蔽继承的工具名 + `system-prompt/assemble` 摘除对应 section），复用它即可让失败激活退化为「无浏览器工具的会话」。

## 可选方案（供维护者裁定）

1. **失败也降级**：启动失败时按 `blocked` 处理（记录日志 + 摘除提示段），让 Agent 创建/恢复正常完成。语义与已有的 busy-attachment 分支统一。
2. **把取舍显式化**：新增 provider 配置（例如 `onStartupFailure: 'fail' | 'degrade'`），默认保持现状，由部署方决定。
3. 仅在 provider 层不写死 `failOnStartupError: true`，改由既有 `blocked`/mask 机制兜底。

## 附带的可观测性问题

`mcp-client/src/index.ts:201` 抛出的包装错误把真实原因放进了 `cause`，而 Host/客户端只看到 `initial connection or tool synchronization failed` 这一句，无法区分「服务器根本起不来」「工具列表冲突」「协议协商失败」。建议至少在消息中带上底层原因，或确保 `cause` 能到达日志与前端——本次故障难以定位，很大程度源于此。

---

**说明**：本 issue 不主张某次具体线上故障由 `inputSchema` 词汇导致。实测（master 未打补丁源码、生产参数、`failOnStartupError: true`）显示带 `$schema` 的 `inputSchema` **不会**导致注册或启动失败：24 个 `@playwright/mcp@0.0.80` 工具全部注册成功，`upstream.e2e.ts` 全链路 2/2 通过。此处讨论的是「一旦启动真的失败，代价是否应该这么大」。

discussions.title: [Bug] compaction 辅助调用丢弃路由 reasoningEffort：off 档映射非法的路由上 /compact 必然 400 失败
discussions.body:
**TL;DR (English)** — `BasicCompaction`'s auxiliary summarization call omits `reasoningEffort`, so it falls into the provider's "off" thinking dispatch (`reasoning.effort = model.thinkingLevelMap.off ?? "none"`). On a route whose `off` level maps to a wire value the provider rejects (here: `off: none` on DeepSeek, which only accepts `low/medium/high/xhigh/max`), every `/compact` — manual and automatic — fails with HTTP 400. The routed request header already carries `reasoningEffort`, and this plugin explicitly replays that request's prefix to reuse the provider KV cache, so the effort should be mirrored onto the auxiliary call. A 6-line patch, wire-level evidence, and two related findings below.

### 环境

- dsh `0.1.5-rc.1`（npm 全局安装），Node `24.14.0`，Web profile
- 路由：`api: openai-responses`，经本地 OpenAI 兼容网关（CliProxyAPI）转发到 DeepSeek。模型为 settings 里自定义声明的：

```yaml
llm-pi-ai:
  providers:
    cpa:
      api: openai-responses
      models:
        - id: deepseek-flash
          contextWindow: 1000000
          maxTokens: 384000
          reasoningEfforts:
            minimal: minimal
            low: low
            medium: medium
            high: high
            xhigh: xhigh
            max: max
            off: none          # ← 关键行
```

### 现象

同一个会话连续 3 次 `/compact` 全部失败，UI 只给一句 `Compaction could not produce a useful summary. The conversation is unchanged; the attempt is recorded in the session log.`。会话日志里三次完全相同的错误文本：

```
compaction/start  00:25:27  compactionId=d29757aa-…
compaction/end    00:25:30  error="OpenAI API error (400): 400 status code (no body)"
compaction/start  00:26:44  compactionId=2e3ee906-…
compaction/end    00:26:47  error="OpenAI API error (400): 400 status code (no body)"
compaction/start  00:29:38  compactionId=318c8d41-…
compaction/end    00:29:40  error="OpenAI API error (400): 400 status code (no body)"
```

### 真实原因（网关侧日志）

同一时刻网关记录的是**明确、可操作**的错误（只是没被透出，见文末第 2 点）：

```
thinking: original config from request | provider=openai model=deepseek-flash mode=none budget=0 level=
request error, error status: 400, error message: {"code":"UNSUPPORTED_FIELD",
  "message":"DeepSeek reasoning_effort 只支持 low、medium、high、xhigh、max","data":{"field":"reasoning_effort"}}
```

对照同一时段**正常轮次**：`mode=level level=high` → `200`。

最小复现（任何 OpenAI 兼容网关 + DeepSeek 都能复现）：

```sh
# 400（就是压缩那次发出的形状）
curl -s $BASE/v1/responses -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"deepseek-flash","input":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"hi"}]}],"reasoning":{"effort":"none"}}'
# 200（不写 reasoning 字段）
curl -s $BASE/v1/responses -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"deepseek-flash","input":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"hi"}]}]}'
# 200（显式 high）
curl -s $BASE/v1/responses -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"deepseek-flash","input":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"hi"}]}],"reasoning":{"effort":"high"}}'
```

### 根因链路

1. `dsh-llm-pi-ai` 的 `resolveModelReasoning()` 把 settings 中声明的 `off: none` 物化成 `thinkingLevelMap.off = "none"`；
2. pi-ai `api/openai-responses.js`（约 L263-267）在**调用方没有传 `reasoningEffort`** 时走 else 分支：`params.reasoning = { effort: model.thinkingLevelMap?.off ?? "none" }`，于是发出 `"none"`；
3. `dsh-compaction-basic` 的 `summarizeWithLlm()`（安装包 `lib/index.js` L269-301）构造这次辅助调用时只带 `provider / model / messages / tools / maxTokens / sessionId / purpose / signal`，**唯独没有 `reasoningEffort`**，因此必然落进上面的 off 分支；
4. 而这个函数自己的注释写得很清楚：这次调用应当是"最近一次路由请求的真前缀"（"a genuine prefix of the last routed request"）以便复用 provider 的 KV cache。路由头 `agent.session.requestHeader()?.config` 里本来就带着 `reasoningEffort: "high"`（同一会话的正常轮次都在用它），只是被丢掉了 —— 丢掉它恰好破坏了该函数声称要维持的前缀一致性。

### 影响面 / 为什么用户在 UI 里自救不了

- 手动 `/compact` 与"上下文超限自动压缩"（`compactIfNeeded(agent, "context-overflow", …)`）走的是同一个 `summarizeWithLlm()`，两条路径一起坏；
- `target = configured ?? latest ?? agentTarget` 优先 `latest`，所以**切换模型对压缩无效**：实测第 2、3 次尝试分别发生在切到其它 provider 之后（会话日志有 `model/selection` 记录），三次请求仍全部打到原路由，报同一个 400；
- 同类"没有 effort 的辅助调用"还有 `dsh-session-title-llm` 的 `generateSessionTitleWithLlm()`：options 同样只有 `provider/model/messages/system/maxTokens/sessionId/purpose/signal`，尽管 `resolveRoute()` 返回的 `request.route` 就是带 `reasoningEffort` 的完整路由记录。表现是该路由下会话标题一直走 `source: fallback`（本机该 provider 上所有会话都是 fallback），且每次新建会话后端都会记录一次同样的 400；
- 报错文本没有信息量，且容易让人误判方向（见文末两点）。

### 建议修复（本机已按此打过补丁并验证）

只在"压缩目标 = 最近一次已路由请求"时镜像它的 effort；用户显式配置了独立 `summarizationProvider/Model` 时保持原样，避免把不支持该 effort 的模型拖下水：

```diff
--- a/dsh-compaction-basic/lib/index.js
+++ b/dsh-compaction-basic/lib/index.js
@@ -278,6 +278,13 @@
 	} : void 0;
 	const target = configured ?? latest ?? agentTarget;
 	if (target === void 0) throw new Error("no provider/model available for summarization: set both BasicCompactionConfig summarization fields, route one request, or set both AgentOptions fields");
+	/**
+	* The routed request's reasoning effort, mirrored onto the auxiliary call so
+	* it stays a genuine prefix of that request. Omitting it re-dispatches the
+	* provider's "off" thinking level, which routes whose provider rejects that
+	* wire value answer with an HTTP 400 instead of a summary.
+	*/
+	const routedEffort = configured === void 0 ? latest?.reasoningEffort : void 0;
 	const assembler = new BlockAssembler();
 	const messages = [...input.messages, createUserMessage({
 		content: [{
@@ -294,6 +301,7 @@
 		model: target.model,
 		messages,
 		...input.tools === void 0 ? {} : { tools: [...input.tools] },
+		...routedEffort === void 0 ? {} : { reasoningEffort: routedEffort },
 		maxTokens: config.maxTokens,
 		sessionId: agent.session.id,
 		purpose: "compaction",
```

桩测试（对打完补丁的产物调用 `summarizeWithLlm()`，记录传给 `ctx.llm.stream()` 的 options）：

```
routed 请求带 effort "high"   -> options.reasoningEffort = "high"   (cpa/deepseek-flash)
routed 请求无 effort          -> undefined   （行为不变）
尚未路由过任何请求            -> undefined   （行为不变）
purpose/sessionId/maxTokens   -> 均保持原样
```

再用真实网关验证三种 request 形状：`effort:"none"` → 400、不写该字段 → 200、`effort:"high"` → 200。`dsh-session-title-llm` 可用同一形状修（`route` 里已经有 `reasoningEffort`）。

### 附带发现（两点，都与本次误判有关）

**1) `resolveModelReasoning()` 的注释与 pi-ai 实际行为相反。** 注释说 "A declared `off` with no value … stays absent from the map, which pi-ai reads as 'supported, send nothing'"；但 `openai-responses.js` 只在 `thinkingLevelMap.off === null` 时才**不写**该字段，`off` 键缺席会走 `?? "none"`。实测（真实网关）：

| settings 里的写法 | 物化后的 `map.off` | 实际发出 | 结果 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `off: none` | `"none"` | `reasoning:{effort:"none"}` | 400 |
| `off:`（值为空/null） | 键被省略 → `undefined` | `reasoning:{effort:"none"}` | 400 |
| 整个省略 `off` 键 | `null`（钉死） | 不写 `reasoning` 字段（网关日志 `no config found, passthrough`） | 200 |

即：照注释写 `off:`（空）反而踩坑，**省略 `off` 键**才安全。建议让"声明为空"同样物化为 `null`，使注释与实现一致（对 `openai-completions` 路径同样成立：`openai-completions.js` 的 off 分支也是同样的 `off !== null` 判定）。用户侧规避：删掉 `off: none` 这一行即可让 `/compact` 与标题生成恢复。

**2) provider 返回的可操作错误体被丢弃。** 网关明确返回了 `{"code":"UNSUPPORTED_FIELD","message":"DeepSeek reasoning_effort 只支持 low、medium、high、xhigh、max","data":{"field":"reasoning_effort"}}`，harness 只 surface 出 `OpenAI API error (400): 400 status code (no body)`（`utils/error-body.ts` 的 `normalizeProviderError()` 取不到 body 时的形态）。这直接导致排查方向被带偏：`400 status code (no body)` 还正好命中 pi-ai `utils/overflow.ts` 里"Cerebras 400/413 (no body)"这条**上下文超限**特征（只因该正则带 `^` 锚点、前缀 `OpenAI API error (400): ` 使其侥幸未命中），很容易被读成"上下文太大压不动"。建议 body 缺失时至少保留 HTTP 状态与原始响应文本片段。

### 相关

- #6857（插件里调模型做结构化输出默认关推理）说明这类辅助调用确实常需要"关掉推理"；但"关闭"必须是**不写该字段**或写 provider 认识的值，落到 provider 不认识的 `none` 就是硬失败。
- #6839（压缩次数计数）同属压缩可观测性方向。

discussions.title: [Bug] subprocess-local: Windows 上每条受管命令都会弹出可见的控制台窗口（windows-job.ts 漏了 windowsHide）
discussions.body:
## 环境

| 项 | 值 |
| --- | --- |
| DSH | 0.1.6-alpha.1（commit 0a15e36e7f） |
| OS | Windows 11 |
| Node | v26.7.0 |
| 终端 | Windows Terminal（Win11 默认终端） |

## 现象

在 Windows 上运行 Web profile，**每执行一条命令**（bash / pwsh 工具调用、以及任何走 DSH 子进程层的操作）都会**闪烁一个可见的终端窗口**。窗口标题为 `C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe`，窗口类 `CASCADIA_HOSTING_WINDOW_CLASS`。

实测数据（用 EnumWindows 每 100ms 轮询新增可见顶层窗口）：

- 修复前：13 分钟内 **247 个新窗口事件**，其中 **226 个**是上述 Windows Terminal 窗口
- 给下述位置加上 `windowsHide: true` 后：同样的操作序列，**0 个新窗口事件**

## 根因

`packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/windows-job.ts` 第 135-143 行：

```js
child = (internals.spawn ?? spawn)(command, [
  ...prefix,
  '--',
  ...spec.argv,
], {
  cwd: process.cwd(),
  env: runnerEnvironment(WINDOWS_RUNNER_SELECTION, invocation),
  stdio: runnerStdio(spec, true, ignoredStdinFd ?? 'pipe'),
}) as RunnerProcess
```

这是 Windows 上**每个受管命令都要走的作业对象运行器**，但 spawn 选项里**没有 `windowsHide`**。

DSH 自身没有控制台（它自己是被隐藏启动的），所以在 Windows 上当控制台程序不带 `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` 启动时，系统会**新分配一个控制台**；Win11 的默认终端是 Windows Terminal，于是每次都弹出一个可见窗口。

## 为什么上游已有的修复没覆盖

`spawn.ts` 里已经有两处 `windowsHide`（L120 与 L466），但它们分别在「分离式回退路径」和「taskkill 助手」上，**与主路径（作业对象运行器）无关**。所以这个窗口问题一直没被治好。

## 建议修复

在 `windows-job.ts` 的 spawn 选项里加一行：

```js
windowsHide: true,
```

## 同一轮排查发现的其他同类位置（建议一并修）

都在 Windows 上会起控制台程序，同样缺 `windowsHide`：

| 文件 | 触发时机 |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/experimental/ptc-runtime-python/src/index.ts` L510 / L1200 | 运行 Python（PTC）时 |
| `packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/process-inspector.ts` L120 | 进程巡检的 exec 默认实现 |
| `packages/sandbox/sandbox-local/src/index.ts` L103 | Windows ACL 沙箱探测（`cmd /c exit 0`） |
| `packages/sdk/client/src/client.ts` L214 | SDK 客户端起 dsh 子进程 |
| `packages/ssh/ssh/src/index.ts` L230 / L263 | SSH 远端工作区 |
| `packages/bundle/web-app/src/index.ts` L173 | 打开浏览器时的启动器 |

已确认**不需要**处理的：`subprocess-local/src/index.ts` 的 `nodePty.spawn`（ConPTY 是伪控制台，不开可见窗口）；`linux-scope.ts`（Linux 专用）；`experimental/webworker-packer`（仅打包时运行）。

## 复现方式

1. Windows 11，Windows Terminal 设为默认终端
2. 用隐藏方式启动 DSH Web（即 DSH 进程自身没有控制台）
3. 连续执行几条命令
4. 观察：每条命令都会新增一个 `CASCADIA_HOSTING_WINDOW_CLASS` 顶层窗口（可用 EnumWindows 轮询 + `IsWindowVisible` 记录）

discussions.title: [Bug] client-connection is missing the webServer injection: every third-party rpc.handle registration fails silently
discussions.body:
## 一句话

`client-connection` 的 RPC 通道注册路径访问了它没有声明的 `webServer` 注入，导致**任何第三方插件调用 `ctx.connection.rpc.handle()` 都会静默失败**（无日志、无异常冒出），客户端只能看到 `HTTP 405`。

## 现象

第三方客户端插件（宿主半边调用 `ctx.connection.rpc.handle('/foo', handler)`）在浏览器侧请求 `POST /foo/bar` 时得到 **405**，宿主日志干净无报错。

同一实例实测对照：

| 请求 | 状态 | 含义 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /plugin-center/listInstalled` | **405** | 未匹配命名路由 → 静态服务兜底 |
| `POST /api/plugin-center/listInstalled` | **404** | `/api` 处理器在，但不认识该通道 |

两条对照说明通道**根本没注册**，而不是路径写错或 `/api` 未挂载。

## 根因

`packages/client/connection/src/rpc-host.ts:178-181`：

```ts
return owner.effect(
  () => owner.webServer.register(route),
  `client-connection: ${channel} rpc channel`,
)
```

`owner` 由同文件的 `get rpc()`（`rpc-host.ts:79-86`）定为 **Connection 服务自身的 fiber**（`const owner = this.ctx`）。

而该插件的注入声明是（`packages/client/connection/src/index.ts:69`）：

```ts
export const inject = ['credentials']
```

`webServer` 不在其中，cordis 的属性代理拒绝访问并抛错：

```
Error: cannot get property "webServer" without inject
    at Fiber.<anonymous> (…/packages/client/connection/src/rpc-host.ts:179:19)
    at Proxy.register (…/packages/client/connection/src/rpc-host.ts:178:18)
```

异常发生在 `owner.effect(...)` 的注册回调内部：通道从未注册，且不影响其它插件、不产生日志。调用方（第三方插件）通常既不 `try/catch` 也不检查 `handle()` 的返回值，所以缺陷完全静默。

`api-remotes` 的 Typert Remote 对第三方包是关闭的（显式官方 `./remote` 白名单），因此 `rpc.handle()` 是第三方插件暴露宿主能力的**唯一**手段——它失效等于第三方插件的宿主半边整体不可用。

## 复现

1. 源码形态启动：`node --import tsx/esm apps/cli/src/bin.ts web --port <port>`（本地为 `dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2`）。
2. 装任一第三方客户端插件，其宿主半边调用 `ctx.connection.rpc.handle('/foo', handler)`。
3. 浏览器发 `POST /foo/bar` → **405**，宿主 stderr 无输出。

## 形态差异线索

同一份插件代码（同版本）：

| 运行时形态 | 结果 |
| --- | --- |
| 打包内核（Electron 壳内 `kernel-child.bundle.mjs`） | **正常** |
| 源码形态（`dsh-web-runtime`） | **405** |

差异在装配形态，不在插件代码。

## 我们已落地的绕过（供参考）

改用 `connection.fetch.register()`（`rpc-host.ts:139-156`）：它只写 Connection 自己的 `fetchRoutes`，不触碰 `owner.webServer`。

```ts
connection.fetch.register({
  path: '/api/<ns>',
  methods: ['POST'],
  requestBody: 'buffered',
  fetch: async (request) => { /* {endpoint, payload} → RpcResult 信封 */ },
})
```

配套两点（也是排查中得到的事实）：

- `connection` 服务在插件 `apply` 时**尚未就绪**（实测 `ctx.get('connection') === undefined`），且 `ctx.plugin(P)` 不等待依赖，必须用 `ctx.inject(['connection'], cb)`；
- 老宿主（无 `fetch`）回退逻辑通道；浏览器侧先试新路由，**收到 404 才回退**（新路由未注册时 `/api/*` 是 404，根路径才是 405）。

绕过后的实测：两个端点均 **200**，面板恢复，控制台 0 errors。

## 建议修法（任一）

1. 在 `client-connection` 的 `inject` 中补上 `webServer`（若装配确实保证其可用，这是最小改动）；
2. 或在 `register()` 内改用 `this.ctx.get('webServer')`，取不到时**显式抛错**，让失败发生在插件作者能看到的位置；
3. 无论哪种，建议让注册失败**可见**：`handle()` 无法注册时同步抛错，或宿主侧打一条 warn——避免同类问题再次以「405 + 无日志」的形态出现。

## 附：探针原始输出

在插件 `dist` 内临时插探针（`console.error` + `handle()` 包 `try/catch`）后重启捕获：

```
[probe:index] apply called (inject satisfied); {"get.loader":true,"get.tools":true,"get.skills":true,
  "proxy.connection":"throw","get.connection":false,"get.webServer":false,...}
[probe:rpc] constructor: ctx.get(connection) available = false
[probe:rpc] inject callback fired; connection available = true
[probe:rpc] registering /skill-mcp via inject-callback
[probe:rpc] handle() THREW via inject-callback:
  Error: cannot get property "webServer" without inject
    at Fiber.<anonymous> (…/packages/client/connection/src/rpc-host.ts:179:19)
    at Proxy.register (…/packages/client/connection/src/rpc-host.ts:178:18)
```

（探针仅用于取证，验证后已回滚；未对 DSH 源码做任何修改。）

discussions.title: DSH | NextTavern | Long-form roleplay workspace with semantic memory, worldlines and SillyTavern cards
discussions.body:
**Community project, independently developed and maintained. Not affiliated with DeepSeek.**

NextTavern is a roleplay workspace for DeepSeek Harness: its own runtime, UI and memory layer, installed as a profile bundle rather than a thin wrapper around the built-in chat.

- Repository: https://github.com/a86582751/dsh-nexttavern
- Release (v0.2.5, 2026-09-16): https://github.com/a86582751/dsh-nexttavern/releases/tag/v0.2.5
- Screenshots: https://github.com/a86582751/dsh-nexttavern/blob/main/SCREENSHOTS.md

![NextTavern in play](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a86582751/dsh-nexttavern/main/screenshots/play.png)

## What it does

**Long-form memory.** Four mechanisms instead of one summary: a frozen settings prefix that is never compacted and is always injected; a hard-cut context window that advances on complete prose boundaries and keeps the tail; background director notes written by a separate task, each carrying a source hash and a same-worldline anchor so provenance is machine-checkable; and on-demand history recall in keyword (default), semantic and hybrid modes over player input plus valid story text, including archived and evicted prose. Status text, tool output, CSS, decision cards and reasoning stay out of the retrieval corpus.

![Hybrid retrieval: keyword, semantic and hybrid modes over the current worldline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a86582751/dsh-nexttavern/main/screenshots/retrieval.png)

**Embeddings, online or local.** An Embedding management page handles DashScope, OpenAI-compatible endpoints and OpenAI official, plus local models (BGE small zh, Qwen3-Embedding 0.6B, Jina Nano, Jina Small INT8, Nomic q8) on ONNX Runtime 1.29 in a separate encoding process — local serving needs no API key and no network. Vector recipes are fingerprinted on model, revision, dimensions, task role, pooling, quantization and runtime; a mismatch marks the index stale instead of serving from it.

![Embedding management: online providers and local models](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a86582751/dsh-nexttavern/main/screenshots/embedding.png)

**Worldlines.** Regenerate, edit-and-send and version switching all stay inside one visible conversation; an explicit clone creates a new one. State panels, decision cards, director notes, worldbook rows and retrieval results are scoped per worldline, and late results from a superseded branch are rejected rather than merged.

**Cards, both directions.** Import SillyTavern/TauriTavern character cards (PNG `chara`/`ccv3`, JSON v1/v2/v3, embedded worldbooks) or author a new one through an interactive flow with a twelve-item completeness check. A long TXT novel can be turned into a playable card through either an intensive segmented reading pass or a coarse multi-round relation-frontier pass, with every research note gated on a quote that actually appears in the batch it cites.

![Interactive card authoring](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a86582751/dsh-nexttavern/main/screenshots/authoring.png)

**Reading and play.** A dedicated tavern reader tab, the main agent consulting worldbooks on demand, action suggestions in a standalone decision card instead of the prose tail, a character agent cluster with per-character model overrides, 16 built-in styles with scoped presets (current conversation, designated conversation, global) and three explicit style modes, plus card and novel export.

![Character agent cluster](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a86582751/dsh-nexttavern/main/screenshots/characters.png)

**Presentation.** The bundled `dsh-nexttavern-amber` skin redraws the whole interface from one set of design tokens with day and night themes; it installs disabled and the bundled third-party market (dshmarket 1.39.0, MIT) toggles it from 设置 → 插件市场 → 已安装 in about a second, without a restart.

![The bundled amber skin, day theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a86582751/dsh-nexttavern/main/screenshots/skin-day.png)

## Compatibility and installation

Tested target: **Harness 0.1.2-alpha.3** with pi-ai 0.84.4. Project-owned code is **GPL-3.0-only**; bundled third-party material keeps its own terms.

Two install paths, both self-contained and binding `127.0.0.1` only (port chosen from 3510–3599):

- One-click installers from the v0.2.5 release — `NextTavern-Setup.exe` (Windows GUI, x64 and arm64, in-place upgrade from an older installation) and `NextTavern-Setup.sh` (Linux, x86_64 and aarch64 glibc, no root and no system packages beyond a POSIX shell). Both provision their own Node.js runtime, verify every download against SHA-256, cache what they verified and resume after an interrupted download.
- The prebuilt package `dsh-nexttavern.tgz` from the same release, or the repository itself.

The Harness itself needs the documented, explicit six-unit compatibility patch (upload/read_document, anydoc, pi-ai and the official UI/controller units) applied after stopping the instance; installation follows that procedure step by step. **No patch runs during npm postinstall, and nothing is fetched or written at install time beyond the package itself.**

## Dependencies and provenance

The package depends on a formal GitHub fork release, `a86582751/dsh-file-upload` (`v0.4.3-nexttavern.1`). Upstream does not support Harness 0.1.2-alpha.3, so the fork exists only for that compatibility; it keeps its fork relationship, upstream history, original MIT license and NOTICE attribution. The optional document/file tools use the same kind of fork (`a86582751/dsh-plugin-anydoc`, `a86582751/pi`). NextTavern ships its own runtime, UI, memory and export behaviour — the forks are additional dependencies, not its content.

## Verification

Every pull request in the repository runs a generated-file consistency check (each shipped `.js` must equal its TypeScript source) and 53 contract suites, including an end-to-end suite that drives a real turn, its maintenance, a fork through the branch route and both sides of the resulting worldlines. TypeScript is the only maintained source, and the build map that regenerates the shipped JavaScript is part of the package.

## Known limits

- Targets Harness `0.1.2-alpha.3` only; it is not a drop-in for other Harness lines.
- The six-unit patch procedure is required, and it is manual and documented rather than automatic.
- Windows installers are not code-signed.
- Synthetic embedding evaluation is not a long-term quality guarantee, and coarse novel coverage does not promise comprehension of every detail.

---

### 中文摘要

NextTavern 是面向 DeepSeek Harness 的角色扮演工作台（社区项目，非官方）。长篇记忆由四件事撑住：固定设定前缀不压缩始终注入、硬切窗口按完整正文边界推进并保留尾部、后台导演笔记带来源哈希与世界线锚点、按需的历史召回（关键词／语义／混合，在线或本地嵌入）。世界线都在同一对话内，重新生成／改后发送／版本切换不新建对话，显式克隆才另建，且状态、决策、笔记、世界书与检索结果都按世界线隔离。人物卡既可导入（SillyTavern／TauriTavern 的 PNG 与 JSON）也可交互式现写；长篇 TXT 可用精读或粗颗粒度两种方式改编成卡。另有独立酒馆阅读 TAB、主动查阅世界书、独立决策卡、角色 Agent 集群、16 种自带文风的作用域预设，以及卡／小说导出。面向 Harness `0.1.2-alpha.3`，安装需按文档应用显式六单元兼容补丁；Windows 与 Linux 一键安装器同 Release 提供。

discussions.title: Two hosts sharing one DSH_HOME silently overwrite each other's stored state
discussions.body:
### What happens

Running two hosts against the same `$DSH_HOME` makes `storages/` state silently regress: data written by one host disappears when the other writes.

Observed on Windows with DSH `0.1.5-rc.2`. The symptom that surfaced it: **142 of 235 sessions were never registered to their workspace** — the workspace listed 29 session ids, all created inside a three-day window; every session created after that window was missing, and nothing was ever reported to the user.

### This is not a third-party deployment mistake

The shipped desktop host derives its paths from a home documented as shared with npm-installed `dsh`:

```ts
// apps/desktop/src/paths.ts
/** @param dshHome - Harness home shared with npm-installed dsh. */
export function resolveDesktopPaths(dshHome: string = resolveDshHome()): DesktopPaths {
  return {
    profile: join(dshHome, 'profiles', 'desktop'),
    lock: join(dshHome, 'profiles', 'desktop', 'lock'),
    // …
  }
}
```

It owns `profiles/desktop` exclusively — with its own lock — but **not `storages/`**. So the desktop host running alongside `dsh web` (or an npm-installed `dsh`) shares the same storage directory: the collision is reachable inside the shipped product line, not only to downstream integrations.

### Why it is silent

`packages/storage/storage-json` writes a whole unit by atomic replace, and its module comment states the assumption:

> `Rename is an atomic replace on POSIX and on Windows …` **`writer per process and last-write-wins is correct.`**

A second process holding a stale in-memory snapshot wins the race and overwrites the other's writes. `storage-domain` serializes writes **within one process only**, so nothing detects the conflict.

`packages/storage/storage-sqlite` does not help either — its README says:

> **No busy-wait or retry policy** — a competing connection holding a write lock rejects the operation immediately instead of waiting; the domain layer's write chain serializes writes within one process, and **cross-process coordination is out of scope**.

There is also a client-side amplifier: the failure only reaches `console.warn` (`packages/client/ui-workspace/src/client/navigation.ts`, `'new session failed:'`), so the user never sees an error.

### Why a backend-level fix cannot cover it

The update window spans the whole read-modify-write cycle, not a single write. An application-level holder reads the unit, mutates in memory, and writes the whole unit back later. A lock inside a backend cannot cover that window, which is why swapping backends does not fix it.

Affected `$DSH_HOME` state observed here:

| Path | Effect |
|---|---|
| `storages/workspace.json` | workspace membership lost (confirmed) |
| `storages/memory.json` | cross-session memory lost (same full-document write pattern) |
| `storages/query-log.json` | counters drift |
| plugin-owned stores under `~/.dsh/*.json` | favorites / state lost |

Sessions and profiles are not affected when the hosts use separate session roots — only `storages/` is shared by default.

### Reproduction sketch

1. Start two hosts against one `DSH_HOME` (for example `dsh --profile web`, plus a second host with its own profile but the same home).
2. In host A, create a session bound to a workspace.
3. Let host B perform any write to the same storage unit.
4. The session from step 2 is no longer accounted: the UI shows it under "ungrouped" and the storage file no longer lists it.

### What we would like

Any one of:

1. **Cross-process coordination in `storage-domain`** — a lock around the unit lifecycle, or a version check that rejects a stale whole-unit write instead of applying it.
2. **A stale-write detector** — for example a mutation counter per unit, so a writer can tell its snapshot is stale and report it rather than overwrite.
3. If neither is in scope soon, **document the constraint**: "one writer per `DSH_HOME`; concurrent hosts require separate homes", and let a host detect and refuse that configuration instead of losing data silently.

Option 3 alone would already remove the silent part, which is the worst property here.

discussions.title: [Bug] Native HMR starts replacement activation before asynchronous disposal finishes
discussions.body:
A live Host reload can start the replacement plugin before the previous instance's asynchronous disposer finishes. A plugin holding an exclusive resource then fails to reactivate even though its disposer eventually releases that resource.

Reproduced directly with **DSH 0.1.5-rc.2, Node 24.19.0, macOS ARM64**. The attached reproduction invokes the installed DSH entry with native Cordis HMR; it does not use dsh-developer, a browser, a model, or plugin installation.

The fixture acquires a file with `open(path, 'wx')`. Its `ctx.effect()` disposer awaits 200 ms, closes the handle, and unlinks the file. Changing an imported module produces:

| Relative time | Instance | Event |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 0 ms | old | disposer starts |
| 1 ms | replacement | apply starts |
| 1 ms | replacement | exclusive acquisition fails with `EEXIST` |
| 201 ms | old | disposer finishes |

Expected: awaited cleanup finishes before replacement activation reacquires an exclusive resource. Actual: cleanup and replacement activation overlap. This is **live reload**, separate from SIGTERM or forced process shutdown.

In the installed `@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-hmr` implementation, `partialReload()` calls `ctx.registry.delete(plugin)` and proceeds to `reload(...)`. Cordis registry `delete()` starts each `fiber.dispose()` without awaiting it. The replacement also takes over the loader entry's current fiber, so awaiting current entries does not establish that the removed fiber has drained. This appears to be the lifecycle handoff that needs attention; I have not implemented an upstream repair.

<details>
<summary>Self-contained reproduction (Node built-ins only)</summary>

Save as `native-hmr-disposal.mjs`, then run against an installed runtime:

```sh
node native-hmr-disposal.mjs /absolute/path/to/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib/bin.js
```

The script uses a disposable DSH home, disables browser opening, keeps the lock and trace outside the watched directory, prints the observed ordering, and removes its temporary files after stopping the owned process.

```js
// Usage: node native-direct-repro.mjs /absolute/path/to/@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib/bin.js
// Node built-ins only. No dsh-developer, pnpm install, browser, or model call.
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { mkdir, mkdtemp, readFile, writeFile, rm } from 'node:fs/promises'
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
import { dirname, join, resolve, sep } from 'node:path'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { setTimeout as sleep } from 'node:timers/promises'

if (!process.argv[2]) throw new Error('Pass the installed native DSH lib/bin.js path')
const dsh = resolve(process.argv[2])
const runtime = JSON.parse(await readFile(join(dirname(dirname(dsh)), 'package.json'), 'utf8')).version
const root = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'native-hmr-disposal-'))
const source = join(root, 'source'), trace = join(root, 'trace.jsonl')
const lock = join(root, 'exclusive.lock'), patch = join(root, 'hmr.patch.yml')
let child, closed, diagnostics = ''
try {
  await mkdir(source)
  await writeFile(trace, '')
  await writeFile(join(source, 'value.mjs'), 'export const version = 1\n')
  await writeFile(join(source, 'index.mjs'), `
import { appendFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { open, unlink } from 'node:fs/promises'
import { setTimeout } from 'node:timers/promises'
import { version } from './value.mjs'
const log = event => appendFileSync(${JSON.stringify(trace)}, JSON.stringify({ time: Date.now(), version, event }) + '\\n')
export const name = 'async-disposal-repro'
export const inject = ['hmr']
export async function apply(ctx) {
  log('apply-start')
  let handle
  try { handle = await open(${JSON.stringify(lock)}, 'wx') }
  catch (error) { log('lock-failed:' + error.code); throw error }
  log('lock-acquired')
  ctx.effect(() => async () => {
    log('dispose-start')
    await setTimeout(200)
    await handle.close()
    await unlink(${JSON.stringify(lock)})
    log('dispose-end')
  })
  ctx.effect(() => ctx.get('appReady').onReady(() => log('ready')))
}
`)
  await writeFile(patch, `- id: web-runtime
  config:
    openBrowser: false
    printUrl: false
- id: hmr
  disabled: false
  config:
    base: ${JSON.stringify(pathToFileURL(source + sep).href)}
    root: ["."]
- insert:
    - id: async-disposal-repro
      name: ${JSON.stringify(pathToFileURL(join(source, 'index.mjs')).href)}
`)
  const env = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(process.env).filter(([key]) =>
    /^(PATH|PATHEXT|SYSTEMROOT|WINDIR|COMSPEC|TEMP|TMP|TMPDIR|LANG|LC_ALL)$/i.test(key)))
  Object.assign(env, { DSH_HOME: join(root, 'home'), DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: '1', CI: '1', NO_COLOR: '1' })
  child = spawn(process.execPath, ['--expose-internals', dsh, '--profile', 'web',
    '--patch', patch, '--port', '0', '--no-open'], { cwd: root, env, stdio: ['ignore', 'ignore', 'pipe'] })
  child.stderr.on('data', chunk => { diagnostics = (diagnostics + chunk).slice(-4096) })
  closed = new Promise((accept, reject) => { child.once('error', reject); child.once('close', accept) })
  void closed.catch(() => {})
  const records = async () => (await readFile(trace, 'utf8')).trim().split('\n').filter(Boolean).map(JSON.parse)
  const until = async predicate => {
    const deadline = Date.now() + 30_000
    while (Date.now() < deadline) {
      const rows = await records()
      if (predicate(rows)) return rows
      if (child.exitCode !== null || child.signalCode !== null) throw new Error('DSH exited: ' + diagnostics)
      await sleep(25)
    }
    throw new Error('Timed out: ' + diagnostics)
  }
  await until(rows => rows.some(row => row.event === 'ready' && row.version === 1))
  await sleep(500)
  await writeFile(join(source, 'value.mjs'), 'export const version = 2\n')
  const rows = await until(rows => rows.some(row => row.event === 'dispose-end' && row.version === 1)
    && rows.some(row => row.version === 2 && ['lock-acquired', 'lock-failed:EEXIST'].includes(row.event)))
  const start = rows.find(row => row.event === 'dispose-start' && row.version === 1).time
  const timeline = rows.filter(row => row.time >= start).map(({ time, ...row }) => ({ ms: time - start, ...row }))
  console.log(JSON.stringify({ runtime, node: process.version, platform: process.platform, timeline }, null, 2))
  assert(rows.some(row => row.version === 2 && row.event === 'lock-failed:EEXIST'),
    'Expected the reported race; native behavior may have changed')
} finally {
  if (child?.pid && child.exitCode === null && child.signalCode === null) {
    child.kill('SIGTERM')
    const force = setTimeout(() => child.kill('SIGKILL'), 1500)
    try { await closed } finally { clearTimeout(force) }
  }
  await rm(root, { recursive: true, force: true })
}

```

</details>

Separate development-wrapper trials observed the same overlap on 0.1.1-rc.2 and 0.1.5-rc.2. The wrapper correctly reported failed activation with one inactive entry; the direct reproduction above isolates the current native runtime behavior. Windows and other versions are not established by these observations.

Until the handoff is resolved, plugins requiring an exclusive resource should restart the process or explicitly coordinate that resource's lifetime. There is no claim here that all plugins fail to reload.

discussions.title: [Desktop 2.0.10] All subprocesses fail on Windows: private runner launched via process.execPath without ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE
discussions.body:
**Component:** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local@0.1.6-alpha.1`
**Environment:** DSH Desktop 2.0.10 (Electron 43.3.0, bundled Node 24.18.1), Windows x64

---

## Symptom

On the packaged desktop build, **every** subprocess spawn fails. The code-execution tool, the shell tool and plugin installation are all unusable.

```
Error: subprocess-local: Windows Job runner exited with exit code 0
       before proving its managed range empty
    at settleRange (<install>\resources\app\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\dsh-subprocess-local\lib\index.js:611:38)
    at ChildProcess.<anonymous> (<install>\...\lib\index.js:668:3)
```

The DSH server is hosted in Electron's utility Node process:

```
"DSH Desktop.exe" --type=utility --utility-sub-type=node.mojom.NodeService ...
```

## Root cause

`spawnRunnerInvocation()` (`lib/runner-launch-*.js`) resolves the private runner through `process.execPath`:

```js
function spawnRunnerInvocation() {
    if ("pkg" in process) return [process.execPath];
    if (extname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) !== ".ts")
        return [process.execPath, fileURLToPath(import.meta.resolve("@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local/runner"))];
    ...
}
```

Inside Electron's utility Node process `process.execPath` is **`DSH Desktop.exe`**, so the spawn becomes:

```
"DSH Desktop.exe" "<install>\...\dsh-subprocess-local\lib\runner.js" -- <target argv>
```

This starts a **second app instance**. It hits the single-instance lock, forwards its argv to the already-running instance and exits immediately with code 0. The parent then observes exactly the three conditions that `settleRange()` treats as infrastructure failure:

```js
if (exitCode === 0 && signal === null) {
    if (directResultType !== void 0) { rangeExit.resolve(); return; }
    if (!ipcDisconnected) return;
}
// -> failInfrastructure(...)
```

exit code 0, no signal, and the IPC channel disconnected before any `direct-result` message arrived.

`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` is **never set anywhere in the package** (0 occurrences in `lib/index.js` and `lib/runner-launch-*.js`).

## Deterministic reproduction outside the app

```powershell
> & "DSH Desktop.exe" "<install>\...\lib\runner.js" -- cmd.exe /c "echo RUNNER_OK"
  # no output, exit=0 after ~235 ms, and the running DSH Desktop window is raised to the foreground

> $env:ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE='1'
> & "DSH Desktop.exe" "<install>\...\lib\runner.js" -- cmd.exe /c "echo RUNNER_OK"
  # Node.js v24.18.1 starts and executes the script -> the flag is the only missing piece
```

## Regression: 0.1.5-rc.2 already handled this

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local@0.1.5-rc.2` contained, inside `runnerEnvironment()`:

```js
// Electron hosts must launch the private Windows runner in Node mode.
// Target env arrives separately over IPC; never add this flag to it.
if (selection === WINDOWS_RUNNER_SELECTION && process.platform === "win32" && process.versions.electron !== void 0) {
    for (const name of Object.keys(env)) {
        if (name.toUpperCase() === "ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE") Reflect.deleteProperty(env, name);
    }
    env.ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE = "1";
}
```

`0.1.6-alpha.1` deleted the whole block. Combined with the desktop build moving the server from a standalone `node.exe` into an Electron utility process, the assumption behind `process.execPath` ("this is Node") no longer holds.

## Additional finding: fixing only the runner is not sufficient

The code-execution worker is *also* spawned as the Electron binary:

```
"DSH Desktop.exe" "...\lib\runner.js" -- "DSH Desktop.exe" --max-old-space-size=512 "...\dsh-ptc-runtime-node\lib\process.js" 134217728
```

so its target environment 鈥?built by `targetEnvironment()` (`childEnv(spec.env)`) and by the direct `spawnSubprocess()` path (`controlEnvironment(childEnv(spec.env), ...)`) 鈥?needs the flag as well. Without it the failure merely moves one level down:

```
Error: code run failed (worker-exit): Node process exited before completing (0)
```

Verified: patching only `runnerEnvironment()` reproduces the second error; patching the target environment as well fixes it.

## Suggested fix

1. Restore the 0.1.5-rc.2 block in `runnerEnvironment()`.
2. Additionally inject the flag for the **target** environment, but only when the command about to be spawned is the host's own binary, so that unrelated Electron GUI applications launched through the same seam keep starting normally:

```js
function electronNodeEnv(command, env) {
    if (process.versions.electron === void 0 || typeof command !== "string") return env;
    const self = process.execPath;
    if (typeof self !== "string") return env;
    const stem = (value) => String(value).split(/[\\/]/).pop().toLowerCase();
    if (stem(command) !== stem(self)) return env;
    return { ...env, ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE: "1" };
}
```

applied at the two places that build a target environment (`targetEnvironment()` and the direct branch of `spawnSubprocess()`).

> Note: a naive fix that adds the flag inside `childEnv()` does make everything work, but it leaks `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` into **every** spawned process, which breaks launching any other Electron GUI application (e.g. VS Code via `Code.exe`) from inside DSH. That is exactly what the 0.1.5-rc.2 comment warned about. The scoped version above avoids it.

## Impact

Complete loss of a core capability on the packaged Windows desktop build (no shell tool, no code execution, no plugin install). The only workaround is patching files inside `resources\app`, which any future update wipes.

---

*Found on a standard Windows x64 installation. Happy to provide further detail or to test a patched build.*

discussions.title: Feedback: Web search quality and token cost make DSH unusable for professional research
discussions.body:
I am writing as a professional user who was eager to adopt DeepSeek Harness (DSH) as a paid alternative to other AI subscription services. I believe in your model — it outperforms competitors I was paying $40/month for — and I wanted to redirect that budget to DeepSeek.

However, after extensive daily use of DSH, I must share feedback that I hope is taken constructively. The product currently falls short of DeepSeek's own free web version in critical areas, which makes it impossible to justify paying for it as a primary tool.

1. Web Search: Inferior to the Free Web Version

This is the most severe issue. DSH's web search is not just slower or less parallel — it is qualitatively worse. It fails to find what the free web version finds. It does not enter documents, does not cite sources with precision, and often requires repeating searches. I have spent money and time building custom search plugins with multiple meta-search engines to try to close this gap, i've also tried many community plugnis. They did not work. The result was slower (up to 15x), more expensive (60K–250K tokens per search), and still far below the free web version in quality.

By contrast, the free web version can search 40–80 pages in seconds, read them, and cite exact passages. That is the baseline I expect from a paid product.

2. Token Consumption: Unsustainable Cost per Response

This is not just "context accumulation" over a long conversation. A single response in DSH can exceed 1 million tokens. A moderately complex conversation can easily reach 100 million tokens. I spent $10 in two days using DSH for basic tasks, when my reference point was $40/month on a competitor. The cost-per-response makes DSH economically irrational even for tasks where it might technically perform well.

3. Product Incoherence: Paid Version Inferior to Free Version

It is illogical that a paid, specialized agent harness is worse than the free web product in search, cost, and speed. I am willing to pay more for a product that improves on every dimension. What I cannot accept is paying for something that is inferior in the basics. A flexible product would allow switching between a "web mode" (with full search) and an "agent mode" (for offline/document-heavy work) within the same project. DSH does not offer this.

4. Attempts to Fix It Have Failed

Community plugins (ModSearch, etc.) and my own custom developments have not solved the problem. They either compromise quality, increase time, or increase cost. The architectural gap between DSH and the web version appears too large to bridge with plugins alone.

5. Suggestions

- Improve the native web search to match or exceed the free web version's depth, speed, and citation accuracy.
- Implement efficient context management: aggressive compression, selective pruning, and strict per-response token budgets.
- Allow users to switch between "web mode" and "agent mode" within the same session or project.
- Provide transparent token consumption metrics per response so users can understand and control costs.
- Consider offering a paid tier that includes the full web search capability as a baseline feature, not an add-on.

I am not writing to complain. I am writing because I want to pay for this product. The model is excellent. The harness is not ready, and the cost structure makes it unusable for professional research work. I hope this feedback reaches the product team.

Thank you for your time and for the work you do.

discussions.title: [Bug] subprocess-local: the 15 ms owner wait rescans all of /proc synchronously, costing ~15% of a core per long-lived process group
discussions.body:
## Summary

`fallbackOwner().waitForExit()` waits for the managed process group to disappear by polling every
15 ms. While the direct child is still alive that poll is cheap (a single `kill(-pgid, 0)`). But as
soon as the direct child has exited and the group still has members, **every tick performs a full
synchronous scan of `/proc`**: `readdirSync('/proc')` plus one `readFileSync('/proc/<pid>/stat')`
for *every PID on the machine*.

On a 2-vCPU host with ~220 PIDs that is ~220 blocking syscalls every 15 ms — about **66 sweeps/s,
~15 000 `read()` syscalls/s, ~15 % of one core**, per affected group, sustained for as long as the
group lives. It is synchronous, so it also runs on the main thread and blocks the event loop: the
Web GUI becomes visibly janky long before the average latency looks bad.

## Where

- `packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/spawn.ts:86` — fixed interval

  ```ts
  function sleepTick(): Promise<void> {
    return sleepMs(15)
  }
  ```

- `packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/spawn.ts:245-248` — the wait loop

  ```ts
  observation ??= (async () => {
    while (alive()) await sleepTick()
    stopped = true
  })()
  ```

- `packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/spawn.ts:218-224` — `alive()` gates the expensive call
  behind `directSettled` (this is exactly the state a long-lived group reaches):

  ```ts
  process.kill(-pid, 0)
  if (directSettled && platform === 'linux' && linuxGroupHasLiveMembers(pid) === false) return false
  return true
  ```

- `packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/process-inspector.ts:204-221` —
  `linuxProcessGroupHasLiveMembers()` re-reads the whole process table on every call:

  ```ts
  entries = internals.readDir('/proc')
  ...
  for (const entry of entries) {
    if (!/^\d+$/.test(entry)) continue
    const stat = readLinuxStat(internals, Number(entry))   // one readFileSync per PID
    ...
  }
  ```

Note `DEFAULT_INTERNALS` uses `readdirSync` / `readFileSync`, so both are blocking.

`kill(-pgid, 0)` alone is not sufficient because it also succeeds when the group contains only
zombies — the `/proc` walk exists to tell "only zombies left" from "live members left". That is the
check being repeated at 15 ms.

## How the expensive branch is reached

Any managed command whose process group outlives its shell. The ordinary way this happens is a
daemonizing command (`nohup CMD &`), but a non-interactive shell does not create a new process group
for `&`, so it is really "any survivor". Verified on the host:

```
shell pgid=146802
  nohup ... &  -> child pgid=146802   (same group: never drains)
  setsid ... & -> child pgid=146811   (new group: drains when the shell exits)
```

The cost also scales with the **number of PIDs on the machine**, not with any work the harness is
doing, and it multiplies by the number of affected groups.

## Measurements

Two affected groups had been alive for 12 h 46 m and 4 h 51 m (both idle development servers):

| Metric | Before | After removing them |
|---|---|---|
| `syscr` rate of the main process | 32 568 reads/s | 2 240 reads/s |
| Main-thread CPU (`/proc/<pid>/task/<pid>/stat` delta) | 33.4 % of one core | ~5 % |
| Affected process groups | 2 | 0 |

A longer sample caught a burst of **176 071 reads/s** with `/proc` holding 221 PIDs — that is ~800
sweeps/s, i.e. **~12 concurrent wait loops** (12 affected groups), since one loop alone is ~67/s.

CPU profiling attributed **~84 % of the main thread's active JS time** to this path
(`readFileUtf8` + `readdir` + `parseProcStat`), with the process oscillating between ~19 % and ~100 %
of a core.

## Suggested fix

The loop's purpose (the comment right above it) is that the awaited teardown must keep the event loop
alive until the tree really exits — so the loop itself is intentional. The problem is a **fixed 15 ms
interval combined with an O(PIDs) synchronous scan**.

A minimal change that keeps the semantics is **exponential backoff once the direct child has settled**
— which is the only moment the expensive branch is reachable:

```ts
let settledStep = 0
while (alive()) {
  await sleepTick(directSettled ? Math.min(15 * 2 ** settledStep++, 1000) : 15)
}
```

Keeping 15 ms while the direct child is alive preserves responsiveness (that path is a single
`kill()`), while an affected group goes 15 → 30 → 60 → … → 1000 ms. I applied exactly this locally
and measured a live, controlled case: **66 sweeps/s → ~0.85–1 sweep/s, a 66× reduction**, confirmed
with the actual code in a running process. Normal short-lived commands are unaffected.

A fuller fix is event-driven and O(1): `pidfd_open` + `epoll`, `waitid`, or a per-job cgroup v2
waiting on `cgroup.events` (`populated 0`). Independently, the scan could avoid `readLinuxStat` for
every PID — e.g. by caching the previously observed member list — which alone would cut the per-tick
cost by an order of magnitude.

## Versions

Reproduced with DSH `0.1.5-rc.1` (bundled `subprocess-local` `0.1.5-rc.2`, Node 24, Linux aarch64).
The code is unchanged in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local@0.1.5-rc.2` and `@0.1.6-alpha.1`, so
upgrading does not help today.

Happy to provide the exact patch, a repro script, or the raw CPU profiles if that is useful.
