discussions.title: [BUG] `@` mention menu (session-reference) surfaces subagent-origin sessions it should hide
discussions.body:
## Summary

`SessionReferenceResolver.listCandidates` (`packages/context/session-reference/src/index.ts`) only excludes the requesting agent's own session id from `ctx.sessionQuery.listSessions()`. It never checks `SessionHeader.origin`, so a subagent-origin session (`origin: 'subagent'`) shows up as an ordinary candidate in Web's `@` reference-completion menu.

```ts
const records = (await settleWithCancellation(this.ctx.sessionQuery.listSessions(signal), signal))
  .filter(record => record.header.id !== agent.id)   // only excludes self
```

## Why this is inconsistent

Elsewhere in the codebase, `origin: 'subagent'` is already treated as a reason to hide a session from ordinary navigation:

```ts
// packages/client/ui-workspace/src/client/tree.ts
function sessionVisible(session: SessionSummary, ...): boolean {
  return session.origin !== 'subagent' && ...
}
```

A subagent-origin session is a delegation artifact of its parent, not independent cross-session discussion — it's already reachable through the durable subagent catalog (`packages/subagent/subagent`, and the Web subagent conversation UI). Reference discovery disagrees with this existing product rule.

## Impact

Typing `@` in the Web chat input shows delegation/subagent child sessions mixed in with independent sessions worth referencing, with no way to distinguish them beforehand and no config to suppress them. `SessionReferenceResolver.Config` has no relevant field (`maxReferences`, `candidateLimit`, `maxReferenceBytes`, `referenceContextFraction` only).

## Suggested fix

Filter `record.header.origin !== 'subagent'` in the same step that already excludes `record.header.id !== agent.id`, inside `listCandidates`. `remoteExportCandidates` (the Web Remote face) inherits the fix automatically since it calls `listCandidates` directly. No config addition needed — `origin` is a fixed structural classification of the session, not a deployment-varying preference.

## Repro

1. Run a task that spawns a subagent/delegation child in Web.
2. In any session, type `@` to open the reference menu.
3. Observe the subagent's session appears as a candidate alongside ordinary sessions.

discussions.title: [Windows] Every ordinary subprocess spawn allocates a console window — visible terminal popup on each agent command
discussions.body:
## Summary

On Windows, **every command the agent runs through a shell executor pops a visible terminal window** (Windows Terminal, when it is the default terminal application). The ordinary subprocess creation path in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-win32-process` creates targets without `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, so a console-subsystem target (`powershell.exe`, `cmd.exe`, `bash.exe`) gets a **fresh console allocated** by Windows. The fallback spawn path already behaves correctly (Node's `windowsHide`), so the two paths disagree.

## Environment

- Windows 11 (10.0.26200, x64)
- Windows Terminal 1.24 installed and selected as the default terminal application (`HKCU\Console\%%Startup` either zeroed — "let Windows decide" — or explicitly delegating to Windows Terminal)
- Packaged desktop app `0.1.6-alpha.1` (locally built, unsigned), session permission preset = full access, i.e. the ordinary path rather than the ACL sandbox

## Steps to reproduce

1. Windows 11 with Windows Terminal installed and selected as the default terminal application.
2. Run any command through a harness shell executor — e.g. ask the agent to run `echo hi`.

## Observed

A Windows Terminal window appears for the duration of every command. Captured process/window timeline for one command (console-window poller, millisecond stamps):

```
t+0.0s  DeepSeek Harness.exe (Electron main → host → Job runner; all GUI subsystem)
t+0.9s  OpenConsole.exe -Embedding            parent=svchost   ← console host activation for a NEW console
t+1.1s  powershell.exe -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "[Console]::OutputEncoding = …"
                                              parent=DeepSeek Harness.exe (the Job runner)
t+1.2s  WindowsTerminal.exe -Embedding        parent=svchost   ← default-terminal delegation
t+1.7s  visible window: CASCADIA_HOSTING_WINDOW_CLASS / PseudoConsoleWindow, owner = that powershell.exe
```

## Root cause

`packages/subprocess/win32-process/src/process.ts` → `spawnCurrentTokenJobProcess()` passes only:

```ts
abi.CREATE_SUSPENDED | abi.CREATE_UNICODE_ENVIRONMENT,
```

and the STARTUPINFO built for that call sets `dwFlags` to `STARTF_USESTDHANDLES` only. Neither `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` nor `STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW` + `SW_HIDE` is passed.

In the desktop app the whole ancestry is GUI-subsystem (`DeepSeek Harness.exe`: Electron main → dsh host → Job runner), so there is no console to inherit; Windows therefore allocates a **new console** for the console-subsystem target. With the default terminal delegated to Windows Terminal, that allocation is rendered as a visible window — WT does not honor hidden-window hints (an OS behavior, not something the caller can suppress by other means).

The fallback path does set the flag, so only the Job path is affected: `packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/spawn.ts` passes `windowsHide: platform === 'win32'` to Node's `spawn` (= `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`).

## Suggested fix

Add `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` to the ordinary path's flags:

```ts
abi.CREATE_SUSPENDED | abi.CREATE_UNICODE_ENVIRONMENT | abi.CREATE_NO_WINDOW,
```

and update `packages/subprocess/win32-process/tests/ordinary-process.spec.ts`, which asserts the exact flag expression.

Do **not** add it to the restricted-token path (`spawnInheritedJobProcess` → `CreateProcessAsUserW`): `packages/sandbox/sandbox-windows-acl/src/index.ts` documents that `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` children die with `STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED` under the restriction, which is exactly why that path inherits the caller's console. Commands run under the ACL sandbox therefore stay affected — that case likely needs a different answer.

## Verification

- **A/B outside the harness**: a console-less parent spawning `cmd.exe` *without* the flag produces a visible Windows Terminal window; with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` (Node `windowsHide`) no window appears.
- **With the one-flag change applied** and a desktop package rebuilt, agent shell commands no longer create any console window (watched for newly appearing console windows across repeated commands: zero events).

## Related observation (different layer)

`apps/desktop/src/project-manager.ts` spawns the bundled Node for pnpm without `windowsHide`, so plugin install/update can pop a window the same way. `apps/desktop/src/host-process.ts` also omits it — harmless in practice because that target is GUI-subsystem, but inconsistent with the rest.

discussions.title: [Bug] claimed 的输入在 prepareRequest 抛错时会永久丢失：本机 154 份存档里 14 例
discussions.body:
先钉版本：我本机装的是 `@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.1.5-rc.1，跑起来的内部包是 0.1.5-rc.2（`dsh-agent-loop` / `dsh-api-session-controller` / `dsh-client-ui-chat`），Windows 11，web profile。每条都给两处行号：我本机安装目录里的编译产物（0.1.5-rc.2），和 2026-09-17 的 master 源码。行号会漂，标识名和事件形状为准。

## 一句话

我在一轮里发的消息，会先进 pending inbox，等下一个 step 边界被 claim；而它被写成 durable `user/message` 的那一次 append，排在 `step()` 里 `prepareRequest()` **之后**。于是 `prepareRequest` 一抛错，这条消息就既不在 inbox、也不在日志里 —— 我在自己的 154 份会话存档里量到 14 例，合计 6379 字符，最长一条 5746。

## 事件形状（脱敏，取自那 14 例之一）

```
agent/inbox/spliced  {target:"next-turn", start:0, inserted:[<msg>]}   <- 接受
turn/start           {turn:N}
agent/inbox/spliced  {target:"next-turn", start:0, removedCount:1}      <- claim：只动投影，不写 user/message
turn/end             {reason:{kind:"error", error:{code:"UNKNOWN", ...}}}
（到此为止：这份存档里没有这条消息的 user/message，也没有别的位置收留它。）
```

## 代码位置

1. **窗口本身。** master `packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts`：`:245` 在 pre-step 里 `this.inbox.claim(target, position.turn)`；那条 `user/message` 直到 `:376` 才 `this.session.append('user/message', …)`，中间隔着 `:361` 的 `await this.prepareRequest(turn, step, signal)`。claim 自己只写一条 `agent/inbox/spliced`（master `packages/core/agent-loop/src/inbox.ts:109-113`），不写那条 `user/message`。本机 0.1.5-rc.2 对应 `dsh-agent-loop/lib/index.js:104-107` 与 `:1028`。
2. **`prepareRequest` 会抛什么。** master 的 `prepareRequest` 里有三处：`agent/request` waterfall 抛的、`if (!proposedConfig.provider || !proposedConfig.model)` 那条守卫、以及 `await this.loopCtx.llm.prepareCall(proposedConfig, signal)`。后者在本机是 `dsh-llm-pi-ai/lib/index.js:1824` 的 `prepareCall` → `modelInfo` → `modelOf`，会抛两类**配置类**错误：模型不在目录里时 `UNKNOWN_MODEL`（`:1779`）、profile 记了 `modelErrors`/catalog 失败时 `INVALID_CONFIG`（`:1776`）。顺带一句：同一段代码把 `NO_ADAPTER` 显式吞掉继续走（`catch (error) { if (… code !== 'NO_ADAPTER') throw error; … }`），所以它不是这条路径的入口；`UNKNOWN_MODEL` / `INVALID_CONFIG` 是。
3. **同类：`cancel` 会把整队摘掉。** master `agent.ts:151` / 0.1.5-rc.2 `lib/index.js:799`：`keepInbox` 不为真时 `inbox.clear()`。宿主侧 Stop 带的是 `keepInbox: true`，但 disposal 那条路（0.1.5-rc.2 `lib/index.js:1656` 的 `cancel({ kind: 'disposed' })`）没带。我这边另有 12 例 `outcome:"canceled"` 之后再没出现过的输入。

## 实测

- 面：`$DATA_HOME/sessions/<workspace>/<session>/session*.jsonl.zstd`，我扫了 **154 份**（扫描时点 2026-09-17）。
- 口径：解帧后按 `agent/inbox/spliced` 折叠出 inbox 投影，跟 durable `user/message` 的 id 集合比对（必须先扫全档再折叠，否则那些随后就被正常 append 的条目会被误判）。
- **14 例**被 claim 之后再没出现（2026-09-04/05；字符数 5746 / 521 / 44 / 14 / 14 / 11 / 7 / 7 / 6 / 2 / 2 / 2 / 2 / 1），**12 例** `outcome:"canceled"` 之后再没出现。
- **909 条**消息「先进 inbox 再落盘」的延迟：p50 61 ms、p90 41.8 s、>5 min 55 条、最长 5.6 小时。
- 扫描脚本十几行、只读，需要我贴出来。

## 复现

不需要任何特别的内容或端点，任选一个让 `prepareRequest` 抛错的入口即可：

1. 把某个会话钉到一个 provider 目录里**不存在**的模型 id（或被改成畸形、profile 报 `INVALID_CONFIG` 的条目）；
2. 在这个会话里开一轮、发一条消息；
3. 存档里就是上面的形状：`turn/end` 判 `UNKNOWN_MODEL`（或 `INVALID_CONFIG`），而这条消息的 `user/message` 永远不出现。

说明一句我在自己机器上的诚实边界：那 14 例的现场是同一个 `prepareRequest` 里另一个抛错（我当时一份畸形的模型条目，`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')`），`UNKNOWN_MODEL` 这条入口我是读调用链确认的，没有为它单独构造现场 —— 那要动正在跑的宿主的模型配置。

## 建议（按成本排）

1. **claim 与落盘之间别夹可抛错的调用**：要么先 `append` durable 再消费 inbox，要么在 catch 里把 claimed 的消息放回去。现在这一步失败，我打进去的字就没了，日志里连痕迹都没有。
2. `inbox.clear()` 别静默：cancel/disposal 摘掉了哪些消息，至少留一条记录，产品事后才有机会告诉我「那句话没发出去」。

这些是我给自己做会话体检、解存档数事件的时候量出来的；跟模型、provider 和对话内容都无关。

discussions.title: [Bug] Missing high-resolution Apple Touch Icon causes blurry or distorted icon on iOS
discussions.body:
## Summary

When adding the DeepSeek Harness web application (`apps/web`) or the documentation site (`website`) to an iOS / iPadOS home screen ("Add to Home Screen"), the resulting app icon appears visibly blurry, low-resolution, or distorted.

This occurs because neither `apps/web/index.html` nor `website/.vitepress/config.ts` declares a `<link rel="apple-touch-icon" ...>` tag pointing to a dedicated high-resolution raster icon (e.g. 180x180 PNG). iOS Safari falls back to scaling the SVG favicon or capturing a page thumbnail, which renders with noticeable artifacts or transparent/black backgrounds.

## Reproduction

1. Open DeepSeek Harness Web UI (`apps/web`) or the documentation site on an iPhone/iPad in Safari.
2. Tap the Share button in Safari.
3. Select **"Add to Home Screen"**.
4. Inspect the generated icon on the iOS home screen.

## Current behavior

- The icon displayed on the home screen is pixelated, blurry, or renders with artifacts (e.g. black background due to transparent SVG rendering).
- `apps/web/index.html` and `website/.vitepress/config.ts` only declare `<link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="/favicon.svg">`, with no `apple-touch-icon` defined.
- `apps/web/public/manifest.webmanifest` only contains a single SVG icon entry without standard raster sizes (192x192, 512x512).

## Expected behavior

- A crisp, high-resolution icon (180×180 PNG with an opaque background conforming to Apple HIG) is rendered when added to iOS/iPadOS home screens.
- `<link rel="apple-touch-icon" sizes="180x180" href="/apple-touch-icon.png">` is declared in `<head>` for both `apps/web` and `website`.
- `manifest.webmanifest` provides standard PNG icons (192x192, 512x512) for PWA compliance.

## Environment

- Device: Apple iPhone / iPad
- OS: iOS 17 / iOS 18
- Browser: Safari / WebKit
- Affected components: `apps/web`, `website`

## Suggested Fix

1. Generate high-resolution PNG assets from the brand icon:
   - `apple-touch-icon.png` (180x180 px, solid background)
   - `pwa-192x192.png` and `pwa-512x512.png` for PWA manifest
2. Add `<link rel="apple-touch-icon" sizes="180x180" href="/apple-touch-icon.png">` to:
   - `apps/web/index.html`
   - `website/.vitepress/config.ts` (`head` configuration)
3. Update `apps/web/public/manifest.webmanifest` to include PNG icon entries alongside `favicon.svg`.

discussions.title: 弱网重连后打开会话一直卡在 Loading history（首帧 4~9 MB 全量下发）
discussions.body:
环境：dsh `0.1.6-alpha.1`（npm 安装，web profile），Linux，`dsh web` 监听 127.0.0.1:3080，前面有个自己写的 Python 反代提供局域网 https 入口；客户端是手机浏览器，走 WiFi 连内网。会话都是日常在用的，几百条事件，不算长。

现象：手机信号抖一下、页面断线重连之后，再点进之前那个还在跑任务的会话，就停在「载入历史…」，等多久都一样。刷新无效。等网络稳定重新进去，同一个会话能正常打开。

先怀疑的是反代，毕竟是自己写的。所以用 ws 客户端直连 127.0.0.1:3080 的 `/api/remote.mux`，发一条 `session/follow`（`address.kind=session`、`maxMessages: 50`、`assistantStream: true`），量首帧到底多大：

| 会话 | 事件条数 | 首帧体积 | 服务端准备首帧耗时 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 当前会话 | 373 | 4.25 MB | 56 ms |
| 正在跑任务的会话 | 393 | 5.18 MB | 69 ms |
| 另一个大会话 | 457 | 8.62 MB | 109 ms |

服务端一百毫秒以内就把数据准备好了，慢的是把它发出去。同一批会话直连和走反代各测一次，首帧大小、到达时间基本一致，反代可以排除。单条最大的记录是 `assistant/message`，1.07 MB，里面带着完整的 reasoning 流。

从代码看，`session/follow` 打开时先发一个大快照帧（`packages/api/session-controller` 的 `SessionHistoryController.follow()`，`type: 'snapshot'`），把整个窗口的 records 一次性带走，之后才逐条推增量。`maxMessages: 50` 限的是消息条数，一条 assistant 消息里包含大量流式 chunk，展开后是几百个事件、好几 MB。

断线重连会把这件事放大。客户端拿到新 generation 直接 publish `replace`，等于首帧从头再拉一遍。4 到 9 MB 在 1 Mbps 链路上要 30 到 140 秒，中途再断一次就回到起点。前端这边 `Session.doOpen()` 只有 `open` 和 `error` 两个出口，`error` 只在 `isRemoteFailure(error)` 成立时才设置，所以一直等不到首帧就一直是 `loading`，没有超时也没有提示。

另外观察到一点，重连时所有还开着的会话都会重拉一遍完整快照。我这边同时开着几个，加起来几十 MB 一次性涌过来，弱网下基本没戏。

讨论区里相关的帖：#6950 报的是大会话全量传输（22.5 MB / 4.2 万事件）；#6092 是 mux 心跳误杀健康连接导致重连循环；#6954、#6921 报的同样是停在 Loading history、但根因不同的另外两种。我这边的情况是几百条事件的日常会话就已经 4 MB 以上，比 #6950 出现得更早。

版本我核对过，`0.1.6-alpha.2` 和 master 当前代码跟上面描述一致。

谢谢。

discussions.title: [Bug] 0.1.6-alpha.2 source launch (pnpm dsh) splits @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools across src/lib — every tool call fails with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')"
discussions.body:
## Summary

On **0.1.6-alpha.2**, the documented source launch vector (`pnpm dsh <app>`, i.e. `node --import tsx/esm apps/cli/src/bin.ts`) boots normally, but the first turn that calls a tool ends with:

```
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')
```

recorded as `turn/end` with `reason.kind: "error"` and `code: "UNKNOWN"`. From then on **every** tool call in that process fails — in new sessions and in pre-existing ones alike. The built launch (`node apps/cli/lib/bin.js <app>`) is unaffected.

Unlike #6529 / #6416 (a profile that owns a second *physical* copy of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`) and #4508 (web mode, scope-proxy hypothesis), this reproduces on a **single clean checkout with no version skew and no profile-local install**: the source launch itself loads the package from two planes (`src` and `lib`), and the 0.1.6-alpha.2 resolution-default change made that split reach the tool path.

This is the same double-load phenomenon already documented for another package in #2091 ("Source launch loads workspace packages twice"), now fatal because `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` keys its scheduler by a module-private `Symbol`.

## Environment

- `@deepseek-ai/dsh` **0.1.6-alpha.2**, source checkout of `master` at `ddefc45fbc`
- Windows 11, Node **v24.21.0**, pnpm workspace install, `pnpm install && pnpm run build` completed
- profile `web` (default). Also reproduced with `--profile headless` in an isolated `DSH_HOME`
- Upgrade path that exposed it: checkout moved `0d1f50007f` → `ddefc45fbc` (882 commits). Sessions before the update completed tool calls; the first tool-attempting turn after it failed (a text-only turn in the same process still completes).

## Root cause

`dsh-agent-loop` reads the tool scheduler through a module-private symbol key:

```ts
// packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:170
const prepared = await ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER].prepare(call.exec)
```

```ts
// packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:463
export const TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER: unique symbol = Symbol('@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools.scheduler')
```

Under the source launcher the process ends up with **two module instances** of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`, so two distinct symbols exist. The loop imported one; `ctx.tools` was constructed from the other; the lookup is `undefined` and the property read throws.

Instrumented `module.register` `load`/`resolve` hooks in a single boot (paths relative to the checkout):

```
LOAD tools packages/core/tools/src/index.ts
LOAD tools packages/core/tools/lib/index.js
LOAD loop  packages/core/agent-loop/lib/index.js

RESOLVE @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop -> packages/core/agent-loop/lib/index.js  << from apps/cli/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-base/package.json
RESOLVE @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools      -> packages/core/tools/lib/index.js      << from apps/cli/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions/package.json
RESOLVE file:///<checkout>/packages/core/tools/src/index.ts -> same            << from packages/core/agent-loop/lib/index.js
```

i.e. plugin **entries** are imported from the runtime anchor (`lib/`), while the tsx ESM hook re-projects the bare workspace specifiers made *inside those lib files* to `src/` through tsconfig `paths`. Two planes in one process.

Symbol identity check from the same boot (symbols compared with `===`, not by description):

```json
{"tools": ["packages/core/tools/src/index.ts", "packages/core/tools/lib/index.js"],
 "loop":  ["packages/core/agent-loop/lib/index.js"],
 "loopSymbolFoundInTools": [["packages/core/tools/src/index.ts"]]}
```

which means the outcome depends on **which copy registered the `tools` service** — a load-order race. The same boot with the **built** entry (`node apps/cli/lib/bin.js`) loads exactly one copy (`lib`) and is stable.

## Suspected trigger (regression in the pulled range)

`#4471` / `9ddef327a4` ("feat: resolution mode link to runtime") changed the non-packaged default in `apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts:263`:

```diff
-  const resolutionMode = packaged ? 'runtime' : options.resolutionMode ?? 'link'
+  const resolutionMode = packaged ? 'runtime' : options.resolutionMode ?? 'runtime'
```

Under `link` the loader resolves plugins by bare specifier, so tsx's `paths` projection keeps the whole graph on the `src` plane. Under `runtime` the resolution generation hands out runtime-anchor (`lib`) entries, and the two planes coexist. The **desktop half of the same change was reverted before the release** (`d9a55c7c0d` "fix: revert desktop"), the CLI half shipped in 0.1.6-alpha.2.

## Reproduction (keyless, ~1 minute)

Uses the in-repo mock provider, so no API key is needed:

```sh
# 1. scripted model: one tool call, then a final text response
node --import tsx packages/test-support/llm-mock-server/src/bin.ts \
  --port 8125 --api-key mock-key --sequence tool_call_success,success --repeat-last \
  --tool-name pwsh --tool-arguments '{"command":"echo probe","description":"probe"}'

# 2. real source launch against it
mkdir -p /tmp/dsh-probe && printf 'llm-deepseek:\n  protocol: chat-completions\n' > /tmp/dsh-probe/settings.yaml
DSH_HOME=/tmp/dsh-probe DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 \
DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=mock-key DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8125/v1 \
  node --import tsx/esm apps/cli/src/bin.ts --profile headless "run a probe"
```

Observed: `dsh: UNKNOWN: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')` on the tool-executing turn.

- In an isolated `DSH_HOME` this is intermittent (roughly 1 in 7 fresh boots; presumably the service-registration race).
- On the reporting checkout (profile `web`, users' normal `pnpm dsh web`) it was consistent: a text-only turn completed, the next tool-calling turn failed; a brand-new session failed on its first tool call as well.

## What does *not* work as a workaround

Reverting the default to `'link'` is not viable on 0.1.6-alpha.2 for an existing profile — the boot then fails outright:

```
dsh: startup failed: 1 required plugin did not activate
  agent-loop (required)
    Package: @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop
    failed to import
```

Workaround that does work (verified): launch the built entry, i.e. `pnpm run build` once and then

```sh
node apps/cli/lib/bin.js web      # equivalent of `pnpm dsh web`
```

## Secondary observation from the same default change

Plugins inserted through a profile patch that are **not in the install-anchor closure** now fail to import under `runtime` mode, where they used to resolve through tsx in a source launch:

```
dsh: warning: 2 entries did not activate
computer-use (@deepseek-ai/dsh-computer-use): failed to import
computer-use-cua-driver-native (@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-computer-use-cua-driver-native): failed to import
```

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-computer-use` exists in the tree but is not a dependency of `apps/cli`, so the runtime generation cannot route it. Installing them into the profile via the documented command restores them:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @deepseek-ai/dsh-computer-use
```

## CI gap

Nothing in the current gates covers the source launch's plugin plane:

- `test:snapshot` resolves workspace imports through vite + tsconfig `paths` (single plane);
- `apps/cli/tests/built-bin.e2e.ts` launches the built `lib/` (single plane);
- `apps/cli/tests/source-launch.compat.spec.ts` only asserts the TTY refusal.

A gate that boots the source vector and asserts a single `dsh-tools` module instance (or that executes one tool call) would have caught this.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Keep the source launch on one plane.** In a source launch the runtime generation should not import plugin entry files from `lib` while tsx re-projects their internal workspace specifiers to `src` — either route every workspace specifier through the same plane, or keep the tsconfig `paths` projection from applying to files under `lib/`.
2. **Harden the seam.** `Symbol.for('@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools.scheduler')`, or a string-keyed/`Service`-method scheduler, would make a duplicate instance degrade instead of taking down every tool call in the process (same suggestion as #5758).
3. **Fail loud at the access site.** `tool-calls.ts:170` could name the duplicate-instance cause instead of emitting a bare property-read `TypeError` (#5758).

## Related reports

- #2091 — source launch loads workspace packages twice (`dsh-typert-protocol`, silent `@Remote` split): same root phenomenon, different consumer
- #6529 / #6416 — same `prepare` crash when a profile owns a second physical copy of `dsh-tools`
- #5758 — diagnosability of `prepare()` failures; maintainer comment confirms the symbol-identity mechanism
- #4508 — same symptom in web mode (0.1.1-rc.2), scope-proxy hypothesis, unresolved

---

**中文摘要**：0.1.6-alpha.2 上，用文档里的源码启动方式（`pnpm dsh web`）时，`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` 会从 `src` 和 `lib` 两个平面各加载一份，两个模块私有的 `Symbol('@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools.scheduler')` 不相等，于是 `ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER]` 为 `undefined`，任何工具调用都抛 `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')`。触发点是本版把非打包运行的 `resolutionMode` 默认值从 `link` 改成 `runtime`（#4471；desktop 那一半已在发版前回退）。临时可用办法是用构建产物启动（`node apps/cli/lib/bin.js web`）。

discussions.title: Web UI input box breaks Chinese IME composition (pinyin fragments appear as literal text)
discussions.body:
### Bug description

The chat input box in dsh web is a `<div contenteditable="true">` with class `uV2eY6_input`, not a `<textarea>`. When typing Chinese with an IME (Microsoft Pinyin / Sogou), React re-renders the input during IME composition, which breaks the composition state. Raw pinyin fragments get inserted as literal text instead of being converted to Chinese characters.

Example observed output in the input box:
```
手动shou'dongshou'dshou'S'ho
```

This makes it impossible to type Chinese directly into the dsh web chat box. Typing Chinese in other apps (Doubao, WeChat, Edge address bar) works fine — the bug is specific to dsh web's input component.

### Environment
- OS: Windows 11
- Browser: Microsoft Edge (latest)
- dsh version: 0.1.5-rc.1
- IME: Microsoft Pinyin (also reproduced with Sogou)
- Deploy: `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`, default settings

### Reproduction steps
1. Launch dsh web and open the chat page
2. Focus the input box
3. Type Chinese using pinyin IME (e.g. press `s`, `h`, `o` to type 手)
4. The pinyin letters appear as literal text in the input box instead of showing the IME candidate window

### Expected behavior
The IME candidate window should appear normally and pinyin should convert to Chinese characters on Space/Enter.

### Workaround
- Type Chinese elsewhere and paste with Ctrl+V
- Use Windows voice input (Win+H)

### Suggested fix
- Either replace the contenteditable div with a real `<textarea>` (auto-resize), or
- Ensure no React re-render happens on the input element during `compositionstart` / `compositionend` (preserve the DOM node while IME is active)

### DOM inspection
Confirmed via DevTools:
```
tag: DIV, contenteditable: true, class: uV2eY6_input
```

discussions.title: [Bug] 仅有 reasoning、无 text 与 tool-call 的轮次未被空响应重试兜底
discussions.body:
## 环境

DSH Desktop 2.0.10，Windows 11，上游为固定版本。模型 deepseek-flash，provider deepseek-official。

## 现象

同一会话内连续三轮（turn 54、55、56），assistant 消息只含一段 reasoning，既无 text 也无 tool-call，随后 step 与 turn 均正常结束。用户侧看到的是完全空白的回复，没有任何提示。

## 存档证据（session.v3.jsonl.zstd 事件序列）

- turn 54 step 1：assistant/message parts=[reasoning] len=619，随后 step/end、turn/end
- turn 55 step 1：assistant/message parts=[reasoning] len=2088，随后 step/end、turn/end
- turn 56 step 1：assistant/message parts=[reasoning] len=1199，随后 step/end、turn/end
- 三轮均无 error、无中断标记、无 llm/retry 事件

## 对照

同一会话另有两次真实失败并触发重试，位于 turn 21 step 5 与 turn 23 step 2，finish reason 为 error，failure code 为 TRANSPORT，policyKey 中含 EMPTY_RESPONSE。可见空响应已有重试策略，但上述三轮未被其覆盖。

## 期望

只产 reasoning、不产 text 与 tool-call 的轮次，应视为空响应的一种纳入现有重试策略；或者至少在界面上给出提示，而不是静默结束。

## 影响

用户看不到任何输出，也无从察觉该轮其实产生了推理而未交付；只有翻会话存档才能发现。

discussions.title: [Bug] 未思考直接输出文本时 Chat 出现空的思考块（0.1.6-alpha.2 / deepseek-flash + Messages 协议）
discussions.body:
**TL;DR (English)** — On 0.1.6-alpha.2, when the model answers with text and no thinking, Chat still shows an empty "思考 / Think" block. The Messages protocol emits a `block-start(reasoning)` for a signature-only empty `thinking` block, the harness persists `{"type":"reasoning","text":""}` into the assistant message, and the Chat renderer draws a Think row for every reasoning block.

---

### Summary

模型没有产生思考内容、直接输出正文（且不是工具调用）时，Chat 里会出现一个标题为“思考”但内容为空的思考块；该空块同时被写进会话日志的 assistant 消息内容里。

- 版本：0.1.6-alpha.2（checkout `ddefc45fbc`），Windows
- provider `deepseek-official` / model `deepseek-flash`（Messages 协议，thinking enabled）
- 关联代码：`packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/protocols/messages/translate.ts`、`packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/chat/AssistantMarkdown.tsx`

### Reproduction

1. 用 `deepseek-official` / `deepseek-flash`（Messages 协议）发一条会直接作答、不需要推理的请求，例如“只回复两个字：收到”。
2. Chat 时间线里回答上方多出一个空的“思考”折叠行：收起态只有“思考”标题、没有摘要，展开后正文为空。
3. 会话日志 `session.v3.jsonl` 中该条 `assistant/message` 的 `content` 以空 reasoning 块开头。

复现证据（本机真实会话，节选自 `assistant/message` 的 `stream` 记录）：

```json
{ "type": "chunk", "chunk": { "type": "block-start", "index": 0, "blockType": "reasoning" } },
{ "type": "chunk", "chunk": { "type": "block-end", "index": 0, "block": { "type": "reasoning", "text": "" } } },
{ "type": "chunk", "chunk": { "type": "block-start", "index": 1, "blockType": "text" } },
```

持久化结果：

```json
{ "role": "assistant",
  "content": [ { "type": "reasoning", "text": "" }, { "type": "text", "text": "..." } ],
  "source": { "kind": "model", "provider": "deepseek-official", "model": "deepseek-flash",
              "replayState": { "response": { "kind": "deepseek-messages", "version": 1 },
                               "blocks": [ { "type": "reasoning", "signature": "…" }, { "type": "text" } ] } } }
```

本机已有会话统计：400 条 `assistant/message` 中 52 条带空 reasoning 块，形状均为 `["reasoning","text"]` 或 `["reasoning","tool-call"]`。

### Current behavior

- Messages 协议在 `content_block_start`（`type: "thinking"`）就发出 `block-start(reasoning)`；DeepSeek Messages 在没有思考内容时仍会返回带 `signature` 的空 thinking 块且没有任何 `thinking_delta`，于是 `block-end` 落下 `{ "type": "reasoning", "text": "" }`，被 `BlockAssembler` 组装进 assistant 消息并持久化。
- Chat 的 `AssistantMarkdown` 对每个 `reasoning` 块无条件渲染 `ReasoningRow`，空 reasoning 块因此渲染成空“思考”行（组件快照中 `data-variant="think"`，摘要 `<span class="_summaryText_…">` 为空）。
- 同类判定在仓库里本已把空 reasoning 视为不可见（`assistant.ts` 的 `blockIsVisible`、`turn-process.ts` 的 `visibleChunk`、`llm` 的 `isVisibleChunk`），只有最终渲染循环漏掉了；`chat-completions` 协议也已有“空 reasoning 不建块”的等价保护，`messages` 协议没有。

### Expected behavior

未产生思考内容时不应出现任何思考块：Chat 不渲染空 reasoning 行，assistant 消息也不应因这次“假思考”而多出内容块。

### Fix (verified locally)

`packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/chat/AssistantMarkdown.tsx`：新增 `paintsContent`，与 `assistant.ts` 的可见性判定对齐——`text`/`reasoning` 仅在去除空白后非空时算可见；渲染循环跳过空白 reasoning 块，`hasVisible` 也改用它，避免只剩空块时画出空壳。

新增测试 `packages/client/ui-chat/tests/coverage-tails.client.spec.tsx`：空 reasoning 不渲染 Think 行、流式下等首个思考 token 到达才出现 Think 行、仅空 reasoning 时不渲染根壳。移除修复后这 3 条测试全部失败（已本地验证）。

本地验证：`test:gui` 433 个测试文件 / 6183 用例通过，`run-oxlint` 无告警，`pnpm run build` 成功，运行中的 `dsh web` 实时 graph 已在提供含修复的 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-chat` bundle。

可选的上游修复（更彻底，未采用）：让 `messages/translate.ts` 推迟发出 `thinking` 块的 `block-start`，使空 thinking 块根本不进入持久化内容；需同时保持 `replayState.blocks` 与 `message.content` 的下标对齐。

discussions.title: Skill descriptions silently truncate in the model-facing catalog
discussions.body:
Two repository skill descriptions exceed the catalog limit that `dsh-tool-skill` renders with, so the model receives them truncated. The interesting part is *what* gets cut.

**Reproduce on current master:**

```sh
npx tsx -e "console.log(require('node:fs').readFileSync('.agents/skills/record-browser-gif/SKILL.md','utf8').match(/^description: (.*)$/m)[1].length)"   # 569
npx tsx -e "console.log(require('node:fs').readFileSync('.agents/skills/dsh-doc/SKILL.md','utf8').match(/^description: (.*)$/m)[1].length)"             # 518
```

`DEFAULT_CATALOG_DESCRIPTION_MAX_LENGTH` is 500, and `catalogDescription()` hard-truncates with an ellipsis. So:

- `record-browser-gif` loses `which MUST include a GIF recorded from the pull request's real server and model flow` — the hard requirement the skill exists to enforce.
- `dsh-doc` loses the end of its `Use for` list.

Truncation happens at render time against an intact source file, so every existing gate passes and review cannot see it. The tail is also where a description conventionally states when the skill applies, which is the only signal the model uses to pick a skill.

## Proposal

Rewrite the twelve descriptions so each states its trigger and carries no implementation detail (tool names, flag names, encoding steps belong in the skill body), then gate the property:

- per-description length at or under 450 — the 500 render limit less headroom, so ordinary rewording cannot silently cross it
- a trigger clause (`Use when` / `Use before` / `Use for` / `Use to`) or a boundary clause (`Do not use`) instead
- boundary language whenever a description names another repository skill, so a cross-reference disambiguates rather than duplicating
- an aggregate catalog budget, since `catalogDescriptionMaxLength` bounds one description and nothing bounds their sum

Result: longest 569 -> 412, total 4460 -> 3925 against a 4500 budget.

Branch (based on `ddefc45f`, the current master): https://github.com/ManfredCh/deepseek-harness/tree/pr/skill-description-catalog-budget

## Testing

- `pnpm run test:docs` — 21 passed, 0 failed, with `skill-descriptions` registered as a `doc-quick` leaf
- `pnpm run lint` — 0 warnings, 0 errors
- new `scripts/verify-skill-descriptions.spec.ts` — 14 passed, covering the rejection paths (over-limit, whitespace-padded overrun, missing trigger, boundary-less cross-reference, pairwise-overlap, aggregate budget) and the real-repository regression

## One thing worth deciding

The gate bounds the total at the source, but the renderer itself has no aggregate bound. OpenAI's published behavior for the same catalog is a budget of 2% of the context window (8000 characters when unknown), degrading by shortening all descriptions first and then announcing omitted entries. Reaching that shape needs renderer changes in `dsh-tool-skill`, and a decision about what the model should be told when a skill is withheld. I did not attempt it here — the source-side gate is the small, reviewable half. Happy to hear whether you would rather solve it in the renderer.

discussions.title: 0.1.6-alpha.2 regression: a source checkout now loads harness packages from both src/ and lib/, crashing the first tool call and leaving the session unresumable
discussions.body:
**Environment**

- dsh 0.1.6-alpha.2, commit `ddefc45fbc`, master, clean working tree, after `git pull` from `0d1f50007f`
- Launch: `pnpm dsh web` from the source checkout (`node --import tsx/esm apps/cli/src/bin.ts`), Node v26.7.0, Linux x86_64
- Profile: `web` (bundles `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app`), default DeepSeek Messages protocol
- No third-party plugin declares `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` in `dependencies` or `peerDependencies`, and there is no second physical copy of the package: every `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` position in the checkout resolves through symlinks to `packages/core/tools`, the only `@deepseek-ai` directory under the DSH home is the flat fallback whose entries are also symlinks into the checkout, and the profile's `.pnpm` directory holds no packages

**Summary**

After this update, the first tool call of the first turn after launch dies with

```
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')
```

at `ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER].prepare(call.exec)` in `dsh-agent-loop`. The turn ends with `code: UNKNOWN` after the assistant message and its `tool/call` events are already durably recorded, and because no `tool/result` follows, every later turn in that session fails with `DeepSeek Messages tool calls need immediate results` (locally thrown, no request is ever sent). The session is permanently unresumable, exactly as reported in #1337.

Unlike #1337, #2078 and #2130, this needs **no community plugin and no duplicate package on disk**. The two module instances are created by the launcher itself, from the same package directory.

**Reproduction**

1. Clean source checkout at `ddefc45fbc`, `pnpm install`, `pnpm run build`.
2. `pnpm dsh web`.
3. Send any message that makes the model call a tool.
4. The first tool call of that turn fails as above; the session is then unresumable.
5. Registering the symbol globally (see below) makes the same tree work; on the first call of the previous turn the identical tool calls completed normally. I did not test whether forcing `link` mode also fixes it.

**Current behavior**

- `turn/end` error `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')` (`code: UNKNOWN`) on the first tool dispatch.
- The assistant message with two `tool-call` blocks is committed, one `tool/call` event is written for the first call, and no results are written for either.
- Every subsequent turn in that session: `DeepSeek Messages tool calls need immediate results`, `code: INVALID_REQUEST`, thrown during serialization before any HTTP request.

**Why the update changed this**

`TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER` is a module-local `Symbol` (`packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:463`) and the scheduler is a per-instance class field, so `undefined` at that lookup means the `tools` service instance and the importing `dsh-agent-loop` came from two different copies of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`.

Commit `9ddef327a4` ("feat: resolution mode link to runtime") changed the launcher default in `apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts:263`:

```diff
-const resolutionMode = packaged ? 'runtime' : options.resolutionMode ?? 'link'
+const resolutionMode = packaged ? 'runtime' : options.resolutionMode ?? 'runtime'
```

Measured on the same checkout, with no plugins loaded:

| Importer | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` resolves to |
| --- | --- |
| Any file under tsx (`import.meta.resolve`, from both `.ts` and `.mjs`) | `packages/core/tools/src/index.ts` |
| The `runtime` generation's entries for `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`, `dsh-agent-loop`, `@deepseek-ai/cordis` | `packages/core/tools/lib/index.js`, `packages/core/agent-loop/lib/index.js`, `vendor/cordis/lib/index.js` |

So the source plane (tsx + tsconfig `paths`) and the artifact plane (the installed generation) are both live in one process. `link` mode left resolution alone, which is why this worked before the update.

Both halves of that table are reproducible in seconds on a clean checkout, with no model request:

```bash
# source plane: what every tsx-loaded file sees
node --import tsx/esm -e "console.log(import.meta.resolve('@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools'))"
# -> file:///…/packages/core/tools/src/index.ts
```

```js
// artifact plane: what the generation routes profile rows to.
// Save as probe.mts in the checkout root, then: node --import tsx/esm probe.mts
import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { createProfileResolutionGeneration, loadProfileDirectory } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot'

const anchor = new URL('./apps/cli/package.json', import.meta.url).pathname
const home = process.env.DSH_HOME ?? `${process.env.HOME}/.dsh`
const profile = loadProfileDirectory('dsh', `${home}/profiles/web`, anchor, { userLayer: true })
const generation = await createProfileResolutionGeneration({ installAnchor: anchor, profile })
for (const entry of generation.entries) {
  if (entry.name !== '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools') continue
  console.log(entry.name, createRequire(entry.declarer).resolve(entry.name))
}
// -> @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools /…/packages/core/tools/lib/index.js
```

I confirmed the packages themselves are single copies on disk; the duplicate is the *module instance*, not a directory. That is why none of the plugin-side remedies in #2130 apply here.

**Expected behavior**

A source launch should keep one module plane — or the scheduler lookup should survive the split — and a turn that dies mid-dispatch should leave a resumable session.

**Two secondary notes**

- There is no escape hatch: `parseDshArgs` has no resolution-mode flag, `runCli` calls `runProfile` without `resolutionMode`, and nothing reads an environment variable for it. A source-checkout user cannot select `link` without editing source. It also means `pnpm run build` is now mandatory after every pull, because the packaged rows read `lib/`.
- The crash is unrecoverable by construction. `agent-loop` documents "Scheduler failure drains dispatches without committing synthetic recovery results", so a dispatch failure writes no results where cancellation writes `ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH` pairs. Any dispatch failure therefore poisons the session permanently. A synthetic result pair (or any recovery path) for failed dispatch would turn this class of bug into a single failed turn.

**Local unblocker (not a proposal)**

Registering the symbol globally makes the lookup survive the split:

```diff
-export const TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER: unique symbol = Symbol('@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools.scheduler')
+export const TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER: unique symbol = Symbol.for('@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools.scheduler')
```

I run that plus `pnpm run build`, applied and reverted automatically around `git pull`, purely as a local unblocker. I have read #2130's trade-off argument and agree it is a stopgap rather than the fix; I am reporting the new trigger, not proposing this as the direction. Which direction is yours to choose — keeping source launches on a single plane, or making the collision fail loud and name both copies. DSH recommended I post this and drafted the preceding text. I hope this saves someone some time!

discussions.title: [Bug] Source launch (pnpm dsh) on 0.1.6-alpha.2: every tool call fails with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')"
discussions.body:
### Summary

On `dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2` (`ddefc45fbc`, current master tip), a **source launch through `tsx`** — the vector the repo's own `dsh` script uses — fails on **every tool call**:

```
dsh: UNKNOWN: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')
```

The built launch (`node apps/cli/lib/bin.js`) is unaffected at the same commit. The two module instances are created by the launcher itself from a **single package directory**: no duplicate package on disk, no community plugin involved.

This trigger is new in 0.1.6-alpha.2, but the symptom is not — it is the same `reading 'prepare'` crash that has been reported since August under two *other* triggers. I have tried to collect everything into this one post, including material from the other threads, so the next person starts from one place instead of five.

**Most of the depth below is not mine.** Credit to #6967 (LLKernel) and the macOS probe in its comments (DreamStan), #6974 (TRAVI5TY), and the August threads by leether (#2078, #2130) and zoahdev.

Flagging a few people who may have context, since the failure mode makes this hard to diagnose from the error alone:

- @imccyu — this bisects to `9ddef327a4` ("feat: resolution mode link to runtime"), which is yours; you also committed the `release(dsh): 0.1.6-alpha.2` commit.
- @CreatixChu — you authored the `dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2` release commit (PR #4469), the version this regressed in.
- @tianyicui — `7c9bb5914c` ("refactor(ptc): align runtime packages and services with PTC naming") shaped the scheduler and service contract that now throws, so you may have a view on the intended direction.

No blame intended — the split is subtle and the error message points at the wrong thing entirely. What I'd most like to know is which fix direction you'd prefer.

### If you are hitting this right now

- **Source checkout?** Edit `apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts:263` to `?? 'link'` (§ Workarounds). Takes effect immediately under `tsx`; no rebuild.
- **Can you use the built launcher?** `node apps/cli/lib/bin.js web` is unaffected.
- **Is your session already broken?** Patching the resolution will **not** revive it. A session that died this way cannot be resumed — see § Consequence. Repair the log first.
- **Non-source install (npm/pnpm global, desktop)?** This particular trigger is specific to `tsx` source launches. If you see the same message there, you are probably in the *other* trigger family — a second physical copy of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`.

### Environment matrix

The same crash at the same commit, reported on three platforms by three people:

| report | OS / arch | Node | pnpm | launch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| this post | Windows 11 x64 | v22.22.3 | 11.7.0 | `tsx` source + built |
| #6967 comment (DreamStan) | macOS arm64 | v25.2.1 | 11.7.0 | `tsx` source |
| #6974 (TRAVI5TY) | Linux x86_64 | v26.7.0 | — | `tsx` source |

Not platform-specific.

### Reproduction, and the A/B that isolates it

Verified here on a **pristine checkout** at `ddefc45fbc` — zero local modifications, `git status --porcelain` empty. Same tree, same command each time; the only variable is `apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts:263`:

```diff
-  const resolutionMode = packaged ? 'runtime' : options.resolutionMode ?? 'runtime'
+  const resolutionMode = packaged ? 'runtime' : options.resolutionMode ?? 'link'
```

```sh
node --import tsx/esm apps/cli/src/bin.ts --profile headless \
  "Read package.json and reply with only the value of its name field. Do nothing else."
```

That task needs exactly one `read` call. (If the `headless` profile does not exist yet, initialize it from the shipped template with `--from-default-profile headless`.)

| launch | `resolutionMode` | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| source via `tsx` | `runtime` (new default) | exit 1 — `dsh: UNKNOWN: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')` |
| source via `tsx` | `link` (previous default) | exit 0 — tool ran, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-root` printed |
| `node apps/cli/lib/bin.js` (same task) | `runtime` | exit 0 — unaffected |

So `runtime` is not broken in itself — it is fine whenever the whole graph comes from `lib/`. It is the `tsx` + `runtime` pairing that splits the package, and it splits it deterministically.

On the boundary: every session log on my install back to 2026-09-13 had zero occurrences of this message; after the `0d1f50007f → ddefc45fbc` move, 8 of 8 attempted tool calls failed — across both `read` and `pwsh`, including a brand-new session dying on its **very first** tool call at turn 1, step 1. Not tool-specific, not tied to pre-existing session state.

### The raw evidence

A crashed turn, straight out of `session.v3.jsonl.zstd` (ids trimmed):

```
tool/call   seq 2098  turn 15 step 1  name=read  args={"file_path":"…\\DSH…md"}
step/end    seq 2099  turn 15 step 1
turn/end    seq 2100  reason={"kind":"error",
                        "error":{"message":"Cannot read properties of undefined
                                          (reading 'prepare')","code":"UNKNOWN"}}
```

Two details are worth reading off this:

- The `tool/call` is **durably recorded before** the throw, and `step/end` closes the step anyway. The events line up exactly with `tool-calls.ts`: `appendToolCall` (line 168) runs, then `.prepare()` (line 170) throws. The `turn/end` records the failure and nothing else.
- No `tool/result` follows — which is what poisons the session (§ Consequence).

(If you are reading logs yourself: these files are **concatenated zstd frames**, and `zlib.zstdDecompressSync` silently returns only the *first* frame — 254 bytes out of 1.35 MB in my case. Decode with `scanZstdFrames` from `packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/src/zstd.ts`, or every crash looks like it never happened.)

### The two probes — seconds, no model request

Both from #6974, and both worth running before anything else. They show the two planes independently:

```sh
# source plane: what every tsx-loaded file sees
node --import tsx/esm -e "console.log(import.meta.resolve('@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools'))"
# -> file:///…/packages/core/tools/src/index.ts
```

```ts
// artifact plane: what the profile generation routes plugin rows to.
// Save as probe.mts in the checkout root, then: node --import tsx/esm probe.mts
import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { createProfileResolutionGeneration, loadProfileDirectory } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot'

const anchor = new URL('./apps/cli/package.json', import.meta.url).pathname
const home = process.env.DSH_HOME ?? `${process.env.HOME}/.dsh`
const profile = loadProfileDirectory('dsh', `${home}/profiles/web`, anchor, { userLayer: true })
const generation = await createProfileResolutionGeneration({ installAnchor: anchor, profile })
for (const entry of generation.entries) {
  if (entry.name !== '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools') continue
  console.log(entry.name, createRequire(entry.declarer).resolve(entry.name))
}
// -> @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools /…/packages/core/tools/lib/index.js
```

Two planes, one process. This is also a ready-made smoke test — see § Questions.

### Where it throws, and why the message misleads

`packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:170`:

```ts
const prepared = await ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER].prepare(call.exec)
```

`ctx.tools` resolves, but `ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER]` is `undefined`. That key is a module-private symbol, not a string:

`packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:463`

```ts
/** Scheduler entry point omitted from the generated named service API. @internal */
export const TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER: unique symbol = Symbol('@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools.scheduler')
```

`Symbol()` is not `Symbol.for()`, so it is only equal across a process while the package is loaded exactly once. Two instances produce two symbols, the lookup is silently `undefined`, and the property read is what throws.

**The message is why this family has been re-diagnosed five times.** Nothing checks that the scheduler exists, so what surfaces is `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')` — naming a method on a value that was never there, and pointing at `agent-loop` when the fault is in module identity. Every reporter so far has had to rediscover that the real question is "how many copies of `dsh-tools` are alive in this process". #2130's "Diagnosis" row calls this the third unclosed feedback loop, and I think that is exactly right.

For reference, the build output does contain two independent definitions of the symbol:

- `packages/core/tools/lib/index.js:2526` — `const TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER = Symbol("@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools.scheduler");`
- `packages/core/tools/lib/types/index.js:51` — `export const TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER = Symbol('@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools.scheduler');`
- `packages/core/tools/lib/types/ptc.js:13` imports it from `./index.js`, so that subtree is internally consistent

### The change that introduced it

`9ddef327a4` "feat: resolution mode link to runtime" flipped the non-packaged default in `apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts` and `apps/desktop-host/src/index.ts`:

```diff
-  const resolutionMode = packaged ? 'runtime' : options.resolutionMode ?? 'link'
+  const resolutionMode = packaged ? 'runtime' : options.resolutionMode ?? 'runtime'
```

`link` materialised junctions on disk and left resolution to `tsx`; `runtime` installs an in-process resolver (it reaches Node's internal ESM/CJS loader through `node-addon-require-builtin`; see `packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile-resolution/resolver.ts`) and mounts the plugin tree from `lib/`. Both planes are then live in one process, and `tsx` keeps re-projecting workspace imports to `src`.

The tool-call code itself did not change. Between `dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1` (where tool calls worked) and `dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2`, the only changes inside `packages/core/agent-loop/src` and `packages/core/tools/src` are `inbox.ts` (−5/+2, inbox projection registration dedup) and `agent-loop/src/index.ts` (+2). `tool-calls.ts` and `tools/src/index.ts` are byte-identical between the two tags. This is a module-identity regression, not a logic one.

Nor is the phenomenon new in kind: **#2091 already documented source launches loading workspace packages twice**, splitting a different registry. What is new is that it now reaches a `Symbol()`-keyed contract, which turns a previously silent split into a fatal one.

### Independent confirmations of the split

- **LLKernel captured it directly** (#6967), with `module.register` load hooks in a single boot:

  ```
  LOAD tools packages/core/tools/src/index.ts
  LOAD tools packages/core/tools/lib/index.js
  LOAD loop  packages/core/agent-loop/lib/index.js
  ```

- **DreamStan confirmed the symbol identity in-process on macOS** (#6967 comment): `ctx.tools[<lib-plane symbol>]` is defined, `ctx.tools[<src-plane symbol>]` is not, and `srcSymbol === libSymbol` is `false`. No model involved, so it cannot be a provider-protocol artifact. Their resolution matrix shows `tsx` projecting the bare specifier to `src` from *every* parent, while the runtime generation mounts from `lib` — the split is in the process, not in any one importer.

- **TRAVI5TY measured both planes on Linux** (#6974): both probes above, plus the conclusion that the packages are single copies on disk — the duplicate is the **module instance**, not a directory. That is why none of the plugin-side remedies in #2130 apply to this trigger.

Three platforms, same commit, same one-line cause.

### The report family — same symptom, three different triggers

Worth separating, because the remedies differ:

| # | date | trigger |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [#1337](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1337) | 08-14 | community plugin resolves a **second physical copy** |
| [#2078](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/2078) | 08-15 | same; one-line fix proposal |
| [#2091](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/2091) | 08-15 | source launch loads workspace packages twice (different registry) |
| [#2130](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/2130) | 08-15 | pitfall map for the copy family |
| [#4508](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/4508) | 08-25 | web mode, mechanism unconfirmed |
| [#6416](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/6416), [#6529](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/6529) | 09-12/13 | **profile-local** copy (any `pnpm install` in the profile, e.g. via the plugin-manager UI) |
| [#6967](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/6967), [#6974](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/6974), this post | 09-17 | **source launch splits the package across `src/` and `lib/`** — new |
| [#6971](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/6971) | 09-17 | the same thing seen from the user side |

The existing remedies for the plugin/profile-copy family (#2130's guidance) do not apply here — this trigger has no duplicate on disk and no third-party plugin involved.

### Consequence: the session is left unresumable

This deserves its own heading, because it is easy to miss and it is what confuses users most.

When the dispatch fails, the assistant message and its `tool/call` events are **already durably recorded**, and no results are ever written. Every later turn replays that history, and the provider protocol rejects it during serialization — before any HTTP request:

```
DeepSeek Messages tool calls need immediate results      (INVALID_REQUEST)
```

`packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/protocols/messages/serialize.ts:117`

So the damage is two-stage: one failed turn, then a session that can never continue. #6971 is exactly this seen from the UI — a new session reports `reading 'prepare'`, an old session reports `tool calls need immediate results`, which reads like "even downgrading doesn't help".

As TRAVI5TY points out (#6974), this is **by construction** rather than bad luck: agent-loop drains dispatches on a scheduler failure *without* committing synthetic recovery results, whereas cancellation writes `ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH` pairs. Any dispatch failure therefore poisons the session, not just this one. A synthetic result pair for a failed dispatch would reduce this entire class to a single failed turn — separately worth doing, whatever happens to the resolution question.

LLKernel also worked out a repair for already-damaged logs (#6967 comment): truncate each log after the last `tool/call` of the damaged step, so the built-in crash repair closes that turn on the next resume. Verified against the real serializer there: the original log is rejected with `history ends with unresolved tools`, the repaired log serializes clean with every tool call paired to a result; only the failed turn's own artifacts are lost.

### There is no escape hatch

Also from #6974, and worth knowing before you go looking: `parseDshArgs` has no resolution-mode flag, `runCli` calls `runProfile` without `resolutionMode`, and nothing reads an environment variable for it. A source-checkout user **cannot select `link` without editing source**. It also makes `pnpm run build` mandatory after every pull, because the packaged rows read `lib/`.

### Workarounds

1. **One line, source launches only** — verified above:
   ```diff
   -  const resolutionMode = packaged ? 'runtime' : options.resolutionMode ?? 'runtime'
   +  const resolutionMode = packaged ? 'runtime' : options.resolutionMode ?? 'link'
   ```
   Under `tsx` this takes effect immediately; no rebuild needed.

2. **Run the built launcher**: `node apps/cli/lib/bin.js web`. Works on Windows and macOS (confirmed in #6967's comments), including with third-party bundles — at the cost of rebuilding after every source change.

3. **A branch already exists**: Honghe linked `fix/resolution-mode-link-default` on #6971, which is the same direction.

4. **Make the symbol global** — `Symbol.for()` instead of `Symbol()` (#2078, branch `leether/deepseek-harness → fix/tool-runtime-scheduler-symbol`). See the trade-offs below; both the original proposer and zoahdev now treat it as a local unblocker.

5. **Damaged sessions need separate repair** — patching the resolution does not revive them.

### Prior proposals, and why they were not adopted

This part matters for anyone thinking about the fix, because the obvious one-liner has already been round-tripped once.

**#2078 — `Symbol.for()`.** The standard dual-package-hazard remedy: the key becomes identical across all module instances while staying a `Symbol`, preserving the `@internal` intent. Verified there against duplicate copies on 0.1.0-rc.6.

**The gap zoahdev raised in #2078's comments — version skew.** `Symbol.for` makes the *key* identical but not the *value's protocol*. If two copies come from different trains (say the host's and an older one hoisted from a plugin), the global key means one copy now reads the other copy's scheduler. If their protocol shapes differ, that is a silent cross-wire — which "works" until it doesn't, and is harder to attribute than the original `undefined`. Their branch adds a `TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER_PROTOCOL_VERSION` guard on top.

**#2130 — the proposer's own revised position.** Symbol.for is a defensive stopgap with side effects, not the fix, because it: makes the key semi-public (breaking `@internal`), freezes the key string forever, silently cross-wires across versions, and removes the only signal we have (a loud `undefined` becomes a silent success or a silent cross-wire). "In a single-instance world preserved by relink + a check, `Symbol()` is strictly better."

That thread also frames the whole family as two reasonable defaults colliding — a private-identity `Symbol()` on one side, npm's "import X → dependencies" default on the other — with three feedback loops never closed: **documentation** (`publish.md` never says host packages must be `peerDependencies`), an **install-time check** (`dsh plugin` is a bare pnpm forwarder that silently accepts a plain `@deepseek-ai/*` dependency), and **diagnosis** (the crash reports `undefined`, not "two physical copies, one from the host and one from plugin X"). It maps five ways a duplicate appears with rough frequency shares — note those are *estimates from discussion frequency, not measurements*.

I find that framing convincing, and it applies to this trigger too: the source-launch split is a sixth path, and none of the three loops would have caught it either.

### Two constraints on the fix space

Both come from the other threads, and are worth not rediscovering:

- **"Route everything to `lib/`" does not work.** DreamStan tried `TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH` pointed at a paths-less tsconfig; the plugin tree and the launcher graph then do agree on `lib`, but the source launch dies at import time with `SyntaxError: The requested module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' does not provide an export named 'FiberState'`. `FiberState` is a `const enum` (`vendor/cordis/src/fiber.ts:147`) that `tsc` inlines, so `vendor/cordis/lib/index.js` carries no runtime enum object. A source launch must therefore keep the `src` plane for the launcher's own graph — which rules out "everything to lib" and supports the "source → link, built → runtime" direction.
- **Globalising the symbol** is the other axis, with the trade-offs above.

### Questions

1. Is the `tsx` source-launch path covered by CI? If not, that would explain how this reached a release tag while the built path stayed green. Both probes in § The two probes reproduce it in seconds with no model request, so a smoke test looks inexpensive.
2. Which direction do you want — keep source launches on a single module plane, or make the collision fail loud and name both copies, rather than throwing at `.prepare`?
3. Separate from the resolution question: should a dispatch failure write synthetic results, so that it cannot poison a session at all?

discussions.title: [Bug] Chat: "Load earlier" can succeed without adding any rows
discussions.body:
### What happens

Clicking **Load earlier** in Chat can return a successful page while no new rows appear on screen. Clicking it repeatedly looks like the button is simply broken. A browser refresh that replays the same history window can expose the same symptom.

### Where

`packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/conversation-nodes/message.ts`

### Cause

The `input-message` Context id is derived from the producer id:

```ts
? { id: String(event.data.id), role: 'start' }
```

When two append-surface `user/message` events carry the same producer `data.id`, both match a single `input-message` Context as two separate starts. That violates the assembler's unique-start invariant, so the later occurrence is folded away and produces no visible row. Neither symptom requires missing persisted events or a server restart.

### Observed evidence

With a long transcript, paging twice produced:

| step | anchor elements | Chat text (characters) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| initial | 193 | 10,613 |
| after 1 page | 401 | 32,767 |
| after 2 pages | 597 | 41,633 |

### Suggested fix

Use the event's own position for row identity, and keep the producer id for the things that genuinely need it:

```ts
? { id: String(event.seq), role: 'start' }
```

`data.id` is still required for Inbox correlation and steering classification, so it should stay in the payload — only the Context/row identity needs to change.

### Why this cannot be a plugin

The `conversation.chat.node` slots render nodes, but they do not let a plugin change how node identity is computed, and there is no public seam for registering or overriding a `ConversationNodeDefinition`. So this appears to need a change inside `ui-chat`.

### Process note

Issues are disabled on this repo and `CONTRIBUTING.md` states external pull requests are not accepted, so I am posting here as instructed. Sorry if this is the wrong category — happy to move it.

discussions.title: [Bug] Android/Termux：0.1.6-alpha.2 完全无法启动 —— host preparation 依赖 node-addon-require-builtin，而它没有 android-arm64 绑定
discussions.body:
### 环境

- Android / Termux，`aarch64`，两台设备（Android 14 与 Android 16 构建），Node **v26.4.0**（ABI `v147`）
- DSH **`dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2`**（commit `ddefc45fbc`），源码 checkout，profile `web`
- 启动方式：仓库自带的源码启动形态 —— `node --import tsx/esm apps/cli/src/bin.ts web`
- 该 checkout 已包含社区为更早的 addon 问题（#1588、#6148、#6767）打的 Termux 补丁。这里与它们无关：失败发生在**任何插件挂载之前**。

### 现象

在 Android/Termux 上，0.1.6-alpha.2 **完全无法启动**，`boot()` 在 host preparation 阶段就中止：

```
Error: dsh: host preparation failed: No usable native binding found for node-addon-require-builtin-android-arm64 (auto)
    at boot (packages/boot/app-boot/src/index.ts:979:11)
    at async runProfile (apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts:306:17)
  [cause]: Error: No usable native binding found for node-addon-require-builtin-android-arm64 (auto)
      at noUsableBindingError (node-addon-native-custom-loader/lib/index.js:478:19)
      at loadEntry (node-addon-native-custom-loader/lib/index.js:541:11)
      at createEntryApi (node-addon-native-custom-loader/lib/index.js:554:20)
      at Object.<anonymous> (node-addon-require-builtin/lib/index.js:11:13)
```

原生加载尝试（摘自抛出的诊断信息）：

```
attempts: [
  { source: 'optional-package', request: 'node-addon-require-builtin-android-arm64',
    error: Cannot find module 'node-addon-require-builtin-android-arm64' },
  { source: 'local-build', backend: 'nodeabi',
    path: '.../node-addon-require-builtin/build/nodeabi/node-v147-android-arm64/require_builtin.node' },
  { source: 'local-build', backend: 'napi',
    path: '.../node-addon-require-builtin/build/napi/napi-v9-android-arm64/require_builtin.node' },
]
```

这不是"功能降级"：**没有任何启动方式能走到插件树**，profile 起不来，会话也开不了。

### 根因

1. 这个依赖本身是 0.1.6-alpha.2 新引入的：commit `6aa2e4633c` *"feat(boot): add profile resolution modes"*（2026-09-13）让 host preparation 通过 `packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile-resolution/resolver.ts` 依赖原生 addon `node-addon-require-builtin`。因此失败与 `resolutionMode` 无关 —— 它在 resolver 加载时发生，早于模式生效。
2. `node-addon-require-builtin@0.1.6` 只发布了桌面平台的预编译包：

   ```
   darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-arm64-gnu, linux-x64-gnu,
   win32-arm64-msvc, win32-x64-msvc, win32-ia32-msvc
   ```

   **没有 android 目标**。Termux 是 `linux-android`（bionic），`linux-arm64-gnu` 预编译包同样加载不了。
3. 官方退路（上面两条 `local-build` 路径）在用户侧无法产出：发布 tarball 只含 `lib/` 与 `README.md`（没有原生源码或构建配置），且 workspace 明确禁止其构建脚本（`pnpm-workspace.yaml` → `allowBuilds: node-addon-require-builtin: false`）。
4. 影响范围：在更早的 `flock` / `link(2)` 问题时期，安卓靠社区补丁仍可用（#1588）；自 0.1.6-alpha.2 起变成硬性启动失败，而这个原生 addon 现在位于**所有**启动方式的关键路径上。

### 诉求

1. **补 `android-arm64` 预编译包**（`node-addon-require-builtin` 以及 `node-addon-*` 家族其余成员），或明确声明 Android/Termux 不受支持，免得大家继续在这上面耗时间。
2. **让绑定改成懒加载**：缺少平台绑定时应当降级（例如运行时包解析不可用、回退到 `link`），而不是让 host preparation 在任何启动方式下直接中止 —— 现在一个可选原生依赖就能让整个应用在它没有发布的平台上起不来。
3. 如果"本地构建"就是设计中的退路，**请随包发布可构建的源码/构建配置并给出文档**（Termux 侧 `clang`、`cmake` 都可用：`pkg install clang cmake make python`），同时放开 `allowBuilds`。目前 `allowBuilds` 是禁止的，这条退路永远不可能成功。

### 关联

- #6974、#6975 —— 0.1.6-alpha.2 源码启动的回归（同一发布窗口；触发点不同，但同样表现为首次工具调用即崩）
- #6148、#6767 —— `flock is not supported on android-arm64`（更早的 addon，同一类"无 Android 支持"问题）
- #1588 —— "dsh runs on Termux (Android) — with 5 small patches"

如果需要，我可以在两台 Termux 设备（aarch64，Node v26.4.0）上验证候选预编译包或补丁，并回报结果。

Human approvals that arrive after a restart: what a deployment cannot do today
discussions.body:
## What we are building

We run DeepSeek Harness server-side: one long-lived runtime process per tenant, many human users behind it. The agent does business work, and that work regularly needs a decision from a person who is **not** the person in the thread: a budget owner, a data owner, a manager. Those decisions come back in hours or days, and the process restarts on every deploy in between.

This is not the sandbox-escalation case. That one is correctly synchronous and should stay that way. This is about a business decision whose answer is slow by nature.

Everything below was checked against `0.1.5-rc.2` (`latest`).

## What we need

Two properties. The first is the one we are actually asking about.

**P1. A resumed transcript should tell the truth about a gated action.**

A tool call that was waiting for a human decision did not perform its action. If a resumed session cannot distinguish "was gated, never ran" from "ran, outcome not recorded", then a model reading its own history cannot tell whether a payment was sent or an email went out. That ambiguity is the opposite of what the gate exists to produce.

**P1 alone unblocks us.** With a truthful transcript we can deliver the late decision ourselves: resume the session, state that the decision arrived, and let the agent proceed.

**P2. A deployment should be able to deliver a decision after the asking process is gone.**

Ideally without the agent having to re-derive the step. We are **not** requesting this one. We can see that it implies continuing an interrupted turn, and that is explicitly out of scope today (quoted below). We mention it only so the shape of the need is visible.

## What we found

Both human-interaction seams are bounded by the turn, and the turn is bounded by the process.

`ctx.userQuestions` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-user-questions` 0.1.5-rc.2) exposes `ask(request): Promise<AskUserQuestionAnswer>`, described as the service used "when it needs to pause work and ask the human for a decision".

`ask_user_question` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ask-user` 0.1.5-rc.2), Known Limitations:

> **A pending question blocks the tool call until the human answers** — the tool declares no `timeout-policy` budget; cancellation rides the turn's `exec.signal` only.

`approval/request` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-user-approval` 0.1.5-rc.2) is a waterfall returning `Promise<ApprovalOutcome>`, Known Limitations:

> **Requests are valid only inside an open turn** — an idle or between-turn caller throws before auditing; a durable out-of-turn approval workflow is deferred.

While a request is pending, this is what exists and where:

| Piece | Where it lives | Survives a restart |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `approval/asked` | session log | yes |
| the unresolved `Promise<ApprovalOutcome>` | process memory | no |
| the `AbortSignal` bounding it | process memory | no |
| the answerer closure that will settle it | process memory | no |
| `approval/decided` | session log, written only at settle | never written |

Nothing bounds the wait: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop` 0.1.5-rc.2 lists "**No built-in turn budget**". `ctx.jobs` is not an escape either, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-jobs` 0.1.5-alpha.1:

> **The contract is in-process** — `JobStart.run()` passes callbacks and exact `Agent` objects; a durable or cross-process backend must reshape identity, restart, ownership, and observation semantics before it can implement this seam.

And the durable half we would build on is deliberately limited, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence` 0.1.5-rc.2:

> **Synthetic closers are the only crash story** — resume appends `interruptedTurnClosers` through the write handle; there is no partial-turn resume that continues an interrupted turn instead of closing it.

We read that as a real boundary, which is why P2 is not a request.

## What we can do ourselves

We want to be clear about which half is ours, because most of it is.

Routing a question to the right approver, holding it durably, rendering it, surviving a browser reload, and letting a different person answer are all ours. We compose our own terminal answerer and our own surface, and we have to: the shipped Web answerer follows the session's live client scope (`dsh-user-approval`: "agent-scoped listeners receive only that agent"; `dsh-user-questions`: "Remote Events route the shipped Web answerer only when the request carries a live Agent scope"), and a delegated approver is not in that scope.

What we have today is an answerer that refuses to wait: it records the request in PostgreSQL with an assignee, returns a terminal outcome immediately, and lets the turn close. A worker resumes the session once a human answers. This works, and we are not blocked. What it costs is that the recorded outcome is not the real one, and the resumed agent has to be told out of band what actually happened, which pollutes the transcript it later reasons over.

## What we could not determine

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/repair` exports two recovery codes:

- `TOOL_NOT_STARTED`, "an assistant tool request that never reached a recorded call start"
- `TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, "a recorded tool call whose completed outcome was not durably recorded"

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-checkpoint-policy` 0.1.5-rc.2 says "A top-level tool call is flushed before the tool body runs", and `dsh-user-approval` decides "before a sensitive tool action proceeds". From the published types we could not tell where the gate sits relative to the recorded call start, and therefore which code a gated call receives after a crash.

If a gated call already receives `TOOL_NOT_STARTED`, then P1 is satisfied today and we would simply like to know that, and how a deployment is meant to read it. If it receives `TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, then a provably unexecuted action is reported as possibly executed, and that is the gap we are asking about.

## Shapes we considered, and are not requesting

Recording these only to show what we weighed, not to prescribe. Each has an objection we can see ourselves.

- A distinct recovery code for a gated call. Smallest thing that would satisfy P1, but it assumes the gate's position in the pipeline, which we could not verify.
- A new terminal `ApprovalOutcome` meaning "answered later". Rejected on compatibility: `ApprovalOutcome` is consumed by the tools pipeline and by every composed answerer, and widening it would silently reclassify a new value as a denial in existing plugins.
- A settle-from-another-process API on the approval service. Rejected on layering: it would make the approval service drive the agent lifecycle.
- A harness-owned store of pending requests. Rejected as scope: the harness has no database, and the deployment's answerer already owns this state.
- A deadline that expires an unanswered request. Does not help, we need the answer to eventually land rather than expire, though it is a reasonable separate feature and is raised in #5236.

We would rather build against whatever shape you consider right than around it.

## This is not only our problem

From `dsh-plugin-catalog` 2026.917.3416 (3727 plugins, snapshot 2026-09-16), plugins touching approvals fall into exactly two families:

- **17** replace the human with rules or a reviewer model (`dsh-approval-llm`, `dsh-auto-approve`, `dsh-yolo-mode`, `dsh-approve-for-me`, `dsh-perm-guard`, ...).
- **68** in `notify` and `remote` forward the card to Telegram, Feishu, WeChat, Slack, Discord or a phone app so the human answers faster (`dsh-im-gateway`, `dsh-reach`, `dsh-lark-bridge`, ...).
- **0** let a pending request survive a restart.

Both families work around the same limit from opposite sides: the human must answer now, so either remove them or hurry them. Nobody solved it, which suggests it is not solvable from a plugin.

Related and distinct: #5236 asks which answerer owns a request, not how long one may live, and raises the deadline question. #4708 carries a request across a process boundary to an embedding host, but the host long-polls and "the answer releases the tool call, an approved `exit_plan_mode` continues the same turn", so it remains one live turn in one live process. #5147 reports an agent stuck when the policy changes while an escalation is pending, which is the same in-memory pending state seen from another side.

## Questions

- Which recovery code does a call gated on approval receive today? That single answer decides whether P1 is already satisfied.
- If it is not satisfied, is making a resumed transcript distinguish a gated call from an unknown one something you would want in the harness, or something a deployment is expected to reconstruct itself?
- Is "a durable out-of-turn approval workflow is deferred" scoped internally anywhere? If a direction exists, we would rather wait for it than build a shape you would not keep.

Happy to prototype whichever shape you prefer, or to run and report a reproduction if that would help answer the first question.

discussions.title: Loose file-module plugin row in a profile breaks every model request with REQUEST_EXTENSION
discussions.body:
## Summary

A profile that loads a **local plugin module** — a patch-list row whose `name` is a relative path to a `.mjs` file rather than a package specifier — makes **every model request** fail with:

```
REQUEST_EXTENSION: DeepSeek request extension preparation failed
```

The host still boots, the Web UI still serves, and sessions still accept input; only the model calls fail. The symptom therefore looks unrelated to the patch that caused it, and nothing is reported at startup.

## Reproduction

No manual edits to the profile are needed: a profile generated by `dsh --from-default-profile` already has the manifest shape that triggers this.

1. Add a trivial plugin module beside the profile, e.g. `$DSH_HOME/profiles/headless/probe-plugin.mjs`:

```js
export const name = 'probe-plugin'
export function apply() {}
```

2. Reference it from a patch list, e.g. `$DSH_HOME/profiles/headless/probe.yml`:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: probe-plugin
      name: './probe-plugin.mjs'
```

3. Run one request through that profile:

```sh
dsh --profile headless --patch "$DSH_HOME/profiles/headless/probe.yml" "Reply with exactly: ok"
```

With `--profile web` the same patch produces the same per-request failure, with a working UI and a clean boot log.

## Current behavior

```
$ dsh --profile headless --patch "$DSH_HOME/profiles/headless/probe.yml" "Reply with exactly: ok"
dsh: REQUEST_EXTENSION: DeepSeek request extension preparation failed
$ echo $?
1
```

Deterministic: every request fails while the row is active, and removing the row makes the identical command succeed. Adding `"version": "0.0.0"` to the profile's `package.json` also makes it succeed.

## Expected behavior

A row that names a loose module with no package provenance should be skipped by the package inventory — as the resolver's own doc comment states ("Resolve one Loader entry's owning package, or absence for a non-package loose module") — and the request should proceed, with that entry simply absent from `dsh_plugin_packages`.

## Root cause

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-package-inventory-deepseek` owns the `dsh_plugin_packages` request field and prepares it on **every** request through `ctx.deepseekLlmApiExtensions`. Its `prepare()` calls `collectActivePluginPackages()`, which calls `PackageIdentityResolver.resolve()` for each active loader entry.

In `PackageIdentityResolver.resolve()`:

- `barePackageName(specifier)` returns `undefined` for a name starting with `.` (also for absolute paths and anything containing `:`);
- the resolver then computes the module URL and calls `nearestManifest(fileURLToPath(moduleUrl))`, which walks **upwards** from the module's directory;
- for a module placed inside the profile, the first manifest found is the **profile's own** `package.json`, whose stock shape is:

```json
{ "name": "dsh-profile-web", "private": true, "dependencies": {}, "dsh": { "profile": { ... } } }
```

`identityFromManifest(path, allowAnonymous)` is then called with `allowAnonymous = true`, but the anonymous escape only covers `manifest.name === undefined`. A manifest that declares a `name` and no `version` is treated as a malformed package and throws:

```
plugin-package-inventory-deepseek: <profile>/package.json must declare non-empty name and version
```

That rejection propagates out of `prepareExtensions()` inside `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-deepseek` (the `prepareExtensions` call site in `lib/index.js`), which is reported as `REQUEST_EXTENSION` — for every request, because the field is prepared per request.

## Suggested fixes

- When `allowAnonymous` is set, treat "no package identity" as anonymous rather than fatal — e.g. return `undefined` when `version` is missing, or continue to the next candidate manifest instead of throwing.
- Or stop the upward search at the profile root, so the profile's own manifest is never mistaken for an owning package.
- Or isolate failures per entry in `collectActivePluginPackages()`: one unattributable loose module must not take down every model request.

## Impact

The shipped overlay in `apps/cli/config/examples/github-review/` is exactly this shape — a `.mjs` rule file referenced from the patch beside it — so following that example on a stock profile breaks all model traffic with an error that points at request preparation rather than at the patch.

## Environment

- `dsh` 0.1.5-rc.1 (bundled `@deepseek-ai/*` packages 0.1.5-rc.2)
- macOS 26.6.2 (arm64), Node.js 26.8.2
- Profile generated by `dsh --from-default-profile`; only the patch row above added

## Also observed (docs vs CLI, possibly a separate item)

`docs/user/guide/github-review.md` documents starting the overlay as `dsh web --patch <file>`, but this CLI version rejects it:

```
$ dsh web --patch /path/to/cordis.yml
error: unknown option '--patch'
$ dsh --patch /path/to/cordis.yml web --port 3099
error: web takes none of parent --profile, --from-default-profile, --patch, --dump-config, or --dump-default-config
```

The working form is `dsh --profile web --patch <file>`; the guide may want that spelling.
