On Windows, @deepseek-ai/dsh-native-command (lib/index.js L228-230) hands explorer.exe a percent-encoded file:// URL via /select,. On Windows 10 22H2 (build 19045.5247, ANSI codepage 936), explorer.exe fails to resolve such a URL for paths containing non-ASCII characters and exits silently. The implementation deliberately swallows Explorer's exit code 1 (Explorer exit 1 is accepted as a delegated handoff, not proof of selection), and api-session-controller.openWorkspacePath then returns { opened: true }, so the UI reports "Requested display in file manager" while nothing happens.

Verified: reproduces on 0.1.5-rc.1; not fixed in 0.1.6-alpha.2 (package source unchanged). ASCII paths work; the native-path form explorer.exe /select,"C:\…" works for CJK paths.

Suggested fix: use the native path (not a file:// URL) for the Windows branch, and stop reporting unconditional success when the native handoff cannot be confirmed.

On Windows 10 22H2 (build 19045.5247, ANSI codepage 936), explorer.exe fails to resolve such a URL for paths containing non-ASCII characters and exits silently. The implementation deliberately swallows Explorer's exit code 1 (Explorer exit 1 is accepted as a delegated handoff, not proof of selection), and api-session-controller.openWorkspacePath then returns { opened: true }, so the UI reports "Requested display in file manager" while nothing happens. Verified: reproduces on 0.1.5-rc.1; not fixed in 0.1.6-alpha.2 (package source unchanged). ASCII paths work; the native-path form explorer.exe /select,"C:\…" works for CJK paths. Suggested fix: use the native path (not a file:// URL) for the Windows branch, and stop reporting unconditional success when the native handoff cannot be confirmed.

discussions.title: [Fixed in 0.1.7-alpha.1] Dev source launch (pnpm dsh) fails every tool call with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')" — resolutionMode 'runtime' default mixes src/lib module planes
discussions.body:
## Summary

On current `master`, every dev source launch of `dsh` (`pnpm dsh <profile> ...`) fails on **every tool call** with:

```
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')
```

The turn ends with `reason: { kind: 'error', code: 'UNKNOWN' }` before any tool executes. It is not escalation/sandbox-specific — even a plain `bash` call like `git status` crashes. GUI sessions (web profile) show the turn failing with `UNKNOWN`.

## Reproduction (keyless, clean tree)

```sh
pnpm install && pnpm run build        # as documented
pnpm run test:snapshot -t bash-tool-turn
```

Note the snapshot suite run **without** `DSH_EXAMPLE_MODE` (i.e. the default `src` launch mode). It fails:

```
dsh: UNKNOWN: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')
```

The same crash hits any real run, e.g. `pnpm dsh --profile headless "task"` or `pnpm dsh web` — every tool call dies before dispatch.

## Root cause: two module planes in one process

`dsh` source launch runs through tsx (`node --import tsx/esm apps/cli/src/bin.ts`). Every package's leaf tsconfig extends `tsconfig.base.json`, whose `paths` map resolves workspace bare imports to `src/`. So a module loaded from `lib/` still resolves its workspace imports into `src/`.

Since #4471 (commit `9ddef327a4`, "`feat: resolution mode link to runtime`"), the profile loader resolves plugin entries in `'runtime'` mode through built artifacts (`package.json` exports → `lib/`). The result is two executions of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` in one process:

- the `tools` **service instance** is constructed from `packages/core/tools/lib/index.js`;
- `agent-loop`'s static `import { TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools'` binds the copy compiled from `packages/core/tools/src/index.ts`.

Two `Symbol(...)` calls with the same description are not `===`. In `agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:170`:

```ts
const prepared = await ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER].prepare(call.exec)
```

`ctx.tools` is the lib-constructed `ToolRuntime`, which owns the lib-copy symbol, so the lookup with the src-copy symbol is `undefined` and every tool call throws. Instrumenting the bundles confirms it:

```
[registry] [
  'file:///…/packages/core/tools/src/index.ts sameAsImported=true',
  'file:///…/packages/core/tools/lib/index.js sameAsImported=false'
]
// ctx.tools own symbols contain a same-description symbol whose .prepare IS a function;
// the imported binding's lookup is undefined
```

## Introduced by

`9ddef327a4` — the default changed:

```ts
// apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts:263
- const resolutionMode = packaged ? 'runtime' : options.resolutionMode ?? 'link'
+ const resolutionMode = packaged ? 'runtime' : options.resolutionMode ?? 'runtime'
```

Verified causally: reverting only that one default back to `'link'` on the same tree makes `bash-tool-turn`, `bash-startup-timeout`, and `fs-edit` snapshot replays pass again.

## Why the gates miss it

`scripts/run-gates.ts` runs the snapshot suite with `DSH_EXAMPLE_MODE: 'lib'` (pure artifact plane — no mixing, passes). The plain developer flow (`pnpm dsh …`, or `pnpm run test:snapshot` without the env override) runs in `src` mode and crashes.

## Suggested fix

Either:

1. restore the `'link'` default for non-packaged launches (verified working), or
2. keep `'runtime'`, but make the source launch single-plane — e.g. have runtime-mode plugin resolution go through the same resolution the importing modules use, or prevent tsconfig-`paths` resolution for specifiers that the loader resolves through artifacts (identity-sensitive seams like `TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER`, class identity, and branded types otherwise break).

## Environment

- `master` @ `ddefc45fbc` (v0.1.6-alpha.2)
- macOS (Darwin 25.6.0, arm64)
- node v25.3.0, pnpm 11.7.0

discussions.title: 紧凑模式：只要还能「加载更早」，所有已关闭轮次都不折叠（含刚结束的那个）—— 建议折叠门禁从会话级 hasMore 改为逐轮次 turn/start / Compact mode: no closed Turn folds while older history is still loadable, including the one that just finished — gate folding on the Turn's own turn/start instead of session-wide hasMore
discussions.body:
[compact-fold-per-turn.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32428628/compact-fold-per-turn.patch)

### 摘要

「紧凑」显示模式下，只要会话还能点「加载更早」，**所有**已关闭轮次都会保持展开、折叠控件也不出现 —— 包括刚从尾部结束的那个轮次。根因是折叠门禁用了会话级的 `hasMore`，而它真正要防的风险只存在于「自身起始边界尚未加载」的那一个轮次。建议把判据改为逐轮次，并附上基于当前 master 的补丁。

### 现象

对话显示使用默认的「紧凑」时，若会话打开后仍可点「加载更早」（更早历史尚未加载完），推理行、上下文注入、工具行与较早的 Assistant 内容会一直保持展开，轮次过程控件也不出现 —— 对**每一个**轮次都是如此，包括刚结束的那个。只有把「加载更早」点到底、历史全部加载完之后，所有合格的已关闭轮次才会一起收起。

### 复现

1. 打开一个日志长度超过首屏的会话 —— 客户端打开会话时只加载最后 50 条消息（`PAGE_MESSAGES = 50`，`packages/api/session-controller/src/client/sessions/session.ts`），所以大多数真实会话都符合条件。
2. 发一条会产生推理或工具调用的消息。
3. 等 `turn/end`：过程行保持展开，折叠控件不出现。
4. 一直点「加载更早」直到按钮消失：所有合格的已关闭轮次立即收起。

### 为什么确实需要某种限制

当某个轮次自己的 `turn/start` 不在已加载窗口内时，`processStartSeq` 会回退到「已加载的最早证据」（`packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/conversation-nodes/turn-process.ts`）：

```ts
processStartSeq: turn.start?.seq ?? (Number.isFinite(externalProcessSeq) ? externalProcessSeq : answer.finalNode.seq),
```

此时折叠并不安全：翻入更早的一页会扩大这个范围、并移动控件锚点（`controlAnchorSeq`），于是刚进入窗口的行会落进已收起的组里 —— 而那正是读者翻上去要看的内容。

### 建议

把折叠门禁从会话级 `hasMore` 改为按轮次自身的起始边界判定：

```ts
// packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/chat/ChatNodeSeat.tsx
const processWindowReady = processSpec !== undefined
  && processPresentation !== undefined
  && compactTranscript
  && processSpec.answerAnchorSeq !== null
  && processPresentation.turn === processSpec.turn
  && processPresentation.turnClosed
  && processPresentation.membersLoaded   // 原为：&& !historyIncomplete
```

`membersLoaded` 由轮次自身的边界派生（`packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/conversation-nodes/turn-process-presentation.ts`）：

```ts
membersLoaded: location.turn.start !== undefined
```

`TurnLocation.start` 恰好在该轮次的 `turn/start` 事件位于已加载窗口之外时为 `undefined`（`packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/conversation.ts`）。由于已加载窗口是一个连续的 `[head, tail]` 区间，起始落在窗口内的轮次，其全部过程成员必然都已加载 —— 折叠它不可能隐藏尚未翻入的行。

改动后的行为：

- 起始已加载的已关闭轮次立即折叠，无论还剩多少更早的历史；
- 只有窗口头部那个起始页尚未翻入的轮次保持过程行可见，等该页到达后再收起 —— 会话级门禁原本提供的保护，被限定到真正需要它的那个轮次上。

### 补丁（基于当前 master）

附件 `compact-fold-per-turn.patch` 由 `git format-patch` 生成，**基线是当前的 `master`**：

- 基线提交：`ddefc45fbc`（2026-09-17，`Merge pull request #4469 … release-dsh-0.1.6-alpha.2`），即版本 `0.1.6-alpha.2` 的 master 顶端
- 补丁提交：`c8aad2f88d`（2026-09-20）
- 规模：12 个文件，+125 / −24 —— 4 处产品代码与契约、2 个测试文件、双语 README 与配对记录、Agent Note 三件套
- 应用：`git am compact-fold-per-turn.patch`（保留提交信息）或 `git apply compact-fold-per-turn.patch`；若 master 已有前进，可 `git apply --3way`
- 若只想跑测试：`pnpm vitest run packages/client/ui-chat`

### 证据

- 组件测试覆盖两个方向（起始页未加载的已关闭轮次保持可见；起始已加载的已关闭轮次在「加载更早」仍在时即折叠），测试 fixture 也已建模 `TurnLocation.start`：`packages/client/ui-chat/tests/chat-view.client.spec.tsx`、`packages/client/ui-chat/tests/chat-snapshot-fixture.client.ts`。
- `packages/client/ui-chat` 测试套件 358/358 通过。
- 在组装后的 Web GUI 中用长会话手测确认。

### 希望了解

1. 会话级门禁（`hasMore`）是有意为之，还是这里本就该用逐轮次的 `turn/start` 边界？
2. 如果规则确实要保持会话级，它保护的、而逐轮次边界覆盖不到的场景是什么？

---

### Summary

With the default `Compact` conversation display, as long as a Session can still load older history (the `Load earlier` button is visible), **every** closed Turn stays expanded and the folding control never appears — including the Turn that just finished at the tail. The fold gate reads the session-wide `hasMore`, while the risk it guards against only exists for the one Turn whose own start boundary is not loaded yet. The proposal below gates on the Turn itself, with a patch based on the current `master`.

### What happens today

With the default `Compact` display, while older history is still loadable, reasoning rows, Context injection, Tool rows and earlier Assistant material stay expanded and no Turn-process control appears — for **every** Turn, including the one that just finished. Only after `Load earlier` has been clicked until history is exhausted does every eligible closed Turn collapse at once.

### Reproduction

1. Open a Session whose log is longer than the first page — the client opens a Session with its last 50 messages (`PAGE_MESSAGES = 50`, `packages/api/session-controller/src/client/sessions/session.ts`), so most real Sessions qualify.
2. Send a prompt that produces reasoning or Tool calls.
3. Wait for `turn/end`: the process rows stay expanded and no folding control appears.
4. Click `Load earlier` until the button disappears: every eligible closed Turn collapses immediately.

### Why some restriction is needed

When a Turn's own `turn/start` is outside the loaded window, `processStartSeq` falls back to the earliest loaded evidence (`packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/conversation-nodes/turn-process.ts`):

```ts
processStartSeq: turn.start?.seq ?? (Number.isFinite(externalProcessSeq) ? externalProcessSeq : answer.finalNode.seq),
```

Folding such a Turn is unsafe: paging an older page in widens that range and moves the control's anchor (`controlAnchorSeq`), so rows that just landed in the window would be hidden inside an already collapsed group — exactly the rows the reader paged up to read.

### Proposal

Gate the fold on the Turn's own start boundary instead of the session-wide `hasMore`:

```ts
// packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/chat/ChatNodeSeat.tsx
const processWindowReady = processSpec !== undefined
  && processPresentation !== undefined
  && compactTranscript
  && processSpec.answerAnchorSeq !== null
  && processPresentation.turn === processSpec.turn
  && processPresentation.turnClosed
  && processPresentation.membersLoaded   // previously: && !historyIncomplete
```

`membersLoaded` is derived from the Turn's own boundary (`packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/conversation-nodes/turn-process-presentation.ts`):

```ts
membersLoaded: location.turn.start !== undefined
```

`TurnLocation.start` is `undefined` exactly when that Turn's `turn/start` event is outside the loaded window (`packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/conversation.ts`). Since the loaded window is one contiguous `[head, tail]` range, a Turn whose start is inside it has all of its process members already loaded — folding it can never hide rows that are still to be paged in.

Resulting behavior:

- every closed Turn with a loaded start folds immediately, no matter how much older history remains;
- only the Turn at the window head, whose start page is still paged out, keeps its process rows visible until that page arrives — the protection the session-wide gate provided, scoped to the Turn that actually needs it.

### Patch (based on the current master)

The attached `compact-fold-per-turn.patch` is produced by `git format-patch` and **targets the current `master`**:

- Base commit: `ddefc45fbc` (2026-09-17, `Merge pull request #4469 … release-dsh-0.1.6-alpha.2`), the tip of `master` at version `0.1.6-alpha.2`
- Patch commit: `c8aad2f88d` (2026-09-20)
- Size: 12 files, +125 / −24 — four production/contract files, two test files, the bilingual README and its pairing record, and the Agent Note triplet
- Apply with `git am compact-fold-per-turn.patch` (keeps the commit message) or `git apply compact-fold-per-turn.patch`; use `git apply --3way` if `master` has moved
- To run only the tests: `pnpm vitest run packages/client/ui-chat`

### Evidence

- Component tests cover both directions (a closed Turn whose start is paged out stays visible; a closed Turn whose start is loaded folds while `Load earlier` still owns the head), and the fixture models `TurnLocation.start`: `packages/client/ui-chat/tests/chat-view.client.spec.tsx`, `packages/client/ui-chat/tests/chat-snapshot-fixture.client.ts`.
- `packages/client/ui-chat` suite: 358/358 passing.
- Verified by hand in the assembled Web GUI on a long Session.
[compact-fold-per-turn.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32428627/compact-fold-per-turn.patch)


### What I would like to know

1. Is the session-wide gate (`hasMore`) intended, or is the per-Turn `turn/start` boundary the rule you would want here?
2. If the rule should stay session-wide on purpose, what case does it protect that the per-Turn boundary does not?

discussions.title: [Bug] Agent rebuilds user-owned files from stale backups, silently discarding manual edits / 用旧备份重建用户文件，静默丢弃手工编辑
discussions.body:
# [Bug] Agent rebuilds user-owned files from stale backups, silently discarding manual edits

**Package**: `@deepseek-ai/dsh` `0.1.5-rc.1`
**Environment**: Linux; the user was editing the same file in VS Code
**Impact**: user's manual edits silently overwritten; the pre-overwrite backup then deleted by cleanup

---

## Summary

When asked to modify a file **the user was also editing**, the agent did not apply targeted
edits to the current file. Instead it rewrote the whole file as
**"head of an earlier backup + freshly generated tail"**.

Every manual edit the user had made after that backup was **silently discarded** — no diff,
no confirmation, no warning. The agent then deleted, during cleanup, the only copy
preserving the pre-overwrite state.

---

## Steps to reproduce

1. The user manually edits and saves file `F` (~1500 lines in this case) in an editor.
2. The agent had, at some earlier point, copied `F` to a backup `B`.
3. The user asks the agent to modify one part of `F`.
4. The agent generates new content with a script, composes the whole file as
   **`head of B` + `newly generated tail`**, and writes it to `F` in a single `write`.
5. All user edits made after `B` are gone.
6. While cleaning up temporary files, the agent runs `rm` and deletes the
   pre-overwrite snapshot it had taken just before step 4.

**Result**: the user's manual work survives only as a snapshot in the editor's local history.

---

## Why this behavior is dangerous

- **Silent.** At no point does the agent announce "I am rebuilding this file from an older
  version". The user has no way to notice.
- **Irreversible.** The only pre-existing backup is deleted within the same task.
- **Wrong object.** `F` is a user artifact, not a file the tool generated. Rebuilding from
  a backup silently assumes "changes made after the backup do not exist or do not matter" —
  an assumption with no basis.

## Aggravating factor: recovery analysis produced a false negative

During the post-incident investigation, the agent inspected the editor's local history using
a heuristic **unrelated to the actual problem** — counting occurrences of `\begin{block}`
inside the affected region — and concluded that
"the user's edits were captured by no snapshot; no copy remains on disk."

The user's edits were in fact fully present in the editor local history. This false negative
led the user to believe the work had been permanently lost.

---

## Suggested behavioral constraints

1. **Never reconstruct a user-owned file from a backup.** For user-owned paths, always apply
   targeted edits to the *current* content.
2. **Verify freshness before writing.** If a path's content hash or mtime differs from what
   the agent last read, re-read it first; if it changed, copy the **current** content to a
   timestamped backup before proceeding.
3. **Backups must not be deleted.** A backup created during a task should not be removed by
   that same task's cleanup. Cleanup should be scoped to tool-created, regenerable temp files only.
4. **Require explicit confirmation for full rewrites.** When a wholesale rewrite is genuinely
   needed, write to a new path first, show the user a diff or a plan, and replace only after approval.
5. **Consider a hard guard.** When the target of a `write` has changed since the agent last
   read it, refuse by default unless the agent explicitly acknowledges the change.

---

## Recovery status

After the user pointed it out, the pre-overwrite snapshot was located in the editor's local
history (VS Code `User/History`) and fully restored, along with annotations that had been
mistakenly removed. **No permanent data loss.**

---

## Note

This failure is unrelated to model capability. It is a matter of the **agent's editing
strategy**: in the common situation where a user may be editing the same file, it chose the
most destructive possible write path. Constraints 1–3 above would eliminate this class of incident.

discussions.title: [Bug] Right sidebar (file preview) has no visible exit control after entering fullscreen — trapped until app restart
discussions.body:
**Environment**

- DSH: `0.1.5-rc.2` (DeepSeek Harness Web GUI, `deepseek-harness` repo)
- Affected packages: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-right` (panel chrome / fullscreen), `dsh-client-ui-sidebar-files`, `dsh-client-ui-sidebar-documentpreview`
- OS / Browser: Windows, Chrome / Edge
- Viewport width: normal (≥768px, i.e. not the `autoFullscreen` branch)

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open the right sidebar "Files" tab.
2. Click any file to open its preview (PDF / image / Markdown / code text — all seem to trigger it).
3. Click the "Fullscreen" button in the panel's top-right chrome (`data-sidebar-right-mode="fullscreen"`).
4. The panel covers the whole viewport (`data-sidebar-right-panel="fullscreen"`, CSS `position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 40`), including the conversation header.
5. **The "Exit fullscreen" button is not visible at all** — no `data-sidebar-right-mode="push"` control is rendered/shown, only the preview content remains. There is no way out of fullscreen.
6. There is no Esc / keyboard fallback (`ui-sidebar-right` registers no keydown handler).
7. **Reloading the page (F5) does not recover** — the app comes back still stuck in fullscreen. Only fully quitting and relaunching the app recovers.

**Expected behavior**

Clicking "Exit fullscreen" (or pressing Esc) returns the panel to its normal docked width (push mode). The exit control must stay visible and usable whenever the panel is fullscreen.

**Actual behavior**

After entering fullscreen the exit control is missing entirely; no keyboard fallback exists; reloading does not help; only an app restart recovers.

**Possible cause (initial code inspection, for maintainers)**

1. `SidebarPanel` in `packages/client/ui-sidebar-right` passes `PanelChrome` (which contains the exit button, `data-sidebar-right-mode="push"`) unconditionally as `chrome` to `DockSurface`, which renders it at the end of the active pane's top tab strip (`data-dockkit-strip-chrome`). In fullscreen the panel is `position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 40` and covers everything; if the strip/chrome is covered by the preview content or clipped out (panes use `overflow: hidden`), there is simply no exit entry point. Checking in DevTools whether `[data-dockkit-strip-chrome]` / `[data-sidebar-right-mode]` exist inside `[data-sidebar-right-panel="fullscreen"]` would tell whether the control is "not rendered" vs "rendered but hidden".
2. The exit handler and store path (`setMode` → `planSetMode`: `t.mode === r ? [] : [{ type: "setMode", mode: r }]`) have no guards, so the state transition itself is sound — pointing to a rendering/hit-testing issue.
3. No Esc handling anywhere in the right-sidebar code; even independent of the root cause, an Esc fallback should be added.
4. The fullscreen layout state (`layout.mode === "fullscreen"`) appears to survive page reloads and gets replayed on restore — a stuck state being persisted means the user is permanently trapped; worth checking the session-restore path as well.

**Workaround**

Fully quit and relaunch the app (currently the only recovery).

discussions.title: [0.1.6-alpha.2] dsh web fails to boot on Windows: every loader entry fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND (same profile boots on 0.1.5-rc.2)
discussions.body:
# [0.1.6-alpha.2] `dsh web` fails to boot on Windows: every loader entry fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` (same profile boots on 0.1.5-rc.2)

## Summary

On Windows, `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.6-alpha.2` cannot boot the `web` profile. The launcher itself starts fine — `dsh --version` prints `0.1.6-alpha.2`, and `dsh --profile web --dump-config` composes and prints the tree — but plugin loading fails: **218 distinct loader entries** fail to import, all with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.

`@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.5-rc.2` boots the same profile on the same machine without issue.

## Environment

- Windows (win32 x64)
- Node `v24.18.0`
- pnpm `11.17.0`
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.6-alpha.2` (the `alpha` dist-tag)

Reproduced three ways, all failing identically:

1. `pnpx @deepseek-ai/dsh@alpha web --port 0 --no-open`
2. pnpm global install (`pnpm add -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@alpha`), then `dsh web`
3. any of the above with a brand-new empty `DSH_HOME`

## Reproduction

```
pnpx @deepseek-ai/dsh@alpha web --port 0 --no-open
```

Exit code `1`. The `--allow-build` flags for native deps are not needed to trigger this; they change nothing about the failure.

```
		      ^

    at async EntryGroup.update (.../cordis-plugin-loader/lib/index.js:97:21)
    at async [cordis.init] (.../dsh-app-boot/lib/index.js:184:3)
    at async file:///<USER>/AppData/Local/pnpm/store/v11/links/@deepseek-ai/cordis/4.0.2/<hash>/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/cordis/lib/index.js:1160:22
    at async Fiber._reload (.../cordis/lib/index.js:1355:5)
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm' imported from <DSH_HOME>\profiles\web\
Did you mean to import "@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm/lib/index.js"?
    at Object.getPackageJSONURL (node:internal/modules/package_json_reader:301:9)
    at packageResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:768:81)
    at moduleResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:859:18)
    at defaultResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:992:11)
    at #cachedDefaultResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:701:20)
    at #resolveAndMaybeBlockOnLoaderThread (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:721:38)
    at ModuleLoader.resolveSync (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:759:56)
    at file:///<USER>/AppData/Local/pnpm/store/v11/links/@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot/0.1.6-alpha.2/<hash>/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot/lib/index.js:1667:77

Error: failed to import loader entry deepseek-llm-api-extensions (@deepseek-ai/dsh-deepseek-llm-api-extensions): Cannot find package '@deepseek-ai/dsh-deepseek-llm-api-extensions' imported from <DSH_HOME>\profiles\web\
    ... (repeats for the remaining 216 packages)

Node.js v24.18.0
```

</details>

## What I ruled out

| Hypothesis | How it was tested | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `pnpx` / dlx cache problem | pnpm global install of the same version | still fails |
| Stale shared fallback (`$DSH_HOME/profiles/node_modules` holding `0.1.5-rc.2` links from earlier runs) | booted with a brand-new empty `DSH_HOME` | still fails |
| A third-party bundle in my profile is at fault | brand-new `DSH_HOME`, default `web` template only, no custom bundles | still fails |
| Profile config is broken | `dsh --profile web --dump-config` composes and prints the full tree | works |

## Observation 1 — the shared fallback directory is never created

After the failed boot with a fresh `DSH_HOME`, the tree is:

```
<DSH_HOME>\profiles\web\cordis.patch.yml
<DSH_HOME>\profiles\web\cordis.yml
<DSH_HOME>\profiles\web\package.json
<DSH_HOME>\profiles\web\pnpm-workspace.yaml
```

`<DSH_HOME>\profiles\node_modules` **does not exist**. On `0.1.5-rc.2`, the same fresh boot creates it and populates it with symlinks into the installation closure (258 entries on this machine) — which is what makes the imports resolve through Node's ordinary parent-walk.

## Observation 2 — alpha.2 defaults the resolution mode to `runtime`

From the CLI's `lib/profile-boot-*.js`:

```js
const resolutionMode = process.pkg !== void 0 ? "runtime" : options.resolutionMode ?? "runtime";
```

and:

```js
if (resolvedProfile !== void 0 && resolutionMode !== "runtime") healIsolatedProfileModuleFallback(resolvedProfile);
// ...
resolution: resolutionMode === "runtime" || resolvedProfile !== void 0
  ? await createProfileResolutionGeneration(resolutionOptions)
  : await healProfilesModuleFallback(resolutionOptions),
```

`createProfileResolutionGeneration` calls `healProfilesModuleFallback({ ..., materialize: false })`, so on the default (`runtime`) path nothing is written to disk; resolution is instead meant to be served by `installProfileResolution`, which wraps Node's ESM/CJS resolvers. This lines up with observation 1.

## Observation 3 — the resolver wrapper is installed and does route, but the native resolve from the routed anchor still misses

The stack shows the wrapped resolver being reached:

```
at ModuleLoader.wrapped [as resolveSync] (.../dsh-app-boot/lib/index.js:1675:8)
at adapted (.../dsh-app-boot/lib/index.js:1617:16)
```

Line 1617 is the `behavior === "enforce"` branch that re-runs the native resolve against `route.entry.declarer` (`routedParent`). So the request is routed to a declarer anchor, and the native resolve **from that anchor** still throws `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for the package.

I did not trace further than this. Reporting it because the combination of observation 1 (no materialized fallback) and observation 3 (native resolve from the routed anchor misses) may be enough to locate it.

## Notes

- `0.1.6-alpha.1` also fails to boot, but earlier and differently: `SyntaxError: The requested module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot' does not provide an export named 'watchUserPatches'`.
- Possibly related: #7135 (runtime deps / stale `latest`), #7031 (CJS routing crash on `require("punycode/")` under alpha.2), and the cluster of `resolutionMode` / `prepare` reports: #6967, #6974, #6992, #7011, #7030, #7107.

discussions.title: [llm-pi-ai] HTTP 200 HTML is reported as TRANSPORT / missing finish_reason, causing futile retries
discussions.body:
## Summary
DSH 0.1.6-alpha.2 (`@earendil-works/pi-ai` 0.85.1) reports `TRANSPORT: Stream ended without finish_reason` when an OpenAI-compatible endpoint returns **HTTP 200 + text/html**, not an SSE stream. This hides a configuration error behind what looks like a transient transport failure.

Upstream pi-ai report with an executed, keyless, network-free reproduction: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9790

## Observed behavior and resolution
Our gateway serves its console HTML from a catch-all at `POST /chat/completions`, while the API is at `/v1/chat/completions`. A route baseURL lacking `/v1` therefore receives 200 HTML. pi-ai yields no content and reports missing `finish_reason`; DSH retries five times with exponential backoff, ending with the same error and zero reported tokens.

After changing the route's baseURL to include `/v1`, the **same real DSH headless invocation** completed and returned `ok` (5,525 input / 5 output tokens); a second headless request also completed. The configuration problem is resolved. We are **not claiming a new-version regression or requesting that DSH automatically append `/v1`**.

## Suggested diagnostic improvement
Distinguish an unexpected non-SSE response from an interrupted SSE stream, preserving safe HTTP status/content-type metadata across the pi-ai adapter. This would let users identify an incorrect endpoint and avoid futile transport retries. If an excerpt is shown, it should be bounded and redacted; no complete HTML pages or credentials should enter logs. Genuine truncated SSE streams must still fail integrity checks and retain appropriate retry behavior.

Related Discussion #2299 also concerns a non-SSE response, but shows a JSON completion body; this report isolates HTTP 200 HTML and links a minimal upstream reproduction.

## Environment
DSH 0.1.6-alpha.2; pi-ai 0.85.1; Node 24.15.0; macOS; OpenAI-compatible gateway with a console SPA catch-all. No private endpoint, credential, or conversation content is included.

*AI-assisted diagnostic report, submitted with the account owner's authorization.*

discussions.title: fix(ui-chat): TurnNavigator fails to scroll when navigating to collapsed or unloaded history turns
discussions.body:
### Problem Description
When clicking an earlier turn in the conversation's right-hand rail navigation (`TurnNavigator`), the transcript occasionally fails to respond, and the view does not scroll to the target turn.

### Root Cause
1. **Collapsed nodes filtered by `:not([hidden])`**:
   `anchorElement()` in `ChatView.tsx` searched elements using `[data-chat-anchor-key]:not([hidden])`. When a turn process (e.g. reasoning/tool execution) is folded, its nodes are marked with `hidden="until-found"`. CSS `:not([hidden])` excludes them, causing `anchorElement` to return `null`.
2. **Silent exit on null element**:
   `navigateToTurn` did `if (row === null) return`, silently aborting navigation without revealing collapsed containers or falling back to the parent turn element.
3. **No fallback for custom/synthetic anchors**:
   When a turn's exact `anchorKey` was not rendered in the view, there was no fallback to `[data-chat-turn]`.

### Proposed Fix
1. **Multi-level target resolver (`resolveNavigationElement`)**:
   - Searches unhidden exact anchors.
   - Searches collapsed/hidden anchors and flags them as `isHidden`.
   - Falls back to the turn container `[data-chat-turn]`.
2. **Auto-reveal hierarchy (`revealElementHierarchy`)**:
   - Dispatches `beforematch` events upward along the DOM tree to trigger `useSearchableHidden` expansion callbacks.
   - Cleans up `hidden` attribute as an immediate fallback for geometry calculation.
3. **Smooth scroll & visual highlight**:
   - Executes smooth scroll inside `requestAnimationFrame` post-reveal.
   - Adds `.highlightTarget` with design tokens (`--dsw-alias-interactive-bg-active` & `--dsw-alias-link`) to flash the target turn.
4. **Unit test coverage**:
   - Added tests in `chat-view.client.spec.tsx` verifying auto-revealing hidden nodes and falling back to turn containers.

discussions.title: All tool calls fail with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')" on a fresh profile
discussions.body:
## Summary

Every tool call fails immediately with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')` on a completely fresh, vanilla profile with zero third-party plugins. Plain chat (no tools) works fine every time; the moment the model calls *any* tool — a third-party plugin's tool or a shipped built-in one — the run crashes.

## Reproduction (minimal, no third-party plugins involved)

```sh
# Fresh profile from the shipped template, nothing else installed
dsh --profile my-clean-test --from-default-profile headless
dsh --profile my-clean-test "读取文件 /path/to/any/file.txt 的前 3 行内容并告诉我"
```

Output:

```
dsh: reasoning:
The user is asking me to read the first 3 lines of ... Let me just use the read tool with limit 3.

dsh: UNKNOWN: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
```

The model's reasoning shows it correctly decided to call the built-in read tool; the crash happens at the moment of actually dispatching that call. A prompt with **no tool need** (`"你好,用一句话回复即可"`) completes normally (exit 0, correct reply) every time.

## What I ruled out

- **Not a specific plugin.** Reproduced identically with: (a) a third-party plugin's own tools, (b) dsh's own built-in read/bash tools, (c) a profile that has never had any third-party plugin installed or referenced anywhere (no `dsh.profile.bundles` entry, no home-level `cordis.patch.yml` row).
- **Not stale build artifacts.** A full `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm run build` (clean exit, no errors) did not change the symptom.
- **Not plain generation/chat.** Only reproduces once a tool call is actually dispatched.

## Likely crash site

`packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts`:

```ts
const prepared = await ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER].prepare(call.exec)
```

`ToolRuntime` (`packages/core/tools/src/index.ts`) assigns `[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER]` as an **unconditional class-field initializer**:

```ts
readonly [TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER]: ToolRuntimeScheduler = {
  prepare: exec => this.prepareScheduledExecution(exec),
  ...
}
```

Since that assignment can't be skipped once the constructor runs, `ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER]` reading as `undefined` at the point `tool-calls.ts` uses it points at `ctx.tools` not being the same `ToolRuntime` instance/module-identity that defined the symbol — the shape of a dual-package-instance / symbol-identity mismatch, not a missing-property bug. I haven't traced further into the Loader/host-runner internals to confirm exactly where the two copies would come from.

## Environment

- Commit: `ddefc45fbc7f8e46dd73185e68295696d1297887` (repo has local uncommitted changes — see below — but they're confined to `packages/web/web-fetch-http/*` and unrelated docs/lockfile, not `agent-loop`/`core/tools`)
- Node: v24.18.0, pnpm: 11.7.0
- macOS, Apple Silicon
- `dsh` launched from source (`pnpm dsh ...`), both `web` and `headless` profiles affected

## Note on the local checkout

This checkout has an unrelated in-progress local change (an HTML-decoding fix under `packages/web/web-fetch-http`) that I can't rule out interacting with this somehow, though the touched files don't overlap with the tool-execution code path above. If anyone can reproduce (or not) on a clean `git clone` at this same commit, that would help separate "real regression at this commit" from "something specific to one local tree."

Happy to run additional diagnostics against this reproduction if useful — this currently blocks *all* tool-calling, which is a pretty core piece of functionality.

discussions.title: Source launch loads workspace packages twice (src + lib) and crashes tool dispatch with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')"
discussions.body:
## Summary

On a source launch (`node --import tsx/esm apps/cli/src/bin.ts`, i.e. `pnpm dsh`), the same workspace
package gets loaded as **two separate module instances** — one from `packages/<...>/src`, one from
`packages/<...>/lib` — and the duplicated module-level `Symbol` identity makes tool dispatch crash with
an unhelpful error:

```
dsh: UNKNOWN: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')
```

Source launch is the documented zero-build dev loop, so this affects `pnpm dsh`, the dev Web/TUI, and
source-mode tests. Built/published launches are unaffected (everything resolves through `node_modules`
consistently there).

## Environment

- `dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2(ddefc45fbc)` (origin/master at the time of writing, 2026-09-17)
- Node v25.8.1, macOS arm64 (Darwin)
- tsx 4.22.4, pnpm 11.7.0
- Reproduced on a checkout whose only relevant difference from master is the one-line fix shown below
  (master lacks it); with that line reverted, the regression case below fails.
- `pnpm install` already run; `lib/` build output present in the affected packages.

## Reproduction

Keyless, no API key needed (uses the repo's own `cli-mock` fixture and the headless test profile):

```sh
REPO=/path/to/deepseek-harness   # checkout at ddefc45fbc
cd "$(mktemp -d)"
cat > source.patch.yml <<'EOF'
- id: headless-startup
  disabled: false
- id: headless-runner
  disabled: false
- id: agent-default-model
  config:
    provider: cli-mock
    model: cli-mock
EOF

TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=$REPO/tsconfig.json \
DSH_HOME=$PWD/.dsh DSH_AGENTS_HOME=$PWD/.agents \
node --import "file://$REPO/node_modules/tsx/dist/esm/index.mjs" "$REPO/apps/cli/src/bin.ts" headless \
  --patch "$REPO/apps/cli/tests/profiles/headless/tests/fixtures/cli.patch.yml" \
  --patch "$PWD/source.patch.yml" \
  "test tool dispatch"
```

## Current behavior

Exit code 1; the model turn runs and then the tool call crashes before dispatch:

```
dsh: reasoning:
Inspecting the task before the tool call.

dsh: UNKNOWN: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')
```

`TSX_DEBUG=3` on the same command shows the duplicated replicas:

- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` resolves **both** to
  `packages/core/tools/src/index.ts` (through tsconfig `paths`) **and** to
  `packages/core/tools/lib/index.js` (through disk/node_modules).
- `packages/core/agent-loop/lib/index.js` is the only agent-loop copy loaded.
- `dsh-llm`, `dsh-subagent`, `dsh-goal`, `dsh-commands`, `dsh-plugin-manager`,
  `dsh-permission-presets`, `dsh-command-feedback` also show `lib/` copies.

With the fix below applied, only `packages/core/tools/src/index.ts` and
`packages/core/agent-loop/src/*` appear, the spec passes, and the run exits 0.

## Expected behavior

One module instance per workspace package, as the source-launch contract states:
`.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md` says the tsx ESM hook
owns both TypeScript transformation and tsconfig `paths` projection. A request routed through profile
resolution must not silently bypass that projection.

## Root cause

1. tsx applies tsconfig `paths` only when the importer is not under `node_modules` (bundled hook,
   `resolveTsPaths`): `if (aliasSpecifier && parsedTsconfig && !parentURL?.includes("/node_modules/"))`.
2. `installProfileResolution` resolves an eligible bare request through a `fallback` route and hands
   Node's native resolver a parent taken from the entry's **declarer**
   (`packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile-resolution/resolver.ts`, ESM adapter):

   ```ts
   const routedParent = pathToFileURL(route.kind === 'fallback' ? route.entry.declarer : route.parent).href
   ```

3. `declarers` is populated in `packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile.ts` with the declaring package's
   `package.json`. For transitive dependencies that path lives **under `node_modules`**
   (e.g. `apps/cli/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-base/package.json`, a pnpm symlink into the workspace).
   So tsx classifies the request as "from node_modules", skips `paths`, and the package resolves to its
   built `lib/` output while other import paths already resolved the same package to `src/`.
4. Two replicas ⇒ duplicated module-scope values. `TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER` is
   `Symbol('@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools.scheduler')` (`packages/core/tools/src/index.ts`), so the scheduler
   registered by one replica is invisible to the other: `ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER]` is
   `undefined` in `packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts`, and `.prepare(...)` throws.

## Suggested fix

Canonicalize the declarer path before handing it to the resolver, so source-loader hooks see the real
workspace path. `canonicalPath` already exists in the same file:

```diff
-      const routedParent = pathToFileURL(route.kind === 'fallback' ? route.entry.declarer : route.parent).href
+      // tsx excludes node_modules parents from workspace paths, including symlinks into source packages.
+      const routedParent = pathToFileURL(route.kind === 'fallback' ? canonicalPath(route.entry.declarer) : route.parent).href
```

A regression case that covers this was verified alongside the fix
(`apps/cli/tests/source-launch.compat.spec.ts`: "executes a tool turn through the source profile and
workspace dependencies"): red without the line, green with it (3/3). Note the case's final assertion
executes a real shell tool call, so it needs a usable sandbox backend on the host; where nested
`sandbox-exec` is unavailable the round trip returns the sandbox error instead of the marker.

Optional extra: the underlying trigger is tsx's heuristic that "parent under `node_modules`" means
"third-party built package", which misreads pnpm-style symlinked workspaces. The DSH-side fix is
correct on its own and does not depend on tsx changing.

## Impact

- Affects source launches only (`pnpm dsh`, dev Web/TUI, source-mode tests); built/published launches
  resolve everything through `node_modules` and see a single instance.
- The symptom is an opaque `UNKNOWN: Cannot read properties of undefined` with no stack, so it is hard
  for users to diagnose or work around. Local workaround: apply the one-line change above.

---

**中文摘要**

源码启动（`pnpm dsh`）下，profile resolution 对 `fallback` 路由把 `entry.declarer`（常常是
`node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-base/package.json` 这类路径）直接当作 ESM parent 交给 Node，
而 tsx 只在 importer 不在 `node_modules` 下时才应用 tsconfig `paths`，于是同一个工作区包被解析成
`src` 与 `lib` 两份实例，模块级 `Symbol` 身份错位，
`ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER]` 变成 `undefined`，工具调用崩在
`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')`。
修复：把该 parent 先 `canonicalPath()` 再交给 resolver（同文件已有该函数）。

discussions.title: connection.rpc.handle() never mounts its WebRoute when webServer comes from a sibling plugin
discussions.body:
## Summary

`HostConnectionService.rpc.handle(channel, handler)` is a public API for mounting an
independent HTTP channel. It registers the channel through
`owner.effect(() => owner.webServer.register(route), …)`, where `owner` comes from
the *Connection plugin's own* context (`packages/client/connection/src/rpc-host.ts`:

```ts
get rpc(): HostConnectionRpc {
  const owner = this.ctx
  return {
    handle: (channel, handler) => this.register(owner, channel, handler),
    …
```

That context does not declare `webServer` in the plugin's `inject` list
(`export const inject = ['credentials']`). Reading `owner.webServer` therefore resolves
through the ancestor-only Context property walk, which cannot reach a `webServer`
provided by a **sibling plugin row** — the real profile topology.

The read throws `cannot get property "webServer" without inject`. Cordis swallows the
throw (no `unhandledRejection`, plugin load still succeeds) but **the caller's
`ctx.inject(deps, cb)` callback is aborted**, so everything after that statement never
runs and nothing is logged.

Net effect: **no channel is mounted, no error surfaces anywhere, and the browser sees
HTTP 405 on POST** (the path is simply unregistered; the web server answers
`POST → 405 / GET → 404` for any unknown path).

## Impact

Any plugin that mounts a legacy channel through `rpc.handle` is silently non-functional
in a real profile. Two third-party plugins are affected in our deployment (both verified
against the running service):

- `dsh-mnemon@0.5.5` — all 7 channels (`/dsh-mnemon-read`, `-view`, `-view-settings`,
  `-settings`, `-activation`, `-write`, `-pack`)
- `dsh-vision-router@2.1.6` — `/vision-router-settings`

For `dsh-mnemon` the abort is worse than "one channel missing": `registerRpc()` is the
first statement in its `ctx.inject(['connection'], …)` callback, so the abort also skips
`registerSettingsRpc()`, `registerViewRpc()` and `new MnemonRemoteService(...)` — the
Typert-Remote `/api` service included. The plugin's browser UI therefore has **no working
transport at all**, on loopback *and* remotely, while all of its host-side tools keep
working (which is why the failure is easy to misdiagnose as a UI bug).

## Reproduction

Four-cell matrix. Two variables: where `webServer` is provided, and what the caller
injects. Real packages, isolated in-process Cordis trees
(`@deepseek-ai/cordis@4.0.2` + the shipped `dsh-client-connection/lib/index.js`):

| `webServer` provided by | caller injects | `handle()` throws | channel mounted |
|---|---|---|---|
| root ctx (`ctx.provide`, as the current spec does) | `['connection']` | no | **yes** |
| root ctx | `['connection','webServer']` | no | **yes** |
| **sibling plugin** (real profile) | `['connection']` | **yes** — `cannot get property "webServer"` | **no** |
| **sibling plugin** | `['connection','webServer']` | **yes** — same | **no** |

The last row matters: **a caller cannot work around this on its side.** Adding `webServer`
to the caller's own inject list does not help, because the throwing read happens inside
the service, on the service's context. `dsh-vision-router` is the proof — its source
already carries this exact reasoning and mitigation:

```js
// dsh-vision-router/lib/remote-settings-bridge.js
// DSH client-connection scopes rpc.handle() registrations to the caller
// Context and mounts their WebRoute through owner.webServer. Keep webServer
// on this exact injected fiber so strict Cordis service access in 0.1.5+
// cannot turn remote-settings registration into a startup error.
ctx.inject(['settings', 'connection', 'webServer'], (remoteCtx) => { … })
```

…and its channel is still unregistered (measured: `POST /vision-router-settings/describe`
→ 405, byte-identical to a deliberately bogus path).

### Minimal in-process reproduction

```js
const ctx = new Context()
ctx.provide('credentials', new RecordCredentials())
ctx.provide('webServer', fakeWebServer)          // ← sibling row in a real profile
const fiber = ctx.plugin({ inject: connection.inject, apply: connection.apply })
await fiber.await()

// this is what a plugin does:
ctx.inject(['connection'], (c) => c.connection.rpc.handle('/my-channel', handler))
// → throws inside handle(); '/my-channel' never appears in fakeWebServer's registry
```

Swapping `ctx.provide('webServer', …)` for `ctx.plugin({ apply(c){ c.provide('webServer', …) } })`
is the only change needed to move from "works" to "silently nothing".

## Why the existing tests don't catch it

`packages/client/connection/tests/node-half.host.spec.ts` mounts the fake web server on the
**root** context:

```ts
provideBrowserCredentials(ctx)
ctx.provide('webServer', fakeHttpServer(routes, upgrades) as WebServer)
const fiber = ctx.plugin({ inject: [...inject], apply }, config)
```

With `webServer` on root, the ancestor walk from the Connection plugin's context finds it,
so every `rpc.handle` spec passes. No spec exercises a sibling-provided `webServer`, which
is how every shipped profile mounts it (`packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml` has
`webserver` and `connection` as separate rows). This is the same class of gap as
post-mortem 0001 — the harness was never driven through its real composition.

## Suggested fix

Declare the dependency instead of reading it opportunistically:

```diff
-/** Services required before providing Connection. */
-export const inject = ['credentials']
+/**
+ * Services required before providing Connection.
+ *
+ * `webServer` is declared rather than read opportunistically: `rpc.handle()`
+ * mounts every channel's WebRoute through this service's own `webServer`
+ * property, and that read resolves by an ancestor-only fiber walk.
+ */
+export const inject = ['credentials', 'webServer']
```

The JSDoc on `apply()` ("When `webServer` is present, the plugin also mounts the `/api`
browser transport…") should be updated in the same change — after this, `webServer` is
always present.

Verified: with this change the fourth matrix row mounts successfully
(`routes = ["/api", "/test-channel"]`), no throw, and `/api` still mounts. Rebuilt and
deployed here; all 7 mnemon channels plus `/vision-router-settings` moved from 405 to 401
and the GUI works.

**Deployment note (worth confirming before shipping):** this makes `webServer` a hard
requirement of the Connection plugin. In our deployment that is harmless — the only profiles
that load `dsh-web-app` (`web`, `clawchat`) always provide it, and `headless`/`acp` don't
load Connection at all. If a deployment exists that loads Connection without a web server,
the alternative is to mount channels from inside the plugin's own
`ctx.inject(['webServer'], …)` callback rather than from `rpc.handle` — see below.

## Alternatives that were tried and measured (all failed)

Keeping `webServer` optional is *not* achievable with the obvious rewrite. Each variant was
run against the same sibling-provided `webServer`:

| Variant | Result with `inject: ['credentials']` |
|---|---|
| `register()` returns `owner.inject(['webServer'], cb)` from its `effect` callback | **nothing mounts.** An `effect` callback must return a disposer *function*; returning the `Fiber` object discards the fork, so `cb` never fires (it fires **asynchronously**, so the failure looks like "no error, no effect") |
| same, but the callback returns `() => fork?.dispose()` (a real disposer) | still **nothing mounts** with `inject: ['credentials']`; mounts fine only once `webServer` is in the plugin's own inject list |
| `fetch.register()`-style route instead of `rpc.handle` | not applicable — exact Fetch routes are restricted to the `/api` channel |

Also measured while diagnosing: `owner !== this.ctx` inside `register()` (the value passed
from `get rpc()` is not the service's own context object identity), which is why a
service-context rewrite behaves differently from a caller-side one. We did not determine the
full semantics of that indirection.

## Severity

Silent, topology-dependent, and not workaroundable from the caller side. It also converts a
missing route into a **partial plugin initialization** (aborted `ctx.inject` callback), which
is far harder to diagnose than a thrown load error. Either fixing the mount path or
explicitly deprecating/removing `rpc.handle` (the harness itself no longer calls it outside
tests) would resolve the ambiguity for plugin authors.

discussions.title: [Bug] pre-commit hangs in "whitespace (staged)" because the hook job starts a pager
discussions.body:
### Summary

With a pager that waits for input, `git commit` blocks forever in the `whitespace (staged)` pre-commit job. The other jobs finish normally.

### Environment

- `lefthook` v2.1.9 (the version pinned in this repository)
- macOS (arm64), zsh; `LESS=-R` exported, `PAGER` unset
- `master` @ `ddefc45fbc`, hooks installed by `scripts/install-lefthook.mjs`

### Symptoms

With anything staged, `git commit` stops at

```
┃  whitespace (staged) ❯
⠹ waiting: whitespace (staged)
```

and never returns; Ctrl-C is the only way out.

### Root cause

Lefthook runs hook jobs on a pseudo-terminal (the shipped binary links `github.com/creack/pty`), so a job's stdout is a TTY. The job is

```yaml
- name: whitespace (staged)
  run: git diff --cached --check
```

`git diff` is pager-enabled, so on a TTY git starts `less`. Git only forces `LESS=FRX` when `LESS` is unset; with `LESS=-R` the pager waits for a keypress even for empty output (it draws `(END)` and blocks). This is reachable beyond that one setting:

- any `LESS` without `-F`, or `core.pager` pointing at a waiting pager (`delta`, `bat`, ...);
- with git's default `LESS=FRX`, `--check` output longer than one screen still blocks: a commit with more than a screenful of whitespace errors hangs instead of failing.

### Reproduction

From a terminal, with no working-tree changes needed:

```sh
LESS=-R lefthook run pre-commit --job "whitespace (staged)" --no-auto-install
# hangs; the same job with stdout redirected to a pipe returns immediately
```

Minimal equivalent of what the job runs:

```sh
git --no-pager diff --cached --check   # returns
git diff --cached --check              # TTY + LESS=-R: draws (END) and waits for a key
```

### Expected

The hook never blocks on input: it reports whitespace errors (or nothing) and exits.

### Fix (verified locally)

```yaml
- name: whitespace (staged)
  run: git --no-pager diff --cached --check
```

`--no-pager` is shell-agnostic, unlike an inline `GIT_PAGER=cat` assignment, which would not work under `cmd.exe`. Verified by running the job through a pty before/after: before it hangs on `(END)`, after it prints `✓ whitespace (staged) (0.02 seconds)`; a staged file with trailing whitespace still fails the check.

The other pre-commit jobs cannot page: their git calls run with piped stdio or inside `$(...)`, so their stdout is not a terminal.

I have this as a one-line local commit and am happy to share it, but I understand external pull requests are not accepted at the moment, so this is a report.

---

### 中文摘要

`git commit` 会永久卡在 `whitespace (staged)` 作业上。原因：lefthook 用伪终端跑作业，作业的 stdout 是 TTY，于是 `git diff --cached --check` 拉起分页器；`LESS` 未设置时 git 才会用 `LESS=FRX`，一旦 `LESS=-R`（或 `core.pager` 配了 delta/bat 之类），空输出也会显示 `(END)` 等你按键。对照实验与修复（`git --no-pager ...`）均已验证。

discussions.title: [Bug] A nested AGENTS.md that symlinks an ancestor file is injected twice (one file, two scopes)
discussions.body:
### Summary

When a workspace symlinks its root `AGENTS.md` into a subdirectory (a common layout for per-task checkouts or shared repository metadata), a filesystem tool that touches a file in that subdirectory makes DSH inject the same physical file a second time as `Additional instructions from: <subdir>/AGENTS.md`.

### Environment

- `dsh` 0.1.6-alpha.2, source launch (`pnpm dsh`)
- macOS; session cwd = workspace root
- Layout:

```
workspace/
├── AGENTS.md
└── task-x/
    ├── AGENTS.md -> ../AGENTS.md
    ├── file.txt
    └── ...
```

### Evidence

The session log carries two `agent-instructions` changes with the **identical `digest`**, i.e. the whole file is in the request twice:

```
scope "."       path "AGENTS.md"          digest 3dba89b8a54128bfd8a82571ffa13030ca404c4c
scope "task-x"  path "task-x/AGENTS.md"   digest 3dba89b8a54128bfd8a82571ffa13030ca404c4c
```

In our workspace that is ~12 KB of duplicated instruction text in every request after the touch, and duplicated guidance for the model.

### Reproduction

1. Create the layout above (root `.git`, `AGENTS.md`, `task-x/AGENTS.md` symlinked to `../AGENTS.md`, `task-x/file.txt`).
2. Start a session with cwd = workspace root, so the baseline injects `AGENTS.md`.
3. Have the agent read `task-x/file.txt` (any first-party `read`/`write`/`edit` on a descendant path).
4. The next request contains both `Instructions from: AGENTS.md` and `Additional instructions from: task-x/AGENTS.md`, with the same body.

### Root cause

`packages/context/agent-instructions` deduplicates candidates in two places, and neither looks through a symlink:

- discovery (`src/files.ts`, `discoverInstructionFiles`) keeps a `Set` of raw absolute paths, and a symlink has a different path than its target;
- reconciliation (`src/state.ts`, `reconcileInstructionContext`) deduplicates only by *(directory, trimmed content)*, and the nested candidate lives in a different directory than the baseline file.

### Note on intended behavior

The README documents per-directory dedup as content-based, and distinct same-content *copies* in different directories are deliberately separate scopes. So the fix should identify the resolved file, not the content: a nested symlink that resolves to an already-loaded file should add nothing, while a real copy with identical content in another directory should still load on its own.

### Fix direction (implemented and verified locally)

Identify each candidate by the file its path resolves to (`ctx.fs` target key; `realpath` for the host path), deduplicate discovery by that identity, and carry the identity through reconciliation so one file is reserved once, released when a scope retargets to another file, and restored when a directory group rolls back to its last-good context.

Verification on a checkout of `master`: 167 package tests pass, the package keeps 100% per-file coverage, the keyless recorded-session snapshot for `agent-instructions` replays through the shipped headless profile, and every regression test was checked to fail without its fix. Two follow-on defects found while fixing this (a retargeted baseline symlink that left the old file reserved, and a rollback that re-injected a preserved file) are covered by the same change.

I have this as a local commit; happy to share the diff or a fork branch if it is useful — reporting rather than opening a pull request, since external PRs are not accepted at the moment.

---

### 中文摘要

工作区把根 `AGENTS.md` symlink 进子目录（如 per-task checkout）时，第一次 `read` 子目录下的文件会触发嵌套发现，把同一个物理文件再注入一遍：会话日志里两条 `agent-instructions` change 的 `digest` 完全相同，scope 分别是 `.` 与 `task-x`。根因是发现阶段按绝对路径去重、对账阶段只在同目录内按内容去重，都不穿透 symlink。修复方向是"按解析后的文件身份去重"（保留"不同目录中内容相同的独立副本各自加载"这一既有设计），本地已验证（167 测试 / 覆盖率 100% / 快照回放 / 逐项负向对照）。

discussions.title: DSH | dsh-short-tool-ids | fix "string too long ... maximum length 64" tool-call ID errors on OpenAI-compatible providers
discussions.body:
## The failure

A session suddenly stops accepting messages. Every new turn, even "hi", fails before the model answers:

```text
Invalid 'input[5].call_id': string too long. Expected a string with maximum length 64, but got a string with length 81 instead.
```

## Why it happens

Some gateways and relays generate long tool-call IDs (81 characters in my case). DSH stores tool-call IDs verbatim in the session history, and every new turn replays that history to the provider. A strict upstream rejects any ID over 64 characters, so the session is stuck: each turn resends the same invalid history. On a custom `openai-completions` route the built-in ID normalization doesn't cover same-model replay, and renaming the provider doesn't help.

## What I shipped

**[dsh-short-tool-ids](https://github.com/mrbeandev/dsh-short-tool-ids)** adds its own **Settings → Short tool-call IDs** tab, which lists every provider with a switch (all off by default).

- At request time, ordinary IDs longer than 64 characters become `call_` + 48 hex characters of a SHA-256 hash (53 total), and each matching tool result gets the same mapping. It's deterministic, so retries are stable.
- Saved session files are never modified. Turn the toggle off and nothing is rewritten.
- It refuses the request on an ID collision instead of pairing the wrong result.
- Only pi-ai `openai-completions` models of the providers you enable are affected.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-short-tool-ids
```

Restart `dsh web`, refresh the page, then switch on the provider that returns the error in **Settings → Short tool-call IDs**.

## Limits

- It doesn't fix empty/null tool-call IDs, duplicate or reused IDs (see #5732), or dangling `tool_calls`. Those are different bugs.
- Compound Responses `call_id|item_id` IDs are left untouched, and when rewriting would break signed/native replay it refuses the request instead of guessing.
- Supports DSH `0.1.5-rc.1` up to (not including) `0.3.0` since 0.4.0; tested on 0.1.5-rc.1/2/3, 0.1.7-rc.2, 0.2.0-rc.1 and 0.2.0-rc.2. Node `^22.19.0` or `>=24`. Outside that range it refuses to load instead of patching blindly.
- Related but separate: `yuanc1204/dsh-ollama-tool-call-id-fix` (Ollama reusing `call_0`).

MIT licensed. [GitHub](https://github.com/mrbeandev/dsh-short-tool-ids) · [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-short-tool-ids). I'm the author, so feedback and bug reports are welcome.

**中文摘要：** 某些网关会生成超过 64 字符的 tool_call ID（我遇到的是 81 字符），严格的上游会直接拒绝，而会话每一轮都会重放这段历史，于是每一轮都返回 400。dsh-short-tool-ids 在请求时把超长 ID 缩短为 53 字符，并同步改写对应的工具结果，不修改已保存的会话；在 设置 → Short tool-call IDs 里按提供方开启即可。支持 DSH 0.1.5 至 0.2.x。仅适用于 openai-completions；不解决空 ID / 重复 ID 问题。

**My other plugins:** [dsh-hypercompact](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/8422) (byte-budget compaction with no LLM call) · [dsh-reconnect](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/8423) (retry failed model requests with backoff)
