discussions.title: [Bug][Recovery] Crash recovery loses host termination provenance (signal / exit cause)
discussions.body:
## Summary

After a real `dsh web` process termination on Windows, session repair correctly makes the transcript resumable, but the durable recovery record only says:

```text
turn/end { reason: { kind: "interrupted" } }
```

The original host termination provenance is lost. From the recovered session it is therefore impossible to distinguish an external console/process termination, `process.exit`, an uncaught exception / unhandled rejection, an orderly shutdown while a turn is open, or another fatal host termination.

This became especially confusing in a real incident because two long-running background jobs terminated at almost the same time as the host. The durable log contains their normal `tool-jobs` completion notices, but nothing says whether those job outcomes were causal, collateral, or merely adjacent to the host termination.

## Environment

- Windows 11 x64
- Node.js `v24.13.0`
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh` `0.1.5-rc.1`
- `dsh web`
- default zstd JSONL session persistence

## Observed incident

One session had completed turn 12 normally. Later, the repaired durable log contains the following sequence around an otherwise idle period:

```text
pwsh-52: mitmdump background job finished
  exit code = 3221225786 = 0xC000013A (STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT)

pwsh-53: mitmdump background job finished
  status = killed, "killed before exit"

turn 13: turn/start
turn 13: step/start
tool-jobs completion notices are injected
turn 13: step/end
turn 13: turn/end { reason: { kind: "interrupted" } }
```

There is no `request/header` for turn 13, so the host disappeared before the next LLM request was durably started.

Important timestamp caveat: the synthetic `interrupted` closers reuse the last real event timestamp, so their displayed time is **not** the recovery time. OS process inspection showed the replacement `dsh web` process was created at `23:48:56`; the session later appended `session/end-seed` at `23:51:05`, confirming reload/recovery.

Windows Application Error / WER / Resource Exhaustion logs contained no `node.exe` crash or OOM record in the relevant window.

Also, neither `pwsh-52` nor `pwsh-53` was explicitly `job_kill`ed; there were no `job_kill` calls after the relevant sequence boundary.

## What the source lets us conclude

### 1. Recovery deliberately loses the host termination cause

`packages/core/session/src/repair.ts` synthesizes the closer as effectively:

```ts
{ type: 'turn/end', data: { turn: openTurn, reason: { kind: 'interrupted' } } }
```

`interruptedTurnClosers()` receives the durable event prefix, not host process exit metadata. There is no signal, exit code, shutdown source, boot id, or recovery-time field in this reason.

### 2. The background-job notices were not produced by `jobs-local` teardown cancellation itself

`packages/jobs/jobs-local/src/index.ts` sets `job.reported = true` for explicit `kill()` and for owner/service teardown cancellation. `packages/jobs/tool-jobs/src/index.ts` suppresses completion delivery when `snapshot.reported` is true:

```ts
if (snapshot.reported || owner === undefined) return
```

So a durable plugin completion notice is inconsistent with that job having been settled *by* `job_kill`, owner disposal, or jobs-service disposal. This does **not** prove the external cause; it only rules out that specific causal chain.

### 3. Child-process death can also be collateral to host exit

The repository already contains `packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/tests/process-exit.spec.ts`. I ran its Windows ordinary-process scenarios on this machine:

- host `process.exit(...)` -> managed process tree removed: **PASS**
- host uncaught exception -> managed process tree removed: **PASS**
- host unhandled rejection -> managed process tree removed: **PASS**
- normal runtime dispose -> managed process tree removed and exit listener removed: **PASS**

This confirms that background subprocess termination observed near a host exit cannot automatically be treated as the root cause of the host exit.

## Negative reproduction result (to avoid a false diagnosis)

I also tested the tempting Windows-console hypothesis directly.

An isolated Node host spawned a PowerShell child with `detached: false`. `GetConsoleProcessList()` confirmed the child, Node host, and parent PowerShell were in the same console. The child called:

```text
GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent(CTRL_C_EVENT, 0) -> True
```

In the clean run the Node host remained alive and its SIGINT handler did not fire. A `detached: true` control also left the host alive.

Therefore I am **not** claiming that `detached: false` or console sharing is the root cause of this incident. The exact termination trigger remains unknown — and that is the observability gap this report is about.

## Why this is hard to diagnose today

After restart, the durable evidence can establish that a turn was crash-orphaned, but not **why the host terminated**. In this incident several plausible explanations remain observationally equivalent:

- external Ctrl+C / console close / parent termination
- an external `Stop-Process` / task kill
- uncaught exception or unhandled rejection in the host
- orderly shutdown triggered elsewhere while a turn is open
- another fatal runtime path with no Windows Error Reporting entry

The repaired session only says `interrupted`, so postmortem analysis cannot resolve these cases.

## Suggested improvement

Persist host-lifecycle provenance separately from the synthetic turn closer, for example:

1. Assign each web runtime a `bootId` and persist a small startup marker (`pid`, `startedAt`, version).
2. Before handled shutdown paths dispose jobs, persist a shutdown tombstone with a normalized cause such as `sigint`, `sigterm`, `process-exit`, `uncaught-exception`, `unhandled-rejection`, `user-requested`, etc.
3. On next startup, if the previous boot has no shutdown tombstone, explicitly classify it as `unclean/unknown` rather than silently losing the distinction.
4. When repairing an orphaned turn, expose a real `recoveredAt` plus the previous boot provenance (or an explicit `unknown`) through a structured recovery event / diagnostic surface.
5. Keep the provider-valid synthetic `turn/end {kind:"interrupted"}` if needed; the missing piece is a durable host-level crash ledger / recovery provenance, not a different transcript repair algorithm.

Even when the OS cannot reveal the exact cause after a hard kill, distinguishing **known handled shutdown** from **unclean unknown termination**, and recording the real recovery time, would make these incidents much more diagnosable.

## Related discussions

- #6107 covers how crash-recovery synthetic tool outcomes are presented and how their timestamps reuse the last real event time. This report is narrower on the missing **host termination provenance** needed to answer “why did the Harness process exit?”.
- #6407 covers a different interrupted-turn + background-job resume persistence corruption case.
- #7520 is a separate model-switch / pi-ai context-overflow report; the earlier overflow in this session recovered normally and is not being proposed as the cause of this host termination.

No credentials, API keys, provider endpoints, or account secrets are included here.

discussions.title: 希望尽快发布官方桌面端
[Bug] 解析拦截器对只读 stack 赋值抛 TypeError，导致全部插件元信息报错（v0.1.7-alpha.2 / tsx 启动）
discussions.body:
> 本仓库 Issues 已关闭，因此这份 bug 报告发布在 Discussions。下面是完整的环境、根因、最小复现与修复建议。

## 环境

- DSH 版本：`dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.2`（`active.json` 指向的已安装版本）
- 平台：Windows，Node `v22.20.0`（DSH Desktop 内置 runtime）
- 启动方式：`node --import tsx/esm apps/cli/src/bin.ts web --no-open --port 0`

## 现象

设置 → 插件页面里，**几乎所有插件**的元信息都报错：

```
包元信息错误：Plugin metadata for @deepseek-ai/dsh-persona: TypeError: Cannot assign to read only property 'stack' of object 'Error: Package subpath './locale/en.json' is not defined by "exports" in C:\...\versions\dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.2\repo\apps\cli\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\dsh-persona\package.json imported from C:\...\dsh-home\profiles\web\'
```

不止 persona：`@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill`、`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill` 等大批包同样报错（用户反馈"这样的还很多"）。

## 根因

1. `packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile-resolution/resolver.ts` 的 `throwWithImporter()` 在把解析路由到 declarer 后失败时改写诊断：

```ts
const stack = error.stack
error.message = message
if (stack !== undefined) error.stack = stack.replace(originalMessage, message)  // ← 罪魁
```

2. 当宿主用 tsx（`--import tsx/esm`）启动时，Node 抛出的 `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` 错误，其 `stack` 是 **own data property 且 `writable: false`**：

```json
{"value":"Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: ...","writable":false,"enumerable":false,"configurable":true}
```

3. 于是 `error.stack = ...` 抛 `TypeError`，而 `TypeError` **没有 `code`**。
4. `packages/boot/app-boot/src/package-meta.ts` 的 `missingResource()` 只识别 `error.code`，认不出"这个包没有导出 locale"，导致 `optionalResourcePath()` 不再返回 `undefined`，`readPluginMeta()` 把它当作元信息错误上报。
5. 绝大多数包本来就没有 `./locale/en.json` 导出（仓库 `packages/` 下 578 个包目录里只有 6 个带 `locale/en.json`），因此**凡是缺 locale 的包全部中招**。

## 最小复现

```ts
// 用 DSH 自带的 node 执行：node --import tsx/esm repro.ts
import { ModuleLoader } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader'

const loader = ModuleLoader.fromInternal()!
const base = 'file:///C:/Users/<user>/AppData/Roaming/dsh-desktop/dsh-home/profiles/web/'
try {
  // Node 22 / loader v1；Node 24 v2 为 resolveSync(parentURL, { specifier, attributes })
  loader.resolveSync('@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona/locale/en.json', base, {})
} catch (e: any) {
  console.log(e.code)                                      // ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED
  console.log(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(e, 'stack'))  // {"writable":false,"configurable":true}
  e.stack = 'x'                                             // TypeError: Cannot assign to read only property 'stack'
}
```

去掉 `--import tsx/esm` 后，同一错误的 `stack` 可写，问题不出现。

## 建议修复

改写 stack 时不要假定可写：

```ts
function rewriteStack(error: Error, original: string, message: string): void {
  const stack = error.stack
  if (stack === undefined) return
  const rewritten = stack.replace(original, message)
  if (rewritten === stack) return
  try {
    error.stack = rewritten
  } catch {
    try {
      Object.defineProperty(error, 'stack', { value: rewritten, writable: true, configurable: true })
    } catch {
      // 保留原 stack 文本即可；message 已标注真实 importer
    }
  }
}
```

`throwWithImporter` 与 `throwWithoutCjsAnchor` 两处都应改用它。

可选加固（防御任何包装层丢失 `code`）：`missingResource()` 除了 `error.code`，也识别 Node 的 `is not defined by "exports"` / `Cannot find module` 文本，避免把"没有元数据"误报成错误。

## 影响面

- 设置页插件清单大面积显示"包元信息错误"，掩盖真实症状，误导排查方向；
- 插件与技能的元信息（标题、描述、图标）全部退化为 fallback；
- 所有依赖 `readPluginMeta` 的界面都受影响。

## 修复后验证

- `readPluginMeta('@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona' | '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill' | '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill')` 恢复正常元信息，`error` 字段消失；
- 拦截路由后的错误保留 `code = ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`，不再被 TypeError 顶替；
- `packages/boot/app-boot/tests/package-meta.spec.ts` + `tests/profile-resolution.spec.ts`：**303 passed / 1 skipped，0 failed**。

discussions.title: [Bug] 0.1.7-alpha.1 and alpha.2: a failed startup still consumes settings.yaml - legacy sections import into a disposed context and are lost permanently
discussions.body:
## Summary

Upgrading `0.1.6-alpha.2` → `0.1.7-alpha.1`, the first launch **consumed** `~/.dsh/settings.yaml` although that launch had failed its startup audit. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot` disposes the plugin tree when the audit rejects a required entry, and the one-shot legacy import is a continuation of the same loader-settled moment, so all 10 sections were written into an already-disposed context:

```
settings-forms: settings: section %s of %s was not imported into entry %s
  'ui-onboarding', '$HOME/.dsh/settings.yaml.imported', 'ui-settings-general'

settings-forms: Error: cannot get required service "configEditor" in inactive context
    at SettingsForms.write (packages/settings/settings/src/index.ts:382:37)
    at SettingsForms.update (packages/settings/settings/src/index.ts:349:16)
    at SettingsForms.importLegacyDocument (packages/settings/settings/src/index.ts:251:20)
```

The document is renamed to `settings.yaml.imported` *before* the first write (`index.ts:245-246`, described in `packages/settings/settings/README.md:35`), and the import returns early whenever `settings.yaml` is absent (`index.ts:244`), so no later launch retries. The operator-visible result: the settings page comes up with defaults — LLM providers, theme, permission preset, default agent preset, default model, subagent model selection all reverted — and the only surviving copy of those values is the renamed file.

This matters beyond one deployment because the import path is new in this release (`601d6761e4`, "feat(settings): project volatile Config through profile-backed forms (#4587)", contained in `dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1`): every user upgrading from ≤0.1.6 goes through it exactly once. The same upgrade also makes a *failing* first launch likely, since 0.1.7 refuses to activate entries whose artifacts are stale (`web-app` frontend dist, `client-modules` bundles), and the documented upgrade step is a rebuild — one launch before the rebuild finishes is enough to lose the settings. The import path is unchanged in `dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.2`: between the two tags this package differs only in its `package.json`, so the failure reproduces there as well.

## Environment

- `dsh 0.1.7-alpha.1` (`c36a83ff6b`), source launch, macOS 15 (arm64), Node v24.18.0
- profile `web`; its patch enables HMR (`- id: hmr`, `disabled: false`)
- also checked on `dsh 0.1.7-alpha.2` (`00102833df`): the settings package differs between alpha.1 and alpha.2 only in its `package.json`, so this reproduces there too
- `$HOME/.dsh/settings.yaml` left by `0.1.6-alpha.2`, 10 sections: `ui-onboarding`, `ui-theme`, `agent-presets`, `permission`, `agent-default-model`, `llm-pi-ai`, `provider-quotas`, `dsh-better-sidebar`, `glance-theme`, `subagent-model-selection`

## Timeline

From the startup diagnostics dump of that launch (`$HOME/.dsh/logs/startup-2026-09-22T14-06-35.304Z-<uuid>.log`):

```
ts 1790085985630 = 14:06:25.630Z  launch: 2 required plugins did not activate
                                  (stale frontend dist / client bundles — an understood, separate failure;
                                   the loader needs ~10 s to settle the pending entries)
ts 1790085995278 = 14:06:35.278Z  hmr: 'config reload at %C failed', '$HOME/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json'
ts 1790085995278 = 14:06:35.278Z  hmr: Error: HMR is disposed            (packages/boot/hmr/src/index.ts:142)
ts 1790085995288 = 14:06:35.288Z  settings-forms: 'section ui-onboarding … was not imported'
ts 1790085995288 = 14:06:35.288Z  settings-forms: Error: cannot get required service "configEditor" in inactive context
… 10 sections, all at ts …288
```

`settings: imported %s into profile %s` (`index.ts:257`) appears in no log of any launch.

## Root cause

1. `packages/settings/settings/src/index.ts:235` — the import is a one-shot continuation of Loader settlement:
   `void ctx.root.loader.await().then(() => this.importLegacyDocument()).catch((error) => { ctx.logger.error(error) })`.
2. `packages/boot/app-boot/src/index.ts:971-977` — the startup audit is a continuation of the same moment: `await ctx.get('loader')?.await()`, then `await auditStartupEntries(ctx, binName)` throws `StartupError` for inactive required entries, and the catch disposes the tree with `await ctx.fiber.dispose()`. On a failed launch, the import and the disposal of its own fiber therefore start from the same settled Loader.
3. `index.ts:382` — every write resolves `this.ownerContext.configEditor` on the context captured in the constructor. After disposal that is `cannot get required service "configEditor" in inactive context` (`vendor/cordis/src/reflect.ts:160`).
4. `index.ts:248-256` — the per-section `try/catch` downgrades that to a warning and the loop continues; the same `catch` is the intended path for "the running composition rejects this section" (README:35), so a dead service and a rejected section are indistinguishable here.
5. `index.ts:245-246` renames the document before any write — deliberate, so that a partial import never repeats; `index.ts:244` then skips everything on later launches because `settings.yaml` no longer exists. The values survive only in `settings.yaml.imported`, and nothing tells the operator.
6. `this.closed` already exists (set by the effect disposer, `index.ts:227`) but `importLegacyDocument` never consults it, so the service keeps writing after its own disposal. Note also that `index.ts:257` logs `settings: imported …` unconditionally after the loop: a launch that imported nothing can still report success.

The `hmr: config reload … failed` / `HMR is disposed` pair in the same 10 ms window is a symptom of that teardown (`closing` is only set when the HMR service itself is disposed), not a second cause; a profile recomposition during the same window would fail in exactly the same way.

## Minimal reproduction

```sh
# a harness home holding a legacy document
printf 'ui-theme:\n  preference: dark\n' > "$HOME/.dsh/settings.yaml"

# start a profile whose startup audit must fail: e.g. leave lib/ or dist/ older than
# sources so @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-modules or @deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app refuses to activate
dsh --profile web --no-open
# ⇒ settings.yaml becomes settings.yaml.imported; one warning per section:
#    cannot get required service "configEditor" in inactive context

dsh --profile web --no-open        # this launch succeeds
# ⇒ no import attempt, no warning; the value stays in settings.yaml.imported forever
```

## Suggested fixes

1. **Import only after a healthy startup.** Schedule `importLegacyDocument` from application readiness (`appReady` / the `app-boot/config-reload` path) rather than from `loader.await()`; a launch that failed its audit then leaves the document untouched for the next launch.
2. **Make the rename a postcondition.** Import first, rename afterwards (or record per-section completion, or delete imported sections from the source), so a pass that wrote nothing can be retried.
3. **Treat a disposed service as a failure, not as a section rejection.** Check `this.closed` / context liveness before each write and abort the loop with an error that keeps the document, instead of 10 warnings and a success line.
4. **Report loudly when nothing was imported.** A boot that could not import any section should say so (`settings: 0 of N sections imported; values remain in <path>.imported`), so providers do not vanish without a trace.

## Our workaround (no data was lost)

We restored all restorable sections by hand: each one became a config override row in `$HOME/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` (`- id: <entry id>` plus `config: …`), validated against the 0.1.7 Config schemas; `provider-quotas` needed no restore because that plugin now keeps its own storage. Two sections could not be restored by configuration at all and are third-party plugin work: `glance-theme` (the plugin still calls the removed `ctx.settings.register`) and `dsh-better-sidebar` (not mounted any more).

## Test to extend

`packages/settings/settings/tests/configuration.spec.ts:310` ("imports the removed settings.yaml into the profile once and keeps rejected sections in the renamed file") covers rename-first and rejected sections, but never disposes the settings fiber while the import is in flight. A case that disposes the tree between `start()` and the first write — or that makes `configEditor` unavailable — would pin the ordering.
