discussions.title: [Idea] 将 --unsigned 本地打包路径扩展到 macOS（目前仅 win-x64）
discussions.body:
### 背景

`--unsigned` 打包路径目前只支持 Windows x64（`apps/desktop/README.md` 的 "Unsigned Windows test installer"），用于无签名凭据的本地安装测试。macOS 没有对等路径：`package:mac:arm64` 硬性要求 Developer ID 证书、公证凭据、keychain 配置，以及 prepare 阶段的 seed Mach-O 签名。没有发布证书的贡献者，无法从源码构建一个可直接安装进 /Applications 的桌面 App。

### 我的本地实践

我在一个本地分支上维护了一组约 90 行的补丁，把现有 `--unsigned` 路径扩展到 macOS，跟随 master rebase 使用，从 0.1.6 到 0.1.7-alpha.2 在 arm64 上一直可用。改动全部以既有的 `DSH_DESKTOP_UNSIGNED` 环境变量 / `--unsigned` 标志为条件，签名与 CI 路径不受影响：

1. `electron-builder-config.mjs` — 允许 darwin 平台使用 unsigned；unsigned 时跳过签名/公证环境解析，`forceCodeSigning: false`、`notarize: false`，并跳过 afterSign 的签名验证与 DMG 公证 hook。
2. `package-target.ts` / `smoke-packaged-runtime.ts` — `--unsigned` 接受 `mac-*` target；跳过签名 keychain 包装与 notarize 步骤；smoke 检查改从 `unsigned-artifacts/` 取产物。
3. `prepare-dsh.ts` — unsigned 时跳过 seed Mach-O 签名（本地没有 Developer ID 证书）。
4. unsigned 构建不内嵌 `dshMandatoryUpdatePolicy`（原因见下面的开放问题）。

产物写入 `unsigned-artifacts/`，天然不可作为发布件，定位与 Windows unsigned 一致：仅限本地安装测试。

### 携带成本（为什么希望官方支持）

每次 release 我都需要把分支 rebase 到新 master，打包流程演进时会真实撞上冲突，两个最近的例子：

- 0.1.7 调整打包 stages 后，本地补丁需要一次专门的适配 commit；
- 0.1.7-alpha.1 把 `dsh-api-gateway` 变为 desktop 生产依赖，但 electron-builder 的收集器只跟随 dependencies，共享 peer 依赖 `@deepseek-ai/cordis` 没有进入 `app.asar/node_modules`，Electron 启动即 `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`。我临时加了一个把 cordis 声明为生产依赖的 workaround；alpha.2 上游正式修复（直接把 cordis 加进 dependencies）后，又与这个已多余的 workaround 在 rebase 时冲突。

### 建议

- 将 `--unsigned` 官方扩展到 macOS target，镜像 Windows 的本地测试定位：不要求签名/公证凭据，产物写入 `unsigned-artifacts/`，永远不具备发布上传资格。
- 开放问题：unsigned 构建是否应该内嵌 mandatory-update policy？目前 Windows unsigned 仍然要求选择 origin 并内嵌策略；而个人构建通常连不上发布源，内嵌策略会留下一个空白且阻塞退出的认证窗口，所以我在 macOS 上直接省略了 `dshMandatoryUpdatePolicy`。两个平台的 unsigned 行为是否应当统一（统一省略，还是统一要求提供可达 origin）？

如果团队觉得方向可行，我可以把这组补丁整理成 PR 提上来。

discussions.title: Agent-Body — plugins as organs: 26-organ catalog, a heartbeat, zero-model-call reflex arcs, sleep-time memory, closed-loop self-healing
discussions.body:
**Agent-Body** turns the plugin list into a body. Instead of another bundle of tools, it lets each plugin declare itself an **organ** — capabilities, senses, reflexes — and then runs the physiology *around* it: command routing, a heartbeat, reflex arcs, sleep, memory consolidation and closed-loop self-healing. Then it hides the capabilities you are not using this turn.

**Repo:** https://github.com/1420079678-ctrl/agent-body · MIT · topic `dsh-plugin`
**Catalog:** [`catalog/organs.json`](https://github.com/1420079678-ctrl/agent-body/blob/main/catalog/organs.json) declares **26 organs** in four install tiers (`core` / `general` / `professional` / `experimental`), each with its permissions and its fallback chain written down. Only **core + general** install by default, so a fresh session does not start with the entire capability surface on screen.

---

### The mechanisms

**1. Command → nerve impulse → organ.** The operator's sentence is routed deterministically to the organ that owns the intent, and the impulse says *which capability to use* — no model call, so the same sentence always reaches the same organ. Unrouted intents are counted rather than silently dropped.

**2. A heartbeat, not a loop wrapper.** A pacer carries law + interoception + homeostasis alerts to every organ. It is a real variable-rate clock: faster under alerts, slower when the body is quiet. Every plugin can subscribe to the heartbeat and join the circulation.

**3. Reflex arcs that fire with zero model calls.** Deterministic conditions (`error` / `ok` / `slow:N` / `hit:` / `miss:`, combinable), no `eval`, with re-entrancy suppression, cooldown and quotas so a reflex cannot become a loop. A repeated failure is answered by *logic*, not by thinking about it again.

**4. Sleep and consolidation.** Two minutes of quiet → light sleep; five → deep sleep. During deep sleep a **deterministic** pass (still zero model calls) turns run history into memory cards — pitfalls, playbooks, weak spots, unresolved items — which are then recalled when a matching command arrives.

**5. Closed-loop self-healing.** Failure → attribution (`tool_missing` / `arg_error` / `permission` / `timeout` / `network` / `not_found` / `conflict`) → prescribed remedy (read-only ones run automatically; side-effecting ones are left to the model; **argument errors are never auto-retried**) → **re-check**, which only closes the wound when that organ actually succeeds next time. Plus: intent-gated tool schemas. Capabilities are surfaced per turn; a gated capability is one `body_call` away, never gone.

---

### See it work in 30 seconds — no install, no host, no API key

```bash
git clone https://github.com/1420079678-ctrl/agent-body && cd agent-body
npm run demo
```

Real output from a fresh clone (trimmed; the demo is bilingual and drives a real end-to-end chain — command → impulse → dispatch → execute → failure → attribution → reflex fires):

```
full tool schema        55154 tokens  (256 entries)
surfaced this turn      11031 tokens   (47 entries)
saved 80.0%
...
48 representative commands: mean token saving 84.71%, median 85.67%, worst 75.20%
correctness guardrail: 0 defects (must be 0) · 6 truncated · 0 unrouted
```

The truncated / unrouted ones are counted separately instead of being folded into the saving, because they cost an extra hop to recover. `benchmarks/results/REPORT.md` documents how the number was measured, and `npm run check` re-runs it offline.

### Install an organ into DSH

The self-contained organs ship prebuilt tarballs on the release page; the manifest declares `dsh.bundle`, so installing also mounts it on the next start:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/1420079678-ctrl/agent-body/releases/download/v0.1.0/dsh-external-dsh-organism-0.1.0.tgz
```

Ten organs ship this way (the ones needing no external toolchain); the rest are built from the repo by `replay-*.ps1` scripts.

### Evidence, not adjectives

| Command (run by me, on this repository) | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `node scripts/verify-repo.mjs` | `11 ok · 1 warning(s) · 0 failure(s)` |
| `node scripts/run-tests.mjs` | `tests 30 / pass 30 / fail 0` |
| `node workspace/plugins/dsh-organism/scripts/smoke-test.mjs` (installed harness) | `197 通过 / 0 失败` |

### Honest status

- **Not on npm yet.** Installs come from the release tarballs or the repo. I would rather say this than imply an `npm i`.
- First public release 2026-09-11; the repo ships offline regressions and a reproducible benchmark instead of a feature list.
- If you try it and something is wrong, telling me is more useful to me than praise — the honest failure modes are the interesting part.

---

## 中文

**Agent-Body** 把插件表变成一具身体：插件不再是一堆工具，而是各自声明为**器官**（能力、感知、反射），生理机制跑在它们周围——命令路由、心跳、反射弧、睡眠、记忆巩固、闭环自愈，再把这一轮用不到的能力收起来。

**仓库：** https://github.com/1420079678-ctrl/agent-body · MIT · topic `dsh-plugin`
**目录：** [`catalog/organs.json`](https://github.com/1420079678-ctrl/agent-body/blob/main/catalog/organs.json) 声明 **26 个器官**、四个安装分级（核心 / 通用 / 专业 / 实验），每个器官写明权限与代偿链。默认只装核心 + 通用，新会话第一屏不会铺满全部能力。

**五个机制：** ①命令按意图确定性路由到负责它的器官，指明用哪个能力，零模型调用；②真起搏器式心跳，按内环境变速（告警加快、静默放慢）；③反射弧用确定性条件求值（无 `eval`），命中即执行、零模型调用，带重入抑制与冷却；④静默 2 分钟浅睡、5 分钟深睡，深睡里用确定性规则把经历巩固成记忆卡；⑤失败走「归因 → 处方 → 复检」，参数错误绝不自动重试，器官下次成功才闭合伤口。外加按意图显影工具 schema——被收起的能力一次 `body_call` 就能取回。

**30 秒看到它在干活（不用装、不用宿主、不用 API key）：**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/1420079678-ctrl/agent-body && cd agent-body
npm run demo
```

Demo 在本机真实跑出的结果（节选）：全量 tool schema 55154 token（256 项）→ 这一轮显影 11031 token（47 项），省 80.0%；48 条代表性命令平均省 84.71%、中位 85.67%、最差 75.20%，正确性缺陷 0。可信度不靠形容词：`benchmarks/results/REPORT.md` 写明口径，`npm run check` 离线复跑。

**装进 DSH：** 自带预构建 tarball、声明了 `dsh.bundle`，一条命令即装（见上文命令）。

**当前状态：** npm 包尚未发布（从 release tarball 或仓库安装）；2026-09-11 首次公开发布，仓库里放的是离线回归与可复现基准，不是功能清单。有反馈直接说，哪里不对告诉我比夸我更有用。

discussions.title: V3 accepts {kind:'plugin'} but V4 refuses it — plugin-authored injected messages have no literal that satisfies both
discussions.body:
V3 validation and V4 admission disagree about plugin-authored message sources, and there is **no literal that satisfies both**. Every out-of-tree plugin that injects messages the way the V3 tree taught will fail on 0.1.7 with `format v4 message requires a producer-owned source kind`. Reporting it with source citations; corrections welcome if I have misread something.

## The two rules

**V3 accepts `'plugin'`, and refuses anything it does not recognise.** `packages/session/session-format-v2-to-v3/src/payload.ts`:

```ts
const SOURCE_KINDS = new Set(['user', 'plugin', 'model', 'tool', 'agent-instructions', 'session-reference', 'team-message', 'goal', 'skill-invocation', 'skill-catalog', 'coordinator', 'subagent-report', 'subagent-settled', 'webhook', 'agent-message'])

function assertSource(message) {
  const source = record(message['source'], 'message source')
  if (typeof source['kind'] !== 'string' || !SOURCE_KINDS.has(source['kind']))
    throw new SessionFormatUnsupportedMigrationError('cannot safely transform unclassified message source')
}
```

`'plugin'` is in that closed set; `'plugin:<name>'` is **not**. Line 237 of the same file goes further and *requires* the retired literal for system messages: `if (source['kind'] !== 'plugin' || typeof source['plugin'] !== 'string' …) throw new SessionFormatError('system message requires plugin source')`.

**V4 refuses `'plugin'`** — `packages/session/session-format-v3-to-v4/src/message-sources.ts`, with the rejected set pinned by the spec (`null, [], {}, {kind:''}, {kind:1}, {kind:'plugin',plugin:'compact'}`):

```ts
if (!isSessionFormatJsonObject(value) || typeof value['kind'] !== 'string'
    || value['kind'].length === 0 || value['kind'] === 'plugin')
  throw new SessionFormatError('format v4 message requires a producer-owned source kind')
```

So on a V3 host, `{kind:'plugin', plugin:'X'}` is the only accepted form; on a V4 host it is the one refused form, and the accepted form (`{kind:'plugin:X'}`) fails V3 admission with `cannot safely transform unclassified message source`. Neither literal is portable.

## Why this only bites out-of-tree plugins

In the 0.1.6 tree, **every** producer writes the retired literal — first-party included: `session-title-llm` (`session-title-llm/src/index.ts:250`), `plan-mode` (`:461`), `cordis-host-runner` (five sites), `time-context` (`:217`), `tmux-context` (`:259`), `schedule` (`runtime.ts:271`), `hooks-codex` / `hooks-claude-code` (`PLUGIN_SOURCE`), `agent-instructions` (`state.ts:96`), `compaction-basic` (`summarizer.ts:148`), `tools-ptc` (`ptc.ts:635`), plus the migration paths themselves. A code search of current `master` for that literal returns **nothing**: the repo-wide sweep happened in-tree, and the V3→V4 migration converts V3 *rows* on read — so nothing in the shipped configuration breaks.

An installed third-party plugin has neither benefit. It keeps emitting the retired literal on a V4 host, `encodeCurrentEvent` refuses it on the write path, and the user sees exactly the failure reported in #7546 — "本轮运行失败". Same for the read path, where `assertV4SourceRowAdmission` refuses retired wrappers in every declared message slot before recovery can discard them.

## Measurement on a real machine (0.1.6-alpha.2)

I scanned this host's session logs for the pattern (multi-frame zstd, so the frames have to be walked — a single-frame decompressor misses everything after the first frame). One session, 12,019 rows: **85 messages still carry `{kind:'plugin'}`, from five producers** — `tool-jobs` (76), `repeat-tool-reminder` (4), `user-approval` (2), `@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt` (2), `dsh-session-title-llm` (1). That file is header `version: 0`, so the migration chain converts those rows on read and the session still opens — which is precisely why this stays invisible until a plugin *writes* under V4 rather than having its history read.

## What would close the gap

Two things, either of which is sufficient for plugin authors:

1. **State the migration in the plugin-facing docs** — the mapping is already deterministic in `producerKind()`: third-party producers become `plugin:<their name>` and drop the `plugin` field; the 24 names in `RELEASED_SAME_NAME_PRODUCERS` keep their own name. Right now that rule is discoverable only by reading `session-format-v3-to-v4` source, and the V3 tree still contains hundreds of counterexamples to imitate.
2. **Expose a producer-side helper** (e.g. a session-scoped `injectedSource(name)`) so a plugin asks the host for the version-correct source instead of hardcoding either literal. As long as the source is hand-built, a plugin that supports both harness generations has to branch on the session format version itself, and a plugin that does not branch is silently broken by an upgrade.

Happy to test a candidate helper on both generations if that is useful — I have a 0.1.6 install and a 0.1.7 target, and can report what each accepts. Disclosure so the report is not read as finger-pointing: our own organs write the retired literal too, so they are in the affected population; that is how I found this.

discussions.title: [Bug & RFC][llm-pi-ai] TypeError in modelOf & 关于像 OpenCode Go 这类动态多协议聚合网关的模型治理提案
discussions.body:
# [Bug & RFC / Architecture Proposal]: Defending Custom Providers & Evolving DSH Model Management for Dynamic Multi-Protocol Gateways (OpenCode Go / OpenRouter)

> **Submission Target**: `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness` GitHub Issues / Discussions  
> **Component**: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-model-selection`  
> **Affected Version**: `0.1.7-alpha.1` (and backward compatibility across `0.1.x`)  
> **Author**: DSH Community Contributor & Power User  

---

## Part 1. Urgent Bug Report: Unhandled TypeError in `PiAiAdapter.prototype.modelOf`

### 1.1 Summary
In `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai@0.1.7-alpha.1`, the internal lookup method `modelOf` attempts to retrieve model-specific diagnostics via `profile.modelErrors.get(model)` without defensive optional chaining (`?.`). When an adapter or dynamic provider profile does not instantiate an explicit `modelErrors` Map, this triggers an unhandled `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'get')`.

When `buildModelCatalog` in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-session-controller` invokes `ctx.llm.resolveModelInfo` during startup, this exception collapses the entire provider group into a failure state, rendering an unrecoverable orange banner in the Web UI:
> `OpenCode Go 加载失败: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'get') [重试]`

### 1.2 Exact Stack Trace
```text
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'get')
    at PiAiAdapter.modelOf (file://.../@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai/lib/index.js:1779:39)
    at PiAiAdapter.modelInfo (file://.../@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai/lib/index.js:1814:30)
    at file://.../@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai/lib/index.js:1809:16
    at buildModelCatalog (file://.../@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-session-controller/lib/index.js:1957:33)
```

### 1.3 Root Cause Code
In `dsh-llm-pi-ai/lib/index.js` (line 1779):
```js
// Current implementation (v0.1.7-alpha.1):
modelOf(snapshot, provider, model) {
    const profile = this.profileOf(snapshot, provider);
    const failure = profile.modelErrors.get(model) ?? (profile.piProvider === void 0 ? profile.catalogError : void 0);
    ...
```

### 1.4 Immediate Suggested Fix (1-line PR)
```diff
- const failure = profile.modelErrors.get(model) ?? (profile.piProvider === void 0 ? profile.catalogError : void 0);
+ const failure = profile.modelErrors?.get(model) ?? (profile.piProvider === void 0 ? profile.catalogError : void 0);
```

---

## Part 2. RFC & Architectural Feedback: How DSH Should Better Manage Dynamic Multi-Protocol Model Gateways

Beyond the 1-line crash fix, this issue highlights a fundamental architectural tension in DSH's current model management design: **the gap between static single-provider assumptions and the reality of modern multi-model aggregators (e.g., OpenCode Go, OpenRouter, SiliconFlow).**

### 2.1 Current Pain Points for Developers & End Users

#### Pain Point 1: Static YAML Inventory vs. Rapidly Evolving Gateway Offerings
* **The Reality**: Gateways like OpenCode Go or OpenRouter add and update models almost weekly (e.g. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GLM-5.3, Qwen 3.8, Kimi K3, MiniMax M3).
* **The DSH Friction**: Currently, users must either:
  1. Manually curate a 200+ line static YAML catalog in `cordis.patch.yml` under `llm-pi-ai.config.providers.<id>.models`, requiring manual copy-pasting of context windows, reasoning formats, and max tokens, followed by full host restarts; OR
  2. Write handwritten adapter plugins that resort to **monkey-patching `ctx.llm.listModels` and `ctx.llm.resolveModelInfo`**, bypassing the intended lifecycle.

#### Pain Point 2: Heterogeneous Protocols within a Single Provider Route
* Modern aggregators do not speak a single API dialect. For instance, in OpenCode Go:
  - **Qwen 3.8 / MiniMax M3**: Routed via Anthropic Messages protocol (`/v1/messages`);
  - **Grok 4.6 / GPT 5.6 Luna**: Routed via OpenAI Responses protocol (`/v1/responses`);
  - **GLM 5.3 / Kimi K3**: Routed via OpenAI Chat Completions protocol (`/v1/chat/completions`).
* DSH's native configuration binds the entire provider block to a single `api: <dialect>` property (e.g., `api: openai-completions`), making it impossible to support heterogeneous multi-protocol gateways natively in declarative configuration without writing custom adapters.

#### Pain Point 3: Fragile Internal Coupling & Breaking Changes across Minor Versions
Because DSH does not yet expose a first-class, versioned public API for registering dynamic model providers, developers who build adapters must hook directly into internal primitives (like `PiAiAdapter`, `ctx.waterfall('llm/stream')`, or monkey-patching `ctx.llm`). As a result:
* In `v0.1.2`, removing `deepFreeze` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` broke custom adapters with ESM link errors.
* In `v0.1.7`, introducing unguarded `profile.modelErrors.get()` broke catalog resolution.

#### Pain Point 4: Coarse Error Blast Radius in UI
When metadata resolution for a single model throws an unexpected error, `dsh-api-session-controller` fails the *entire* provider group (`kind: "failure"`). The UI then completely disables all models from that provider and shows an opaque JavaScript exception (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'get')`) rather than isolating the failure to the specific problematic model or providing actionable debug logs.

---

### 2.2 Proposed Architectural Blueprint for DSH

We propose three high-leverage enhancements for future DSH releases:

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   DSH Unified LLM Subsystem (RFC)                      │
└──────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                                   │
         ┌─────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                   ▼
┌───────────────────────────────┐           ┌────────────────────────────────┐
│   Static Declarative Routes   │           │    Dynamic Provider Protocol   │
│   (cordis.patch.yml / yaml)   │           │ (ctx.llm.registerProvider API) │
└──────────────┬────────────────┘           └───────────────┬────────────────┘
               │                                            │
               │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐  │
               └─►│  Per-Model Multi-Protocol Dispatch   │◄─┘
                  │  - /v1/chat/completions              │
                  │  - /v1/messages                      │
                  │  - /v1/responses                     │
                  └──────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                                     │
                                     ▼
                  ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │    Resilient Catalog & Isolation    │
                  │    - Partial model-level degradation│
                  │    - Auto-metadata fallback (1M ctx)│
                  │    - Live catalog refresh (/models) │
                  └─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

#### Proposal A: First-Class `ctx.llm.registerProvider()` Extension Point
Instead of requiring plugins to monkey-patch `ctx.llm.listModels = ...`, introduce a formal Cordis service interface:

```typescript
export interface DynamicLlmProvider {
  id: string;
  displayName: string;
  /** Live or cached model discovery */
  listModels(): Promise<ModelDescriptor[]>;
  /** Model-specific metadata (contextWindow, reasoning, inputModalities) */
  resolveModel(modelId: string): Promise<ResolvedModelInfo>;
  /** Stream execution with multi-protocol support */
  stream(options: StreamOptions): AsyncIterable<StreamChunk>;
}

// In plugin apply():
ctx.llm.registerProvider(new OpenCodeGoProvider(config));
```

#### Proposal B: Native Support for Per-Model Protocol Specifications
Allow declaring `api` (and corresponding protocol-specific `compat` flags) at the individual model level within `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: llm-pi-ai
  config:
    providers:
      opencode-go:
        displayName: OpenCode Go
        baseURL: https://opencode.ai/zen/go
        models:
          - id: qwen3.8-max
            api: anthropic-messages      # <-- Per-model protocol routing
            contextWindow: 1000000
          - id: grok-4.6
            api: openai-responses         # <-- Per-model protocol routing
            contextWindow: 500000
          - id: glm-5.3
            api: openai-completions       # <-- Per-model protocol routing
            contextWindow: 1000000
```

#### Proposal C: Live Model Catalog Discovery with Metadata Enrichment
Gateway `/v1/models` endpoints provide real-time lists of available model IDs, but often omit context windows, pricing, and token bounds.
DSH could natively integrate a **hybrid model catalog strategy**:
1. **Discovery Layer**: Fetch `/v1/models` from the gateway endpoint.
2. **Enrichment Layer**: Merge with standardized community metadata registries (such as [models.dev/api.json](https://models.dev)) or apply sensible defaults (e.g. `contextWindow: 1_000_000`, `maxTokens: 131_072`).
3. **Resilience Layer**: If an individual model's descriptor cannot be resolved, mark that single model as unavailable while keeping the rest of the provider's models functional in the dropdown.

---

### 2.3 Community Impact
Adopting these proposals will:
1. Make DSH the most developer-friendly harness for Chinese & international multi-model gateways (OpenCode Go, OpenRouter, SiliconFlow, Together AI, DeepInfra).
2. Eliminate frequent regressions where custom adapters break upon minor core harness updates.
3. Greatly enhance UI resilience and user experience when external gateway catalogs experience transient issues.

discussions.title: v0.1.5-rc2使用npm 11 无法启动
discussions.body:
触发原因：在 Windows 上跑 `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`，但 @deepseek-ai/dsh 依赖的 koffi 带了一堆平台专属的可选二进制包。日志里可以看到：
```
22 silly fetch manifest @koromix/koffi-darwin-x64@3.3.0     ← 这是 macOS(x64) 的二进制包
26 silly placeDep ROOT @koromix/koffi-darwin-x64@3.3.0 ...
```
npm 11.x 的 arborist 在处理这种「平台不匹配的可选依赖」做 dedupe 时，对可选平台的版本占位符解析成了空串，撞上 semver 空版本 bug。这是 mailto:npm@11.6.2 + 含多平台可选依赖的包的一个已知兼容问题，不是命令写错了。

处理办法：
不使用官网的npx，而是使用pnpm：
```
npm i -g pnpm
pnpm dlx @deepseek-ai/dsh web
```

discussions.title: dsh-taskflow · AI 合同式任务看板 —— AI 拆解实现举证，人来验收，done 由你说了算
discussions.body:
## dsh-taskflow · AI 合同式任务看板 —— 你出验收标准，AI 交活，done 由你说了算

一个 dsh Web 插件：把「让 AI 干活」变成一份份**合同**。你创建任务（验收标准可给可不给），AI 自己拆解、自己实现、自己举证；人来验收，通过才算 done，不通过打回继续迭代，全过程状态留痕。

![任务看板](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LuckVd/dsh-taskflow/main/design/previews/opt3-light.png)

### 为什么是「合同」？

卡片不是提示词的容器，而是一份合同：**做什么 + 怎么算做完 + 准许动用什么**。看板是共享黑板的实时视图，调度器把「就绪的合同」喂给会话，验收人让「done」两个字有含金量。

### 核心功能

- **📋 合同式建卡** —— 目标 + 验收标准（可让 AI 起草/细化）；权限模式（完全权限 / 需要审批）；能力预设（修 Bug/新功能/技术调研/清理）；工作目录钉定、任务级并发与模型覆盖；cron 定时建卡 + webhook 远程建卡（CI 可用）
- **🤖 AI 拆解与执行** —— 自动拆成子任务 DAG，按依赖调度；WIP 并发上限、依赖守卫防死锁、受挫显式标记、Token 用量回采
- **⚖️ 验收只对合同，过程归 AI** —— 子任务跑完 AI 自动跑「任务级终检」产出交付证据卡；验收台判定面优先，交付物直接预览；打回只写批语，AI triage 自动定位返工范围（沿 DAG 回退下游）
- **🔗 任务接续 / 血缘 DAG** —— done 卡「接续新任务」签新合同，逐父交接摘要注入下次拆解；看板血缘连线、族谱视图
- **🔔 通知、批量与统计** —— 提权审批通知、浏览器系统通知、批量验收/归档、吞吐/一次通过率统计

### 验收工作台

![验收工作台](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LuckVd/dsh-taskflow/main/design/previews/review-opt3-light.png)

### 流程可视化与任务接续

任务详情「流程」tab：完整管线 **AI 拆解 → 子任务 DAG → AI 终检 → 人工终批**，点任意节点看执行轨迹。

![流程 tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LuckVd/dsh-taskflow/main/design/previews/lineage-flow-light.png)

done 卡可「接续新任务」，看板上实时渲染血缘连线（hover 高亮本链）：

![血缘连线](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LuckVd/dsh-taskflow/main/design/previews/lineage-board-light.png)

### 安装

```sh
git clone https://github.com/LuckVd/dsh-taskflow.git
cd dsh-taskflow && npm install && npm run build
dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-taskflow
# 重启宿主，侧栏出现「任务看板」即成功
```

详细配置（本地 link 开发、cron/webhook 建卡等）见 [README](https://github.com/LuckVd/dsh-taskflow#安装与配置)。

### 状态

M1–M3 全量落地，PRD FR 清单收口；211 个测试全绿（unit / e2e / 客户端渲染冒烟）。欢迎试用 + 提 issue：https://github.com/LuckVd/dsh-taskflow

反馈方向特别想听：验收台的判定面信息密度、打回 triage 的返工范围定位准不准、以及大家想要什么样的统计口径。

discussions.title: 进一步扩大子代理自定义程度（如原会话使用极简模式而子代理使用PTC模式）
discussions.body:
结合社区使用和实际表现来看，Deepseek v4.1 flash是一个能力很强但理解能力较差的模型，想要用好这个模型依赖高质量的提示词或干脆使用能力更强的模型进行指导
出于以上考虑，我结合这两周的使用经验以模型预设的形式为Deepseek v4.1 flash设计了一套防止过度思考的约束，在特定的场景下（如指令明确的算法题或边输出、边检查实现情况的长轮次对话中），可以有效抑制过度思考，并在维持模型能力的同时减少Token消耗。

于是此处出现了新问题：我想使用尺寸更大或能力更强的模型做规划，并以子代理的形式让v4.1flash执行任务。但实际操作中子代理必须继承原对话的预设，导致无法实现原会话使用“极简模式”而子代理使用特殊预设。
虽然可以通过跨会话派出实现这一点，但还是希望官方能给一处接口，或者提供标准的编辑方式，以防后续每次更新都需要重新适配

discussions.title: [Feature] 让外壳原生支持文件路径右键菜单（在资源管理器中打开 / 复制路径）
discussions.body:
正文

现状

聊天区经常出现文件路径，交付物包也已经把「本轮生成的文件」渲染成可点击 chip。但右键这类路径时菜单是空的，只能先用鼠标选中再 Ctrl+C。

桌面外壳其实已经有一个原生右键菜单（ 的 buildContextMenuTemplate），只是覆盖面止步于三类目标：

命中目标 | 现有菜单项 -- | -- 链接 | 在浏览器中打开链接 / 复制链接地址 图片 | 复制图片 可编辑区 | 撤销/重做/剪切/复制/粘贴/全选

文件路径不属于任何一类，菜单模板为空，直接 return。labels 字典里已经有中英文案，说明这套菜单是按"跟随系统、贴近编辑器体验"的思路做的，缺的只是路径这一类。

为什么值得做成原生能力

  1. 路径是高频内容。 交付物 chip、工具调用摘要、模型回复里的文件引用都会产生路径。现在每一条都要手动选中复制，再去资源管理器里粘贴。
  2. 路径语义已经存在，只是没被用上。 dsh-client-ui-deliverables 已经有一套 Codex 风格的路径识别（localPathReference）：绝对路径前缀、含分隔符、或带已知扩展名的裸文件名才当作路径，注释里明确说明裸文件名不猜。这套判断标准可以直接复用，不需要外壳重新发明。
  3. 能力已经在 preload 上，只差菜单项。  已经把 dshDesktop.openInFinder(path) 通过 contextBridge 暴露给渲染进程，主进程侧对应 harness:open-in-finder → shell.openPath(path)。也就是说"用默认程序打开"这条路已经通了，只是没有 UI 入口。

建议实现

菜单项按目标类型追加一节：

  • 在资源管理器中打开（，选中该文件）
  • 用默认程序打开（复用现有 harness:open-in-finder）
  • 打开所在文件夹（shell.openPath(dirname(path))）
  • 复制路径
  • 复制文件名

后两项纯剪贴板操作，在渲染层即可完成；前三项需要一个从渲染进程到外壳的转发。当前 preload 只暴露了 openInFinder，建议补两个：

js
revealInFolder: (path) => electron.ipcRenderer.invoke("harness:reveal-in-folder", path),
openContainingFolder: (path) => electron.ipcRenderer.invoke("harness:open-containing-folder", path)

实现时需要注意的四个坑

1. 路径识别不能太宽松。 内联代码里绝大多数内容是命令、包名、符号，不是路径。按下面的规则压误判效果较好：

  • 绝对前缀（、、、）直接认定
  • 含路径分隔符的认定
  • 裸文件名必须扩展名在已知格式白名单内

放宽到"有点号就认路径"会误报 、user@example.com、；再加一条"以 @ 开头的不认"可以排掉 npm scope 包名（@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm）。

2. 相对路径要按会话 cwd 解析，且要能报错。 用户手打的路径多半是相对工作区的。聊天区自己走的是 ctx.remote.session.openWorkspacePath，由宿主按会话 cwd 解析并在失败时给出精确原因；而 openInFinder 只接受绝对路径，相对路径会直接报"路径不存在"。原生菜单如果新增打开动作，建议走前者那条链路，或至少明确失败信息。

3. 可编辑区必须让路。 输入框里的右键菜单（撤销/粘贴/全选）比文件操作重要得多，任何拦截都要先排除 input、textarea、contenteditable。

4. 与波浪号展开的既有缺陷相关。 显示层刻意用  标注 home 路径（dsh-home-paths 的 dshHomeDisplay 注释写明 "never returns an absolute machine path"），而 Windows 分支 openWindowsPath 不展开 ~，导致这类链接在 Windows 上必然打不开。同一个模块里已经有 expandHomePath()，只是这条路径没调用它。原生菜单如果要做路径动作，建议一并修掉，否则右键「在资源管理器中打开」对 ~ 开头的路径同样会失败。

我做的验证

用一个纯客户端插件加两处外壳补丁做了原型，验证这套设计可行：

  • 插件走标准  声明加载，不改任何打包产物
  • 菜单按"外壳能力逐项探测"，缺方法就隐藏该项，因此 Web 版（没有 ）不会报错
  • 路径识别 20/21 通过（唯一残留是  这类无意义点号串，要排掉它就得拒绝多点的裸文件名，反而会误杀正常文件名，不值得）
  • 相对路径解析、绝对路径透传、~ 不拼工作区根，均验证正确

原型依赖两处外壳补丁才能在桌面端拿到全部功能，这也正是建议把它做成原生能力的原因：每次应用升级都要重放补丁，不是可持续的用法。

附：期望的最小可用范围

如果完整方案成本偏高，先做「复制路径 / 复制文件名」两项也很有价值——这两项不需要任何外壳新通道，纯渲染层就能完成，而且覆盖了最高频的痛点（现在必须手动选中复制）。

写客户端插件时的一个坑（顺带反馈）

纯客户端插件（ 声明 + ）的宿主半边仍然必须导出可加载的插件。若宿主半边是一个不导出任何东西的模块，加载器会报：

invalid plugin, expect function or object with an "apply" method, received object

因为该行是经 patch 层 insert 挂载的，这个失败会中断整棵插件树，harness 起不来，桌面端只能退到安全模式。宿主半边"什么都不做"与"不存在"是两回事，最小可用形态是：

js
export function apply() {}
export const inject = []

discussions.title: [Bug] revealNativePath does nothing on paths containing non-ASCII characters (e.g. CJK) - and reports success
discussions.body:
**TL;DR** — `revealNativePath` hands `explorer.exe /select,` a percent-encoded `file:///` URL where the switch expects a filesystem path. Explorer resolves that fine for purely ASCII paths, but for a path containing non-ASCII characters (CJK) it does **nothing at all** — no window, no error, no dialog. Since `explorer.exe` exits `1` even on success, that silent no-op is swallowed by the existing `catch`, the route answers `204`, and the Web client reports success. Net effect: **"Reveal in File Explorer" on a CJK path looks like it worked and nothing happens.**

### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| `dsh` | `0.1.5-rc.2` (also checked `0.1.5-rc.3`, `0.1.6-alpha.2`, `0.1.7-alpha.2`) |
| OS | Windows 11, system locale zh-CN |
| Package | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-native-command` → `revealNativePath` |
| Surface | Web client, deliverable card → "Reveal in File Explorer" |

### Where

The logic is byte-identical in every published version I checked — `0.1.5-rc.2` lines 228–234, `0.1.7-alpha.2` lines 239–245:

```js
const target = pathToFileURL(windowsPath, { windows: true }).href.replaceAll(",", "%2C");
try {
	await run("explorer.exe", ["/select,", target], signal);
} catch (error) {
	signal.throwIfAborted();
	if (!(error instanceof Error) || !("code" in error) || error.code !== 1) throw error;
}
```

For `C:\示例目录\报告.md` that produces

```
explorer.exe "/select," "file:///C:/%E7%A4%BA%E4%BE%8B%E7%9B%AE%E5%BD%95/%E6%8A%A5%E5%91%8A.md"
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a file at a path containing non-ASCII characters, e.g. `%TEMP%\示例目录\报告.md`.
2. Press "Reveal in File Explorer" on it (or invoke `revealNativePath` directly).
3. Nothing happens. No window, no error, HTTP `204`, the client shows the success toast.

Repeat with a pure ASCII path (`%TEMP%\plain\report.md`) and it works — which is why this goes unnoticed in ASCII-only environments.

### Measurements

Selection state read through UI Automation (`SelectionItemPattern.IsSelectedProperty`) rather than inferred, because `Shell.Application`'s `Document` refuses `FocusedItem`/`SelectedItems` with `DISP_E_NOTACOLLECTION`. Each trial uses a brand-new directory so Explorer window reuse cannot confuse the result. `A` = the code above, `B` = `["/select,", nativePath]`.

| file name | A (upstream `file:///` URL) | B (native path) |
|---|---|---|
| `plain.md` | opens + selects ✅ | opens + selects ✅ |
| `spa ced.md` | opens + selects ✅ | opens + selects ✅ |
| `pl,ain.md` | opens + selects ✅ (`%2C` works) | **no window** ❌ |
| `中文文件.md` | **no window** ❌ | opens + selects ✅ |
| `中文 文件.md` | **no window** ❌ | opens + selects ✅ |

`A` is consistent across five independent runs: **6/6 successes on ASCII-only names, 11/11 failures on any name containing CJK.** Interleaving A and B with three repetitions each (to cancel the ordering effect described below) gives A `3/3` failures and B `3/3` opens on a CJK path.

### Two separate defects

1. **Correctness — non-ASCII paths never reveal.** The percent-encoded URL form is not resolved by `explorer.exe /select,`. This is the common case for the users hit by it: any CJK project directory makes the feature a no-op. The same code path is used from WSL, after `wslpath -w`.

2. **Observability — the failure is reported as success.** `explorer.exe` returns `1` for both a successful handoff and a failure to resolve the path, and the `catch` deliberately treats `1` as success (the JSDoc even says *"Explorer exit 1 is accepted as a delegated handoff, not proof of selection"*). So `handlePresentOpen` returns `204`, the client shows a success toast, and there is no log line, no non-2xx status, and no user-visible error anywhere. This is what made the bug expensive to diagnose — the user-visible symptom is "the button does nothing", and every instrument says it succeeded.

### Suggested fix

The durable fix is to stop routing this through `explorer.exe` argument parsing at all and use the Shell API meant for it — `SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems` — which the package is already well placed to do, since it embeds and compiles C# for Windows file associations (`WINDOWS_ASSOCIATIONS`).

As a minimal interim change, keep the `%2C` substitution (it is load-bearing: a raw comma in the URL fails, verified 2/2, and a raw comma in a native path also fails 2/2) but stop percent-encoding non-ASCII:

```js
// Only the comma is escaped: Explorer does not decode a UTF-8 percent-escape
// such as %E4%B8%AD, so the URL form silently no-ops on non-ASCII paths.
const target = `file:///${windowsPath.replaceAll("\\", "/").replaceAll(",", "%2C")}`;
```

### What I could not verify

- **Whether the interim fix above is complete.** Individually I verified that the native path works for CJK (3/3 opens, 2/3 selections) and that `%2C` is required for commas, but I could not get a clean pass on the combination: Explorer coalesces rapid successive `/select,` invocations, so whichever variant runs later in a batch looks worse. That artefact is in my harness, not necessarily in the product — but it means I am proposing that line as a direction, not as a tested patch.
- **Whether failing paths are code-page dependent.** All measurements are from a zh-CN system; I did not test a non-Chinese Windows where the ANSI code page differs.
- A path containing `%` would become ambiguous under the interim fix (it would look like an escape), which is another reason to prefer the Shell API.

Happy to re-run anything or provide the matrix scripts if useful.

---

**中文摘要**：「在文件资源管理器中显示」对**含中文的路径完全无反应**（纯 ASCII 路径正常）。原因是 `revealNativePath` 把 `pathToFileURL(...).href` 这个百分号编码的 `file:///` URL 传给了 `explorer.exe /select,`，而该开关期望的是文件系统路径；`%E4%B8%AD` 这类 UTF-8 转义不会被解析，于是 Explorer 静默什么都不做。又因为 Explorer 成功失败都返回 1，这个静默失败被现有的 `catch` 当作成功，接口返回 204，前端提示成功——所以现象是「点了没反应，但哪里都显示成功了」。五个版本的代码逐字相同。附了复现矩阵与两处缺陷说明。

discussions.title: dsh-session-isolation — 每个会话独立工作目录 / Per-session working directories for parallel agents
discussions.body:
中文 | English

---

## 中文

我开发了 **dsh-session-isolation**：一个为 DSH Workspace 提供“每个会话独立工作目录”的插件。

### 解决的问题

同一 Workspace 里的多个会话默认共用工作目录，并行 agent 很容易互相覆盖文件。

### 功能

- Workspace 开启隔离后，每个**新会话**都会获得自己的 `session-<id>/` 目录。
- 该目录成为会话的 `workspace-write` 沙箱写入根，因此并行会话无法写入彼此的工作树。
- 已存在的会话不会被移动。
- 项目文件仍然可读，会话在侧边栏里仍归属于原 Workspace。
- 可以通过 Web 界面、`session_isolation` 工具或 `.dsh-isolate` 标记文件开启。
- 插件只包装两个可逆的 Cordis 接缝，不修改 DSH 源码。

### 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add \
  https://github.com/sweet-boby/dsh-session-isolation.git
```

安装后重启一次宿主，让浏览器模块表发现插件的 `dsh.client` bundle。

仓库：https://github.com/sweet-boby/dsh-session-isolation  
Release：https://github.com/sweet-boby/dsh-session-isolation/releases/tag/v0.1.0

已在 DSH `0.1.6-alpha.2` 上验证，25 个测试全部通过，MIT 许可。

### 重要限制

它隔离的是写入目录，不是 git worktree 的替代品。如果会话必须编辑仓库根目录中的文件，通常应保持关闭。

欢迎反馈和建议。

---

## English

I built **dsh-session-isolation**, a plugin that gives every new session its own working directory when a Workspace opts in.

### Problem

By default, multiple sessions in one Workspace share the same working directory, so parallel agents can overwrite each other's files.

### What it does

- When isolation is enabled for a Workspace, each **new** session gets its own `session-<id>/` directory.
- That directory becomes the session's `workspace-write` sandbox root, so parallel sessions cannot write into each other's working trees.
- Existing sessions are not moved.
- Project files stay readable, and sessions still belong to the original Workspace in the sidebar.
- Isolation can be controlled from the Web GUI, through the `session_isolation` agent tool, or with a `.dsh-isolate` marker file.
- The implementation uses two reversible Cordis seam patches and does not modify DSH source.

### Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add \
  https://github.com/sweet-boby/dsh-session-isolation.git
```

Restart the host once after installation so the browser module table discovers the plugin's `dsh.client` bundle.

Repository: https://github.com/sweet-boby/dsh-session-isolation  
Release: https://github.com/sweet-boby/dsh-session-isolation/releases/tag/v0.1.0

Verified against DSH `0.1.6-alpha.2`; the repository currently has 25 passing tests. MIT licensed.

### Important limitation

This isolates writes to a private session directory. It is not a git-worktree replacement, and it should generally stay off for repositories where the session must edit the repository root.

Feedback and suggestions are welcome.

discussions.title: [Bug Report] windows-acl: hook commands silently fail because `workspaceRoot` falls back to `process.cwd()` (elevated launch → C:/Windows/System32)
discussions.body:
> 整理：2026-09-17 · Windows 11 家庭版 (build 26200) · DSH 0.1.5-rc.2 (npx) · 由本机实测得出，非推测。中文摘要见文末。


## Summary

On a Windows host where the DSH server process happens to have been started with
`cwd = C:\Windows\System32` (the default working directory for an elevated launch),
**every `hooks-claude-code` bridge hook silently fails to execute**, and the error the
user is shown points them at Linux/macOS remedies.

The bridge is fail-open by design, so a fully dead guardrail layer looks exactly like
"nothing happened": `decision: pass`, no UI surface, no log the user would notice.

`workspaceRoot` defaults to `process.cwd()`, and the docs describe it as *"Absolute
fallback root for **agentless calls** and sessions without a cwd"*. Hook processes are
agentless calls, so they inherit the **server's cwd** — which, for an elevated launch,
is `C:\Windows\System32`. The ACL runner then tries to grant a write ACE on a system
directory, is refused, exits 127, and the seam re-classifies that as
"no sandbox backend is usable on this host".

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| OS | Windows 11 家庭版, build 26200 |
| DSH | `0.1.5-rc.2` (npx) |
| Node | v24.20.0 |
| Sandbox backend | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-windows-acl` (restricted-token ACL runner) |
| Server launch | elevated (token has `BUILTIN\Administrators` **enabled**), `cwd = C:\Windows\System32` |
| Session permission preset | `danger-full-access` (session-scoped) |
| Deployment default | `workspace-write` (`DSH_PERMISSION_MODE` unset) |

## Observed error

Every hook invocation records:

```
{"point":"PreToolUse","handlerId":"claude-code:PreToolUse:1","decision":"pass",
 "stderrSummary":"sandbox mode \"workspace-write\" is requested but no sandbox backend
  is usable on this host; refusing to run the command unconfined.
  Install bubblewrap or run a Landlock-enforcing kernel (Linux), ensure sandbox-exec
  is usable (macOS), or ensure the ACL restricted-token runner can start (Windows)
  — otherwise switch the consumer to danger-full-access.
  Runner failure: windows-acl-run: SetNamedSecurityInfoW failed (Win32 5):
  grantWrite(C:\\Windows\\System32)"}
```

165 consecutive `hook/result` events carried this same signature. `decision` is `pass`
throughout — the bridge never blocks, so **the hook layer was dead for the entire
session without any user-visible signal**.

## Root cause (reproduced by invoking the published runner directly)

The runner can be exercised standalone:

```powershell
node "<npx>\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\dsh-sandbox-windows-acl\lib\runner.js" `
     --workspace <DIR> --temp "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Temp" `
     --mode workspace-write -- cmd /c "echo ok"
```

| `--workspace` | Result |
|---|---|
| `D:\ai大类\codex plant` (a normal workspace) | `sandbox-child-ok`, **exit 0** — the sandbox itself works fine, even elevated |
| `C:\Windows\System32` | `SetNamedSecurityInfoW failed (Win32 5): grantWrite(C:\Windows\System32)`, **exit 127** — reproduces the production error byte-for-byte |

So the backend is healthy; it is simply handed an unusable workspace root.

Chain:

1. Server starts elevated → `process.cwd()` is `C:\Windows\System32`.
2. `sandbox-policy.workspaceRoot` defaults to `process.cwd()`.
3. Hook processes are **agentless calls** → they take `workspaceRoot`, not a session cwd.
4. Runner calls `grantWrite(C:\Windows\System32)` → Win32 5 (ACCESS_DENIED) → exit 127.
5. The seam classifies the runner failure as "no sandbox backend is usable on this host".
6. The bridge is fail-open → `decision: pass` → **all guardrails silently no-op**.

## Why this is worth fixing

- **The diagnostic actively misleads.** It tells Windows users to install `bubblewrap`
  or enable Landlock — both Linux-only. Two existing discussions complain about the
  same wording; this report adds a *specific, reproducible* cause behind it.
- **Fail-open + misleading wording = invisible.** The affected user believes hooks are
  protecting them. Ours were not, for hours, and every hook event said `pass`.
- **The blast radius is "every elevated Windows launch".** Launching a harness elevated
  is common, and `C:\Windows\System32` is the default cwd in that case.
- It also breaks the documented composition advice: a user who follows the error text
  and switches the consumer to `danger-full-access` abandons confinement entirely —
  which is what we initially did, and then hit a *second*, unrelated startup crash
  (see below).

## Suggested fixes (any of these resolves it)

1. **Make the runner validate `--workspace` before granting.** If the target is not
   writable by the caller, fail with a message that names the path and says *why*
   (e.g. `--workspace is not writable by this process: C:\Windows\System32`), rather
   than surfacing it as "no sandbox backend is usable".
2. **Do not fall back to `process.cwd()` for agentless calls**, or reject obviously
   unsuitable roots (system directories / non-writable paths) at resolve time.
3. **Distinguish "runner refused because of a bad policy input" from "no backend
   installed"** in the seam's failure classification. The two need different fixes and
   different user advice.

## Workaround (verified on the affected host, no core change)

Pin the fallback root explicitly in the profile patch:

```yaml
- id: sandbox-policy
  config:
    workspaceRoot: D:/path/to/your/workspace
```

Leave `mode` and `approval` to `base` so the pair stays `(workspace-write, ask)` — a
valid preset. (Setting `sandbox-policy.mode` alone leaves `approval=ask`, the pair
matches no preset, `derive()` returns `custom`, and `dsh-permission-presets` throws
during construction: `plugin tree failed to load` → the process exits. Worth a
separate hardening pass: a preset-derivation failure taking down the whole plugin tree
is a very sharp edge.)

After pinning `workspaceRoot`, the sandbox works end-to-end and hooks execute
confined to the declared root.

## Related reports

- Discussion #758 — Windows sandbox (workspace-write): permanent crash after Temp cleanup (P0)
- Discussion #2287 — private temp dir under `C:\Windows\Temp` loses creator access after ACL re-apply
- Discussion #5570 — `danger-full-access`: `sandbox_permissions` still advertised when approval is forced to `never`
- openai/codex #18821, #33388, #39245, #46062 — same `SetNamedSecurityInfoW failed: 5` signature on the Windows ACL approach

---

## 中文摘要

**现象**：Windows 上以提权方式启动 DSH 时，服务器 `cwd` 是 `C:\Windows\System32`；
而 `sandbox-policy.workspaceRoot` 默认取 `process.cwd()`，且官方文档写明它是
"**agentless calls 的兜底根目录**"——**钩子进程正属于 agentless 调用**，于是 runner
去给 `C:\Windows\System32` 授写 ACE → `Win32 5 拒绝访问` → runner exit 127 →
seam 归类为"本机没有可用沙箱后端" → 桥是 fail-open → **所有护栏静默失效**。

**复现**（直调已发布 runner，无需改源码）：
`--workspace` 指向普通工作区 → exit 0（沙箱本身完全正常，提权下也是）；
指向 `C:\Windows\System32` → 一字不差复现生产报错。

**危害**：报错文案把 Windows 用户引向 Linux 专属方案（bubblewrap/Landlock）；
fail-open 让"护栏全死"表现得和"什么都没发生"完全一样。

**建议**：① runner 授 ACE 前先校验 `--workspace` 可写，失败时点名路径与原因；
② agentless 调用不要兜底到 `process.cwd()`，或在解析期拒绝系统目录；
③ 把"策略输入非法"与"后端未安装"分成两类失败信息。

**规避（本机已验证）**：在 profile patch 里钉死
`sandbox-policy.workspaceRoot` 为真实工作区绝对路径，`mode`/`approval` 留给 base。

discussions.title: Custom agent preset mounting `subagent` tool outside an `isolate` group fails to mount → agent loses subagent spawn capability
discussions.body:
## Description

### Environment

- DeepSeek Harness (dsh), desktop app build
- Custom agent preset produced by authoring a composition modeled on the shipped `standard` preset

### Summary

When switching an agent session from the built-in `standard` preset to a custom preset, the `subagent` tool is not exposed in the session's tool list. The session only has `list_agents`, `send_message`, and `interrupt_agent`. As a result, the agent cannot spawn nested subagents (`spawn-tool-unavailable`), which breaks multi-agent orchestration flows that rely on nested delegation.

### Root cause (tentative)

The custom preset mounts the `subagent` delegation tool **at the top level of the composition**, i.e. without the wrapping `cordis:group` that carries the `isolate: { workflowEngine: true }` realm.

The shipped `standard` preset (and the `cordis` preset) mount the subagent delegation toolset inside such a group:

```yaml
- id: delegation
  name: cordis:group
  group: true
  isolate:
    workflowEngine: true
  config:
    - id: tool-subagent-control
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control'

    - id: tool-subagent-list-agents
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control/list-agents'

    - id: tool-subagent
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
      config:
        provider: spawn
        toolName: subagent
        modelSelectionSettings: true
        backgroundMode: continuable
    # ... fork, codex, claude-code, workflow, ralph ...
```

The custom preset instead mounts it directly:

```yaml
- id: tool-subagent
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
  config:
    provider: spawn
    toolName: subagent
    modelSelectionSettings: true
    backgroundMode: continuable
- id: tool-subagent-control
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control'
- id: tool-subagent-list-agents
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control/list-agents'
```

The `standard/agent.cordis.yml` header documents this constraint explicitly:

> A service row here MUST sit inside a group carrying an `isolate` realm. Without one it publishes into the root realm, where it is process-global — another preset publishing the same name collides, and a host reader would resolve one preset's instance for every session; `dsh-agent-presets` rejects that at mount.

And in the delegation section:

> The `subagents` registry and its spawn/fork backends live in the HOST composition: the registry is a process singleton ... `workflows` is different — nothing outside an agent reads it — so every row that reaches it shares one entry-local realm here.

So the hypothesis is: mounting `tool-subagent` at the root realm (without the `isolate` group) causes a mount-time collision that `dsh-agent-presets` rejects, leaving the session without the `subagent` tool. `list_agents`/`send_message`/`interrupt_agent` still appear because those control tools mounted fine, but the actual spawn tool is missing.

### Expected behavior

A custom preset modeled on `standard` should be able to expose the `subagent` spawn tool when the delegation toolset is mounted with the same `isolate: { workflowEngine: true }` grouping as the shipped presets — or, failing that, the mount rejection should fail **loudly** at preset load time with a clear diagnostic (rather than silently omitting the tool from the session's tool list, which surfaces only later as an opaque "tool not available" at the point the agent tries to delegate).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Copy the `standard` preset into a new preset directory and author a custom persona/instructions (keep the rest, including the `delegation` group, intact in this first step).
2. In the custom preset, move the `tool-subagent` row (and its siblings) **out** of the `delegation` `cordis:group` / `isolate` block so they sit at the composition top level.
3. Switch the session's agent preset to this custom preset (default preset mapping).
4. Start a session and ask the agent to delegate to a subagent.
5. Observe the agent's tool list contains only `list_agents` / `send_message` / `interrupt_agent`, not `subagent`.

### Impact

Multi-agent orchestrator flows that delegate through nested `subagent` spawn fail with "tool subagent not exposed in session tool list", blocking the entire workflow. The failure only appears at delegation time, making it hard to trace back to the preset composition.

### Possible improvements

1. **Fail loudly at mount time** — `dsh-agent-presets` should emit a noticeable error/warning when a `subagent` (or other registry-backed) tool row is mounted outside its required `isolate` realm, instead of silently leaving the tool absent.
2. **Document the constraint** — the `standard/agent.cordis.yml` header already states it; consider surfacing it in the public docs on authoring custom presets (a "delegation must live inside an `isolate: workflowEngine` group" note), since presets are the official customization path.

discussions.title: Feature request — automatic notifications when an agent pauses for user input or completes a long-running flow
discussions.body:
## Motivation

When an agent session stops and waits for the user (e.g. asking a question, waiting for approval, or surfacing a subagent failure), there is currently no built-in way to **notify** the user outside the Web UI. The user has to keep the tab open and watch for state changes, which defeats the purpose of long-running / background agent flows.

The runtime already exposes a rich `SessionEventMap` (`approval/asked`, `tool/call`, `assistant/message`, `subagent/descriptor`, etc.) and ships a `notify` tool with many channels (Telegram, Slack, Discord, webhook, desktop bell, …). What is missing is the **automatic bridge** between "agent entered a waiting/completed state" and "user gets notified on their preferred channel".

## Proposal

Add a core-level notification layer that fires automatically on well-defined agent-state transitions, with two complementary surfaces:

### 1. Auto-notify (opt-in per channel, off by default)

When the agent enters one of the states below, DSH sends a notification through every channel the user has configured (respecting per-channel opt-in / quiet-hours if those settings exist):

| Trigger | Suggested event name | Payload (minimum) |
|---|---|---|
| Agent calls `ask_user_question` and pauses for a reply | `user/question-asked` | session id, question text / options summary |
| Agent hits an approval gate (sandbox escalation, out-of-scope write, …) and waits for approve/reject | `approval/asked` *(already exists)* | session id, tool name, reason |
| A subagent fails / blocks / escalates and needs user intervention | `subagent/escalated` | session id, subagent id, failure reason |
| A long-running task or flow completes successfully | `task/completed` | session id, task/flow identifier, summary |

Auto-notify should be **off by default** (to avoid surprise noise) and enabled per-channel via settings. When enabled, it uses the same delivery path as the existing `notify` tool so channel configuration is reused.

### 2. Open event / hook for plugins and presets

In addition to the built-in auto-notify, expose the same state transitions as **first-class events** on `SessionEventMap` (or an equivalent public surface) so that:

- Custom presets can subscribe and implement their own notification logic (e.g. aggregate multiple questions into one digest, route different triggers to different channels, apply custom throttling).
- Third-party plugins can integrate with external systems (ticket trackers, dashboards, mobile apps) without forking core.

The existing `approval/asked` event is a good template; the new events (`user/question-asked`, `subagent/escalated`, `task/completed`) should follow the same shape and lifecycle guarantees.

## Why this belongs in core

- The state transitions are **defined by core** (only core knows when `ask_user_question` pauses the turn, when an approval gate blocks, when a subagent escalates). A plugin cannot reliably detect these without a core event.
- The notification delivery stack already lives in core (`notify` tool + channel registry). Auto-notify reuses it rather than duplicating channel logic in every preset/plugin.
- This matches the existing architecture: core owns state + events + delivery; presets/plugins subscribe and customize.

## Non-goals / boundaries

- **Not a replacement for the `notify` tool.** Agents should still be able to send ad-hoc notifications explicitly; auto-notify only covers the "agent is waiting / done" cases users most often miss.
- **Not opinionated about channel choice.** Core provides the trigger + delivery hook; which channels fire is a user setting.
- **Not synchronous.** Notifications are best-effort, fire-and-forget; they must never block the agent's state machine or delay the turn.

## Open questions for the team

1. Is there already an internal mechanism that tracks "agent is waiting for user" that could be surfaced as an event, or does this need new instrumentation?
2. Should auto-notify respect a global quiet-hours / do-not-disturb setting, or is that left to each channel plugin?
3. For `task/completed`, what counts as a "long-running" task worth notifying about? A configurable duration threshold, an explicit tag from the agent, or every terminal state change?

discussions.title: Feature request: auto-pause tasks during peak hours and auto-resume during off-peak
discussions.body:
**Summary**

Long-running or non-urgent work — goal loops, batch jobs, overnight research/refactor sessions — currently runs whenever it is started, regardless of the clock. I'd like to propose a scheduling capability that **automatically pauses running tasks when peak hours begin and automatically resumes them when off-peak hours begin**, so heavy work can slide into the cheaper/quieter windows without anyone babysitting it.

**Motivation**

- DeepSeek API pricing is peak/off-peak. Per the current rules, peak is Mon–Fri 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–18:00 (Beijing time); everything else — including weekends — bills at the off-peak discount. Multi-hour agent work that overlaps the peak windows pays peak rates for no benefit, and peak is also when latency and contention are worst.
- Today the only way to exploit this is manual: stop the agent when peak starts, restart it later. That also isn't free — interrupted turns are not always cleanly resumable (see #7318, #7370), so "kill it and restart later" carries real risk.
- It's also good for the platform: shifting non-urgent agent traffic out of peak windows spreads load.

**The pieces already exist — the glue is missing**

- Phase detection + countdown: [dsh-price-phase](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/6379) (#6379), dsh-billing-tui (#3307), dsh-deepseek-balance (#1778).
- Pause / resume mechanics for running tasks: [dsh-task-control](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/2164) (#2164) — its `safe` mode already pauses only after the current tool / reasoning step settles, which is exactly the safe boundary this feature needs, and it publishes a `taskControl` service that other plugins can drive.
- Time-based runners: dsh-cron-scheduler (#3109), schedule-core + dsh-schedule (#2564).
- Auto-resume for unattended sessions: #2924.

What I haven't found is anything that connects _"peak window is starting" → "pause gracefully, resume when it ends"_. Users hand-roll it (or simply don't).

**Proposed behavior (sketch)**

1. **Config** — peak/off-peak windows + timezone (default: the official pricing windows; fully configurable, since pricing rules have changed before and the timezone footnote issue in #4258 shows how easily that drifts).
2. **At peak start** — pause running tasks at a safe boundary (finish the current tool call / step; never interrupt mid-request), persist state for lossless resume.
3. **At off-peak start** — auto-resume schedule-paused tasks (configurable order/concurrency) with a notification; tasks waiting on an approval stay paused until the user answers.
4. **Overrides** — per task: "run now (ignore schedule)", "pause now", "resume now".
5. **Visibility** — `paused by schedule — resumes at HH:MM` in the session/task UI, so an idle agent is never ambiguous.

**Open questions**

- What's the canonical safe pause boundary in the turn model — between turns, or after each tool result settles? (#7318 / #7370 suggest partial turns are the risky area.)
- Should a schedule-paused task hold its session slot in memory, or serialize to disk and be re-adopted when off-peak starts? (#2564 / #2924 territory.)
- Is this a core scheduling capability, or a community plugin composing the pieces above? Curious which direction the team prefers — and if it's plugin territory, I'd be glad to prototype one.

Thanks for the great work on DSH — the plugin architecture makes this kind of glue genuinely fun to think about.

discussions.title: Fix for Google Gemini thought_signature HTTP 400 error on tool calls (ready branch with tests)
discussions.body:
Hi DeepSeek team!

Since PRs are currently closed on this repository, sharing a ready fix here:

### Problem
Google Gemini 2.5 and 3.x require any historical `functionCall` part in a `model` turn to include a valid `thought_signature`. When converting/replaying across models in `dsh-llm-pi-ai`, tool calls lack valid thought signatures, causing Gemini endpoints to immediately fail with `HTTP 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT: Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall parts`.

### Solution
We implemented a clean fix on top of `0.1.7-alpha.2`:
1. Preserve `thoughtSignature` from replay state during assistant message adaptation in `packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/replay.ts`.
2. Hook `repairGoogleThoughtSignatures` into `onPayload` in `PiAiAdapter`, restoring original signatures or defaulting to Google's official bypass sentinel `skip_thought_signature_validator`.
3. Added full unit/integration test coverage (349 tests pass) and a bilingual Agent Note.

**Branch / Commit link:**
https://github.com/FURYER/deepseek-harness/commit/278b30a513511ebdd3a48e715fa016e7fbce6e71

Feel free to cherry-pick this into master if useful!

discussions.title: Sessions silently leave their Workspace and reappear under "Ungrouped" (membership filter + startup-only cwd index + durable prune)
discussions.body:
## Summary

Sessions that were created inside a specific Workspace intermittently show up under **"Ungrouped"** in the sidebar instead of their Workspace. Once it happens, the eviction can become **permanent**, even though the durable workspace record still lists the session.

## Environment

- dsh `0.1.7-alpha.2` (source analysis at commit `00102833`)
- macOS arm64, desktop app

## How "Ungrouped" is decided

`ungroupedMemberIds` in `packages/client/ui-workspace/src/client/rows/WorkspaceBrowser.tsx` is simply "every session not contained in any `workspace.sessionIds`". So "session moved to Ungrouped" ⇔ "some workspace's `sessionIds` no longer contains the session".

## Mechanism (source analysis)

`Workspace.sessionIds` is a **live-filtered projection**, not the durable account:

```ts
// packages/workspace/workspace/src/entity.ts
get sessionIds(): readonly SessionId[] {
  return this.record.sessionIds.filter(id => this.host.sessionPath(id) === this.record.path)
}
```

`sessionPath(id)` reads a `sessionPaths` index that is built **only during `WorkspaceRegistry` startup** (`Service.init` → `replaceHeaderIndex(listStoredHeaders())` + `indexLiveSessions()` in `packages/workspace/workspace/src/index.ts`). There is no `session/created` / resume / persistence-change listener that keeps it current — `packages/workspace` registers no `session/created` listener at all.

Consequences:

1. **Silent eviction on index mismatch.** Any session whose canonical cwd doesn't match the workspace path *at index time* disappears from the membership projection with no user action involved. Concrete triggers:
   - the project directory was renamed/moved on disk — `workspace.path` is immutable and "never rewritten afterwards, even when the directory disappears" (`packages/workspace/workspace/src/types.ts`), so the divergence is permanent;
   - a transient `fs.realpath`/`stat` failure on the cwd during Host startup — `indexHeader` records `invalidSessionPaths` on any throw (unmounted external volume, iCloud/permission hiccup);
   - a symlink retarget between workspace creation and session creation.

2. **Eviction becomes durable and destructive.** `WorkspaceEntity.mutate()` prunes `record.sessionIds` through the same filter on **every** accepted workspace mutation (a rename, *another* session's attach, a reorder…). So a transient indexing miss is permanently written into the workspace record by the next unrelated edit.

3. **The Host feed is internally inconsistent.** In `packages/api/workspace-controller/src/feed.ts`, `workspaceView()` (used for the baseline and for *new* workspaces) projects the **filtered** live getter, while `changedWorkspaceView()` (upserts for *existing* workspaces) projects the **raw** `record.sessionIds` with no filter. Depending on which path published the last frame, the client flips a filtered-out session between "in workspace" and "Ungrouped" — visible flip-flopping.

4. **Attach failure at creation parks the session as Ungrouped forever.** `session.create` publishes the session first and attaches second (`packages/api/session-controller/src/commands.ts`); on attach failure the client deliberately keeps the published session visible as Ungrouped ("Publication precedes attachment", `packages/api/session-controller/src/client/sessions/manager.ts`). A transient cwd-resolution failure at that moment leaves the session born-Ungrouped, and nothing re-attaches it later.

The only diagnostic that exists today is a startup `logger.warn` per filtered candidate (`reportFilteredCandidates`), which is easy to miss.

## Reproduction hints

- Create a Workspace with sessions, rename/move the project directory on disk, restart dsh → the Workspace's sessions show under Ungrouped (workspace.path is stale by design).
- Or cause a transient `realpath`/`stat` failure on the cwd during Host startup (unmounted external volume, iCloud/permission hiccup) → same result after restart.
- Once one session is evicted, any unrelated workspace edit (rename the workspace, attach another session) prunes it from the durable record, making it permanent.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Membership projection:** rebuild or reconcile the canonical-cwd index at runtime (e.g. on `session/created` and persistence-listing changes) instead of startup-only.
2. **Don't durably prune on the filtered projection:** reserve record rewrites for explicit user operations (attach/detach/move), or re-validate against a fresh header read before pruning.
3. **Make `workspaceView` and `changedWorkspaceView` consistent** (both filtered, or both raw with client-side reconciliation).
4. **Surface filtered candidates in the UI** (or at least a visible warning) — today the eviction is completely silent.

Happy to provide my storage state (`~/.dsh/storages/workspace.json`) or Host logs if useful.

discussions.title: tvision — the Borland IDE reborn as a window manager for dsh agents
discussions.body:
![tvision demo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hongxin/dsh-tvision/main/docs/screenshots/demo.gif)

**tvision** — a Turbo Vision-style character-cell window manager for DeepSeek Harness agents. The Borland IDE, reborn for the agent era: overlapping windows with drop shadows, a menu bar floating above everything, a function-key strip generated from the keymap (so the legend cannot lie about the keys), a fixed one-line composer, and full mouse support — drag a title bar to move, drag the brightened corner to resize, click `[■]` to close.

The reasoning: an agent's activity is already a stream of file edits, shell commands, diffs, task lists, and subagents — which is what Borland built this interface for in the first place, minus the debugger. So the desktop gives each of those a home: a Conversation window with a one-character gutter (`>` you, `|` the agent, `·` reasoning, `~` a tool, `!` an error — the shape of a turn is visible before its words), a Project window, a live Tasks window, Sessions, Jobs — and approvals and questions as real modal windows with the same keyboard and mouse as everything else.

- Repo: https://github.com/hongxin/dsh-tvision (MIT; carries the `dsh-plugin` topic)
- Install: `dsh plugin --profile tvision add hongxin/dsh-tvision`, then `dsh --profile tvision` — an ordinary Cordis plugin bundle, not a fork, so the whole plugin ecosystem applies and sessions resume.
- Five skins ship: the Borland blue, P1 green phosphor, P3 amber CRT, a modern dark, and a One-Dark-style ANSI that inherits your terminal's own sixteen colours.
- The GIF above is a real pty capture — every frame in it is what a real terminal actually drew.

---

**中文版**

**tvision** — 给 DeepSeek Harness 智能体的 Turbo Vision 式字符窗口管理器。带投影的重叠窗口、浮于一切的菜单栏、由键位表生成的功能键提示条（提示不会说谎）、固定单行的输入框、完整鼠标支持——拖标题栏移动，拖亮色角缩放，点 `[■]` 关闭。

为什么这么做：智能体的活动本来就是文件编辑、shell 命令、diff、任务列表、子智能体——这正是当年 Borland 为之设计这套界面的东西，只少了调试器。于是每样都有了自己的窗口：对话区（一个字符的装订地：`>` 你、`|` 智能体、`·` 思考、`~` 工具、`!` 错误——对话的形状先于文字可见）、项目窗口、实时任务窗口、会话与后台作业；审批与提问也是正经的模态窗口，与全局同一套键盘和鼠标。

- 仓库：https://github.com/hongxin/dsh-tvision （MIT，已带 `dsh-plugin` topic）
- 安装：`dsh plugin --profile tvision add hongxin/dsh-tvision`，然后 `dsh --profile tvision`——普通 Cordis 插件包而非 fork，插件生态全兼容，会话可恢复。
- 五套皮肤：Borland 蓝、P1 磷光绿、P3 琥珀、现代深色、以及继承终端自带十六色的 One Dark 风 ANSI。
- 上面的动图是真 pty 采集——每一帧都是真实终端画出来的。

Would love feedback — especially from anyone using dsh daily: what's missing before this could be your daily driver?

discussions.title: dsh-mail-digest：让每轮回答自动发一封摘要邮件，并能直接回信作答或接着聊
discussions.body:
一句话：每轮回答结束后自动发一封**摘要邮件**到你邮箱；不在电脑前时，**直接回邮件**就能回答我的提问，或者接着聊下去。

## 用起来是什么样

人走开了，手机收到：

```
已把 163 的坑修完了：服务端 SUBJECT 搜索对 MIME 编码主题一律返回空，
所以改成取回候选后本地匹配主题；顺带修了主题被客户端插空格、GBK 正文乱码。

────────────
会话：给 dsh 加邮件插件
工作区：dsh
回合：第 8 轮 · 用时 4 分 12 秒
────────────
直接回复本邮件就能继续对话（主题别改）。
```

直接回这封邮件，正文写你要说的话，约 15 秒后对话就续上了。

需要我选的时候（`ask_user_question`），问题也会发到邮箱；回信正文写 `1. A` 即可作答：

```
1. 【先确认这两点】请告诉我现在的实际情况（可多选）：
   A. 我已经重启过 DSH
   B. 还没有重启
```

## 能力面

| 能力 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| 回答摘要 | 每轮 `turn/end` 发一封；长度**由结论多少决定**，不做固定字数截断 |
| 摘要来源 | 优先我自己写的（`mail_digest` 工具），其次模型压缩，最后确定性兜底 |
| 邮件回信作答 | 主题保持不动、内容写正文；`1. A` 选选项，写文字即自定义答案 |
| 邮件回信续聊 | 回摘要邮件，正文作为新消息注入原会话 |
| 提问转邮件 | 挂在 `user-questions/request` 瀑布上，与界面对话框**并行、先到先得** |
| 防误判 | 每封唯一随机 token + 发件人白名单 + `References` 比对原信 `Message-ID` |
| 设置界面 | `http://127.0.0.1:3080/dsh-mail-digest`，填账号/授权码/开关 |

## 安装

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/Xixixiao2007/dsh-mail-digest
cd dsh-mail-digest
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\安装邮件摘要.ps1
```

装完重启 DSH，打开 `http://127.0.0.1:3080/dsh-mail-digest` 填邮箱账号与授权码，点「发送测试邮件」和「测试收信」验证。

## 零依赖

自己实现的 SMTP 与 IMAP 客户端，不装 nodemailer/imapflow，不经过任何云服务。已实测 QQ 与 163，踩到的坑都写进 README 了：

- **163/126**：登录后必须先发 `ID` 命令声明客户端身份，否则 `SELECT` 直接 `NO SELECT Unsafe Login`
- **163/126**：服务端 `UID SEARCH SUBJECT "..."` 对 MIME 编码主题（`=?gb18030?B?...?=`）**一律返回空**，只好改成取回候选后在本地匹配主题
- **QQ**：回复长主题会按显示宽度**插空格**，把 `[DSH-Q:x]` 变成 `[D SH-Q:x]`

235 项离线自检（含假 SMTP 服务器对发、假邮件喂给收信判定），`node smoke.mjs` 等五个脚本可直接跑。

仓库：https://github.com/Xixixiao2007/dsh-mail-digest

discussions.title: 0.1.7 read-time migration refuses released subagent/descriptor v2 sessions (fix available)
discussions.body:
## Summary

`@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.1.7-alpha.2 refuses to read sessions whose `subagent/descriptor` payload carries `version: 2`, so any session opened between 2026-07-27 (payload v2 shipped in #2663) and 2026-08-28 (v3) fails whole-artifact v0-to-v1 migration with `SessionFormatUnsupportedMigrationError` and becomes unreadable. Downstream aggregation (e.g. the usage-billing plugin) skips these artifacts, so users see silently missing cost statistics for sessions they still actively append to. The raw v0 log stays unchanged on disk — nothing is lost, but there is no self-healing path.

## Reproduction

Open (or continue appending to) a session created in that window on 0.1.7-alpha.2. The reader refuses with:

```
SessionFormatUnsupportedMigrationError: subagent/descriptor <seq> uses unsupported descriptor version 2
```

## Proposed fix

Descriptor v2 is a strict subset of what the v3 payload validator already accepts (required: `mode`/`version`/`provider`; optional: `label` and composition members), so the v0 edge can admit version 2 alongside 3 with the same released-key policy — no new validation branches beyond the version literal. Versions outside {2, 3} keep refusing.

A complete patch (with migration pass/refuse tests and a bilingual Agent Note) is on my fork, based on current master `00102833df`:

https://github.com/kenz1117/deepseek-harness/tree/fix/descriptor-v2-migration

Since both issues and pull requests are disabled in this repository, I am posting it here; happy to move it wherever the maintainers prefer. `session-format-v0-to-v1` passes 111/111 on that branch.
