discussions.title: latest新版打包导致了cordis版本冲突直接无法打开
discussions.body:
# Fresh `npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@latest` assembles a mixed rc.2/rc.3 tree with two cordis copies — `dsh web` fails: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-local` could not be resolved

## Summary

On 2026-09-23, a fresh global install of the `latest` dist-tag on Windows completes with ~280 `ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency` warnings and produces an **unbootable** installation: `dsh web` prints its URL, then dies with `plugin tree failed to load ... @deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-local ... could not be resolved`.

The evidence below points to a **stale `latest` dist-tag**, not a broken release: `latest` still resolves to `0.1.5-rc.2`, whose caret ranges float its subpackages to the newer `0.1.5-rc.3` line, while `@deepseek-ai/cordis: ^4.0.2` can now additionally resolve to the recently published `4.0.4`. The `0.1.5-rc.3` subpackages peer-pin cordis to **exactly `4.0.2`**, so npm overrides hundreds of peer conflicts and assembles a tree containing **two copies of cordis (4.0.2 + 4.0.4)** and **two generations of `cordis-plugin-loader` (1.0.3 + 1.0.5)**. Installing `@next` (`0.1.5-rc.3`, which pins cordis `4.0.2` exactly everywhere) yields a clean tree and boots fine.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| OS | Windows (PowerShell 5.x) |
| Node | v24.16.0 (nvm-windows, `C:\Users\River\AppData\Local\nvm\v24.16.0`) |
| Install method | npm global |
| dsh version | 0.1.5-rc.2 (resolved from `@latest` at install time) |

## Steps to reproduce

```powershell
npm uninstall -g @deepseek-ai/dsh   # clean slate
npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@latest
dsh web
```

Expected: boots the Web UI.
Actual: install completes with a wall of peer-override warnings; `dsh web` crashes during plugin-tree load.

## Full log

Install (the `ERESOLVE` warning line repeats **280 times**; npm printed no conflict details in this mode):

```text
PS C:\Users\River> npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@latest
npm warn ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency
npm warn ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency
npm warn ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency
... (repeated 280 times in total) ...
npm warn deprecated node-domexception@1.0.0: Use your platform's native DOMException instead

added 166 packages, removed 121 packages, and changed 397 packages in 1m
```

First launch, complete output:

```text
PS C:\Users\River> dsh web
dsh web: http://127.0.0.1:3080/?token=1F40LojAj57873bBopwti8AzBG9GA6T3sR_NeDS8M6Y
dsh web: opening the default browser; pass --no-open to disable
file:///C:/Users/River/AppData/Local/nvm/v24.16.0/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot/lib/index.js:1545
                throw new Error(`${binName}: ${stage}: ${detail}${stack}`, { cause });
                      ^

Error: dsh: plugin tree failed to load: dsh: plugin(s) failed to load: @deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-local; Cordis startup failed because these plugin(s) could not be resolved (see the error(s) logged above)
    at boot (file:///C:/Users/River/AppData/Local/nvm/v24.16.0/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot/lib/index.js:1545:9)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:104:5)
    ... 2 lines matching cause stack trace ...
    at async file:///C:/Users/River/AppData/Local/nvm/v24.16.0/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib/bin.js:168:23 {
  [cause]: Error: dsh: plugin(s) failed to load: @deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-local; Cordis startup failed because these plugin(s) could not be resolved (see the error(s) logged above)
      at assertEntriesLoaded (file:///C:/Users/River/AppData/Local/nvm/v24.16.0/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot/lib/index.js:1438:9)
      at assertEntriesActivated (file:///C:/Users/River/AppData/Local/nvm/v24.16.0/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot/lib/index.js:1466:2)
      at boot (file:///C:/Users/River/AppData/Local/nvm/v24.16.0/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot/lib/index.js:1537:9)
      at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:104:5)
      at async runProfile (file:///C:/Users/River/AppData/Local/nvm/v24.16.0/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib/profile-boot-Dk-7KqJc.js:311:14)
      at async runCli (file:///C:/Users/River/AppData/Local/nvm/v24.16.0/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib/bin.js:146:4)
      at async file:///C:/Users/River/AppData/Local/nvm/v24.16.0/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib/bin.js:168:23
}

Node.js v24.16.0
```

## Analysis

All checks below were performed on 2026-09-23.

**1. Dist-tags and ranges (npm registry):**

- `@deepseek-ai/dsh` dist-tags: `latest: 0.1.5-rc.2`, `next: 0.1.5-rc.3`, `alpha: 0.1.7-alpha.2`
- `@deepseek-ai/cordis` on npm: `4.0.2`, `4.0.3`, `4.0.4` published; `latest: 4.0.4`
- `dsh@0.1.5-rc.2` declares `@deepseek-ai/cordis: ^4.0.2` (loose) and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base: ^0.1.5-rc.2` (floats to 0.1.5-rc.3, since prerelease ordering puts rc.3 inside the range)
- `dsh@0.1.5-rc.3` pins `@deepseek-ai/cordis: 4.0.2` **exactly**
- `dsh-sandbox-local@0.1.5-rc.3` peer-pins `@deepseek-ai/cordis: 4.0.2` exactly (plus `dsh-llm`/`dsh-sandbox`/`dsh-session` at `^0.1.5-rc.3`)

So a fresh `@latest` install now mixes an rc.2 top-level with floated rc.3 subpackages under a cordis range that spans both 4.0.2 and 4.0.4 — exactly the combination the rc.3 pinning was designed to prevent.

**2. Reproduced locally (Linux, npm 10): `npm i @deepseek-ai/dsh@latest` in a scratch dir.** `npm ls` shows the split tree:

```text
└─┬ @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.5-rc.2
  ├─┬ @deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-hmr@1.0.17
  │ └─┬ @deepseek-ai/cordis@4.0.4          <-- 2nd cordis copy (newer line)
  │   └─┬ @deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader@1.0.5
  ├─┬ @deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-include@1.0.7
  │ └── @deepseek-ai/cordis@4.0.2 deduped
  ├─┬ @deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader@1.0.3          <-- 2nd loader generation
  ├── @deepseek-ai/cordis@4.0.2
  ├─┬ @deepseek-ai/dsh-acp-app@0.1.5-rc.3              <-- rc.3 subpackage floated in
  │ └─┬ ...
  │   └─┬ @deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-local@0.1.5-rc.3
  │     └── @deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-windows-acl@0.1.5-rc.3
```

**3. Same repro with `@next`:** zero `ERESOLVE` warnings, a single `@deepseek-ai/cordis@4.0.2` throughout the whole tree, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-local` resolves and imports cleanly (`LocalSandboxProvider` exported).

**4. Why the whole tree dies:** `dsh-sandbox-local` is a base-bundle loader entry (`id: sandbox` in [`packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml)), so when its entry cannot be resolved, the entire plugin tree fails to load rather than just the sandbox service.

**5. User-confirmed fix on the affected Windows machine:** switching to `@next` resolved the boot failure immediately (profiles under `~/.dsh` untouched by the reinstall).

## Workaround

```powershell
npm uninstall -g @deepseek-ai/dsh
npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@next
dsh web
```

`@next` (0.1.5-rc.3) is self-consistent: every subpackage and peer pin resolves to one cordis version.

## Suggested fix

Any of these closes the window for other users hitting `@latest` during fresh installs:

1. **Move the `latest` dist-tag to `0.1.5-rc.3`** (the release that already exists to pin cordis 4.0.2 exactly), or
2. Cut a fresh `latest` release from a self-consistent tree with exact-pinned subpackage versions (the repo already does this on newer lines: `0.1.7-alpha.2` uses `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base: 0.1.7-alpha.2` exact and cordis `~4.0.4`), or
3. Republish/patch `0.1.5-rc.2`'s dependency ranges so they cannot float across subpackage lines (e.g. exact pins), so `npm i @deepseek-ai/dsh@latest` can never assemble the mixed tree.

Happy to provide the full 280-warning install log or any `npm ls` output from the broken tree if useful.

discussions.title: Request to land fix(client): re-read the model catalog when a selection menu opens
discussions.body:
## Request: manual merge of a completed fix (upstream PR creation unavailable)

Hi maintainers,

I'd like to request a manual merge of a completed fix. I can't open a pull request against `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness` from my account (`rbh0524`): GitHub rejects PR creation for my account, and my repository `rbh0524/Deepseek-harness` is a standalone repo with unrelated history rather than a GitHub fork, so it can't serve as a PR head (upstream also has `allow_fork_prs: false`). The branch is pushed to my repo; I would be grateful if someone with access could push it to upstream or open the PR on my behalf.

**Branch:** https://github.com/rbh0524/Deepseek-harness/tree/fix/model-catalog-revalidate-on-open
**Commit:** `9312014b5b9e057c3734f1160e9a36fad12de66b` (single commit, based on current `master` at `c389f96bf3` — should apply cleanly)

## Problem

Two selection entries read one Host-generation catalog over ordinary `$on` events, which the event-transport decision deliberately gives no reconnect baseline, cursor, or gap repair. The client also short-circuits a read whenever its retained catalog is `ready`, so reopening a menu returns the retained value without asking the Host. A `settings/document-updated`, `llm/adapters-updated`, or `credentials/reference-updated` frame lost while no Remote event stream is established — page boot, an SSE reconnect gap — therefore leaves superseded provider groups on screen with nothing to repair them until the next connection generation. A model-list edit is the sharpest case: `llm-pi-ai` re-registers its routes only when a provider's id, display name, or retry policy changes, so editing models emits `settings/document-updated` alone, and that single frame carries the whole signal.

## Change

Opening either entry re-reads the catalog rather than trusting the retained value. `ModelCatalogDirectory.revalidate()` invalidates and loads without the `ready` short-circuit `load()` keeps; `ModelDirectory.revalidate()` publishes the result through the same per-session snapshot store both entries already share. The retained value stays published for the whole read, so a delayed replacement costs no loading state. A failed revalidation keeps the retained value and its `ready` status instead of publishing the load error — the read was opportunistic, and an open menu must not be replaced by an error a reader never provoked; only a first read with nothing retained keeps the error. A read a later refresh has superseded restores nothing at all; the in-menu Retry still runs the loud `load()`. Full rationale and rejected alternatives are in the Agent Note included in the commit: `.agents/notes/implemented/bug-fix/2026-09-22-model-catalog-revalidate-on-open.md`.

## Testing

`catalog.client.spec.ts` pins the re-read past a retained value, the retained value surviving a failed re-read, a first re-read keeping its error, joining a read already on the wire, and a superseded re-read restoring nothing. `browser-plugin.client.spec.ts` rewrites the Host catalog with no event emitted and proves the next open shows the new groups. `model-select.client.spec.tsx` pins that opening revalidates while the in-menu Retry still loads. All three files pass locally (30 tests); pre-commit hooks (translation pairing, lint, whitespace, vendor guard) and the pre-push typecheck passed.

## Landing

Happy to rebase, split, or adjust anything before landing. My repo stays private; two ways to get the commit:

1. **Collaborator read access** — name a GitHub account here and I will grant it pull access to `rbh0524/Deepseek-harness`, then push the branch upstream or open the PR:

```sh
git push upstream 9312014b5b9e057c3734f1160e9a36fad12de66b:refs/heads/fix/model-catalog-revalidate-on-open
```

2. **Git bundle** — I attach a bundle file on request; it recovers the branch with `git fetch model-catalog-revalidate.bundle fix/model-catalog-revalidate-on-open`.

Thanks!

discussions.title: [Proposal] 插件会话事件：写侧 ignorable 与轨迹账本行（两个改动，回应 #3191 / #5463 / #5474 / #5793）
discussions.body:
*English summary: Two ready-to-review changes from an out-of-tree plugin author. (1) `Session.append` gains the write-side `ignorable` option the read side already honours — the gap reported in #3191, #5463, #5474 and #5793. (2) A target-owned Trajectory extension row, so a plugin can render a record it wrote into the session log. Both live in fork PRs and both were validated with the repository's own gates. I would like to ask whether this area has a plan, and where an external patch should land, since CONTRIBUTING says external pull requests are not accepted at the moment.*

## 背景与动机

我在写一个仓库外插件（按路径授予 shell 文件权限，并在审批时记录**谁拍了板**：规则 / 默认基线 / 自动复核 / 人工 / 插件自拒）。它要解决两件事，恰好各自撞在一个缺口上。

## 改动 1：`Session.append` 暴露写侧 `ignorable`（PR #1）

读侧早就认这个标记 —— `validateStoredEvents` 只对 `KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES` 之外、且 `ignorable !== true` 的事件抛错。但写侧没有通道：非 surface 类型的 `opts` 是空元组。结果是插件**能写进去**，而会话**冷恢复必被整段拒绝**。

我在自己的部署上实测到了同一句报错（事件类型来自我的插件）：

```
session "..." contains event type "dsh-allow/decision" (seq N) unknown to this
harness and not marked ignorable; refusing to interpret the log
```

**目的**：把「插件记录自己的信息性事件」变成一条**受支持、可恢复**的路径，而不是靠 detached SessionStore 绕过主日志，或给 `KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES` 打本地补丁（升级即失效）。

实现上，非 surface 事件接受 `{ ignorable?: true }` 并落到持久化信封上；已知类型传该标记会被直接拒绝，因为读回路径拒绝带标记的已知类型 —— 让错误在写入处暴露，而不是在下次冷加载时。

## 改动 2：轨迹的插件扩展行（PR #2）

轨迹的贡献类型（`TrajectoryContribution`）与节点联合（`ConversationNode`）在仓库内是封闭的，插件无法在轨迹账本里加行 —— 而「把插件写下的事件显示出来」是写入之后最自然的一步。

我加的是一个**目标自有的通用行**：插件注册普通的 `ConversationNodeDefinition`，产出 `extension` 节点（一行摘要 + 插件自有的 key 与 JSON 负载 + 一个取自封闭集合的 tone）。轨迹渲染摘要、按 tone 给该行标签上色、把负载交给共用的详情负载页 —— **轨迹侧不认识任何插件的字段名或颜色**。

**目的**：给「插件想在轨迹里留一行」一个不引入插件词汇的入口，同时也让核心仓库不必为每个插件新增一种行类型。

## 已跑的检查

- `pnpm run doc-sync` → 42 passed, 0 failed
- `pnpm run hygiene` → 18 passed, 0 failed
- `pnpm run test:gui` → 517 files / 7509 tests passed
- `vitest run packages/core/session` → 545 passed
- `pnpm run duplication` → 0 clones
- `pnpm run verify-persistence-changes` → `changes: []`（不需要持久化变更确认）
- `pnpm run gen-cordis-catalog` 已重跑；`verify-cordis-api`、`verify-export-jsdoc` 通过
- Agent Note 已更新并保持中英一致：`2026-08-30-retain-ignorable-external-session-events`（写入侧现在是它等待的「替代机制」）与 `2026-08-09-client-conversation-node-assembly`（新增 extension 行小节）

如实说明：`DSH_SNAPSHOT=replay pnpm run test:web` 与逐文件覆盖率**尚未跑** —— 前者会重建客户端产物、必须在关闭 GUI 宿主时执行，本地还没安排那个窗口。所以我不声称 CI 等价证据已经完整。

## 与既有讨论的关系

我读过并逐条对照了 #3191、#5463、#5474、#5793，以及 #6614（迁移层）、#7399（界面座位）。

改动 1 与 #3191 中 @Mchsd 实现、@zoahdev 复核的分支解决的是**同一个问题**。为了避免被读成静默分歧，我把三处形态差异列出来：

1. **命名与位置**：我用 `index.ts` 里的 `NonSurfaceAppendOptions`；社区那版是 `types.ts` 里的 `AppendOpts`。
2. **我多了一道闸**：已知类型传 `ignorable` 直接抛错（理由见上）。
3. **我没有做 warn-at-append**（写入「未知且未标标记」时的即时告警）—— 而这正是 #3191 里最有说服力的补充论证。

如果上游倾向社区已经收敛的那一版，我愿意改成那一版；第 2 点是否保留，也听上游意见。

改动 2 我没有找到先例：#3191 通篇只谈持久化；我也确认了生态里最相关的插件（`dsh-draw`，写 `draw/generated` 且带结构化负载）只注册了 `tool.call.toolview` 与 `settings.plugins.tab`，并没有在轨迹里加行。

## 想请教的问题

1. **这个方向目前是否有计划？** 具体是：(a) 写侧 `ignorable` 的暴露；(b) 迁移层对 ignorable 历史事件的处理（#6614）；(c) 给插件一个**轨迹账本行**的渲染入口。
2. **外部补丁希望以什么方式提交或登记？** CONTRIBUTING 说明暂不接受外部 PR，社区里已经出现了 patch queue 的做法（例如 @zoahdev 的 upstream patch queue）。我想按官方偏好的方式来，而不是自己另起一套流程。

## 链接

- PR #1（session）：https://github.com/DWJZ/deepseek-harness/pull/1
- PR #2（trajectory）：https://github.com/DWJZ/deepseek-harness/pull/2
- 直接对比：
  - https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/compare/master...DWJZ:feat/session-ignorable-writer
  - https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/compare/master...DWJZ:feat/trajectory-extension

感谢任何方向上的指正。

discussions.title: [hardening] 写入侧不校验 compaction/* 的 shadowedRange/shadowedSeqs：非法记录静默落盘，直到下次加载才硬失败
discussions.body:
### 摘要

宿主 `Session.append` 只对 **surface 事件**做写入时校验，`compaction/*` 的 `shadowedRange` / `shadowedSeqs` **完全不验**。于是一条违反加载期契约的 `compaction/summary` 会**静默落盘**，当轮会话继续正常运行，直到**下次重启/重开**才以
`SessionFormatError: compaction/summary shadowedSeqs do not name an exact current surface span` 硬失败。日志本体完好、数据未丢失，但用户看到的就是“会话损坏”，且除手工改日志外不可逆。

本 Discussion 只请求**宿主侧写入时加固**；触发它的插件缺陷另案归属，见文末。

### 环境

- dsh host `0.1.7-alpha.2`（Node v22.23.1，Windows）
- 本文所有**宿主行号均绑定该版本**；换版本请以函数名/字段名重新定位
- 所涉包: `dsh-session`、`dsh-session-persistence`、`dsh-session-persistence-jsonl`、`dsh-session-format-v1-to-v2`、`dsh-session-format-v3-to-v4`

### 症状

一个会话整天正常使用；**重启后重新打开即失败**。日志物理层完全健康——多帧 zstd 逐帧可解、全部行可解析、`seq` 连续唯一——被拒的只是宿主**加载期**的关系校验。数据没丢，用户可见效果等同“会话损坏”。

### 写入侧：为什么没人拦（读码推导）

- `Session.append` 只走 surface 事件的校验: `dsh-session/lib/index.js:1326`（`append`）
- 资格集合 `SURFACE_EVENT_TYPES` 仅 5 个消息类事件，**不含** `compaction/*`: `:154-160`
- 没有 `surfaceOp` 即早退: `:438`
- `planSurfaceEvent` 定义 `:422-454`，在 `validateNext`（定义 `:525`）内于 `:532` 调用；`append` 在 `:1346` 调用 `validateNext`
- persistence 只做快照 + 类型接管: `dsh-session-persistence/lib/index.js:182`（`validateStoredEvents`）、`:218`（`materializeAppendBatch`）
- JSONL 写入侧只断言**连续性**: 调用点 `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl/lib/index.js:226`，定义 `dsh-session-persistence/lib/index.js:229`；行序遍历时要求 `seq` 恰为从 0 起的连续序列（`dsh-session-format-v1-to-v2/lib/index.js:243-249`）

结论: 上述路径对 `compaction/*` 的 `shadowed*` 字段**没有任何断言**。

### 加载侧：唯一的拦截点（已实测复现）

- `SessionLogScanner.finish → assertReleasedV4Relationships`: `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl/lib/index.js:1072`
- `Relationships.compact()` 于 `dsh-session-format-v3-to-v4/lib/index.js:701` 调用 `span()`；`span()` 在 `:731-738`——throw `:736`、受保护 system head 守卫 `:737`、两个 `indexOf` 参数外还套了 `earlier(...)`（`:733-734`）
- 报错包装 `stored log is corrupt:` 在 `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl/lib/index.js:2773` / `:2817`

即: **写入侧零告警、读取侧硬失败，且失败只在重启后才可达**——用户无法把因果连起来，损害在无手工介入时不可逆。

### 这是一个“类”，不是单个插件的意外（已实测）

两个**互相独立**的插件撞到**同一条宿主错误串**:

1. `yoza10635/dsh-argp` **issue #2**（2026-09-23 提交）: 该插件在 replace 循环之后才追加 `compaction/summary`（`main` 上 `lib/peratom/flush.js` `:289` 循环先于 `:335` summary；diff 实测 `v1.6.0` → `1.6.1-beta.0` → `1.7.0-beta.0` 与上游 `main` 四处均如此，`1.6.0` 之前的版本**未逐版核对**）。该例的违规是**无条件**的: 只要 flush 正常完成并发出 ≥1 个 replace 步骤，就必然写出不可加载的 summary；完整覆盖窗口同样失败，仅由**发出时序**决定。
2. `flizzywine/dsh-tavern` **#72/#73**（2026-09-22 关闭）: **另一个插件**（`dsh-profile-tavern`），同一条宿主错误串。

同一错误串被两个独立写入者触发，说明问题出在**宿主缺少写入时契约检查**，而非某一插件的偶发失误。

### 与既有帖子的关系（非重复）

- **#6928**（“loader 与 writer 在 shadowed range 上不一致”，open，General）: 报的是**另一个**错误（`sourceEventSeqs must include every shadowed surface node`），写入者是**宿主自身的 `compaction-basic`**，且其正文明确写到写入侧**已有两道断言**把关。**与本帖不同**。
- **#4795**: 讲的是**同一类**问题的一般表述（“只在读取时校验，写入时毫不验证”），但针对**另一条错误路径**，且**未提及** `compaction` / `shadowed`。本贴给它补上 `compaction/*` 这一具体面。
- **#1090**: 相邻但无关，仅作背景参考。

故本 Discussion **不是**以上任何一条的重复。

### 建议

1. 在**写入时**用**加载期同一判据**校验 `compaction/*` 的 `shadowedRange` / `shadowedSeqs`，至少覆盖:
   - `span()` 等价性: `surface.slice(indexOf(start), indexOf(end)+1)` 与 `shadowedSeqs` 深相等，且两端点此刻仍在 surface 上；
   - 每事务**仅一条** `compaction/summary`；
   - 受保护 system head 不得被 shadow。
2. 不合规时**当场拒绝该次 append 并显式报错**，而不是落盘后留到下次加载才炸。
3. 若出于兼容性考虑暂不能拒绝，至少**发出警告**（写入侧可见的告警即可显著缩短因果距离）。
4. 可选: 给 `Session.append` 的 `compaction/*` 分支加一条“写入即校验”的回归测试，避免日后回退。

### 归属

- **插件侧**缺陷（发出顺序 / range 与 seqs 不一致）已单独提交: `yoza10635/dsh-argp` issue **#2**。
- **本 Discussion 只谈宿主侧写入时加固**，与插件修复分开归属、互不替代。
- 本贴不包含任何会话文件或日志样本，也不打算提供。

### 证据分级

- **已实测**: 加载链复现（同一函数链稳定抛出上述错误）、同一宿主契约错误串（`shadowedSeqs do not name an exact current surface span`，前缀随 `event.type` 而异；GitHub 全站检索该子串仅 2 处命中，均在 dsh-tavern #72/#73）、版本扫描（diff 实测 `v1.6.0` → `1.6.1-beta.0` → `1.7.0-beta.0` 与上游 `main`，四处均为 replace 循环先于 summary；`1.6.0` 之前的版本**未逐版核对**，按读码推断同属该发射顺序）。

discussions.title: Source Verification for Legal Content: Why Cross-Validation Must Be Mandatory from the First Response
discussions.body:
Summary
When AI assistants provide legal information—particularly in criminal law—the consequences of unverified sources are not academic. A user relying on AI-generated lawyer recommendations or legal citations may make irreversible decisions about their defense. This post documents a real case where an AI assistant recommended lawyers based on commercial platform visibility rather than authoritative sources, and proposes that cross-validation be enforced as a baseline requirement, even when full source-tier classification is not yet feasible.

The Problem: Source Hierarchy Collapse in Legal Recommendations
In a recent interaction, a user asked an AI assistant for criminal defense lawyer recommendations in Tianjin, China, specifically for fraud-related charges. The assistant's first response recommended four lawyers. Upon scrutiny, the sourcing behind these recommendations was problematic:

One lawyer's profile was found primarily on commercial legal platforms such as (https://www.66law.cn/)—a for-profit directory site with low editorial oversight. This is a C-tier source at best.

Another lawyer's alleged "success record" (a non-prosecution outcome in a high-value fraud case) was sourced only from their own law firm's website. This is self-disclosure, not independently verifiable evidence.

Meanwhile, lawyers with far stronger sourcing were entirely absent from the first response. These included:

A lawyer whose fraud defense work is documented in the Ministry of Justice Legal Aid Case Database—an official government source with case records backed by judicial documents.

A lawyer listed on the Tianjin Lawyers Association's certified criminal law specialist roster—a professional credential requiring peer review and formal evaluation.

A lawyer whose case record appears on both the Bar Association specialist list and the Criminal Law Committee roster.

The AI assistant's second response—after the user challenged the sourcing—acknowledged that the first round had used a "broad search + commercial platform visibility" approach rather than an "authoritative roster + verifiable case" approach. In other words, the first response surfaced whoever had the strongest commercial platform presence, not whoever had the most verifiable credentials.

This is not a minor quality issue. It is a source hierarchy failure with real-world consequences in legal contexts.

Why This Matters in Criminal Law Specifically
Criminal law is uniquely unforgiving of unreliable information. Unlike civil disputes, where a poorly-informed decision may result in financial loss, criminal proceedings involve liberty, reputation, and in some jurisdictions, life. The stakes demand a higher evidentiary standard for every factual claim.

The legal profession itself recognizes this. Courts in multiple jurisdictions have issued formal warnings about AI-generated legal content. In one notable 2026 case in the UK, the Crown Prosecution Service submitted written submissions to the High Court containing references to two non-existent legal cases—likely originating from generative AI use. The court accepted the CPS's apology and found no deliberate deception, but Mr Justice Sweeting emphasized that AI could create serious risks when used without appropriate human oversight. The "operative cause," the court found, was human failure to verify before filing.

Legal professionals have been explicitly warned: "Lawyers using AI in legal research should verify every authority through reliable sources, including official court judgments, legislation databases and established legal research platforms". And in the criminal justice context specifically, police forces in England and Wales were told to pause some generative AI uses, with the stated safeguard being that "important AI-generated material should be checked by a suitably qualified person against the original evidence and independently verifiable facts".

Montana Legal Services Association puts it bluntly: "When it comes to legal advice and legal arguments, you should never rely only on artificial intelligence (AI) technology... The AI technology might misinterpret the information it finds online, and it might even make up information based on what it calculates you want to hear". In legal contexts, the association warns, a fabricated authority "could cause you to lose your case or even be held in contempt of court".

The Technical Landscape: Citation Verification Is an Active Research Area
This is not an unsolved problem in principle. Academic research has developed frameworks specifically for legal citation verification:

L3CV (Legal Contextual Citation Checking and Verification) evaluates citations across three levels: syntactic (format), existential (does the authority actually exist), and contextual (is it jurisdictionally and argumentatively appropriate). It combines rule-based validation with database-backed retrieval and ensemble LLM reasoning to assess correctness.

L-MARS introduces a multi-agent legal QA system with judge-driven evidence checks, auditing each atomic claim against its cited source. A "Faith-Search" post-draft step re-verifies and repairs unreachable citations, dropping the unreachable rate below 1%.

The legal citation checking framework L3CV notes that in the era of LLM-assisted drafting, "plausible but fictitious authorities can be generated," making manual verification "increasingly unreliable".

The technical capability exists. The question is whether it is deployed by default in consumer-facing AI assistants—especially for legal queries.

Proposal: Cross-Validation as a Minimum Baseline
Full source-tier classification is complex to implement. It requires defining tiers, tagging all retrieved content, and training the model to weight sources accordingly. This is a valid long-term goal.

But the minimum viable standard should be simpler: cross-validation from the first response.

If an AI assistant makes a factual claim about a professional's credentials, a case outcome, or a legal authority, that claim should be verified against at least one independent source before being presented to the user. Specifically:

For professional credentials: Do not rely solely on the professional's own website or a commercial directory. Cross-reference against regulatory bodies, bar association rosters, or government registries.

For case outcomes: Do not cite a single self-disclosed "success case" without checking whether it appears in judicial documents, official case databases, or reputable third-party reports.

For legal citations: Verify existence against official databases before presenting. A plausible-looking but non-existent case is worse than no citation at all.

For recommendations of any kind: Weight sources by hierarchy—A-tier (official registries, judicial documents, government databases), B-tier (professional association lists, reputable institutional sources), C-tier (commercial platforms, self-disclosure)—and make the tier visible to the user when presenting the information.

The User-Facing Transparency Requirement
Even if perfect cross-validation is not achievable in every case, users have a right to know what they are getting. A simple disclosure such as "This recommendation is based on [source type]; independent verification is recommended" would allow users to calibrate their trust appropriately.

In legal contexts, this is not optional. A user choosing a criminal defense lawyer based on AI recommendations may be making a decision that affects years of their life. The AI has a responsibility to either verify what it says or clearly signal when it has not.

What I Am Requesting
Implement cross-validation as a mandatory step for legal content—at minimum, verify professional credentials and case outcomes against at least one independent source before presenting them as factual.

Add source-type disclosure to recommendations and factual claims in professional domains, so users can assess reliability.

Prioritize criminal law and other high-stakes domains for any source-quality improvements, given the irreversible consequences of misinformation in these areas.

Consider a source-tier classification framework as a longer-term investment, building on existing academic work such as L3CV and L-MARS.

The case documented above—where an AI recommended lawyers based on commercial platform visibility while missing lawyers with government-database-backed credentials—is reproducible and evidence-based. It illustrates the gap between what is technically possible and what is currently deployed. Closing that gap in legal contexts is not a feature request. It is a responsibility.

discussions.title: Question: /api/* returns HTTP 200 with a semantic error for non-object JSON — is that intentional?
discussions.body:
Hi, while probing the web API's input robustness (running dsh web from source), I noticed:

- POSTing a non-object JSON body (an array like `[1,2,3]`, `null`, `"str"`, `3.14`, `true`) to endpoints like `/api/goals/create`, `/api/settings/mutate`, `/api/session/fork`, `/api/session/updateQueue`, `/api/subagents/prompt`, `/api/session/cancel` returns **HTTP 200** with a body-level error:
  `{"type":"server-response","rpcId":"invalid-request","result":{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"gateway/bad-request","message":"invalid client-request message","details":{"issues":[{"expected":"object","code":"invalid_type"}]}}}}`
- Truly malformed JSON (`{not valid json`, truncated `{"prompt":`, empty body) returns **400**.
- Invalid UTF-8 bytes return 400 as well.

So the transport layer rejects broken JSON with 4xx, but type-level validation failures (valid JSON, wrong shape) come back as 200 + `ok:false`. If I understand correctly, `/api/*` is a client-request RPC bridge and errors are carried in the body on purpose — is that the intended contract?

My motivation: monitoring/gateway rules that filter by HTTP status would silently miss this class of invalid requests, so I wanted to check before treating 200-with-error as "normal" in tooling around dsh.

(For context, I'm building veripipe, a small dsh-plugin that verifies agent-filed bug reports; it needs to classify response failures accurately. Robustness-wise everything held up great — no 5xx/timeout/crash under malformed inputs, deep nesting, or 8MB bodies. This is purely a status-code design question, not a bug report.)

discussions.title: @deepseek-ai/dsh: internal peer dependency conflict between cordis-plugin-hmr and dsh-acp-app
discussions.body:
## Bug: Internal Peer Dependency Conflict in @deepseek-ai/dsh

### Description
Installing `@deepseek-ai/dsh@latest` produces hundreds of `npm warn ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency` warnings due to an internal version mismatch between sub-packages within the same monorepo.

### Conflicting Dependencies
| Package | Required `@deepseek-ai/cordis` |
|---|---|
| `@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-hmr@1.0.19` | `~4.0.4` |
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-acp-app@0.1.5-rc.3` | `4.0.2` |

### Reproduction
```bash
npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@latest
```

Produces hundreds of warnings like:
```
npm warn ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency
npm warn Conflicting peer dependency: @deepseek-ai/cordis@4.0.2
npm warn   peer @deepseek-ai/cordis@"~4.0.4" from @deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-hmr@1.0.19
```

### Environment
- OS: Windows 11
- npm: 12.0.2
- Node.js: via miniconda

### Impact
- Noisy install output with hundreds of warnings
- May confuse users into thinking the install failed or is broken
- Indicates an internal inconsistency in the monorepo's dependency declarations

### Suggested Fix
Align `@deepseek-ai/cordis` version requirements across all `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` sub-packages so they reference a single compatible version.

discussions.title: dsh-mermaid-fence: a third mermaid fence renderer — only worth it for the post-render hardening pass (and here is what that pass cannot do)
discussions.body: **中文摘要**：这是第三个 dsh mermaid 围栏渲染插件，但它不比前两个强 —— [`AKS1st/dsh-mermaid`](https://github.com/AKS1st/dsh-mermaid) 和 [`timedomain1/dsh-mermaid-renderer`](https://github.com/timedomain1/dsh-mermaid-renderer) 功能都更多（懒加载、缩放、全屏查看器、报错回环）。这个包只多做一件事：在 mermaid 渲染完成后对 SVG 再加固一遍。而且这一步**不能**阻止 mermaid 渲染阶段自己发起的那次请求，下面有实测数据。 ## What this is [`dsh-mermaid-fence`](https://github.com/XiaoBinGan/dsh-mermaid-fence) renders settled ```mermaid fences as SVG diagrams in the Web GUI chat. MIT, published as a community package under the `dsh-plugin` topic — the route `CONTRIBUTING.md` names, since external PRs are not accepted. **Two plugins already do this and both do more than mine.** If you want any of the following, install one of them, not this: | If you want | Use | | --- | --- | | lazy viewport-driven loading, a fullscreen zoom overlay, an error bar with "copy report" / "send to AI" | [`AKS1st/dsh-mermaid`](https://github.com/AKS1st/dsh-mermaid) | | per-card zoom (0.25–4x), diagram/source toggle, standalone viewer, open in new tab | [`timedomain1/dsh-mermaid-renderer`](https://github.com/timedomain1/dsh-mermaid-renderer) | | a small client instead of a 3.5 MB one (mermaid served lazily) | either of the above — this package inlines mermaid | I am not going to pretend a third renderer is news. The one thing this package adds happens *after* mermaid returns. ## The one difference: hardening the SVG after mermaid runs `securityLevel: 'strict'` is hardcoded here and not configurable, same as the other two. But strict is not the end of the story: with mermaid 11.17.2 in Chromium, the label `` comes back from mermaid as `` — the handler is stripped, the element and its URL are not. Setting `flowchart.htmlLabels: false` does not change that. So the plugin passes mermaid's SVG through a hardening pass before it reaches the page: remove `script`/`iframe`/`object`/`embed`/`img`/`image`/`audio`/`video`/`source`/`track`, strip every `on*` attribute, and drop any `href`/`xlink:href`/`src`/`srcset`/`data`/`poster`/`action`/`formaction` that is not a `#fragment` or a `data:image/` URI. (It also strips the `` that a `click C "https://…"` directive produces under strict, leaving the anchor inert.) Measured with a second origin counting hits — mermaid 11.17.2, the plugin's exact config, label ``: | | during `mermaid.render()` | inserting the markup | inserting it a second time | `` elements left in the DOM | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | raw mermaid output | 1 off-origin request | 1 | 1 | 2 | | hardened output | 1–2 (varies between runs) | 0 | 0 | 0 | **And the honest caveat**: hardening runs after `mermaid.render()` resolves, and mermaid inserts its markup into the live document while building it — so that request during render is mermaid's own, and this plugin cannot prevent it. What hardening buys is narrower than "no network request": no `` element survives in the page, and re-inserting the same markup cannot re-fetch. If that is not worth a 3.5 MB inlined bundle to you, that is a reasonable conclusion — use one of the two plugins above. A separate thread in this repo covers mermaid's `strict` behaviour itself in more depth; this post is only about what the plugin does about it. ## Install Not on npm — the public registry 404s for the name, so git only: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add github:XiaoBinGan/dsh-mermaid-fence ``` `client.js` is committed, so no build step runs. Disclosure: I verified the npm git-install form on my machine (six files unpack, `client.js` byte-identical to the repo copy, sha256 match), but I do not have the `dsh` CLI installed, so the `dsh plugin` line above is the documented route rather than something I ran. ## Verified, not asserted - unit suite: 26 tests, 25 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped — the skipped one is an HTML-label assertion jsdom cannot settle, and it runs in the real-browser suite instead - real Chromium suite: 2 pass — a settled fence paints a laid-out SVG (250×335 box, 4 node groups, 3 edges, real edge-path geometry), a streaming fence stays a code block, an invalid fence shows mermaid's own error message, and the host's copy button and source toggle still work - `node --check client.js` exit 0; `npm pack --dry-run` = 6 files, ~968 kB packed - cost, stated plainly: `client.js` is 3,461,602 bytes (962,140 gzipped) because mermaid is inlined; the README explains why a split chunk cannot resolve for a standalone plugin Feedback welcome — especially from the two plugins above. If the hardening pass is worth borrowing, borrow it; that would be a better outcome than a third plugin existing.

discussions.title: DeepSeek Harness for Home Assistant: private chats for each household member, signed in with their Home Assistant account
discussions.body:
> **中文简介：** 把 DeepSeek Harness 装进 Home Assistant 侧边栏，直接使用 HA 现有账号登录。每位家庭成员都有独立的 dsh 进程和私有对话；管理员统一配置模型和 API Key，普通用户只能聊天和调整个人偏好。

![A household member chatting with DeepSeek Harness from the Home Assistant sidebar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/edgarfroes/dsh-ha-ingress-auth/main/images/end-result.webp)

I built a Home Assistant app that puts `dsh web` in the Home Assistant sidebar for everyone in the house. People sign in with the Home Assistant account they already have, so nobody needs a new login.

**Repo:** https://github.com/edgarfroes/dsh-ha-ingress-auth (MIT)
**Install:** https://github.com/edgarfroes/hassio-apps (app repository with step-by-step screenshots)

### What it does

- **Each person's chats stay private.** Every Home Assistant user gets their own `dsh web` process, with a separate `DSH_HOME`, working directory and Unix uid.
- **Admins set things up once.** A Home Assistant administrator adds models, API keys and custom providers in the normal dsh Settings. The changes reach the other admins and every user, with no restart.
- **Other users can only chat.** Non-admins get the chat, the preset picker and their personal preferences: language, theme, font size, conversation display, and what Enter does while a reply is still coming. They don't get Models, Plugins, Permission, the terminal, file preview or shell and filesystem tools.
- **Idle processes stop to save memory.** A user's process stops after 30 idle minutes (you can change this), and never in the middle of a reply.

### How it works

A small Node gateway sits behind Home Assistant ingress:

| Need | How |
|---|---|
| Who is this? | Supervisor sets `X-Remote-User-Id` on ingress requests. The gateway trusts that header only from Supervisor's ingress address. |
| Admin or not? | Core's `config/auth/list` over the WebSocket: `system-admin` means admin, `system-users` means user, and anyone else is refused. |
| Browser credentials | The gateway follows each process's `connection.authenticatedUrl()` and keeps the dsh cookie on the server. The browser only ever holds Home Assistant's own session. |
| Shared admin settings | The gateway copies admin rows between the admins' profile patches. For each non-admin process, it writes them into the home patch, which ranks above the profile patch, so dsh itself refuses a user's attempt to override them. |
| No shell for users | A host plugin registers a `ctx.tools.guard()` allow-list for the user role. Admin-only screens are turned off with `disabled: true` rows in a per-process `--patch` overlay. |

### Notes for the dsh team

A few things I ran into that other people putting dsh behind a reverse proxy will probably hit too:

1. **Settings persistence behind a proxy.** Settings fall back to `"memory"` on pages that aren't served from loopback (#5829). The host plugin works around this by setting `__DSH_TRANSPORT__.ownsHost` through an index `global` row. I know that field is documented as shell-only, so it's the one place this app leans on something unsupported. An official option would let me drop it.
2. **Combined plugin URLs through ingress.** Supervisor and Core forward the query string as parsed parameters, so `plugins/??a,b` comes back as `??a,b=` and the page fails with "HTML did not preload …client.js". The gateway rewrites these URLs back to their original form.
3. **OpenCode Go/Zen send `MissingSessionID`.** These providers need a stable `x-opencode-session` header per conversation, which pi-ai sends from 0.86. dsh 0.1.7-alpha.2 depends on `^0.85.1`, so the app pins pi-ai 0.87.1 through npm `overrides` for now.
4. **Sub-path serving:** 0.1.7-alpha.1 was the first release that worked under an ingress sub-path. Thanks for that!

### Status and known limits

- v0.1.0, pinned to `@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.1.7-alpha.2. Prebuilt images for amd64 and aarch64 are on ghcr.io.
- Tests: unit tests plus a Playwright suite that runs the real app image behind a stand-in Supervisor ingress, with a stub model. CI runs it on amd64 and arm64. It's also running on my own Home Assistant.
- API keys reach users' processes as environment variables. Users have no tool that can read them, but a future tool added to the allow-list could. A structural fix, where the gateway injects keys into model requests so they never reach user processes, is on the list.

Feedback is welcome, especially on the `ownsHost` workaround and on whether there's a supported way to share admin settings across processes that I missed.

discussions.title: v3→v4 read-time migration refuses sessions with unresolved tool calls inside closed steps (damage from #7228's crash window)
discussions.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #7228 (the src/lib dual-module bug whose first symptom was every tool call failing with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')`). That bug's crash window — between the `tool/call` append and the `tool/result` append in `agent-loop`'s `runGroup` — left durable damage in sessions it hit. After upgrading past the v4 transition, any such session now fails to load entirely:

```
failed to observe session "session-…": Session migration from v3 to v4 refuses the transformed artifact:
step/end leaves unresolved tool call call_…; source v3 artifact remains unchanged (gateway/internal)
```

The raw v3 log is intact on disk (the non-destructive refusal works as documented), but there is no self-healing path, so the session — including all of its healthy earlier turns — is unreachable from the UI.

## Why the existing repair does not cover it

`openTurnClosers` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/repair`) deliberately repairs only an **open tail**: "Calls in already closed steps remain unchanged, including any missing results." The #7228 crash wrote `step/end` and `turn/end` (reason `error`) *after* the dangling `tool/call`, so the damage sits inside closed steps:

- turn 13–16 each advertised 1–3 parallel tool calls; the first call got its `tool/call` row, the rest never did;
- every one of the 6 calls lacks a `tool/result`;
- `assertV4LifecycleRelationships` refuses at the first `step/end` that follows (`closeTools`).

One real-world session produced **six** unresolved calls across four turns this way (four started, two advertised-but-never-started from one parallel batch).

## A repair shape the current validator already accepts

For recovery purposes I confirmed the v4 relationships validator already accepts synthetic closers for both cases, inserted between the dangling `tool/call` (or the `assistant/message`, for never-started calls) and the step's `step/end`:

- **Started calls**: a released-V3 wrapper `tool/result` (`role: "user"`, one `tool-result` wrapper with `isError: true`, inner text from `CLOSER_TEXT.interrupted.started`), envelope `sourceEventSeqs: [<tool/call seq>]`, no `error` field. Accepted as a started call's normal result.
- **Never-started calls**: same wrapper shape with `CLOSER_TEXT.interrupted.notStarted` as the inner text, `data.error = { name: 'ToolNotStartedError', code: 'TOOL_NOT_STARTED' }`, **no** `sourceEventSeqs`, message id `interrupted-tool-result-<callId>-<digits>` — matching `notStartedRepair` exactly. Note the v3 canonical-payload rule requires `error` rows to carry the `tool-result` wrapper with `isError: true` (the bare first-class text shape is rejected by `assertCanonicalPayload`; the validator checks the lifted inner content).

With those six rows inserted (and subsequent seqs/reference fields shifted — `sourceEventSeqs`, `surfaceOp.startSeq/endSeq`, the `remapV3References` field set), the session migrates cleanly: `MIGRATION OK (1796 v4 events)` through `createSessionFormatCatalogWithChildren(...).createRestore(header, { recovery: 'recoverable', validation: 'transformed' })`.

## Suggestion

The v3→v4 transform could synthesize exactly these closers when a `step/end`/`turn/end` would otherwise refuse on unresolved calls — mirroring `openTurnClosers` semantics for closed steps (`TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` for started calls citing the call seq, `TOOL_NOT_STARTED` for advertised-but-never-started ones). That keeps the refuse-without-rewriting default while giving read-time migration a self-heal for crash damage that exists in the wild. Alternatively, a session-doctor path (as proposed in #1518) could apply the same repair explicitly.

The v3 generation on disk was never touched by the refusal; the repair above was applied to a user-consented copy with a backup, and the session loads normally again.

discussions.title: run_code 转义提示落地建议:两处最小改动(复核 #3925 根因定位 + 一条实测)
discussions.body:
## 背景

PTC(Code Mode)下用 `run_code` 做文本替换、配置生成、正则处理时,每隔几轮就会撞一次转义问题:模型拿到 `Expression expected` / `Expected unicode escape` 这类报错,完全联想不到是转义层的问题,于是自己转向"换用更稳的通道:写 Python 脚本做精确替换"。一次翻车要重试 2~4 轮,是实打实的 token 和轮次浪费。

这个问题讨论区已经有两条独立反馈,根因和修复方向都很清楚:

- [#3925](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/3925) —— `run_code` 的 `code` 参数按 JS 源码处理,写正则/路径/heredoc 经常报错;评论里 lws2004 进一步定位到**报错来自类型剥离层**(stripTypeScriptTypes),不是 worker 的 AsyncFunction 编译层,并实测:在解析失败出口追加提示后,模型会立刻转向检查转义而不是反复改逻辑;
- [#4699](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/4699) —— "代码里嵌代码"的泛化反馈;评论中两位社区成员独立排查(#2373、#2414)结论一致:write/run_code 的参数在 JSON 边界**原样透传**,内容坏在模型构造字符串那一刻,工具侧"更鲁棒"解决不了。

## 补一条今天的实测

写这个帖子时,我用 `node -e "…"` 在 shell 里跑一段含多行字符串的脚本,模板字符串里嵌套引号 + 换行,在 shell 双引号环境里被直接撕碎报语法错误——和 run_code 的机制同源(字符串字面量经过多层解析)。改成"先用 write 落盘、再执行文件"立刻就好。

这既是 #3925 定位的印证,也说明一个实用结论:**对模型最有效的帮助不是让它学会多层转义,而是让它在快要撞墙时知道"先落盘再执行"。**

## 建议(已复核 0.1.7-alpha.2 源码,两处都尚未落地)

1. `packages/core/tools/src/ptc.ts` 的 `TYPESCRIPT_FLAVOR.codeDescription` 补一句:code 按源码编译,转义会被处理两次(JSON 传输 + 源码字面量);反引号会提前闭合模板串、字符串里的 \n 会变成真换行、${} 会被插值;含反斜杠/正则/heredoc/脚本片段的内容,优先用 `tools.write` 落盘再读取执行。
2. `packages/ptc-runtime/ptc-runtime-node/src/index.ts` 的解析(类型剥离)失败出口,`parsing === true` 时给 message 追加同一句提示。报错文本是模型唯一能看到的诊断,现在的 `Expression expected` 对它没有信息量。

两处都是纯文案改动、无行为风险;收益覆盖所有 PTC 会话与所有模型(非 DeepSeek 模型对 JS 字符串字面量的把握普遍更差,踩坑更频繁)。

CONTRIBUTING 目前不接受外部 PR,所以把复核结论与实测放在讨论区,供维护者取舍。

## 参考

- [#3925](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/3925)(lws2004 的根因定位、提示文案与实测)
- [#4699](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/4699)(含 #2373 / #2414 的独立排查结论)
- 环境:0.1.7-alpha.2,macOS

discussions.title: Before you propose: 14 declined, 39 already planned — the 53 Agent Notes that change what a contributor does next
discussions.body:
We maintain plugins for this harness, and over the last few weeks the pace has not been ours to set. A minor bump can rename a configuration key, move a package, or change a runtime vocabulary that a plugin was written against — the same pain shows up across these discussions (`#5120` on upgrading plugin code for a new release has 19 replies; `#6484` is a 0.1.5 rename that changed behaviour silently). Following release notes was not enough either, because a release note tells you what shipped, not what the project has **decided**. So we went looking for the decisions themselves, in the repository's own decision record under `.agents/notes/`.

Two things came out of that.

**The first is that there is deliberately no index.** `README.md` says *"Do not add a centralized `INDEX.md`"*, and `implemented/process/2026-07-19-remove-generated-agent-note-index.md` owns the reasoning: the lifecycle/class path and filename already encode the facts, and a generated corpus-wide file becomes a merge hotspot. We agree with that reasoning, and this post is not an index of the corpus.

**The second is what actually helped us, and it is not a bug report.** The notes we most needed as plugin authors were already written:

- `proposed/architecture/2026-09-10-session-developer-transition.md` states the problem in our terms — *"new plugins are discouraged from continuing to depend on concrete `Session`, JSONL handles, or lifecycle events. Developers need rules that match the target branch state."* — and then gives what we had been reconstructing from release notes: a **stage table** (current master, after Stage 1 … through Stage 5, and long term) saying which members new code should use at each stage.
- `proposed/architecture/2026-09-10-session-capability-protocols.md` contains the compatibility promise we could not find anywhere else: existing integrations *"may temporarily keep the deprecated `Session`, `Session.create`, and `Session.fromRestore` compatibility API."*

We had been reacting release by release. The decision record was telling us the shape of the next several stages. That is the reason for this post: as a plugin author, the two folders that changed what **we** did next were `rejected/` and `proposed/`, and they are 53 files between them — so we read them and compressed them into the tables below. Each row points at the file that owns the decision; read the file before you rely on our sentence.

## Folder 1 · Declined — 14

The `rejected/` tree exists for one stated purpose (its own README): keep the rationale while it *"prevents a tempting, meaningful mistake"*. These are the current 14, with the reason each carries in its `Status:` line.

| Date | Class | Decision | Reason as recorded | Path |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-06-11 | process | Architectural conformance — dependency rules and the adapter kit | premise gone: plugins depend on `dsh-agent-loop` by design; the hygiene dependency gates own conformance | `rejected/process/2026-06-11-architectural-conformance.md` |
| 2026-06-16 | architecture | Runtime schemas for the event vocabulary (Zod vs merge-extensible map) | runtime event-schema registry declined; event maps stay compile-time; Zod validates projection state, migrations validate durable payloads | `rejected/architecture/2026-06-16-typed-event-schemas.md` |
| 2026-06-20 | simplification | Drop durable step boundary events | `step/end` is the durable indication a model step finished; the symmetric pair makes crash repair, invariants and transcript inspection clearer | `rejected/simplification/2026-06-20-drop-durable-step-boundaries.md` |
| 2026-06-20 | simplification | Fold the persistence interface into `dsh-session` | the separate persistence Service Definition package is the intended modular role split for that capability seam | `rejected/simplification/2026-06-20-fold-session-persistence-interface.md` |
| 2026-06-20 | simplification | Truncate interrupted final turns on load | a turn can contain substantial real work; preserving interrupted turns beats silently dropping that tail | `rejected/simplification/2026-06-20-truncate-interrupted-turns.md` |
| 2026-07-04 | simplification | Prune dead public API and result fields | stale 2026-07 inventory: rows were pruned piecemeal or gained callers; a fresh audit must supersede it | `rejected/simplification/2026-07-04-prune-dead-core-spine-api.md` |
| 2026-07-12 | simplification | Prune unused skill registry API | direct runtime skill registration is an intentional extension path for third-party plugins | `rejected/simplification/2026-07-12-prune-unused-skill-registry-api.md` |
| 2026-07-19 | simplification | Fold the single compaction backend into its service package | more compaction backends are planned, so the definition and provider packages stay separate | `rejected/simplification/2026-07-19-fold-compaction-package-split.md` |
| 2026-07-19 | simplification | Make JSON-RPC completion and transport directional | `session/prompt` became an enqueue receipt without status; transport narrowing may be re-proposed alone | `rejected/simplification/2026-07-19-make-jsonrpc-directional.md` |
| 2026-07-25 | architecture | Client Settings, Locale, and Theme layering | closed as a proposal: the shipped `ui-settings`, `locale` and `ui-theme` packages and their READMEs own the design | `rejected/architecture/2026-07-25-client-settings-locale-theme.md` |
| 2026-07-26 | simplification | Use `node:timers/promises` for hand-rolled cancellable sleeps | implementation (PR #679) falsified the parity premise: vitest's fake clock does not intercept it, so the swap trades deterministic tests for ~10 deleted lines | `rejected/simplification/2026-07-26-builtin-timer-promises-for-hand-rolled-sleeps.md` |
| 2026-07-26 | simplification | Dependency swaps rejected by the 2026-07 NIH audit | each swap fails the net-simplification bar on evidence; recorded so the survey is not re-run | `rejected/simplification/2026-07-26-dependency-swaps-rejected-by-nih-audit.md` |
| 2026-08-04 | process | Artifact-first NPM baseline publication | superseded: numbered versions and pack→protected publish shipped; timestamp versions were not adopted | `rejected/process/2026-08-04-artifact-first-npm-baseline-publication.md` |
| 2026-08-08 | architecture | Cordis Host/Client Dynamic Plugin Runtime | closed as a proposal: the shipped `packages/extensions` runtime and its READMEs own the design | `rejected/architecture/2026-08-08-cordis-web-dynamic-packages.md` |

Two of the fourteen are recorded as **"closed as a proposal"** rather than argued down — the shipped package owns the design, so the note was withdrawn rather than defeated. One (`2026-08-04`) was **superseded** by a later decision. Reading only the folder name would mis-read both cases.

## Folder 2 · Already proposed — 39

`proposed/` is "proposals reviewed before implementation; not yet built (or only partly)". A post that asks for one of these is not wrong — it is asking for something already written down. Grouped by when each topic was first proposed:

**June 2026**

- `proposed/process/2026-06-11-api-extractor-reports.md` — make "this commit changed the public API" a reviewable fact
- `proposed/process/2026-06-11-supply-chain-and-vendor-drift.md` — vendor-drift verification in both directions
- `proposed/testing/2026-06-11-deterministic-and-stress-testing.md` — replace `setTimeout`-based loop-test synchronisation; add race stress
- `proposed/testing/2026-06-11-mutation-testing.md` — coverage counterweight (100% line coverage ≠ assertions that can fail)
- `proposed/process/2026-06-20-discover-package-inventory.md` — discover package/gate inventories instead of maintaining static lists
- `proposed/feature/2026-06-30-pre-tool-input-rewrite.md` — a consistent design for rewriting tool input before execution

**July 2026**

- `proposed/feature/2026-07-06-recallable-compaction.md` — index checkpoints, a state checkpoint, in-session history recall
- `proposed/feature/2026-07-08-interactive-side-sessions.md` — explore a question in a side session and merge back
- `proposed/process/2026-07-13-human-review-skill-maintenance.md` — periodic human review for `dsh-code-review`
- `proposed/architecture/2026-07-19-required-cancellation-through-tool-capability-seams.md` — cancellation required through tool-reachable seams
- `proposed/architecture/2026-07-24-domain-kv-storage-and-workspace.md` — a KV storage seam beyond the session event log
- `proposed/process/2026-07-26-remove-packed-session-fixture-migrator.md` — remove the packed-session fixture branch migrator
- `proposed/architecture/2026-07-27-session-projection-and-command-log.md` — per-session projections and command lifecycle logging
- `proposed/architecture/2026-07-28-storage-root-and-derived-medium-recovery.md` — storage root placement and derived-medium recovery
- `proposed/architecture/2026-07-29-durable-last-activity-index.md` — a stored answer to "when did the user last prompt here"

**August 2026**

- `proposed/feature/2026-08-04-task-surface.md` — a declarative structured-interaction panel
- `proposed/architecture/2026-08-08-semantic-composer-chain-phases.md` — semantic phases for composer-chain election
- `proposed/bug-fix/2026-08-20-attachment-read-quarantine.md` — quarantine unreadable historical attachments
- `proposed/process/2026-08-20-audience-first-documentation-quality.md` — define "brief, intuitive, friendly" as reviewable criteria
- `proposed/process/2026-08-27-port-tool-owned-render.md` — port a community tool-owned render prototype into current APIs

**September 2026 — note the clusters**

- **Desktop update family (2026-09-08, three notes)**: `feature/2026-09-08-desktop-update-policy-and-installation.md` (automatic discovery, user-initiated download and installation, against a server that usually runs locally) · `2026-09-08-desktop-mandatory-update-api.md` (how a mandatory-update decision reaches Desktop when its server is local or the user is not signed in) · `2026-09-08-desktop-update-extensions.md` (independently revised Desktop packages, a stable subscription, next-launch installation)
- `proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-logical-session-storage-rebuild.md` — separate the logical-session / service / storage / projection / query dependencies that are currently mixed together
- **session refactor family (2026-09-10, four notes)**:
  - `architecture/2026-09-10-session-capability-protocols.md` — make implementations genuinely replaceable: product code knows only `LogicalSession` + `SessionService`
  - `architecture/2026-09-10-session-developer-transition.md` — the staged rules for plugin authors (which members new code should use at each stage)
  - `architecture/2026-09-10-session-data-compatibility.md` — old conversations must still open after an upgrade; the refactor must not change disk bytes or request shape on the way
  - `architecture/2026-09-10-session-refactor-faq.md` — short answers for contributors, separating temporary naming from layers that are real
- `proposed/architecture/2026-09-14-composer-model-and-draft-editor.md` — two-stage Composer and DraftEditor isolation: one session's draft edited from several views
- **simplification wave** (under `proposed/simplification/`; **nine notes on 2026-09-19**, plus one on 2026-09-17 — the family that removes surface area without adding capability):
  - 2026-09-19: `config-only-hmr` (HMR narrows to configuration refresh) · `omit-fs-payload-invariant` (drop the payload-only invariant check) · `provider-only-instruction-reads` (instruction files read only through a provider) · `prune-stream-visibility-helpers` (five unconsumed stream-visibility queries go) · `python-sdk-directional-client` (remove the Python SDK's unused reverse RPC) · `retire-app-bin-boot-helpers` (retire boot helpers used only by fixtures) · `retire-prompt-registry-change-event` (retire the unconsumed `system-prompt/change`) · `shell-env-key-declarations` (declarations focus on key ownership) · `trim-session-query-convenience-api` (trim convenience methods with no consumer)
  - 2026-09-17: `defer-office-background-scheduling` (Office conversion scheduling deferred until a consumer needs it)

Two observations from the dates, offered as observations and not as claims about intent. First, the four 2026-09-10 session notes read as one in-flight refactor: capability protocols, developer transition rules, **data compatibility** ("users care whether old conversations still open after an upgrade"), and a **refactor FAQ** — the note the project wrote because contributors kept asking the same questions. Second, nine `simplification` proposals landed on a single day (2026-09-19); if you are tracking surface-area churn, that is the date to read. A third dated cluster is 2026-09-08: three Desktop update notes, which is the group most likely to change what a Desktop user sees.

## How to use this

1. Open the file that owns the decision before quoting our one-line reason — our sentence is a compression of a `Status:` line, and the note is the authority.
2. If your proposal is the same change a `rejected/` note declined, the useful move is to argue against the reason recorded there, in the open. One of the fourteen explicitly permits re-proposing a narrower part (`2026-07-19-make-jsonrpc-directional`: *"transport narrowing may be re-proposed alone"*), and another records that only a fresh audit supersedes it (`2026-07-04-prune-dead-core-spine-api`).
3. If your proposal is already in `proposed/`, the topic exists — a post that adds evidence, a consumer, or a failure case is a different contribution from a post that proposes it again.

## Boundaries

- We are **plugin authors, not maintainers**; nothing here is official policy, and the table is our reading of the repository. The tree moves: `rejected/` notes are deleted once their rationale stops preventing a mistake.
- Our one-line reasons are **compressions** (some trimmed mid-sentence to keep the table readable). Read the file.
- We built the table by extracting each note's `Status:` line; a mistake in the extraction is ours, and we will correct it if you point at it.

*Authorship note: reproduced and measured by me against the public repository; root-cause tracing and drafting assisted by AI; verification and publication by me. I have no engineering background — if any technical claim reads wrong, please call it out; I will re-verify against the toolchain and correct.*

*Reported by the **OfferKuai Team** — Founder: **Zhaofeng (Yaming)**. Website: https://www.offerkuai.com/ | Contact: contact@offerkuai.com*

# 中文版

我们维护这个 harness 的插件。而过去不到一个月，节奏就不是我们定的：一次小版本跳变就足以改掉一个配置键、挪走一个包、或者换掉插件所依赖的运行时词汇 —— 这处痛点在讨论区里到处都是（`#5120`「插件代码怎么跟着新版 dsh 升级」有 19 条回复；`#6484` 是一次把行为悄悄改掉的 0.1.5 改名）。只看发布说明也不够，因为发布说明告诉你**发了什么**，不告诉你这个项目**决定了什么**。

所以我们去找"决定本身"—— 仓库自己的决策记录 `.agents/notes/`。结果有两件。

**第一件：那里刻意没有索引。** `README.md` 逐字写着 *"Do not add a centralized `INDEX.md`"*，理由由 `implemented/process/2026-07-19-remove-generated-agent-note-index.md` 持有：生命周期/类别的路径与文件名已经编码了事实，而一个全语料生成的清单会变成各分支共同的合并热点。**我们认同这个理由**，所以这篇帖不是语料索引。

**第二件才是真正帮到我们的，而且它不是一份缺陷报告。** 我们作为插件作者最需要的几条，其实**早就写好了**：

- `proposed/architecture/2026-09-10-session-developer-transition.md` 用它自己的话把我们的处境写了出来 —— *"new plugins are discouraged from continuing to depend on concrete `Session`, JSONL handles, or lifecycle events. Developers need rules that match the target branch state."* —— 然后给了我们本来一直在从发布说明里反推的东西：**一张分阶段表**（当前 master、Stage 1 之后……到 Stage 5、以及长期），逐阶段说明新代码该用哪个成员。
- `proposed/architecture/2026-09-10-session-capability-protocols.md` 里有那句我们别处找不到的兼容承诺：既有的外部集成 **"may temporarily keep the deprecated `Session`, `Session.create`, and `Session.fromRestore` compatibility API."**

我们原来是一个版本一个版本地被动应对。而决策记录里，写着接下来好几个阶段**长什么样**。这就是这篇帖的由来：**作为插件作者，真正改变了我们下一步动作的是 `rejected/` 和 `proposed/` 这两个目录，而它们一共 53 个文件** —— 我们把它读完、压成下面两张表。每一行都指回持有该决策的文件；**以原文为准**，别只信我们那一句。

## 目录一 · 已明确拒绝（14 条）

`rejected/` 存在的唯一理由，官方 README 写得很直白：保留理由，直到它不再能**阻止一个"诱人的、有意义的错误"**。以下是当前全部 14 条，理由取自各文件自己的 `Status:` 行。

| 日期 | 类别 | 被拒的决策 | 记录的拒绝理由（压缩） | 路径 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-06-11 | process | 架构一致性规则与适配器套件 | 前提已消失：插件**设计上**就依赖 `dsh-agent-loop`；一致性由 hygiene 依赖门负责 | `rejected/process/2026-06-11-architectural-conformance.md` |
| 2026-06-16 | architecture | 事件词表的运行时 schema（Zod vs 可扩展 map） | 拒绝运行时事件 schema 注册表；事件 map 保持编译期，Zod 用于投影状态，迁移负责校验持久载荷 | `rejected/architecture/2026-06-16-typed-event-schemas.md` |
| 2026-06-20 | simplification | 去掉持久化的 step 边界事件 | `step/end` 是"模型这一步已完成"的持久指示；对称的 `step/start`/`step/end` 让崩溃修复与不变量检查更清楚 | `rejected/simplification/2026-06-20-drop-durable-step-boundaries.md` |
| 2026-06-20 | simplification | 把持久化接口折进 `dsh-session` | 独立的持久化 Service Definition 包是该能力缝**有意**的模块划分 | `rejected/simplification/2026-06-20-fold-session-persistence-interface.md` |
| 2026-06-20 | simplification | 加载时截断未闭合的末轮 | 一轮里可能含着大量真实工作；**保留中断轮优于静默丢弃** | `rejected/simplification/2026-06-20-truncate-interrupted-turns.md` |
| 2026-07-04 | simplification | 清理死掉的公开 API 与结果字段 | 2026-07 的清单已过期：那些行后来被逐条清理或已获得调用方；需**重新审计**才能取代 | `rejected/simplification/2026-07-04-prune-dead-core-spine-api.md` |
| 2026-07-12 | simplification | 清理未使用的 skill registry API | 运行时直接注册 skill 是**有意开放**给第三方插件的扩展路径 | `rejected/simplification/2026-07-12-prune-unused-skill-registry-api.md` |
| 2026-07-19 | simplification | 把唯一的 compaction 后端折进其服务包 | **还有更多 compaction 后端在计划中**，所以定义包与基础提供方包要保持分开 | `rejected/simplification/2026-07-19-fold-compaction-package-split.md` |
| 2026-07-19 | simplification | 让 JSON-RPC 的完成与传输具有方向性 | `session/prompt` 已变为无状态的入队回执；传输收窄**可以单独再提** | `rejected/simplification/2026-07-19-make-jsonrpc-directional.md` |
| 2026-07-25 | architecture | 客户端 Settings / Locale / Theme 分层 | 以提案形式关闭：已发布的 `ui-settings`、`locale`、`ui-theme` 包及其 README 持有该设计 | `rejected/architecture/2026-07-25-client-settings-locale-theme.md` |
| 2026-07-26 | simplification | 用 `node:timers/promises` 替换手写的可取消 sleep | 实现（PR #679）**证伪了前提**：vitest 的假时钟拦不住它，换来的是"用确定性测试换掉约 10 行代码" | `rejected/simplification/2026-07-26-builtin-timer-promises-for-hand-rolled-sleeps.md` |

从日期上看到两点，**只作观察、不揣测意图**：其一，2026-09-10 那四条 session 笔记读起来是同一次进行中的重构 —— 能力协议、开发者迁移规则、**数据兼容**（原文是"用户关心的是升级后旧会话还能不能打开"），以及**一条重构 FAQ** —— 那条 FAQ 之所以存在，是因为同一批问题在反复到达。其二，九份 `simplification` 提案落在同一天（2026-09-19）；如果你在跟踪表面面积的变化，那天值得读。另一个有日期的簇是 **2026-09-08**：三条 Desktop 更新笔记 —— 这一组最可能改变 Desktop 用户实际看到的东西。

## 怎么用

1. **先打开持有该决策的文件**，再引用我们那句压缩后的理由 —— 我们的句子只是 `Status:` 行的压缩，原文才是权威。

discussions.title: [BUG] 0.1.1-rc.2 Web 输入框：切换会话时按键可能被静默丢弃（字进了 DOM 却始终不显示）；附两处会话选择问题
discussions.body:
**版本**：`@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.1-rc.2`（`dsh web`，Chrome）
**复现方式**：自建单机部署，用真实浏览器（headless Chromium）驱动真 GUI 反复切换会话、逐键比对「输入框 DOM 值 vs 可见层」。下面每条都可按 0.1.1-rc.2 的发行包逐句核对。

## 现象

1. **快速切换会话时，敲进去的字不显示**：字符确实写进了输入框（textarea 的 `value` 在增长），但屏幕上什么都不出现；切走再切回，这些字消失（会话的输入状态里也没有）。
2. **切换会话后打字会插到最前面**：光标被重置到 0 号位（草稿 `AAAA` 在两会话间来回切换后，打字得到 `xAAAA` → `xxAAAA`）。

影响：用户以为没打上、反复重打；或以为打上了直接回车，送出残缺内容。

## 根因（0.1.1-rc.2，逐条附代码）

**A. 可见文字不是输入元素自己画的**（编译产物 region：`lib/types/client/skeleton/InputBar.js`）

```css
.uV2eYG_input   { color:#0000; -webkit-text-fill-color:transparent; ... }   /* 真输入框：字全透明 */
.uV2eYG_backdrop{ color:var(--dsw-alias-label-primary); position:absolute; inset:0 } /* 你看到的字，是这层 */
```

背板 `[data-input-backdrop]` 由 React 的 `draft` 拼出，textarea 才是接收按键的元素 ⇒ **两者一旦不同步，就是"字在、看不见"**（textarea 自带文字是透明的，所以不会出现"错位"这种显眼症状，而是完全看不到）。

**B. `onChange` 会静默丢弃按键**

```js
const onChange = (e) => {
  if (keyboard === void 0 || locked) return;   // ← 无会话 / 被 block 时静默 return：不提示、不回滚 DOM
  if (machineBusy) return;
  ...
  keyboard.setDraft(next, editRangeOf(pending, draft.length, next.length));
};
```

静默 return ⇒ React 不重渲染 ⇒ DOM 保留用户敲进去的字符、可见背板不变、下次渲染再被抹掉 ⇒ 现象 1。

**C. `inert`（无当前会话）状态下输入框可输入但按键被丢**

`ConversationRoot.tsx`：`inert = sessionId === void 0 || (hero && chipTitle === void 0)`
`InputBar`：`workspaceTrigger = inert && !removed && onRequestWorkspace !== void 0`；`textareaDisabled = removed || locked && !workspaceTrigger`

⇒ 该状态下 **textarea 可输入**（`textareaDisabled=false`），而 `locked=true` 使 `onChange` 走上式 B 直接 return ⇒ 白打、且因为 A 完全看不见。`sessionId === void 0` 会在"选中会话不在当前列表"或"当前会话被归档"时出现（见下节）。

**D. 切换会话后的聚焦不还原光标**

```js
useEffect(() => { const el = inputRef.current; if (locked || el === null) return;
  el.focus({ preventScroll: true }); revealSelectionFocus(el); }, [locked, sessionId]);
```

`focus()` 把光标放到 0 号位 ⇒ 现象 2。

**E. 读通道与写通道可能指向不同会话**

写通道 `keyboard` 来自槽位注入（`inputHub.shell(sessionId)`），读通道 `input` / `inputActions` 来自 `sessions.provide` 标准套件（按 binding 解析）——两条独立通道，切换瞬间可能一新一旧 ⇒ 字符写进 A、屏幕画的是 B，同样表现为现象 1。

## 另两处会话选择相关的问题（runtime 侧，同一版本）

- `lib/types/client/sessions/manager.ts`：

```js
const current = selected !== void 0 && (items.some((item) => item.sessionId === selected) || this.addresses.has(selected)) ? selected : void 0;
```

⇒ **选中会话只要不在当前列表里（列表重拉 / reconnect 的窗口），`current` 就被掩成 `undefined`**，整个对话区回落到无会话态（用户观感＝"对话丢了／框没了"）。

- `lib/types/client/workspaces/service.ts`：`if (sessions.current !== void 0 && workspace.archivedSessionIds.includes(sessions.current)) this.sessions.clear();`
  ⇒ **当前会话被归档即清空选中**，同一观感。

## 最小检测片段（贴进 Console 正常使用即可）

```js
setInterval(() => {
  const ta = document.querySelector('[data-composer-card] textarea');
  const bd = document.querySelector('[data-input-backdrop]');
  if (!ta || !bd || !ta.getBoundingClientRect().width) return;   // 输入框被折叠时跳过
  if (ta.value !== bd.innerText) console.warn('[composer desync]', {
    dom: ta.value.slice(0, 60), painted: bd.innerText.slice(0, 60),
    disabled: ta.disabled, readOnly: ta.readOnly, taPhase: ta.getAttribute('data-phase'),
    header: (document.querySelector('header')?.innerText || '').split('\n')[0],
  });
}, 30);
```

实测：正常打字不误报；一旦出现"字进了输入框却没画出来"必定捕获，且 `dom` 与 `painted` 的差异一眼可见。

## 关于更新版本

我在本机比对了 npm 上的 **0.1.5-rc.2**：`dsh-client-ui-conversation` 的 composer 已被**重写为 Lexical contenteditable**（`.uV2eYG_input{ color: var(--dsw-alias-label-primary) }`、不再有 `[data-input-backdrop]` / `[data-input-mirror]`；且 `editable = live && !locked && !machineBusy`，锁定时编辑器直接不可编辑，不会"能打但丢"）。

⇒ 上面 **A/B/C/D 这一族机制在新版里似乎已从设计上消失**。想请教两点：
1. 这组问题是否已在某个版本修掉（我们升级时好逐条核对）？
2. runtime 那两处（列表掩掉 `current`、归档当前会话清空选中）是否也已调整？

## 我们这边的临时处置（供同样受影响的用户参考）

自建部署里加了一个**纯客户端插件**：发现"输入框内容 ≠ 可见层"时，把整份内容写回 `conversation.input.shell(id).setDraft()`（走核心自己的写入路径 ⇒ 字符不丢、切走再切回仍在）；拿不到服务时才退化为"照 DOM 补画一次可见层"。同时在会话切换后把光标放回该会话上次位置。**这只是缓解、不是修**，核心那几处仍建议按上面修。

discussions.title: [Bug] Windows: `windows-acl` rung is auto-selected without a probe, but its host-side write grant always fails without SeSecurityPrivilege
discussions.body:
# [Bug] Windows: `windows-acl` 沙箱档位免探测即被选中，但其宿主侧 write grant 必然失败 → workspace-write 下每条命令都报 Win32 5

> 该文档同时是**本地留档**与**上游 Discussion 正文**，已脱敏（工作区路径、用户名、计算机名均以占位符替代）。
> 提交位置：https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions （General）
> 依据 CONTRIBUTING.md：「Identify and report issues or bugs in GitHub Discussions」

**版本**：`@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.1.7-alpha.1 ｜ **平台**：Windows 11 + PowerShell 7.6.6 ｜ **宿主权限**：非提权标准用户（Medium 完整性）

---

## Summary

On Windows, the ACL sandbox rung (`windows-acl`) is **selected without a probe** (it is the only candidate in `PLATFORM_CHAINS.win32`), yet its **host-side** write grant unconditionally writes a Low mandatory integrity label into the object's **SACL**. Writing a SACL requires `SeSecurityPrivilege`, which a non-elevated host token does not have. The result:

- every single command in `workspace-write` mode fails with `SetNamedSecurityInfoW failed (Win32 5): grantWrite(<workspace>)`;
- the availability probe nevertheless reports the rung as usable, because it only exercises the **runner** child (which runs with `manageDacls: false` and never writes a SACL);
- sessions therefore start in a mode in which **no shell command can run at all**, and users are pushed to `danger-full-access` to get any work done.

---

## Environment

| Item | Value |
|:--|:--|
| `@deepseek-ai/dsh` | `0.1.7-alpha.1` |
| OS | Windows 11 (build via `win32`), PowerShell 7.6.6 |
| Host token | standard user, **Medium** integrity (`S-1-16-8192`), **not elevated** |
| Workspace | a normal directory on a fixed drive, fully writable by the user, no junctions |

`whoami /priv` on the host process shows only:

```
SeShutdownPrivilege            Disabled
SeChangeNotifyPrivilege        Enabled
SeUndockPrivilege              Disabled
SeIncreaseWorkingSetPrivilege  Disabled
SeTimeZonePrivilege            Disabled
```

→ **no `SeSecurityPrivilege`**.

---

## Impact

Observed over 39 recorded sessions (≈850 shell tool calls):

- `workspace-write` mode: **0 successes out of 6** real attempts; every attempt returned
  `Error: SetNamedSecurityInfoW failed (Win32 5): grantWrite(<workspace>)`.
- `danger-full-access`: 828 success / 23 ordinary non-zero exits.
- Net effect: the profile ends up running **99.2 %** of all commands in `danger-full-access`,
  i.e. the file sandbox is effectively off — not because the user chose that, but because the
  only alternative silently fails. This weakens the confinement the feature is meant to provide.

A teammate/session started with `approval: never` has **no recovery path at all**: it cannot
escalate, and every command fails.

---

## Root cause

1. **The rung is chosen without any probe.** `dsh-sandbox-local/lib/index.js`:

   ```js
   const PLATFORM_CHAINS = { linux: [...], darwin: [...], win32: ["windows-acl"] };
   ```

   Per the accompanying comment, a chain is probed "only when it has MORE than one candidate".
   With a single candidate, `windows-acl` is accepted unconditionally.

2. **The probe, if it did run, would not see the failure.** `defaultProbeWindowsAcl` spawns the
   **runner** with `--mode read-only`:

   ```js
   spawnSync(program, [...runnerInvocation.slice(1),
     "--workspace", tmpdir(), "--temp", tmpdir(), "--mode", "read-only",
     "--", "cmd", "/c", "exit", "0"], ...).status === 0
   ```

   while `dsh-sandbox-windows-acl/lib/runner.js` sets `manageDacls: !seamManaged` — i.e. the
   runner **deliberately does not manage DACLs/SACLs**. The part that does is the **host-side**
   `AclWriteGrant`, and that is never probed.

3. **The host-side grant always writes a SACL.** `grantWrite` in
   `dsh-sandbox-windows-acl/lib/types-*.js`:

   ```js
   function grantWrite(api, path, sidPtr, lowLabelSidPtr, worldSidPtr) {
     withPathLock(api, path, () => {
       const { oldAcl, labelAcl, descriptor } = readCurrentSecurity(api, path);
       if (oldAcl !== null && labelAcl !== null && hasExactGrant(oldAcl, sidPtr)
           && hasExactDeny(oldAcl, worldSidPtr) && hasExactLabel(labelAcl, lowLabelSidPtr)) {
         return;                                   // all-or-nothing short circuit
       }
       const label = buildLowLabelAcl(api, lowLabelSidPtr);
       mergeAndApply(api, path, Buffer.concat([...]), oldAcl,
                     { kind: "apply", acl: label }, descriptor, "grantWrite");
     });
   }
   ```

   and `mergeAndApply` applies it with `SecurityInfo = 20` (`DACL_SECURITY_INFORMATION | LABEL_SECURITY_INFORMATION`):

   ```js
   api.setNamedSecurityInfoW(path, 1, labelEdit.kind === "keep" ? 4 : 20,
                             null, null, newAcl,
                             labelEdit.kind === "apply" ? labelEdit.acl : null);
   ```

   When not short-circuited it is **always** `kind: "apply"`, i.e. the label edit rides in the
   same call as the DACL edit → writing the SACL is unavoidable.

4. **No privilege is ever enabled.** A repository-wide search of
   `dsh-sandbox-windows-acl` for `AdjustTokenPrivileges` / `LookupPrivilegeValue` /
   `SeSecurityPrivilege` returns **zero** hits. The package assumes the token can write SACLs.

5. **The short circuit cannot be leveraged as a workaround.** It requires the capability ACE,
   the deny ACE *and* the label to match simultaneously:
   - `workspaceWriteSid(workspaceRoot)` is deterministic, so a one-time pre-grant could match —
     but
   - `tempWriteSid(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "dsh-")))` is a **fresh random directory per
     session**, so the temp grant never matches and always takes the `apply` path.

   Pre-placing an inheritable Low label on `%TEMP%` does not help either, because the
   short circuit is all-or-nothing.

---

## Evidence / reproduction

1. **Token lacks the privilege** — `whoami /priv` (above); `Get-Acl -Path <dir> -Audit` on any
   directory returns:

   ```
   The process does not possess the 'SeSecurityPrivilege' privilege which is required for this operation.
   ```

2. **Independent reproduction without DSH** — set the same integrity label on a scratch directory:

   ```powershell
   icacls <scratch-dir> /setintegritylevel "(OI)(CI)Low"
   # Successfully processed 0 files; Failed processing 1 files
   # <scratch-dir>: Access is denied.
   # exit=5
   ```

   Exit code **5** = `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED`, exactly the Win32 code DSH reports.

3. **Reproduced through DSH** — with the session in `workspace-write`, the very first command:

   ```json
   {"tool":"pwsh","command":"Get-ChildItem \"D:\\...\\node_modules\\@deepseek-ai\" -Name"}
   ```

   returns:

   ```
   Error: SetNamedSecurityInfoW failed (Win32 5): grantWrite(<workspace>)
   ```

   The DACL-only path is *not* the blocker: the workspace directory is owned by the calling
   user and grants them full control, so `WRITE_DAC` is available. Only the SACL edit fails.

## Why we believe this is not machine-specific

The failing operation is guarded by a **token privilege**, not by any directory ACL, so it should
reproduce on any Windows host whose dsh process is not running with `SeSecurityPrivilege`
(i.e. any ordinary non-elevated user, which is the normal way to run the web/desktop app).

---

## Proposed fixes (any one would resolve the reported failure)

1. **Enable what is available.** At `AclSandbox` init, when the token holds `SeSecurityPrivilege`
   (admin tokens have it, disabled by default), enable it via
   `LookupPrivilegeValue` + `AdjustTokenPrivileges` for the grant duration.
2. **Degrade explicitly instead of dying per command.** If the privilege is absent, either
   - fall back to DACL-only confinement and **report the rung as `partial` with a surfaced
     warning**, or
   - fail the mode selection at session start with an actionable message
     (so a session never begins in a mode where every command is guaranteed to fail).
3. **Make the probe honest.** Have `defaultProbeWindowsAcl` exercise the *host-side* grant
   (create a throwaway directory, call `AclWriteGrant.add`, revoke, remove) rather than only
   starting the runner. This would make the rung `unusable` on affected hosts and let the
   platform chain report that properly.

---

## Workaround we applied locally

In the profile patch layer:

```yaml
- id: permission
  name: "@deepseek-ai/dsh-permission-presets"
  config:
    presets:
      workspace-write:    { sandbox: workspace-write,    approval: ask, ... }
      danger-full-access: { sandbox: danger-full-access, approval: never, ... }
      full-access-ask:    { sandbox: danger-full-access, approval: ask, ... }   # added
    defaultPreset: full-access-ask
```

i.e. default new sessions to full access **while keeping the approval gate**, purely so that
sessions stop starting in an unusable mode. This is a mitigation, not a fix: it means the file
sandbox is knowingly off.

---

*Reported after a 39-session / ~65 MB execution-trace review of Windows shell failures.
Full local evidence: `docs/kb-exec复盘与Windows原生化评估.md` §8.*

discussions.title: /plugins/* carrier 路由未做请求信任校验，伪造 Host 即可读取完整插件图（附带定位，细节待私密渠道补充）
discussions.body:
## 现象

宿主内置插件注册的 `/plugins/*` 路由(IHMR 相关)**不校验 `Host`,也不要求任何凭据**。
在 `DeepSeek Harness 0.1.5-rc.3`(Windows 11,`dsh web` 仅监听回环、无反向代理)上实测,
伪造 `Host` 即返回 200,并能取到:

- `/plugins/events` —— 22,985 字节的**完整插件图**(每个条目的 `id` / `url` / `rev` / `inject` 依赖);
- 客户端 bundle 本体(按其帧中给出的地址,实测 200 / 4,653 字节)。

对照:同一伪造 `Host` 下宿主自己的 `/api/sessions` 返回 **403** —— 核心的请求信任栅栏是有效的,
问题只出在这些插件注册的路由上。

## 为什么这不只是"少一道校验"

`Host` 是 DNS 重绑定唯一伪造不了的请求头,而这些路由恰恰不看它。重绑定后攻击者页面与目标
**同源**(同为攻击者域名),因此 CORS 不参与、页面可直接读取响应体 ⇒ **任意网页可枚举用户的
完整插件图并取走客户端 bundle**,无需任何凭据、无需用户交互之外的条件。

## 代码定位

- 路由归属:`packages/client/hmr/src/index.ts`(常量 `EVENTS_ENDPOINT = '/plugins/events'`)与 `src/events.ts`;
  不是 `packages/host/webserver`。
- 该包源码中 `requestRejection` / `isTrustedApiRequest` / `sameOrigin` / `loopback` /
  `remoteAddress` / `origin` / `authoriz` / `token` 的引用次数**均为 0**。
- `packages/host/webserver` 对所有路由同构派发、没有统一拦截点,所以要么在**路由 owner 侧**加判定,
  要么在 **carrier 层**加一道统一判定(后者才能覆盖日后新增的插件路由)。

## 请求(渠道)

我需要一个**私密渠道**来补充精确的请求构造与逐条复现结果 —— 现在这条放在公开板块,
所以按惯例我只给到定位信息,不写可直接照做的步骤。

请任选其一:
1. 为本仓库启用 **GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting**(`Settings → Security → Private vulnerability reporting`),
   或在仓库补一份 `SECURITY.md` 指明渠道;
2. 或直接告我转给谁(内部邮箱/团队均可)。

拿到渠道后我会补上:完整请求构造、`/plugins/<bundle>` 的逐条读数、
以及"哪些版本受影响"的边界测量。

## 关联

dsh-market 的公开议题 **#603** 里,@Ho-J 已经公开描述过同一现象(他测得约 25 KB 插件图,
本报告测得 22,985 B,吻合),并建议"同时覆盖 carrier 层"。本贴是**独立复现**(不同平台、不同版本)
加代码定位,用于把优先级抬起来并落到具体文件。

另:市场侧我另有一项发现(与同一栅栏覆盖面有关)。按 dsh-market 的 `SECURITY.md` 要求,
那一条不在这里复述 —— 细节只走非公开渠道。
