discussions.title: [BUG反馈] 「加载更早」在特定会话上静默失效：装配器抛 "withdrew materialized target"（Windows 桌面版 0.1.7-rc.2）
discussions.body:
## 环境

| 项 | 值 |
|---|---|
| 版本 | **0.1.7-rc.2**（对应 release tag `dsh-v0.1.7-rc.2`） |
| 平台 | Windows x64，官方签名 NSIS 安装版（`D:\DeepseekHarness`） |
| 数据目录 | `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh`（本地库，未做任何客户端改动） |
| 复现会话 | 工作区 **MD** / 会话 **HEA** = `session-e51614ea-6e82-425f-813a-05f9dfb151fa`（7857 事件） |
| 对照会话（正常） | 同工作区 **HEA (1)** = `session-14cfbcb2-0444-4f60-b7aa-3e5b2d3eb23b`（6443 事件，HEA 的 fork） |

## 复现步骤

1. 打开工作区 MD 下的会话 **HEA**（滚到底部，界面正常显示最新内容）；
2. 点击消息列表顶部的 **「加载更早」**（按钮存在且 `disabled=false`）；
3. 观察：**界面毫无变化**（实测可见文本行数 `533 → 533`、滚动高度 `15729 → 15729`），无 toast、无错误提示；
4. 「轨迹」页签里的 **「加载更早的历史」同样失败**；
5. 切走再切回、重启应用后重试 —— 仍然必现；
6. 对 **HEA (1)** 做同样操作 —— **正常**。

## 预期行为

点击「加载更早」应把更早的一页消息追加到当前窗口上方。

## 实际行为

更早的一页**确实从服务端取回来了**（调用栈已到 `Session.prependWindow`），但客户端的对话节点装配在
prepend 时抛错，**整页被丢弃**，UI 因此毫无变化。控制台唯一线索：

```
[session-controller] event feed subscriber failed: Error:
conversation Definition "system-message" withdrew materialized target "chat";
return the same key with hidden visibility instead
    at ConversationNodeAssembler.buildTargetUpserts   (dsh-client-ui-conversation/client.js)
    at ConversationNodeAssembler.flush
    at BoundConversation.flush
    at BoundConversation.publish
    at BoundConversation.accept
    at MutableSessionEventSource.publish
    at MutableSessionEventSource.prepend
    at Session.prependWindow                          (dsh-api-session-controller/client.js)
```

## 宿主侧正常（已排除服务端/数据问题）

用会话 token 直接调宿主 RPC `session/page`（绕过界面），HEA（游标 7856）：

| 请求形状 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| `throughSeq=7856, beforeSeq=6856, maxMessages=500, turnWindow{50,2}` | ok，`records=596`，`hasMore=true`，seq 6260..6855 |
| `throughSeq=7856`（无 beforeSeq） | ok，`records=497`，`hasMore=true` |
| `throughSeq=7856, beforeSeq=7656, maxMessages=50` | ok，`records=418`，`hasMore=true` |
| `throughSeq=7855` / `7851` | ok，`records=596` / `records=3008`（可回溯到 seq 3848） |

日志本身完好：7857 事件、序号稠密（`dense_zero_based`）、逐行 JSON 可解析、有持久标题；
对本地全部 73 个会话做过逐代解压校验，**0 个数据问题**。

## 缩小范围做过的实验（都失败）

1. **用官方 `session/fork` 复制一份**（同内容、`isSeeded=true`、父会话=HEA）→ 同样必现（排除 fork/父链因素）；
2. **重建为"纯 append 表层"副本**：删除全部 **42 个替换事件**（`surfaceOp != 'append'`）以及
   `compaction/*`、`request/header`、`session-log-deepseek/*` 等模型内部事件（6544 事件，替换事件归零）→ **仍然必现**；
3. 在 (2) 基础上再删到**只剩 1 条** `system/message` → **仍然必现**。

⇒ 触发点**不是**压缩/替换事件，**也不是**多份 system prompt，而是 **prepend 后装配器对
`system-message` 上下文的 upsert 重建路径**本身。

## 源码定位

- `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/conversation/assembler.ts:925-942`
  `buildTargetUpserts()`：某 context 本次 `buildNode()` 返回 `null` 而 `context.current.get(target)`
  已有节点时抛错（契约：**只能返回同一个 key 的 hidden 节点**）。
- `packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/conversation-nodes/request-prompt.ts:62-83`
  `systemMessageDefinition.buildViewNode()`：在
  `state === undefined || state.text === '' || context.start?.event.type !== "system/message" || context.start.event.surfaceOp !== "append"`
  时返回 `null`。prepend 重建时 **`context.start` 可能已不可用**（在只剩 1 条 system/message 的副本上也会发生）
  → 对已物化的 `chat` 返回 `null` → 抛错。
- `packages/api/session-controller/src/client/sessions/session.ts:406-425`
  `loadOlder()` 的 `catch` 只对**非远端失败**打日志（`isRemoteFailure(error)` 为真时静默），
  所以用户侧连一条错误都看不到，无法自助排查。

## 建议修法（前两条建议都做）

1. `systemMessageDefinition.buildViewNode()` 在"本会返回 null 但 `context.current.get('chat')` 已是
   `system-prompt`"时，返回**同 key 的 hidden 节点**（照同文件 `requestPromptDefinition:135-148` 的
   `{ visibility: visible ? 'visible' : 'hidden' }` 写法）；
2. `loadOlder()` 的 `catch` 把远端失败也记录出来（当前失败完全不可见）；
3. 若 `context.start` 在重建时确实可能缺失，装配器应在 upsert 前**跳过**该 context（或视作 hidden），
   而不是抛错中断整批 prepend。

## 影响面

对本地 73 个会话逐一扫描，具备相同形状的有 **2 个**：HEA（`e51614ea…`）与
`session-1e68d10b-88c1-4a75-a8a9-da59838e2843`；其余 71 个翻页正常。

## 附：会话结构摘要

```
events=7857  user/message=101  assistant/message=1183  tool/call=1260  tool/result=1295
system/message: append=4 (seq 7, 7157, 7363, 7459)  replace=5 (7205, 7206, 7697, 7698, 7699)
compaction: start=2 summary=2 end=2 prune=35   替换事件合计 42
```

---

## English summary (optional, for the same report)

**Title**: `[BUG] "Load earlier" silently fails on some sessions: assembler throws "withdrew materialized target" (Windows desktop 0.1.7-rc.2)`

Clicking **Load earlier** in session `session-e51614ea-…` (workspace MD) produces no visible change and no
user-facing error. The host is healthy: direct `session/page` RPC calls return the older page
(596 / 3008 records, `hasMore=true`). The renderer throws
`conversation Definition "system-message" withdrew materialized target "chat"` from
`ConversationNodeAssembler.buildTargetUpserts` during `Session.prependWindow`, so the whole prepended page
is discarded. Reproduces after a fork, after removing every replacement/compaction event, and even with a
single `system/message` left — so the trigger is the prepend-time rebuild path, not the log's compaction
machinery. Suggested fix: return the same key with hidden visibility from
`systemMessageDefinition.buildViewNode` (see `requestPromptDefinition` in the same file), and stop
swallowing remote failures in `loadOlder()`.

discussions.title: [Windows] 执行 pnpm / node 时弹出 Windows Terminal 黑框：runtime-commands shim 启动的运行时进程没有控制台
discussions.body:
## 环境

| 项目 | 值 |
| --- | --- |
| OS | Windows 11 专业版 23H2（build 22631.2861） |
| 默认终端应用 | Windows Terminal（`HKCU\Console\%%Startup` 的 DelegationConsole = `{2EACA947-7F5F-4CFA-BA87-8F7FBEEFBE69}`） |
| Windows Terminal | 1.12.10983.0（Store 版） |
| DSH Desktop | 2.0.15（win32，Electron / node v24.18.1） |
| @deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local | 0.1.7-rc.2（已含 f8b1309fe5 的修复） |
| 随应用打包的 pnpm | 11.8.0 |
| 会话策略 | 文件策略 danger-full-access、审批 never |

## 现象

在 DSH 里执行 `pnpm` 命令（例如 `pnpm run <script>`）时，桌面上会弹出一个 Windows Terminal 黑框窗口（标题为 `C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe`）。

- 每个通过 `cmd.exe` 跑脚本的 pnpm 命令都会触发一次；
- 如果该进程以非 0 退出码结束，Windows Terminal 会把窗口保留在桌面上不关闭，内容只剩一行：
  `[已退出进程，代码为 1 (0x00000001)]`
- `pnpm run` 已实测复现；`pnpm install` 的生命周期脚本走同一个 script runner，预计同样触发。

## 复现步骤

```powershell
# DSH Desktop 会用 runtime-commands shim 接管 pnpm，shim 位于
#   %APPDATA%\DSH Desktop\runtime-commands\generations\<hash>\bin\pnpm.cmd
# 在 DSH 会话里（或任何 PATH 含该 shim 的 shell 中）执行：
pnpm --dir <任意含 package.json 的项目> run <任意脚本>
```

同时用「窗口 + 进程创建」双通道监视器观察（`EnumWindows` 轮询 + `Get-Process`/WMI 轮询，15ms）：

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File console-activity-watch.ps1 -Seconds 60
```

## 期望行为

执行 `pnpm` / `node` 命令不产生任何新的可见控制台窗口。

## 实际行为（实测进程链）

```
20:21:09.834 PROC DSH Desktop.exe(41856)  ppid=powershell(41424)
             cmd="...\DSH Desktop.exe" --require "...\runtime-commands\generations\<hash>\private\clear-env.cjs" "...\resources\app\node_modules\pnpm\bin\pnpm.mjs" ...
20:21:10.105 PROC cmd.exe(45572)          ppid=DSH Desktop.exe(41856)
             cmd=cmd.exe /d /s /c node -e "setTimeout(()=>{},1500)"      <- pnpm 的 script runner
20:21:10.233 PROC conhost.exe(45764)      ppid=cmd.exe(45572)            <- ★ 为它新建了一个控制台
20:21:10.456 PROC OpenConsole.exe(43388)  ppid=svchost(DcomLaunch) cmd=... -Embedding
                                                                        <- ★ Windows Terminal 接管该控制台 = 弹出黑框
```

## 根因

1. `runtime-commands` / `host-commands` 生成的 shim（`bin\pnpm.cmd`、`private\node-bin\node.cmd`、`bin\dsh.cmd`）是用 **`DSH Desktop.exe`** 以 `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` 来跑运行时的；
2. `DSH Desktop.exe` 的 PE 子系统是 **`WINDOWS_GUI`**（实测 `Subsystem=2`），GUI 子系统进程**不会自动附着父进程的控制台**。在运行时进程里直接测量：

   ```
   execPath=C:\...\DSH Desktop.exe
   before attach: hwnd=null                    <- 该进程没有控制台
   AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS) -> true
   after attach:  hwnd=6230332 visible=False   <- 附着后才有了（隐藏）
   ```

3. pnpm 跑脚本时创建的是**控制台进程** `cmd.exe /d /s /c ...`；父进程没有控制台时，Windows 会为它**新建**一个控制台；
4. 本机默认终端应用是 Windows Terminal，于是该系统新建的控制台被 WT 接管（`OpenConsole.exe -Embedding`），表现为弹出的黑框；
5. 进程非 0 退出时 WT 保留该 pane，窗口长期驻留桌面（实测桌面残留一个 17:46 的 `cmd.exe` 窗口）。

## 与已有修复的关系

- 讨论 #7216 / commit `f8b1309fe5`（“fix(subprocess): hide Windows shell console windows at creation”，首发 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local` 0.1.6-alpha.2）修的是 **DSH 自己 spawn 时缺 `windowsHide`** 的问题；本 issue 实测确认该修复在当前版本（0.1.7-rc.2）已生效——DSH 自己起的 runner / 目标 shell / 沙箱 runner 的控制台都是隐藏的，不再弹窗。
- 但这条弹窗来自 **被 shim 启动的运行时进程（pnpm）自己 spawn 的控制台子进程**：DSH 不控制那次 spawn，`windowsHide` 补丁覆盖不到。父进程没有控制台才是根因，所以修复应该落在「让被 shim 启动的运行时拥有一个控制台」这一层。

## 另一个同类残留点（顺带报告）

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-local` 的 Windows ACL 探测仍然缺 `windowsHide`：

```js
// node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-local/lib/index.js  defaultProbeWindowsAcl()
return spawnSync(program, [ ...runnerInvocation.slice(1), "--workspace", tmpdir(), ...,
  "--", "cmd", "/c", "exit", "0" ], {
  timeout: timeoutMs,
  stdio: "ignore"          // <-- 缺 windowsHide: true
}).status === 0;
```

这与 9/23 那批本地补丁的第三个目标同源（`dsh-subprocess-local` 的 runner spawn、`dsh-sandbox-local` 的探测 spawn）。本机是 GUI 运行时可执行文件（`process.execPath` = `DSH Desktop.exe`）时不会直接出窗口，但在 CLI/源码方式启动（`process.execPath` = `node.exe`，控制台子系统）时会新建可见控制台，建议一并补上 `windowsHide: true`。

## 建议修复

**方案 A（推荐，已在本机验证有效）**：让被 shim 启动的运行时附着到父控制台，其子进程就会继承该控制台，不再新建窗口。

在 shim 生成处为运行时调用注入一个预加载模块（DSH 已经自带 koffi，可直接用；也可以放在 Electron 的 RUN_AS_NODE 引导里）：

```js
// attach-parent-console.cjs —— 由 shim 以 --require 注入
// 运行时是 GUI 子系统、没有控制台，其子进程（pnpm 的 cmd.exe）会被 Windows 新建控制台；
// 附着到父控制台后子进程继承它，不再新建可见窗口。
try {
  const koffi = require('<app>/node_modules/koffi')
  const k32 = koffi.load('kernel32.dll')
  // ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS = 0xffffffff；已附着时返回 false，忽略即可
  k32.func('bool AttachConsole(uint32 dwProcessId)')(0xffffffff)
} catch { /* 不能影响主程序启动 */ }
```

生成的 shim 只需在运行时调用前多一个 `--require`：

```bat
"C:\...\DSH Desktop.exe" --require "...\attach-parent-console.cjs" --require "%DSH_RUNTIME_PRIVATE%\clear-env.cjs" "...\pnpm.mjs" --config.minimumReleaseAge=0 %*
```

**验证结果（同一台机器，同一条 `pnpm run`，仅差这个预加载）**：

| | 修复前 | 修复后 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pnpm 的 `cmd.exe` 子进程 | `cmd.exe(45572) ppid=DSH Desktop.exe(41856)` | `cmd.exe(38648) ppid=DSH Desktop.exe(45596)` |
| 是否为它新建控制台 | **`conhost.exe(45764) ppid=45572`** | 无 |
| Windows Terminal 接管 | **`OpenConsole.exe(43388) -Embedding`** | 无 |
| 可见窗口 | 弹出黑框 | 无 |

**方案 B（不推荐，已试过无效）**：给运行时用 `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` / `conhost.exe --headless` 之类方式“造”一个隐藏控制台——GUI 子系统进程不会因此获得控制台，实测 `conhost.exe --headless "DSH Desktop.exe" ...` 之后 `GetConsoleWindow()` 仍然是 `NULL`。

**方案 C**：`dsh-sandbox-local` 的 `defaultProbeWindowsAcl` 补 `windowsHide: true`。

## 用户侧临时绕过（如果短期不发版）

把上面的预加载模块写到一个固定路径，并用幂等脚本给所有已生成的 shim 插一个 `--require`：

- 需要处理的文件：`%APPDATA%\DSH Desktop\runtime-commands\**\{bin\pnpm.cmd, private\node-bin\node.cmd}`、`%APPDATA%\DSH Desktop\host-commands\**\bin\dsh.cmd`（本机 15 个）；
- **注意**：这些 shim 是**按 generation 生成**的，DSH 升级或生成新 generation 后需要重放脚本，所以真正的修复还是要落在生成器里。

## English summary

On Windows 11 with **Windows Terminal as the default terminal application**, every `pnpm` command run from DSH pops a black console window (and a non-zero exit leaves that window on the desktop permanently).

Root cause: the generated shims (`runtime-commands\**\bin\pnpm.cmd`, `private\node-bin\node.cmd`, `host-commands\**\bin\dsh.cmd`) run the runtime through `DSH Desktop.exe`, whose PE subsystem is `WINDOWS_GUI`, so that process **has no console** (`GetConsoleWindow()` returns `NULL`). When pnpm spawns its script runner (`cmd.exe /d /s /c ...`), Windows creates a brand-new console for it; with Windows Terminal registered as the default terminal, that console is handed to WT (`OpenConsole.exe -Embedding`) — the visible black window. The `windowsHide` fixes from `f8b1309fe5` / #7216 cover DSH's own spawns (verified working), but not this spawn, which happens inside the shim-launched runtime.

Suggested fix (verified locally): inject a preload into the shim's runtime that calls `AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS)`; the runtime then owns a console, pnpm's `cmd.exe` inherits it, and no new console/window is ever created. `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` / `conhost.exe --headless` do **not** work for a GUI-subsystem image. Additionally, `dsh-sandbox-local`'s `defaultProbeWindowsAcl` spawnSync is still missing `windowsHide: true`.

discussions.title: Termux (platform android): terminal inspection throws before pty spawn — one-line fix included
discussions.body:
## Environment

- DSH `@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.1.7-rc.2, Termux 0.118 (android-arm64, Node v26)
- Confirmed locally since the 0.1.5 era, so not a regression — terminal inspection has never worked on Termux.

## Symptom

Every terminal-creation path that needs a process inspector fails **before** the pty spawn:

```
subprocess-local: terminal inspection is unsupported on platform android
```

This kills:

- the built-in right-sidebar terminal (`ui-sidebar-terminal` → `spawnTerminal` → `createProcessInspector()`),
- `dsh-terminal-bash` (same inspector path).

Everything else on the Termux side works: `node-pty` builds under Termux (verified: pty spawn + interactive bash echo round-trip), `/proc` is mounted with standard Linux semantics, `$SHELL`/bash resolve at `$PREFIX/bin/bash`. The throw in `createProcessInspector` (`packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/process-inspector.ts`) is the only blocker — it enumerates `linux` / `darwin` / `win32` and throws on `'android'`.

## Suggested fix

Termux reports `process.platform === 'android'` but is a Linux kernel: `/proc` semantics (stat fields, fd symlinks, tty devices) are identical. Routing `android` to `LinuxProcessInspector` is the whole fix:

```diff
--- a/packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/process-inspector.ts
+++ b/packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/process-inspector.ts
@@ export function createProcessInspector(
 ): ProcessInspector {
+  // Termux reports 'android' but is a Linux kernel: /proc semantics are
+  // identical, so the Linux inspector works verbatim.
+  if (platform === 'android') return new LinuxProcessInspector(arch, internals)
   if (platform === 'linux') return new LinuxProcessInspector(arch, internals)
   if (platform === 'darwin') return new MacProcessInspector(internals)
   if (platform === 'win32') return createWindowsProcessInspector()
```

Full change with a unit test (`'android'` maps to the Linux inspector, snapshot over fake `/proc`; 13/13 tests in `process-inspector.spec.ts` pass) is on my fork: [`240xu/deepseek-harness` branch `fix/termux-android-process-inspector`](https://github.com/240xu/deepseek-harness/tree/fix/termux-android-process-inspector).

## Verification (real Termux device)

- patched build: `createProcessInspector()` constructs a `LinuxProcessInspector`; pty spawn + interactive bash marker echo passes end-to-end through the real code path;
- unit test added and passing alongside the 12 existing ones.

Since CONTRIBUTING says external PRs are not accepted at the moment and issues are disabled, posting here — happy to adapt the patch (different placement, a Termux capability probe, etc.) if maintainers prefer another shape. Related plugin-side Termux fix: omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar#769.

discussions.title: [Bug] Windows: cancelling a running shell tool call kills the dsh web host (console-wide CTRL_C)
discussions.body:
Hi,

On Windows 11 with dsh 0.1.5-rc.2 (the limitation is still documented in 0.1.7-rc.2), cancelling a
running shell tool call takes down the whole `dsh web` host:

- the host exits silently — no stderr stack, no Windows Application-Error event;
- launched as `dsh web *>&1 | Tee-Object <log>`, the log ends at startup with no error;
- plugins get disposal at that moment (a background git-sync plugin recorded "operation stopped"
  while mid-sync), and the terminal returns to a prompt.

Repro: start `dsh web` from a console → have the agent run a shell command → cancel that tool call
→ the host exits.

My reading: `dsh-subprocess-local` delivers SIGINT on Windows as a `\u0003` write, which conhost
turns into a console-wide CTRL_C (documented in its README under "Known Limitations"). The host is
started from that same console and the provider's tool session is its child, so the host receives
that CTRL_C as well. The same README notes that an application only covers the default signal
disposition by installing a handler — so: does the host install a `SIGINT` handler? If not, that
would explain the silent exit, and installing one (or starting the host detached from the shared
console) would fix it.

Impact: cancelling a tool call tears down in-flight agent sessions and plugin operations, and a
plugin performing a git sync leaves a stale lock directory behind (reproduced several times here).

Happy to test a build. Related: discussions/7531.

<details><summary>Technical details (source references and log evidence)</summary>

Source references (published packages):
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local` `lib/runner-launch-*.js` — Windows inspector returns the shell
  pid as the foreground process group: `foregroundPgid(shellPid) { return shellPid; }`
- same package `lib/index.js` `signalForeground()`:
  `if (signal === "SIGINT") { this.terminal.write("\u0003"); return foreground.processGroupId; }`
  (only SIGKILL on the provider's own pid is refused: "refusing to SIGKILL the terminal shell")
- same package README, Known Limitations: "Windows terminal signalling is console-wide — SIGINT is
  delivered as a `\x03` Ctrl-C input write that conhost turns into a console-wide CTRL_C event…"
- same package README, Shutdown behavior: "…The default OS disposition for an unhandled SIGTERM,
  SIGINT, or SIGHUP bypasses that event; an application covers those signals only by installing a
  handler that performs normal disposal or calls process.exit()."

Observed on this machine:
- plugin history recorded operation failures with reason "stopped" exactly when the host vanished,
  while a git sync was in flight;
- the host process was started from the interactive console (parent = the Windows Terminal's
  powershell.exe) and the tool session is its child → same console;
- the tee'd host log held only startup lines, no error, before the exit;
- Windows Application log shows no Application Error/WER entry, and System log shows no shutdown or
  resource-exhaustion event around those times → not an OS kill, not a native crash.

Suggested fix (host side): install a `SIGINT` handler (dispose-then-exit, or ignore a console-wide
CTRL_C that was not addressed to the host); alternatively start the host detached from the shared
console so console-wide CTRL_C cannot reach it.
</details>

discussions.title: tool-subagent preset-group assembly races the Agent registry on boot (0.1.7-rc.2)
discussions.body:
## Draft issue 1: tool-subagent preset-group assembly races the Agent registry ("standing modelSelectionSettings requires the Agent registry")

**Version:** dsh-v0.1.7-rc.2 (commit 477b4f420553e8a52c2fbccc464d7561b239c443)

**Summary.** During boot, the tool-subagent entry installed by a preset group (e.g. `standard`)
unconditionally resolves its standing `modelSelectionSettings`, which requires the Agent registry
to already be present in the graph. Because the preset group assembles its entries in parallel
(`Promise.allSettled` over the group), whether the Agent-registry-providing entry has finished
activating before tool-subagent's first `apply` is a race that boot regularly loses.

**Observed failure.** On a real machine with existing session data, first launch after upgrade
lost the race: session creation failed with `SlotAssemblyError`, the client tree unmounted, and
the app entered a white-screen/watchdog loop. In a clean environment the same boot usually wins
the race (the loader retries and eventually succeeds), which hides the bug from fresh-install
smoke tests — it only produced log noise there. The failure is intermittent by construction,
not data-dependent beyond timing.

**Reproduction elements.**
1. Boot a desktop host on dsh-v0.1.7-rc.2 with a preset group that includes tool-subagent
   (default `standard` preset does).
2. Ensure the Agent registry entry activates after tool-subagent's first apply — parallel group
   assembly (`Promise.allSettled`) plus existing persisted sessions (work to do immediately on
   boot) makes the loss likely.
3. Observe `SlotAssemblyError` / "standing modelSelectionSettings requires the Agent registry"
   in host logs, followed by client tree unmount.

**Suggested direction (what we did locally).** Make tool-subagent tolerant of a not-yet-present
registry instead of throwing on first apply: when the registry is absent, poll for it (we use a
50 ms interval) and begin the standing installs once it appears; clean up the polling fiber on
unload. Patch: `patches/dsh-tool-subagent@0.1.7-rc.2.patch` (33 lines). After the patch,
watchdog reports in an isolated environment dropped to zero and the real-machine white screen
was resolved.

discussions.title: config-editor edit() read-back validation permanently fails for entries with volatile fields (0.1.7-rc.2)
discussions.body:
## Draft issue 2: config-editor edit() read-back validation permanently fails for entries that declare volatile fields

**Version:** dsh-v0.1.7-rc.2 (commit 477b4f420553e8a52c2fbccc464d7561b239c443)

**Summary.** `edit()` validates a write by reading the entry back through plugin composition
("take the first row with the same id / compose via plugins") and comparing it to the intended
`next` config. For entries that declare volatile fields (e.g. ui-settings-general's
`welcomeNoticeVersion`), composition strips or rewraps the volatile fields, so the composed value
can never equal a `next` that contains them. Every such edit is rejected as
"overridden by home patch" — silently, because the protocol returns `ok:false` by design without
raising. Non-volatile fields in the same namespace (e.g. font size) fail along with them.

**Related observation.** `SettingsForms.write` is volatile-only by design (entries without
volatile fields throw "has no volatile fields"), which confirms volatile handling is special
cased — but the edit() read-back comparison was never adjusted for it.

**Reproduction elements.**
1. Any entry whose spec declares volatile fields; ui-settings-general with
   `welcomeNoticeVersion` is the shipped example (dsh-client-ui-settings-models client bundle,
   settings-general section).
2. Call `edit()` on that entry to set the volatile field (e.g. acknowledging the welcome
   notice sets `welcomeNoticeVersion`).
3. The write reaches the document, but the read-back comparison composes the row (volatile
   fields stripped/wrapped) against `next` (volatile fields present); equality never holds;
   the write is reported as overridden and effectively refused/rolled back at the settings
   layer. No error is surfaced.

**Suggested direction (what we did locally).** Make the read-back validation
document-faithful: after writing, `yaml.load(document)`, merge rows with the same id from the
document itself, and compare that merged config against `next`. This compares what was actually
persisted instead of a composed projection, and is insensitive to volatile wrapping. Patch:
`patches/dsh-config-editor@0.1.7-rc.2.patch` (20 lines). After the patch: welcome-notice
acknowledgement both disappears and persists (the `welcomeNoticeVersion` row lands in the
profile patch), and font-size changes (14→15, ui-theme/fontSize) apply and persist; full chain
verified with zero console errors.

discussions.title: Throughput in turn footer / session stats is unguarded when a step arrives as whole blocks (10^5-10^6 tok/s)
discussions.body:
## Summary

Some steps persisted in `assistant/message.stream` carry packed runs where **every block has exactly one member and `dt` is empty**. For those steps the decode window (first token → assembled message) collapses to 1–5 ms while `usage.outputTokens` stays in the hundreds-to-thousands. Both `deriveTurnMetrics` and the `sessionStats` projection compute throughput as `outputTokens / decodeMs` with nothing but a `decodeMs > 0` guard, so they emit values in the 10^5–10^6 tok/s range and fold them into the session total.

Measured on one machine, same session data:

| session | steps | affected steps | displayed | recomputed from healthy steps only |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `session-56e9f8cf…` (redacted) | 125 | 113 | **1906.2 tok/s** | **149.1 tok/s** |
| `session-3e54dd78…` (redacted) | 9 | 0 | 131.6 tok/s | 131.6 tok/s |

## Impact

- Turn footer and session-wide throughput are not trustworthy for any session containing such steps, and the error grows with their share.
- In a scan of recent local sessions, the affected share ranged from 38% to 93% across 9 sessions.
- `ttftMs` / `ttftSteps` are unaffected (separate accumulators, not derived from the decode window).

## Reproduction

1. Have any session whose `assistant/message.stream` contains steps where every packed run has a single member.
2. Open the session and read the throughput in the turn footer or session stats.
3. Compare against a recomputation that only uses steps whose runs have a non-empty `dt`.

Decode accounting used here matches the server projection: decode window = `assistant/message` event time − `assistantStreamFirstTokenTime(stream)`; throughput = that step's `usage.outputTokens` / decode window.

## Evidence

Packed-run shape, healthy steps vs affected steps (`members` = total `texts`/`args` members across runs):

| turn/step | runs | members | sum(dt) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1/1 | 3 | 927 | 924 |
| 1/2 | 3 | 670 | 667 |
| 2/2 | 3 | 3 | 0 |
| 2/4 | 3 | 3 | 0 |

The first affected step is step 2/2; every step from there on shows the same shape.

## Analysis

Chunks are stamped at the consumption site, `packages/core/agent-loop/src/assistant-stream.ts`:

```ts
this.accumulator.push({ time: Date.now(), chunk })
```

So “one member per block and an empty `dt`” is equivalent to: **the whole SSE stream was consumed within the same millisecond, and each content block arrived as a single delta**.

Neither accounting entry point protects against that:

- `packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/contract/turn-metrics.ts` (`deriveTurnMetrics`) only checks `decodeMs > 0`
- `packages/session/session-stats/src/projection.ts` (`sessionStats`) accumulates unconditionally

## What I could not establish

I did **not** determine the origin of the whole-block arrival. Ruled out so far:

- Upstream always coalescing large requests: control requests through the same gateway and model with 20k / 80k token inputs arrived as 17 / 34 data events with 2–30 ms spacing, i.e. normally streamed.
- Context size: one session with 390k input tokens had 0% affected steps.
- User mid-turn injections or retries: one session with only 2 injections had 78% affected steps.

Not ruled out: the local path (client → LiteLLM gateway → upstream). **The claim in this report is therefore only the missing guard in the accounting layer, which holds regardless of where the coalescing comes from.**

## Suggested fix

In `deriveTurnMetrics` and `sessionStats`: exclude steps where every run has an empty `dt` and a single member from throughput accounting; or, at minimum, add a floor for the decode window (e.g. a step with no incremental members and a sub-50 ms window does not contribute). TTFT should stay as is.

## Related

- Discussion #6129 covers a different client-side read of the same packed-run shape (trajectory panel timing unavailable on historical replay). This report is the throughput accounting face of the same data shape.

---

Environment: `dsh` 0.1.7-rc.2 (npm global install), macOS. Has anyone else seen this? Happy to open a PR with the guard plus tests if that is useful.

discussions.title: 工具入参 `type: 'json'` 编译后丢失 `type`，导致模型被迫猜测 JSON 类型
discussions.body:
用 `cordis_inspect_query` 查 Cordis slot 定义时，连续 21 次撞上同一句报错：

```
Host Cordis inspect Service.listService rejected input: "input" must be an object
```

一开始以为是自己参数写错了，查下去发现不是。根因在 `dsh-tools` 的 schema 编译器：
`type: 'json'` 被静默丢弃，编译产物里没有 `type`。整理成下面这份，想听听维护者的判断——
尤其是修复方向该选哪一种。

环境：`dsh-tools@0.1.7-rc.2` / 宿主 `0.1.7-rc.2` / linux / Node v24.18.0

---

## 复现

无需模型、无需启动宿主，单次函数调用：

```bash
node --input-type=module -e "
import { parameterSchemaSpecToJsonSchema } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools';
const out = parameterSchemaSpecToJsonSchema({
  platform: { type: 'string', required: true },
  input:   { type: 'json',  description: 'Optional query input.' },
});
console.log(JSON.stringify(out, null, 2));
console.log('input 有 type 吗？ ->', 'type' in (out.properties?.input ?? {}));
"
```

输出：

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "platform": { "type": "string" },
    "input": { "description": "Optional query input." }
  },
  "required": ["platform"]
}
input 有 type 吗？ -> false
```

同一 schema 里的兄弟参数 `platform` 正确带着 `"type": "string"`，`input` 什么都没有。

实际调用时，工具边界处真正收到的值：

| 模型意图传入 | DSH 实际收到 | 结果 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{"service":"web"}` | 对象 | 正常 |
| `{}` | `""` | 被拒绝 |
| `[]` | `""` | 被拒绝 |
| `{"a":{}}` | `{"a":""}` | 被拒绝 |

---

## 根因

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools/lib/types/schema.js:152`（打包镜像 `lib/index.js:688`）：

```js
const inputType = Object.hasOwn(input, 'type') ? input.type : undefined;
switch (inputType) {
    case 'json':
        assertAuthorKeys(input, path, [...authorKeys, 'type']);
        copyAnnotations(input, node);
        break;                    // <-- 从未向 node 写入 type
    case 'object':
        ...
        node.type = 'object';
```

`case 'json'` 复制完注解就 break，编译出的节点不带 `type`，该参数在协议层成了无约束属性。
模型拿不到类型信息，只能自己猜。

**顺带一提，两张类型表是互相矛盾的。** `lib/types/json-schema.js:39` 的 `SCHEMA_TYPES` 不含 `'json'`：

```bash
node --input-type=module -e "
import { assertSupportedJsonSchema } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools';
try { assertSupportedJsonSchema({ type: 'json' }); console.log('通过'); }
catch (e) { console.log('拒绝:', e.violations[0]); }
"
# 拒绝: schema.type must be one of object/array/string/number/integer/boolean/null
```

也就是 `'json'` 在编写期 DSL 里合法，在流水线其余部分的封闭类型表里却不存在。
这两处如果对齐，问题会在 `defineTool` 注册阶段就暴露出来，而不是等到运行时。

---

## 排除了「DSH 做了字符串化」

我最初怀疑是 harness 把对象转成了字符串，查下来不是，两项独立验证：

**适配器是纯透传。** `dsh-llm-deepseek/lib/index.js:1884` 原样产出
`argumentsDelta: string(delta.partial_json)`；组装器只做字符串拼接
（`dsh-llm/lib/types/assembler.js:61`）。这条路径上没有 JSON 解析与重新序列化。

**wire 分片里本来就是字符串。** 会话日志的 `tool-call-chunks` 记录了模型自己吐出的分片：

```json
"args": ["", "{", "\"platform\": \"client\"", ", \"provider\": \"Slots\"",
         ", \"method\": \"listSubTree\"",
         ", \"input\": \"{\\\"root\\\": \\\"plugins.item\\\"}\"", "}"]
```

转义后的字符串就在模型自身输出中，DSH 原样转发。

另外 `dsh-util-values` 的 `snapshotJsonValue()` 我直接针对 `{}`、`[]`、`{"a":{}}` 实测过，
三者都正确保留，不参与这个损坏过程。

---

## 实测表现

统计了一次受影响会话里的全部 32 次调用，按工具边界处 `input` 的实际 JSON 类型分类：

| `input` 实际形态 | 次数 | 结果 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 省略 | 9 | 成功 |
| JSON 字符串 | 23 | 21 次被拒，2 次因无关原因失败 |
| **真实对象** | **0** | — |

模型一次都没成功发出过对象。23 次非空输入全是字符串，21 次产生完全相同的报错。
唯一成功的 9 次是**完全省略** `input` 的调用——能过是因为 `inspect-registry.js:179` 做了 `input ?? {}`。

23/23 这个一致性我觉得是关键：如果是随机猜测，总该有偶尔蒙对的时候。完全一致更像是模型在
忠实遵循一份不提供类型信息的 schema，然后默认选了字符串。

---

## 影响范围

整个依赖树里，`type: 'json'` 的其余用法都在**输出侧**（`result` / `output` / `schema`），
值由 harness 提供，不需要类型提示：

| 位置 | 用途 |
| --- | --- |
| `dsh-tool-ralph/lib/index.js:273` | `result` |
| `dsh-tool-workflow/lib/types/index.js:311` | `result` |
| `dsh-tool-subagent/lib/index.js:479` | `output.items` |
| `dsh-mcp-resources/lib/index.js:44` | `schema` |
| `dsh-tool-cordis/lib/index.js:24,47` | `output.schema` |

`dsh-tool-cordis/lib/types/index.js:44` 的 `cordis_inspect_query.input` 是整棵树里**唯一一个
`type: 'json'` 入参**——大概也是这个缺陷一直潜伏的原因。

---

## 关于归因的说明

「模型选了字符串」这个具体表现是所用模型的行为特征，不是 schema 本身的性质。
但底层缺陷我认为与模型无关：不带 `type` 的参数，对任何模型都不提供正确选择的依据，
换个模型可能换个错法，也可能侥幸看起来正常。所以这个讨论我只主张「缺失 `type`」这一条。

据实说明：受影响会话的驱动模型是第三方代理模型（`provider: or`，`api: openai-completions`），
不是一方模型，所以观察到的行为我不认为可以推广。

另有一项**独立的模型侧缺陷**放大了问题：收到 21 次一模一样的报错后，模型始终没改成传真实对象，
最后干脆弃用了这个工具。这是模型的问题，单列出来避免和 schema 问题混在一起。

---

## 修复方向想请大家帮我选

**方案 A：编写期直接拒绝。** `type: 'json'` 在 OpenAI 兼容的函数调用协议里本来就无法忠实表达，
在 `defineTool` 注册时报错，比现在的静默降级要好，而且能和 `SCHEMA_TYPES` 对齐。

**方案 B：投影成具体类型。** 两种都实测可用：

```js
// cordis_inspect_query：input 恒为对象（各 provider 方法的 inputSchema 都是 type:'object'）
{ type: 'object', additionalProperties: true }

// 通用「任意 JSON 值」：oneOf 覆盖各具体类型
// 注意 object 分支必须显式写 additionalProperties，否则编译器报 UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA
{ oneOf: [
    { type: 'object', additionalProperties: true }, { type: 'array' },
    { type: 'string' }, { type: 'number' }, { type: 'boolean' }, { type: 'null' },
] }
```

我个人倾向 A（更诚实，也不会给后来人留下"写了没报错就以为生效了"的坑），但如果维护者觉得
`'json'` 作为一个表达"任意 JSON"的意图本身值得保留，那 B 里的 `oneOf` 投影也能解决主要问题。

另外顺带提一个小的：那句 `rejected input: "input" must be an object` 读起来像是在说调用方参数写错了，
但调用方传的其实是合法 JSON，丢类型的是 schema 本身。如果诊断里带上实际收到的值会好排查很多。

**可验证的预测**：给 `cordis_inspect_query` 的 `input` 补上 `type: "object"` 后，
这类失败应该会归零——模型在结构上就没法为这个参数发字符串了。一行改动，
如果想先确认根因再决定通用方案，可以先试这个。

---

受影响调用链：`tool parameters → schema 编译 → 外发 request/header → 模型 → dsh-cordis-host-runner/lib/types/inspect-registry.js:179`

discussions.title: [Bug] Web shell has no fallback when its own Vite entry/chunk fails to load — pure white page, zero diagnostics (0.1.2-rc.1)
discussions.body:
## Summary The web shell has **no fallback UI when its own Vite entry bundle fails to load**. The user gets a pure white page with zero on-screen and zero console diagnostics. `apps/web` ships an empty `
` and nothing else. The "HARNESS" boot splash is constructed at runtime — `BootPage`'s constructor in `packages/client/web/src/boot-page.ts` builds the wordmark + spinner card and appends it to the container. So the splash only exists **after** `/assets/index-*.js` and its static import `/assets/vendor-*.js` have loaded and evaluated. If either fails, the module graph never runs, the root stays empty, and there is no `window.onerror` handler, no error boundary, and no boot-timeout watchdog in the shell entry. A transient static-subresource failure is therefore indistinguishable from a hang, and impossible for a user to report. > 中文摘要：Web 外壳在自身 Vite 入口 bundle 加载失败时没有任何兜底 UI。`#root` 在 HTML 里是空的，启动画面由 JS 在 `boot-page.ts` 里构造 —— 也就是说启动画面本身依赖那两个 bundle 成功执行。它们一旦失败，用户只看到纯白屏，页面上和控制台里都没有任何提示，无法自助反馈。 ## Reproduction (deterministic) Driven against a running `dsh web` (0.1.2-rc.1) with real Chrome over the DevTools Protocol, blocking one URL at a time via `Network.setBlockedURLs`: | blocked resource | result | | --- | --- | | plugin combo bundle (stale `?rev=`) | ✅ `HARNESS` + **Failed to load plugins** | | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-modules` | ✅ visible error card | | app CSS | ✅ visible (unstyled) | | **`/assets/index-*.js`** | ❌ **white — 0 bytes in root, no splash** | | **`/assets/vendor-*.js`** | ❌ **white** | In every case the HTML itself was served fine and `
` existed; only the painting differed. This is inconsistent with the rest of the boot path. `boot-page.ts:92` already renders a real failure card for plugin load failures, and `assertEntriesActive` in `boot-client.ts` aggregates per-entry reasons. The shell has the primitives — they are simply unreachable when the failure happens one level earlier, in the bundle that contains them. ## Secondary finding: hashed assets carry no cache validators The content-hashed assets are served with **no `Cache-Control`, no `ETag`, no `Last-Modified`, and no `Content-Length`** (chunked, uncompressed length only): ``` HEAD /assets/index-Df-65__b.js Cache-Control: (absent) ETag: (absent) Last-Modified: (absent) Content-Length: (absent) ``` Consequences, both verified: - Without validators browsers cannot revalidate or heuristically cache, so **~5.4 MB is re-downloaded on every single page load** (≈423 KB entry + 740 KB vendor + a 4.16 MB / 1.17 MB-gzip plugin combo). - A truncated response cannot be detected, because there is no `Content-Length` to disagree with and no validator to re-check. Content-hashed filenames are exactly the case where `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` is safe and free — the plugin combo route already does this (`IMMUTABLE_CACHE` in `dsh-client-modules`), so the precedent exists in-tree. ## What I have *not* established I want to be precise about scope, because the original symptom I was chasing is **intermittent**, and I could not reproduce that part: - 10/10 sequential reloads and 100/100 asset requests were clean, with zero truncation and zero errors. - No service worker, no proxy configured, no memory saver involved. - The keep-alive race did not reproduce in 6 rounds of deliberate socket reuse. So I am **not** claiming the intermittent white screen is caused by anything above. What I am claiming is narrower and fully reproducible: **when the shell's own bundle fails for any reason, the failure is invisible.** That is a diagnostics gap independent of the trigger, and it is the reason an intermittent occurrence is currently unreportable — a user who hits it sees a blank page and has nothing to send. I'd also note the practical consequence for triage: distinguishing "the bundle failed" from "boot hung" from "renderer crashed" currently requires guessing, because the page leaves no trace of which. ## Possible direction Not a patch — just where a fix seems to belong: 1. Put a minimal, framework-free pre-boot fallback **in the served HTML** (inline `

discussions.title: [desktop] 登录失败提示「登录未完成，请重试」且重试按钮无反应 —— 本机 HTTPS 中间人（杀软/企业代理）导致 Node 侧证书校验失败
discussions.body:
[desktop] 登录失败提示「登录未完成，请重试」且重试按钮无反应 —— 本机 HTTPS 中间人（杀软/企业代理）导致 Node 侧证书校验失败，且无任何错误暴露

Title (EN): [desktop] Login fails with "登录未完成，请重试" when a local HTTPS MITM (antivirus / enterprise proxy) is active — Node-side cert validation fails, no error surfaced, retry button unresponsive

中文摘要

在 Windows 上，如果本机存在 HTTPS 解密（卡巴斯基「加密连接扫描」、企业 TLS 代理等），桌面版登录会失败并只显示「登录未完成，请重试」，点击「重新登录」毫无反应。根因不是网络问题：登录请求由 dsh host 进程（Electron 以 Node 模式运行）发出，走 Node 的 https/undici，Node 只使用内置 CA bundle，不读 Windows 证书库，于是被本机 MITM 替换后的证书链校验失败（SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN）。同一台机器上 curl 和 Edge 完全正常（它们读 Windows 证书库），所以用户会误判成应用或网络的 bug。关闭杀软的加密连接扫描后立即恢复。

Environment

| Item | Value | | --- | --- | | OS | Windows 11 (build 26200) | | App | DeepSeek Harness desktop 0.1.7-rc.2 (channel nightly, resources/app-update.yml → https://download.deepseek.com/dsh-desk/feeds/win-x64/) | | Bundled packages | @deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop / dsh-desktop-runtime / dsh-desktop-host / @deepseek-ai/dsh all 0.1.7-rc.2 | | Install path | F:\DeepSeek\Harness (electron-builder, resources/app.asar bundles dsh + pnpm + runtime) | | Interception | Kaspersky 21.19, feature「加密连接扫描 / Scan encrypted connections」enabled | | Network | Direct, no proxy; DNS/TLS reachable (verified independently with curl) |

Any equivalent local TLS interception (other AV products' HTTPS scanning, corporate MITM proxy, Fiddler/mitmproxy left running) should reproduce this.

Actual behaviour

  1. Launch the desktop app → sign-in screen reports 「登录未完成，请重试」 / "Login incomplete, please retry".

  2. Clicking 「重新登录」 / "Sign in again" produces no visible reaction at all — no navigation, no browser launch, no error, no spinner.

  3. %APPDATA%\@deepseek-ai\dsh-desktop\logs\ stays empty — there is no way for a user to obtain any diagnostic information.

  4. ~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml never gains account credentials; only the pre-existing client-connection/browser-session record is present.

Root cause

The sign-in requests are issued from the Node side — the dsh-desktop-host process, launched as "DeepSeek Harness.exe" --expose-internals .../dsh-desktop-host/lib/index.js ... (i.e. Electron in Node mode).

Node's TLS stack trusts only its bundled CA store. It does not read the Windows certificate store, so when a local HTTPS interceptor replaces the server certificate chain, Node rejects it. The certificate replaced by the interceptor is signed by a locally-installed root CA — Chromium/curl/schannel trust it automatically, Node does not.

Evidence

Certificate chain as seen from Node during the failure (issuer is the local interceptor, not a public CA):

$ node probe-issuer.mjs
  platform.deepseek.com -> subject=*.deepseek.com  issuer=Kaspersky Anti-Virus Personal Root Certificate
  harness.deepseek.com  -> subject=*.deepseek.com  issuer=Kaspersky Anti-Virus Personal Root Certificate
  api.deepseek.com      -> subject=api.deepseek.com issuer=Kaspersky Anti-Virus Personal Root Certificate

Same probe executed with the application's own binary in Node mode (identical runtime to the host process):

$ ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "F:\DeepSeek\Harness\DeepSeek Harness.exe" probe-verify.mjs
  FAIL https://platform.deepseek.com/ -> SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN
  FAIL https://harness.deepseek.com/  -> SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN
  FAIL https://api.deepseek.com       -> SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN

Control group, same machine, same moment — everything that reads the Windows store succeeds:

$ curl -A "<real browser UA>" https://platform.deepseek.com/   -> 200
$ curl -A "<real browser UA>" https://harness.deepseek.com/    -> 404 (TLS OK)

After disabling the AV's encrypted-connection scanning, the very same Node-mode probe returns platform.deepseek.com -> 200, api.deepseek.com -> 401, i.e. the TLS layer is healthy — proving the failure is purely certificate trust on the Node side, not network, DNS, proxy rules, or the account backend.

Already ruled out

  • Network reachability / DNS / routing. The host's TUN proxy routes *.deepseek.com DIRECT (verified via the proxy's own connection log: match GeoSite(cn) using DIRECT).

  • The account service itself. Reachable and healthy from a browser on the same machine.

  • WAF/UA filtering. platform.deepseek.com returns 429 for UA-less requests, but 200 with a normal browser UA — a red herring worth ignoring.

Impact

Anyone running the desktop app behind local HTTPS inspection — which is the default configuration of several consumer AV suites and of many corporate endpoints — cannot sign in at all, and the UI gives them nothing to work with: no error code, no log file, a dead retry button. The failure mode also silently extends to any other Node-side request the host process makes (harness.deepseek.com, etc.).

Suggested fixes (in order of preference)

  1. Use the Chromium network stack for authentication requests. Requests issued via Electron's net module (main process) or from the renderer use Chromium's stack, which reads the OS certificate store — this alone makes the app work behind AV/enterprise interception, with no user action.

  2. Let the Node-side host process trust the OS store when available: Node 22.15+ supports --use-system-ca on Windows. If the bundled runtime allows it, launching the host with that flag (or exposing it as a config option) resolves the class of problem generally.

  3. Support explicit CA injection (e.g. honour NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, or a configured ca.pem path) so that managed environments can be accommodated without disabling interception.

  4. Surface the real error. At minimum:

    • write the underlying failure (code, target hostname, error message) to %APPDATA%\@deepseek-ai\dsh-desktop\logs\main.log;

    • show it in the sign-in UI;

    • detect this specific failure (SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN / UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE) and tell the user what to do (whitelist the app in their AV / proxy).

  5. Fix the silent retry button. 「重新登录」 giving zero feedback on click is independently a bug — at minimum a loading state, ideally the error from the retried attempt.

Workaround for affected users (current)

  • In the AV/HTTPS-scanner, exclude DeepSeek Harness.exe and enable「不扫描加密流量」, or disable encrypted-connection scanning. Caveat observed on Kaspersky 21.19: an application-level exclusion can be partial — after excluding the executable, api.deepseek.com came back with a real public-CA chain while platform.deepseek.com and harness.deepseek.com were still intercepted. So a per-app exclusion is not a reliable workaround; only disabling the feature worked. This strengthens the case for handling it on the app side.

  • Alternatively, export the interceptor's root CA as PEM and set NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS to it for the app (verified working), but this relies on the user reverse-engineering the cause first.

Probe scripts used

probe-issuer.mjs — prints the actual issuer of each host's certificate:

import tls from 'node:tls';
const hosts = ['platform.deepseek.com', 'harness.deepseek.com', 'api.deepseek.com'];
for (const h of hosts) {
  await new Promise((res) => {
    const s = tls.connect({ host: h, port: 443, servername: h, rejectUnauthorized: false }, () => {
      const c = s.getPeerCertificate(true);
      console.log(`  ${h} -> subject=${c.subject?.CN} issuer=${c.issuer?.CN ?? c.issuer?.O}`);
      s.end(); res();
    });
    s.on('error', (e) => { console.log(`  ${h} -> ERR ${e.code || e.message}`); res(); });
    setTimeout(() => { s.destroy(); res(); }, 8000);
  });
}

probe-verify.mjs — plain request check:

const urls = ['https://platform.deepseek.com/', 'https://harness.deepseek.com/', 'https://api.deepseek.com'];
for (const u of urls) {
  try {
    const r = await fetch(u);
    console.log(`  OK   ${u} -> ${r.status}`);
  } catch (e) {
    console.log(`  FAIL ${u} -> ${e.cause?.code ?? e.message}`);
  }
}

Run them with the application's own binary to reproduce the host-process runtime exactly:

ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "F:\DeepSeek\Harness\DeepSeek Harness.exe" probe-verify.mjs

discussions.title: Terminal on Windows: CJK bytes escaped as M-... in the prompt, and IME (pinyin) input does not work
discussions.body:
### Summary

Two problems in the **DSH terminal on Windows** (Git Bash via the official terminal), both affecting CJK users:

1. **Non-ASCII bytes in the prompt are escaped** (`M-…`) while `pwd` prints the same path correctly.
2. **An IME (pinyin) cannot enter text** in the terminal.

They look independent (one is the shell's prompt string, the other is the frontend input path), so they are reported separately below.

### Environment

* Windows 11 · DSH `0.1.7-rc.2` (`dsh --version`) · web GUI
* terminal: the built-in sidebar terminal, shell = Git Bash
* working directory contains non-ASCII (CJK) characters
* (Additional data point collected on macOS with a real pty, see the reproduction.)

### Problem 1 — CJK bytes in the prompt become `M-…`

**Actual:** the prompt shows the working directory as escaped 8-bit bytes:

```
~/Documents/<workspace-with-cjk>/M-iM-;M-^XM-hM-.M-$M-eM-7M-%M-dM-=M-^\M-eM-^LM-:> 
```

**Same terminal, same directory:** `pwd` prints it correctly:

```
/c/Users/<user>/Documents/<workspace-with-cjk>
```

So the path itself is fine; only the prompt rendering is affected. (This is the same mechanism the user reported as "path display is broken".)

**Minimal reproduction / what I could confirm**

I could not run the Windows build, so I reproduced the mechanism on macOS through a **real pty** with a CJK directory and `PS1='\w> '`:

| locale passed to the shell | prompt |
|---|---|
| `LC_ALL=C` | `/private/tmp/…/M-iM-;M-^XM-hM-.M-$M-eM-7M-%M-dM-=M-^\M-eM-^LM-:> ` (escaped) |
| `LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8` | **escaped identically** |
| `LC_ALL=C` + `TERM=dumb` | **escaped identically** |

Two findings worth noting:

* A **literal** non-ASCII `PS1` (`PS1='中文目录> '`) is **not** escaped in any of those cases. The escaping happens where the *shell itself* decodes the working directory into the prompt (`\w` / `\W`, which the default Git Bash prompt uses). It is therefore not the terminal renderer.
* Contrary to my initial hypothesis, **the locale did not change the behaviour on that macOS/bash build**, so I am *not* claiming the cause. The Windows check is the missing piece — see below.

**Readings requested on Windows** (this is the decisive control):

```
echo "LANG=[$LANG] LC_ALL=[$LC_ALL] LC_CTYPE=[$LC_CTYPE]"
locale
PS1='\w> '          # does the escaped form come back?
export LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8   # or C.UTF-8, whichever Git Bash ships
PS1='\w> '
```

Expected: the prompt persists the path in its original non-ASCII form (or at least the terminal shows readable CJK), like `pwd` does.
Actual: the prompt shows `M-…` escapes.

**A code lead (read-only inspection of my local checkout):** the terminal backend does not pass any locale to the shell. `packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/index.ts` `childEnvironment()` (around `:64-88`) sets `TERM: 'dumb'`, `PAGER`, `GIT_PAGER`, `DSH_*`, `PS1`, `PROMPT_COMMAND` — and no `LANG`/`LC_ALL`/`LC_CTYPE`; the environment is the subprocess provider's scrubbed ambient base, which on Windows has no locale variables. There is no other `LC_ALL` in `packages/terminal/*`, `packages/api/terminal-controller` or `packages/subprocess/subprocess-local` except Linux sandbox helpers pinning `LC_ALL=C` (`subprocess-local/src/linux-scope.ts`). Passing a UTF-8 locale for the terminal shell (or allowing a per-row `env` map) would be an upstream change; a third-party plugin cannot do it today because the terminal row's Config only carries `shell.path` / `shell.name` / `shell.args`.

### Problem 2 — IME (pinyin) does not work in the terminal

**Actual:** typing pinyin in the DSH terminal does not produce characters (composition/candidate window does not commit text).

**Not reproduced locally** (the headless macOS environment has no IME), so this half is reported as observed behaviour plus a code-level pointer rather than a confirmed cause.

**Code-level pointer:** the terminal frontend is **xterm.js** (`packages/client/ui-sidebar-terminal/src/client/terminal.tsx`, `new Terminal({…})`), so composition handling is xterm's own; DSH's terminal code contains no `composition*` handling for the terminal surface — the only composition-aware code in that package is the *title rename input* (`TerminalTitle.tsx`, which skips Enter while `isComposing` is true). If the terminal's hidden textarea loses focus, is covered by an overlay, or the key handler swallows `keyCode 229` / `composition*`, the IME never commits. Related reports exist for the **chat input** ([#4233](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/4233), [#1417](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1417), [#6138](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/6138)) but not for the terminal.

### Impact

Any CJK (and generally non-ASCII) user who works in a directory with a localized name sees a mangled prompt, and cannot type their language into the terminal at all. The second one makes the terminal unusable for them, not just ugly.

### Ask

* Problem 1: is the terminal shell supposed to receive a UTF-8 locale (and would you accept passing one, or a per-row `env` map)? If the escaping is expected on Windows, is there a recommended shell-side setup?
* Problem 2: is IME input in the sidebar terminal supposed to work today? If yes, any pointer to what handles composition there would help us aim the report.

Happy to run anything on Windows, or to provide the exact pty script and raw byte dumps.

discussions.title: Session.append 不透传 ignorable 信封 + 持久化写读校验不对称——下游插件无法以受支持方式持久化可跳过事件（附生产实测）
discussions.body:
## 背景

版本 0.1.5-rc.3。持久化层对插件事件的读写契约不对称，三处叠加：

**写入路径**（`dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` worker）：不校验 `KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES`——任何类型的事件都能落盘。

**读取路径**（同 worker 5679 行）：`if (!KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES.has(event.type) && event.ignorable !== true) throw unsupported(...)`——白名单外且无 `ignorable: true` 标记的事件会导致**整条日志拒收**（报错：`refusing to interpret the log — it was likely written by a newer harness`）。

**Session.append API**（`dsh-session/lib/index.js` 1171-1176 行）：`append(type, data, ...opts)` 的 opts 只透传 `sourceEventSeqs` 与 `surfaceOp`，**没有 ignorable 的透传入口**。

三者叠加：下游插件写入非 surface 事件 → 落盘成功 → 会话日志重载即整档被拒。插件要么不写（功能哑火），要么裸写（档不可达），**没有第三条受支持的路**。

## 生产实测（2026-09-26）

- dsh-talk 0.3.12（无写入门槛）：90 条 `dsh-talk/speech` 事件裸写进 5 个会话档 → 双端全部无法加载（`stored session ... failed validation`）。
- dsh-talk 0.3.13（作者自行加了写入门槛）：事件不再写入 → 语音功能静默失效（见 PerryLink/dsh-talk#22，含作者对同一契约冲突的独立分析）。
- 我们对 5 个生产档做字段级修复（90 条事件补 `"ignorable": true` + 双帧重压缩）后全部恢复加载，web/桌面双端实测通过。

## 复现要点

1. rc.3 实例，插件在会话中 append 一个白名单外类型（如 `dsh-talk/speech`）
2. 重启实例或换另一端打开该会话
3. 报「refusing to interpret the log」整档拒收

## 建议（按优先级）

1. **`Session.append` 增加 ignorable 透传**：如 `append(type, data, { ignorable: true })` → envelope 落 `ignorable: true`。持久化文档自己把这个标记称为「the compatibility mechanism」，但 API 没有入口，机制对下游形同虚设。
2. **写入路径同步校验（fail-fast）**：插件写白名单外事件时写入即报错，而不是等重载时炸整档——把事故从「会话不可达」降级为「单条写入失败」。
3. 至少在插件开发文档中明确「下游插件不得持久化非 surface 事件」的契约与后果。

## 正面印证

0.1.7 线的实验性语音输入（`docs/subsystems/voice-input.zh.md`）明确设计为「识别本身不写入 Session 事件」——官方自己的新功能也选择绕开会话日志，恰好说明当前 API 面对「下游插件瞬态状态持久化」是缺位的。

discussions.title: pnpm run clean fails out of the box on 0.1.7-rc.2: clean.ts rejects the desktop-keyboard-tests tsconfig outDir
discussions.body:
# `pnpm run clean` fails out of the box on 0.1.7-rc.2

## TL;DR

On a clean checkout of current master (`dsh-v0.1.7-rc.2`), `pnpm run clean` exits 1 before deleting anything:

```
$ pnpm run clean

clean: expected TypeScript outDir to end in /types: lib/desktop-keyboard-test-types
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
```

The new `tsconfig.desktop-keyboard-tests.json` declares `"outDir": "lib/desktop-keyboard-test-types"`, and `scripts/clean.ts` only accepts outDirs whose basename is `types` (plus one special-cased native entry), so plan-time validation throws and the tool never reaches deletion.

## Why it matters

This is the recovery command that several threads prescribe for the class of failure where a version switch over a long-lived checkout leaves stale `lib/` output that breaks the typert/tool layer — #7086 documents exactly that symptom and the standard `pnpm run clean → pnpm install → pnpm run build` procedure. With `clean` itself broken, that procedure is currently not executable; the only workaround is removing `lib/` directories and `*.tsbuildinfo` files by hand.

## Root cause

- `tsconfig.desktop-keyboard-tests.json` was added in `6a82709a2b` ("fix(shortcuts): preserve focus and tab layout, block overlay input", 09-22) with `outDir: lib/desktop-keyboard-test-types`.
- Root `tsconfig.json` → `tsconfig.client.json` (reference at its line 46) → `tsconfig.desktop-keyboard-tests.json`, so the file is reachable from the graph `RepositoryCleaner.buildOutputDirectories()` walks.
- That walk validates every reached outDir: `basename(...) === 'types'` or the `native/system/packages/entry/lib` exception; `desktop-keyboard-test-types` matches neither, so it throws before any target is collected.

Verified against current upstream master: `scripts/clean.ts` and the tsconfig are byte-identical in my tree, so this is not a fork artifact.

## Suggested fixes

Either of:

1. Nest the outDir so it ends in `/types` (e.g. `lib/desktop-keyboard-tests/types`), keeping the clean.ts rule as-is; or
2. Extend `buildOutputDirectories()` with this outDir as an explicit exception, the way `nativeEntryOutput` already is.

Happy to send the one-liner for either direction if maintainers say which they prefer.

discussions.title: tool "academic_writing" returned invalid output: value is not lossless JSON
discussions.body:
I looked into this issue, and it seems that the problem isn't that `academic_writing` fails to generate the content. Instead, the returned object contains several optional fields whose values are `undefined`.

For example, when calling `outline`, the actual result looks roughly like this:

```js
{
  action: "outline",
  text: "...",
  issues: undefined,
  passed: undefined,
  items: undefined
}
```

`action` and `text` are both fine. The problem is with the `undefined` fields.

DSH checks whether the tool output can be represented as lossless JSON before processing it further. Since JSON doesn't support `undefined`, the entire result gets rejected with:

```text
value is not lossless JSON
```

I also checked the output schema for this tool. Only `action` is required, while `issues`, `passed`, and `items` are optional. So when these fields don't have a value, they can simply be omitted instead of being included as `undefined`.

As a temporary local workaround, I removed fields with `undefined` values before the result reaches `snapshotToolValue()`:

```js
candidate = Object.fromEntries(
  Object.entries(candidate).filter(([, value]) => value !== undefined)
);
```

After applying this change, the same `academic_writing` `outline` call successfully returned the generated outline.

So it looks like the root cause is that `academic_writing` includes optional fields that aren't used by the current action in the returned object, with their values left as `undefined`.

discussions.title: [Bug][0.1.7-rc.2] Failed turn (HTTP 400/429) leaves all-zero usage samples; contextPressure projection permanently zeroed — ContextMeter shows 0%
discussions.body:
## Summary

When a turn fails with a provider error (HTTP 400/429), a placeholder **all-zero usage chunk**
(`{ inputTokens: 0, outputTokens: 0, totalTokens: 0 }`) is written into the `assistant/attempt`
stream. The `contextPressure` projection in `dsh-token-meter` folds this zero sample as if it were
a valid measurement and **overwrites the last good `pressureTokens` value**. Since the
projection-cache checkpoint sits at the session tail, the zero is never recomputed on later loads —
the UI `ContextMeter` permanently shows **0%** for that session, even though the session data
itself is intact.

## Reproduction

1. Session with a 1M-token context window; last valid usage sample: `input 399 + cacheRead 274560`
   → `pressureTokens = 274959` (ContextMeter ≈ 27%).
2. Submit a turn; the provider fails. Observed with both `400: insufficient credits` (single
   attempt) and `429: token plan entitlement exhausted` (retry loop, 5 attempts, one all-zero
   usage chunk per attempt, `turn/end` error).
3. Reopen the session: the persisted projection checkpoint now holds
   `contextPressure: { pressureTokens: 0, sampledSurfaceTokens: <n> }`; projected tokens evaluate
   to `max(0, …) = 0` → ContextMeter shows **0%** permanently (checkpoint seq equals the session
   tail, so replay never recomputes it).

## Current behavior

- ContextMeter shows 0% forever after a failed turn; `tokenUsage.last` is polluted with all-zero
  buckets the same way (per-session totals unaffected because the turn ended with the error).
- Any projection-cache re-fold re-poisons the checkpoint, because the zero samples live in the
  persisted event log (v4 JSONL) — e.g. a cache rebuild / version migration restores the 0%.
- Observed on 2 of 11 v4-format sessions on this machine — exactly the two whose turns ended in
  provider errors.
- Cross-check: the session JSONL itself is intact (final `assistant/message` usage shows
  `totalTokens = 275685`), and offline replay of the same raw events through the real kernel
  packages (`Session.create` + token-meter measure) returns `totalTokens = 277806`, baseline
  `usage` — the meter computes correctly from events; only the persisted projection checkpoint
  got poisoned.
- No data loss in our case: the checkpoint was repaired by restoring `pressureTokens` to the last
  valid value (input + cacheRead of the last valid sample), after which the meter displays
  correctly again.

## Expected behavior

Usage samples belonging to failed attempts (HTTP 4xx/5xx, turn ended with error) must not be
folded into `contextPressure`. Defensively, an all-zero sample (`totalTokens === 0 &&
inputTokens === 0 && outputTokens === 0`) should be ignored whenever a previous valid sample
exists.

## Environment

- DeepSeek Harness Desktop `0.1.7-rc.2` (exe FileVersion `0.1.7-rc.2`), Windows 11 (build 26200)
- Kernel packages `@deepseek-ai/*` all `0.1.7-rc.2`; affected package `@deepseek-ai/dsh-token-meter`
  (repo path `packages/llm/token-meter`)
- Session format: v4

discussions.title: [desktop 0.1.7-rc.2] Host startup fails in `removeLinkProjections` (`rmSync` → ERROR_INVALID_NAME); files in the linked checkout were deleted during the same `applyRelease`
discussions.body:
## Environment

- DeepSeek Harness desktop **0.1.7-rc.2** (installed at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\DeepSeek Harness`), Electron 44.0.0 / Node 24.18.1, Windows 11 x64 (10.0.26200)
- `DSH_HOME` pointed at the home a **local dev launch** had created:
  `<repo>\apps\desktop\.desktop-build\development\home`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Launch the unpackaged dev build once (`pnpm run start:desktop`), so the desktop's link-backend launch writes its package projections into the profile:
   `<profile>\.dsh-module-fallback\node_modules\**` — measured on this machine: **607 directory junctions into the checkout, 29 plain directories, 0 real files**.
2. Stop it, then launch the packaged 0.1.7-rc.2 against the same `DSH_HOME`.
3. The host process dies during startup and the shell shows *"The application could not start or stopped unexpectedly."*

Repeatable: six crash logs between 00:04:27 and 00:07:17 local.

## Crash

`%APPDATA%\@deepseek-ai\dsh-desktop\logs\crash-2026-09-26T16-07-17-380Z-host.log`

```
source: host
phase: startup
app: @deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop 0.1.7-rc.2
--- error ---
Error: , Unknown error: 系统无法辨识文件名。 '\\?\D:\...\apps\desktop\.desktop-build\development\home\profiles\desktop\.dsh-module-fallback'
    at rmSync (node:fs:1222:18)
    at removeLinkProjections (…/resources/app.asar/lib/main.js:3321:2)
    at …/app.asar/lib/main.js:3476:4
    at DesktopProjectManager.withLock (…/app.asar/lib/main.js:3508:17)
    at DesktopProjectManager.applyRelease (…/app.asar/lib/main.js:3472:14)
  errno: -4094,        // UV_UNKNOWN
  code: '',
  path: '\\\\?\\D:\\…\\.dsh-module-fallback',
  syscall: 'rm'
```

`0x7B` / `ERROR_INVALID_NAME` (the message is the localized Windows text), surfaced by libuv as `UV_UNKNOWN` (`-4094`).

Source at tag `dsh-v0.1.7-rc.2` (commit `477b4f42`), `packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile.ts:274`:

```ts
export function removeLinkProjections(dir: string): void {
  const owned = join(dir, LINK_PROJECTION_DIR)
  if (!existsSync(owned)) return
  const ownedModules = join(owned, 'node_modules')
  for (const link of symlinksUnder(join(dir, 'node_modules'))) {
    if (pointsInto(link, ownedModules)) unlinkSync(link)
  }
  rmSync(owned, { recursive: true, force: true })   // ← throws
}
```

## Collateral damage (the part that matters most)

While the same `applyRelease` ran, files **inside the checkout the projections point at** were deleted — not just the links:

| when (local) | what | evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 00:04:25 (2 s before the first crash) | `vendor/cordis/LICENSE`, `vendor/cordis/bin.js`, `vendor/include/LICENSE` deleted | `git status --porcelain` → ` D vendor/cordis/LICENSE`, ` D vendor/cordis/bin.js`, ` D vendor/include/LICENSE`; directory mtimes 09-27 00:04:25 |
| 13:26:08 (earlier run in the same dev home) | `vendor/cosmokit/**` and `vendor/schemastery/**` emptied completely (including `package.json`) | directory mtimes 09-26 13:26:08; the app then failed to boot with `Cannot find package …/vendor/cosmokit/lib/index.js` |

Both were restored with `git checkout -- vendor`; the working tree is clean again.

Deleting the projection **before** launching the packaged app removes both symptoms: the app then starts normally (host writes its storage ~3 s after launch) and no further files are touched.

## Isolation attempts (so they are not repeated)

- Removing the projection with **one `rmdir` per junction** (`fs.rmdirSync(link)`, never recursing) succeeds: 607/607 junctions unlinked, 30 directories removed, **607/607 junction targets verified intact** — no real file was lost.
- A minimal probe on this machine (Node 24.19.0, Windows 11 26200) shows that a plain `fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })` over a directory containing junctions — with a short target **and** with a 331-character target — **succeeds and leaves the junction targets intact**. I could not reproduce either the throw or the target deletion in isolation, so the trigger is specific to this profile's projection layout (607 junctions, several levels of junction→junction chains into `<repo>\node_modules\.pnpm\…` and `vendor\*`); I did not want to guess further in a report.

## Suggested hardening

1. **Never let projection cleanup abort host startup.** A failure here should degrade to a warning and continue; today it turns a dirty profile into a dead application.
2. **Do not `rmSync(…, { recursive: true })` a tree that can contain junctions.** Walk it, `lstat` each entry, and unlink junction/symlink entries individually (that is the operation that provably works), or move it aside and delete best-effort.
3. **Refuse to clean projections that escape the profile.** Here every projection pointed into the user's checkout; when a link target is outside `DSH_HOME`, the safe action is to report, not to delete.
4. Consider **not sharing one `DSH_HOME` between the dev build and the packaged app**, or documenting that a dev-created profile must not be reused by a packaged launch.

## Attachments

- `crash-2026-09-26T16-07-17-380Z-host.log` (plus five earlier logs from the same session)
- `git status` output for the deleted checkout files

## Crash log (inline)

The Discussions API has no file attachment, so the full log follows. It is also at
`%APPDATA%\@deepseek-ai\dsh-desktop\logs\crash-2026-09-26T16-07-17-380Z-host.log` on the affected machine.

<details><summary>crash-2026-09-26T16-07-17-380Z-host.log</summary>

```text
time: 2026-09-26T16:07:17.380Z
source: host
phase: startup
app: @deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop 0.1.7-rc.2
platform: win32 x64
electron: 44.0.0
node: 24.18.1
locale: en
shell pid: 4120

--- error ---
Error: , Unknown error: ÏµÍ³ÎÞ·¨±æÊ¶ÎÄ¼þÃû¡£ '\\?\<repo>\apps\desktop\.desktop-build\development\home\profiles\desktop\.dsh-module-fallback'
    at rmSync (node:fs:1222:18)
    at removeLinkProjections (file:///C:/Users/<user>/AppData/Local/Programs/DeepSeek%20Harness/resources/app.asar/lib/main.js:3321:2)
    at file:///C:/Users/<user>/AppData/Local/Programs/DeepSeek%20Harness/resources/app.asar/lib/main.js:3476:4
    at DesktopProjectManager.withLock (file:///C:/Users/<user>/AppData/Local/Programs/DeepSeek%20Harness/resources/app.asar/lib/main.js:3508:17)
    at DesktopProjectManager.applyRelease (file:///C:/Users/<user>/AppData/Local/Programs/DeepSeek%20Harness/resources/app.asar/lib/main.js:3472:14)
    at file:///C:/Users/<user>/AppData/Local/Programs/DeepSeek%20Harness/resources/app.asar/lib/main.js:10837:19
    at file:///C:/Users/<user>/AppData/Local/Programs/DeepSeek%20Harness/resources/app.asar/lib/main.js:6367:11 {

  syscall: 'rm'
}

(no error-level renderer console output was captured)
```
